en: The Compendium of the Reality of All Tathāgatas:

Thus have I heard at one time: the Blessed One was endowed with the various distinctions of the wisdom of the commitment (*samaya*) of the vajra-consecration of all Tathāgatas, and had attained the consecration of the sovereignty over the Dharma of the triple world and the jewel-crown of all Tathāgatas.

The great lord of yogis possessing the omniscience of all Tathāgatas; the fulfiller of all hopes of the entire realm of sentient beings, without exception, by accomplishing all activities through the realization of the equality of all mudrās of all Tathāgatas;
the Great Compassionate One, Vairocana, the Eternal, established in the samaya of the three times, the Tathāgata of the vajra of all body, speech, and mind.

He dwelt in the palace of Akaniṣṭha, the king of the gods— a place praised and extolled as the abode of all Tathāgatas, inlaid with great precious jewels, adorned with bells of various colors, and beautified by moon-like ornaments, half-necklaces, necklaces, chowries, and silk streamers fluttering in the wind.
He was there together with ninety-nine koṭis of bodhisattvas.
Namely, with the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, and Ākāśagarbha;
and Vajramuṣṭi, and Mañjuśrī,
and Sahacittotpādadharmacakrapravartin;
With Gaganagañja and Sarvamārabalapramardin at their head, there were ninety-nine billion bodhisattvas;
and with Tathāgatas as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā.
It was just as if a sesame pod were seen completely full within Jambudvīpa.
And by those immeasurable Tathāgatas, from each single body of a Tathāgata, immeasurable and incalculable Buddha-fields were seen;
and in those Buddha-fields, they were teaching this very same method of Dharma.

Then the Blessed One Mahāvairocana—the Vajra of Body, Speech, and Mind eternally abiding throughout the entire realm of space; the Knowledge Being who awakens the entire vajra-realm by virtue of being the convergence of all Tathāgatas; the womb of the wisdom arising from the vajra-consecration of the atoms of the entire realm of space; the great jewel of the vajra-knowledge initiation due to the infinity of all Tathāgatas; and who has become the perfect awakening through the realization of the suchness that pervades all space—[spoke].

Because he is the purity of the embodiment of all Tathāgatas, he is the one whose all phenomena are pure by nature; he is the foremost in the conduct of all space. Because he carries out the unfailing commands of all Tathāgatas, he is the sovereign of all incomparable and unsurpassed universal activities. He is the firm being of the great awakening of all Tathāgatas, the commitment for the summoning of all Tathāgatas, and the lord of the wisdom that brings about the passion of all Tathāgatas.

The expression of "well done" by all Tathāgatas; the great jewel of consecration of all Tathāgatas; the solar disc of light of all Tathāgatas; the crest-jewel of the wish-fulfilling king of gems of all Tathāgatas; the great laughter of all Tathāgatas; the great pure Dharma of all Tathāgatas;
the wisdom-knowledge of all Tathāgatas; the wheel of all Tathāgatas; and the very firm armor of the great heroism of all Tathāgatas.
The Vajrayakṣa who protects and guards all Tathāgatas; the knowledge of the vajra-binding mudrās of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
Praise of Samantabhadra, the Great Reality of Awakening:
Samantabhadra, self-unfailing, the Māra who leads with joy.
Khagarbha, of great majesty, Ratnaketu, and Mahāsmita. // 1 //
And Avalokitamaheśa, Mañjuśrī who is the embodiment of all mandalas, Avāca, Viśvakarman, Vīrya, Caṇḍa, and Dṛḍhagraha. // 2 //
Vajra, Aṅkuśa, Śara, Tuṣṭi, Ratna, Sūrya, Dhvaja, Smṛti, Padma, Kośa, Sucakra, Vāk, Karma, Varma, Ravi, and Graha. // 3 //
Without beginning or end, peaceful, Rudra, Krodha, the greatly patient one; the Yakṣa, the divine Rākṣasa, the steadfast, the son of Sūri, the son of Sūri, the great all-pervading lord. // 4 //
The Lord of Umā, the Protector of Creatures, Viṣṇu, the Victorious One, the Great Sage;
the Guardian of the World, the Sky, and the Earth—the three worlds are indeed the triple realm. // 5 //
He is the Great Element, the Benefactor of all beings, the All, Śarva, and the Grandfather;
he is Saṃsāra and Nirvṛti, the Eternal, Right Conduct, and the Great Festival.

The Buddha is pure, the Mahāyāna, the three realms of existence, the eternal, the destroyer of harm; he is the conqueror of the three worlds, Śambhu, the Lord Śambhu, and the Bestower of Prosperity. // 7 //
Vajranātha, the foremost of excellent grounds, wisdom, the method of the perfections, liberation, the bodhisattva, conduct, and all the Tathāgatas. // 8 //
The meaning of the Buddha, the heart of the Buddha, all unsurpassed awakening; Vairocana, the Victor, the Protector, the Self-Existent One, the dhāraṇī, and mindfulness. // 9 //
The Great Being, the Great Seal, is the meditative absorption that performs the deeds of a Buddha;
he has become the essence of all Buddhas, a being who awakens to the eternal reality. // 10 //
Mahāsthāṇu, Mahākāla, Mahārāga, Mahāsukha;
Mahāpāpa, Mahāgryāgrya, Sarvāgrya, Bhuvaneśvara. // 11 //
The Blessed One, the Great Bodhicitta Samantabhadra, the Great Bodhisattva, dwelt within the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.
Then, this Buddha-field was completely filled by all the Tathāgatas, just like a sesame pod.
Then, indeed, all the Tathāgatas, having assembled in a great gathering, approached the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvārthasiddhi, who was seated at the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*).

Having approached, they manifested themselves through their bodies of enjoyment (*sāṃbhogika-kāya*) and said this to the Bodhisattva: "O son of good family, how will you fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
“Since you do not understand the reality of all the Tathāgatas, how can you venture to undergo all these hardships?

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvārthasiddhi, having been exhorted by all the Tathāgatas, arose from that *āsphāna* samādhi, prostrated before all the Tathāgatas, and addressed them thus: “O Blessed Tathāgatas, give me your command! How should I proceed? What is that reality like?”

When this had been said, all the Tathāgatas spoke with one voice to that Bodhisattva: “Proceed, noble son, by means of the concentration on the examination of one’s own mind, with the mantra naturally accomplished and recited according to one’s inclination: *Oṃ cittaprativedhaṃ karomi*.
Then the Bodhisattva said to all the Tathāgatas: “I have understood, Blessed Tathāgatas; I see the form of a moon disc within my own heart.”
All the Tathāgatas said: "O son of good family, this mind is luminous by nature; it becomes exactly as it is conditioned.
It is just like dyeing a white cloth with color."

Then, all the Tathāgatas, for the purpose of expanding the wisdom of the mind that is luminous by nature, once again generated the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*) for that Bodhisattva with this mantra, naturally accomplished: *oṃ bodhicittam utpādayāmi*.

Then, having again generated the thought of awakening at the command of all the Tathāgatas, the Bodhisattva spoke thus: "That which has the form of a moon disc, I see as nothing other than that very moon disc."
All the Tathāgatas said: "Samantabhadra, this arousal of the mind (*cittotpāda*) is the heart of all Tathāgatas and has become the proper conduct (*sāmīcī*). Therefore, practice it well!
For the sake of strengthening the arousal of the Samantabhadra-mind of all Tathāgatas, contemplate the form of a vajra within the moon disc in your own heart with this mantra: *oṃ tiṣṭha vajra*."
The Bodhisattva said, "I see, Blessed One, Tathāgatas, a vajra within the lunar disc.
All the Tathāgatas said, "Make firm this Samantabhadra-mind-vajra of all the Tathāgatas with this mantra: Oṃ, I am of vajra-nature."

Then, as many vajra-realms of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas as there are, which encompass the entire realm of space—all of them entered that Sattvavajra through the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas.
Thereupon, all the Tathāgatas consecrated that Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Sarvārthasiddhi, with the vajra-name consecration: "Vajradhātu, Vajradhātu!"
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajradhātu addressed all those Tathāgatas in this way: "O Blessed Tathāgatas, I see myself as the body of all the Tathāgatas.
All the Tathāgatas said: "In that case, O Mahāsattva, meditate upon yourself as the Buddha-image, the Sattvavajra endowed with the excellence of all aspects.
Having recited this mantra—which is perfected by its very nature—as much as you desire: *oṃ yathā sarvatathāgatāstathāham* (Oṃ, as are all the Tathāgatas, so am I)."

Then, when this had been said, the Great Bodhisattva Vajradhātu, having awakened himself as the Tathāgata, prostrated to all those Tathāgatas, summoned them, and spoke thus: "O Blessed Tathāgatas, please empower me; make this awakening firm!
When this had been said, all the Tathāgatas entered that Sattvavajra of the Tathāgata Vajradhātu.
Then, at that very moment, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vajradhātu, having fully awakened to the wisdom of the equality of all Tathāgatas,

entered the secret samaya of the mudrā of the vajra-wisdom of the equality of all Tathāgatas; being pure by nature through the realization of the wisdom of the equality of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas,
he became the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, who has become a source of the wisdom of the natural luminosity of the equality of all things belonging to all Tathāgatas.

Then all the Tathāgatas, having again emerged from those *sarvatathāgatasattvavajras*, were consecrated with the great jewel-consecration of the *ākāśagarbha-mahāmaṇiratna*; having generated the Dharma-knowledge of Avalokiteśvara and established [him] in the universal activity (*viśvakarma*) of all the Tathāgatas, they proceeded to the summit of Mount Sumeru and to the gabled chamber on the peak of the *vajramaṇiratna*.
Having approached, they empowered the Tathāgata Vajradhātu in the state of all the Tathāgatas.
They established the lion-throne of all the Tathāgatas, facing in every direction.

Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja, and the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi— having themselves empowered their own selves as the state of all Tathāgatas, and having relied upon the equality of all directions due to the thorough penetration of the equality of all things by the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni— emanated the thirty-seven deities from samādhi.
They were seated in the four directions.
I.1.6 Vajrasattva.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, who had recently attained perfect awakening; who was consecrated with the great jewel of the sky-born initiation of the heart of Samantabhadra of all the Tathāgatas;

who had reached the supreme perfection of the Dharma-knowledge of Avalokiteśvara of all the Tathāgatas; and whose teaching was unfailing and unimpeded in its universal activity for all the Tathāgatas—[spoke as follows].
Having fulfilled his task and realized his aspirations, and having himself empowered his own self as the state of all Tathāgatas,

he entered the samādhi called the Vajra Empowerment of the Sattva Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra of All Tathāgatas; [and then uttered] this Heart of All Tathāgatas called the Realization of the Mahāyāna of All Tathāgatas.
Vajrasattva emerged from his own heart.

Then, as soon as he had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Samantabhadra, having become moon-maṇḍalas and emerged, purified the great bodhicitta of all sentient beings and remained stationed at the sides of all the Tathāgatas.

Then, from those moon-mandalas, the vajras of the wisdom of all the Tathāgatas issued forth and entered the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana. Due to his being Samantabhadra, due to the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, and through the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas, they became a single mass.

Having manifested as a vajra-body composed of the vajras of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas— measuring the entire expanse of space, garlanded with rays of light, five-headed, and possessing a vajra-form—
he emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas and settled upon [the practitioner's] hand.
Then, from that vajra, rays of light in the form of vajras, possessing various colors and forms, issued forth, pervading and illuminating all world-systems.
And from those [emanations] with vajra-light faces, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems issued forth;

through the perfect awakening to the sovereign knowledge and supernormal powers of the equality of all Tathāgatas, throughout the entire expanse of the realm of phenomena, reaching to the limits of the realm of space, within oceans of clouds of spreading world-systems,

they manifested the arousal of the great bodhicitta of all Tathāgatas, the accomplishment of the various practices of Samantabhadra, the gathering of the families of all Tathāgatas, the approach to the great seat of enlightenment, and the subduing of all Māras— [all these they performed].

Having displayed all the miraculous manifestations of the Tathāgatas— beginning with the realization of the great awakening of the equality of the Tathāgatas and the turning of the wheel of Dharma, up to the protection of the realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder, and the accomplishment of all benefit, happiness, and the supreme siddhi of the knowledge and supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas— and having become a single, solid mass as the body of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra due to his universal benevolence and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva samādhi, he appeared.
Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am Samantabhadra, the firm being among the self-existent ones; because of my firmness, though bodiless, I have attained the state of a body of beings."
Then the body of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One and taken his place upon a moon disc in front of all the Tathāgatas, awaited an instruction.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the meditative absorption named the Vajra of the Samaya of the Wisdom of All Tathāgatas, for the sake of the great means, power, and vigor of turning the wheel of Dharma through the morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and vision of the knowledge of liberation of all Tathāgatas for the benefit of sentient beings; for the sake of the samaya of great wisdom that protects the realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder and exercises sovereignty over all; and for the purpose of experiencing all happiness and mental well-being, up until the attainment of the fruit of the supreme accomplishment of the realization of the Great Vehicle and the super-knowledge of the equality-wisdom of all Tathāgatas—he [manifested] that Vajra of the Accomplishment of All Tathāgatas.

Having consecrated that Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra in the sovereignty of all Tathāgatas by means of the crown-ribbon empowerment of the jewel-body of all Buddhas, [the Lord] bestowed [the vajra] upon him with both hands.
Thereupon, he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name empowerment as "Vajrapāṇi, Vajrapāṇi."

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, cradling the left [hand] with the pride of the vajra, and holding that vajra by means of the yoga of drawing it up to his own heart, uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is the unsurpassed vajra of accomplishment of all Buddhas;
I have been given the vajra into my hand, established upon the vajra. Thus he spoke.
I.1.7 Vajrarāja:

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Being Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja; [he then uttered] this heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas called the Samaya for Summoning All Tathāgatas.
The King of Vajras issued forth from his own heart.
Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajrapāṇi became the great hooks of all the Tathāgatas;
having issued forth and entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he appeared as a single, solid, great form of a vajra-hook and took his place in the hand of the Blessed One.
Then, from that great form of the Vajrāṅkuśa, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems issued forth;
having performed all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas, such as the summoning of all Tathāgatas,
and because of his own status as Amogharāja and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, they merged into a single solid mass, becoming the body of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja.
Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am indeed the King of Unfailing Success, the Vajra-born Hook, by which all-pervading Buddhas and the Siddhis are drawn forth. Thus it was said.
Then that body of the great bodhisattva Amogharāja, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One and taken its place upon the lunar mandala to the right of all the Tathāgatas,
once again sought the command.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi named Sarvatathāgatākarṣaṇasamayavajra, for the sake of summoning all Tathāgatas, for the sake of summoning the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, and for the sake of experiencing all happiness and mental well-being,
up to the supreme accomplishment of the empowerment of the assembly of all Tathāgatas, [bestowed] that vajra-hook upon that Amogharāja.
He likewise bestowed [it] with both hands upon the Mahābodhisattva.
Then, he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name consecration: "Vajrākarṣa, Vajrākarṣa!"
Then the Bodhisattva Vajrākarṣa, drawing in all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-hook, uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is the unsurpassed vajra-wisdom of all Buddhas, which is the supreme means of summoning for the sake of accomplishing the welfare of all Buddhas. Thus it was said.
I.1.8 Vajrarāga.

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the "Vajra Empowerment of the Being Arising from the Samaya of the Māra Great Bodhisattva," and from his own heart he uttered this heart-essence of all Tathāgatas, named the "Samaya of the Enamouring of All Tathāgatas": *vajrarāga*.
Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became the flower-weapons of all the Tathāgatas;
having issued forth and entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he appeared as a single mass in the form of a great vajra-arrow and settled in [Vairocana’s] hand.
Then, from that form of the Vajra-Arrow, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems emerged;
having performed all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas, such as the enchantment of all Tathāgatas,
they condensed into a single, solid mass— the body of the Great Bodhisattva Māra— due to the extreme sweetness of the Vajrasattva samādhi and its utter firmness.
Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am the naturally pure passion of the Self-Existent Ones;
for the sake of purification, they indeed discipline those who are detached by means of passion."
Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Māra, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One and taken its place upon the lunar mandalas to the left of all the Tathāgatas,
once again sought his command.
Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi named Vajra of the Empowerment of the Passion of All Tathāgatas,
for the sake of experiencing the passion, joy, pleasure, and mental well-being of the entire realm of beings without exception through the vajra-samaya of slaying all Tathāgatas—
and for the purpose of attaining the fruit of the supreme accomplishment of the activity of slaying all Tathāgatas— directed that vajra-arrow toward that Māra.
He likewise bestowed it upon the Mahābodhisattva with both hands.
Then, he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name-consecration: "Vajradhanu, Vajradhanu."
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajradhanu, slaying all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-arrow, uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is the stainless knowledge of passion of all the Buddhas;
having destroyed dispassion through passion, they indeed bestow all happiness."

I.1.9 Vajrasādhu. Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Being Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Pramodyarāja, and from his own heart he emitted this heart-essence of all Tathāgatas, named the Samaya of the Joy of All Tathāgatas: *Vajrasādhu*.
Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became expressions of approval (*sādhukāra*),
entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, and having become a single solid mass, manifested as the form of Vajra-joy (*vajratuṣṭi*).
It was established in the hand of the Blessed One.
Then, from that form of Vajra-Contentment, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems issued forth;
having performed all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas, such as the "Well Done! (sādhukāra) of all the Tathāgatas, and so forth, [they returned].
Due to his state of supreme joy and because of the extreme firmness of the *vajrasattva* samādhi, he became a single, solid body as the Great Bodhisattva Pramodyarāja;
remaining in the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am indeed the one who utters 'Excellent,' the all-encompassing, the best among all-knowers."
For it certainly produces contentment in those who have abandoned conceptual construction.
Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Pramodyarāja, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana and taken his place upon a moon disc behind all the Tathāgatas,
once again awaited an instruction.
Then the Blessed One, having attained the samādhi named Sarvatathāgata-saṃtoṣaṇa-vajra,

for the purpose of experiencing the great bliss and mental well-being that satisfies the entire realm of sentient beings without exception through the commitment (*samaya*) of the supreme joy and wisdom of all Tathāgatas—
and for the sake of the fruit of attaining the supreme accomplishment of the essence of the highest rapture of all Tathāgatas— bestowed that Vajra-Contentment upon him.
He likewise bestowed [the name] Prāmodyarāja upon the Mahābodhisattva with his two hands;
then, by all the Tathāgatas, he was consecrated with the vajra-name consecration as "Vajraharṣa, Vajraharṣa."

Then the Bodhisattva Vajraharṣa, gladdening all the Tathāgatas with that Vajratuṣṭi by means of shouts of "Excellent!", uttered this inspired utterance: "This is that diamond which sets in motion the 'Excellent' praise of all Buddhas; it brings joy to all, is divine, and increases supreme delight. Thus it was said.
The great bodhicitta,
the commitment for summoning all Tathāgatas, and the wisdom of impassioned devotion to all Tathāgatas.
"Great satisfaction" refers to the Great Samaya Beings of all the Tathāgatas.

I.1.10 Vajraratna: Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment Jewel Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, and from his own heart he emitted this heart-mantra of all the Tathāgatas called the Samaya of the Empowerment of All the Tathāgatas: VAJRARATNAḤ.
Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas— due to the thorough penetration of the wisdom of the equality of all space—
from that very samādhi of Vajrasattva, the Blessed One Vajradhara became the Samaya of the Essence of All Space and issued forth.
By all those rays of light of all space, all world-systems were illuminated.
They became enclosed, equal in extent to the entire realm of space.
Then, through the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas, that entire realm of space entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana.

And because the samādhi of Vajrasattva was perfectly cultivated, there appeared a great body of diamond-jewels, consisting of the essence of the interior of the entire realm of space, equal in measure to the convergence of all world-systems.
It was established in the hand of the Blessed One.
Then, from that form of the vajra-jewel, there emerged as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems;
having performed the consecrations and all the miraculous transformations of the Tathāgatas in all world-systems, [they returned].

Because he is perfectly born from the womb of the entire realm of space and because the samādhi of Vajrasattva is exceedingly firm, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha became a single solid mass;
having arisen and remained in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am indeed the self-consecration, the unsurpassed Vajra-jewel!"
For even the Victors, though free from attachment, are remembered as the lords of the three realms.
Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One and taken his place upon a moon disc in front of all the Tathāgatas,
once again sought their command.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called Sarvatathāgatamaṇiratnavajra, for the sake of fulfilling the intentions of all Tathāgatas through the pledge (samaya), for the sake of bringing about the attainment of all aims for the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, and for the sake of experiencing all happiness and mental well-being,
up until the attainment of the supreme siddhi which is the perfection of the aims of all Tathāgatas, [bestowed] that vajra-jewel upon that Ākāśagarbha.
Having consecrated the Great Bodhisattva in the status of a Vajra-ratna Universal Monarch with the consecration of the Vajra-ratna sprout, he bestowed it upon his two hands.
Then, all the Tathāgatas consecrated Vajragarbha with the vajra-name consecration as "Vajragarbha.
Thereupon, the Great Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, placing that vajra-jewel in the place of his own consecration, uttered this inspired utterance:
This is that consecration of the realm of sentient beings for all Buddhas; "I" and "mine" have been bestowed into my hand, and jewel has been joined to jewel.
I.1.11 Vajratejas.

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Jewel Arising from the Pledge of the Mahātejas Great Bodhisattva, and from his own heart he emitted this heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas called the Pledge of the Rays of All Tathāgatas: *vajrateja*.
Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajrapāṇi became great solar mandalas;
having entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he appeared as a single solid mass in the form of the Vajrasūrya and took his place in the hand of the Blessed One.
Then, from that Vajrasūryamaṇḍala, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems issued forth;
having performed all the miraculous transformations of the Tathāgatas, such as emitting rays of light from all the Tathāgatas,
they coalesced into a single, solid body of a Great Bodhisattva of immense splendor, due to the great majesty of the Vajrasattva-samādhi and its extreme firmness.
Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Truly incomparable is your splendor that illuminates the realm of sentient beings, which purifies even the pure Buddhas, the Protectors."
Then that body of the great bodhisattva Vimalatejas, having descended from the heart of the Bhagavān and taken its place upon the lunar mandala to the right of all the Tathāgatas,
again sought his command.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Light-Mandalas of All Tathāgatas, for the sake of causing all beings without exception to experience incomparable splendor, all happiness, and mental well-being through the pledge of the rays of light of all Tathāgatas,
and for the sake of attaining the supreme accomplishment of the self-radiance of all Tathāgatas, [bestowed] that Vajra-Sun upon that one of great majesty.
In the same manner, he bestowed [the name] upon the Mahābodhisattva with his two hands;
then, by all the Tathāgatas, he was consecrated with the vajra-name consecration as "Vajraprabha, Vajraprabha."
Then the great bodhisattva Vajraprabha, illuminating all the Tathāgatas with that Vajrasūrya, uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is that which destroys the darkness of ignorance of all Buddhas;
its radiance exceeds that of as many suns as there are atoms of dust."
I.1.12 Vajraketu:

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Jewel Empowerment Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Ratnaketu, and [uttered] this heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas called the Samaya that Fulfills the Aspirations of All Tathāgatas.
Vajraketu emerged from his own heart.
Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Lord Vajradhara, having become banners of various colors, forms, ornaments, and shapes, emerged;
he entered the heart of the Lord Vairocana and, manifesting as a single solid mass in the form of a Vajradhvaja, came to rest in the hand of the Lord.
Then, from that form of Vajradhvaja, as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems issued forth;

having performed all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas, such as raising the jewel-banner of all the Tathāgatas, they condensed into a single, solid mass— the body of the great Bodhisattva Ratnaketu— due to the greatness of the Mahāratnaketu and the firmness of the Vajrasattva samādhi.
Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am indeed the peerless banner of all accomplishments of purpose, for I am the fulfillment of all aims for those who have fulfilled all their hopes."

Then that body of the great bodhisattva Ratnaketu, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One and taken its place upon the lunar mandalas to the left of all the Tathāgatas, again requested an injunction.
Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi named Vajra of the Empowerment of the Elevation of All Tathāgatas,

for the sake of raising the banner of the wish-fulfilling king-jewel of all Tathāgatas— the pledge for the purpose of fulfilling all hopes of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, for the experience of all happiness and mental well-being, and as a cause for attaining the fruit of the supreme great accomplishment of all Tathāgatas— bestowed that vajra-banner upon that Ratnaketu.
In the same manner, he bestowed it with both hands upon the Mahābodhisattva.
Then, all the Tathāgatas consecrated him with the vajra-name-consecration, "Vajrayaṣṭi, Vajrayaṣṭi.
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrayaṣṭi, employing that Vajradhvaja to engage all the Tathāgatas in the perfection of generosity, uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is that method of the perfection of generosity, named the 'Wish-fulfilling Jewel Banner,' which fulfills all the hopes and aspirations of all the Buddhas. Thus it is said.

I.1.13 Vajrahāsa. Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Jewel Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Whose Faculties are Constantly Joyful and Delighted; from his own heart, he emitted this Heart of All Tathāgatas called the Samaya of the Joy of All Tathāgatas: *vajrahāsa*.
Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became the smiles of all the Tathāgatas and,
having issued forth, entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana; appearing there as a single solid mass in the form of the Vajra-smile, he established himself in the vital breath.

Then, from that body of Vajrasmitā, there emerged as many bodies of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems; having performed all the miraculous displays of the supernatural power of all Buddhas, such as the manifestation of all Tathāgatas, they coalesced into a single, solid mass—the body of a Great Bodhisattva with faculties eternally joyful and delighted—due to the eternal joy and delight of his faculties and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva samādhi.
Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
Oh, what a great laughter! A most wonderful thing among all that is foremost, which they always employ for the sake of the Buddhas while remaining perfectly concentrated.
Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Nityapriipramuditendriya, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One and taken his place upon a moon disc behind all the Tathāgatas,
once again sought their command.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Miraculous Empowerment of All Tathāgatas, for the sake of causing all Tathāgatas to arise in wonder, and in order that the entire realm of sentient beings without exception might experience the supreme bliss and mental well-being of all their faculties,
and as a cause for obtaining the fruit of the purification of the faculties of all Tathāgatas and the acquisition of the superknowledges of gnosis, [bestowed] that Vajra-smile upon him.
He likewise bestowed [the empowerment] with both hands upon the Great Bodhisattva Nityaprītipramuditendriya;
then he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name empowerment as "Vajraprīti, Vajraprīti."
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraprīti, gladdening all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-smile, uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is the manifestation of the marvelous arising of all Buddhas;
it is the wisdom that produces great joy, unknown to those who teach others."
The great consecration,
the circle of light one fathom wide,
and the welfare of great beings.
And Mahāharṣa—
these are the beings of the great consecration of all Tathāgatas.
I.1.14 Vajradharma.

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Dharma-Support of the Reality-Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart of All Tathāgatas called the Dharma-Samaya of All Tathāgatas: *Vajradharma*.

Then, as soon as he had emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara, because of his thorough penetration of the wisdom of the equality of phenomena that are pure by nature through the samādhi of Vajrasattva, issued forth as rays of light of the True Dharma;
by those rays of light of the True Dharma, all world-systems were illuminated.
They became enclosed, consisting of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu).

And that entire realm of phenomena, having entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, manifested as a single solid mass in the form of a great lotus, equal in extent to the convergence of the entire realm of space,
and came to rest upon the hand of the Blessed One.
Then, from that form of the vajra-lotus, there issued forth Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems.
Having performed all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas— including the samādhis, wisdoms, superknowledges (*abhijñā*), and so forth of all the Tathāgatas— in all world-systems,
they condensed into a single solid mass as the body of the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, due to the sovereignty of his own vision and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi.
Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am indeed the ultimate truth, the self-arisen one who is pure from the beginning;
for the purity of phenomena, which are like a raft, is thus perceived."
Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana and come to rest upon a moon disc in front of all the Tathāgatas,
again requested his command.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Samaya of the Wisdom and Samādhi of All Tathāgatas, for the sake of purifying all Tathāgatas through the samaya, for the purpose of experiencing the complete purification of the self of all sentient beings without exception, and all happiness and mental well-being,
up to the cause for attaining the fruit of the superknowledges and the knowledge of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas, [entrusted] that vajra-lotus to that Avalokiteśvara.
Having consecrated the Great Bodhisattva in the sovereignty of the Wheel-Turning King of the True Dharma through the empowerment of the Dharma-body of all Tathāgatas,
he bestowed [the empowerment] with his two hands.
Thereupon, Sarvatathāgataratnanetra was consecrated with the vajra-name empowerment as "Vajranetra."

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra, observing that vajra-lotus by looking at it in such a way as to perceive its nature as being unstained by the purification of passion through the blossoming of its petals, uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is the realization of the reality of passion belonging to all Buddhas;
I have been given this Dharma into my own hand, and the Dharma is established within the Dharma. Thus he spoke.
I.1.15 Vajratīkṣṇa:

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Dharma-Adhiṣṭhāna Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī; [he then uttered] this heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas called the Samaya of the Great Prajñā-Jñāna of All Tathāgatas.
From his own heart, he brought forth Vajratīkṣṇa.
Then, as soon as he had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara, having become wisdom-weapons and issued forth,
entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana; appearing there as a single mass in the form of a vajra-treasury,
he was established in the hand of the Blessed One.
Then, from that adamantine treasury-form, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems emerged;
having performed all the miraculous transformations of the supernatural powers of all Buddhas, such as the wisdom and gnosis of all Tathāgatas,
they coalesced into a single, solid body of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, due to his being supremely Mañjuśrī and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva samādhi.
Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
Oh, how I am mindful of Mañjughoṣa among all the Buddhas,
since the state of being sound is perceived within wisdom that is formless!
Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One and taken its place upon the lunar mandala to the right of all the Tathāgatas,
once again sought the command.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Wisdom-Knowledge of All Tathāgatas, for the sake of severing the afflictions of all Tathāgatas, for the sake of severing all suffering of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, for the sake of experiencing all happiness and mental well-being, and up to the sake of attaining the supreme accomplishment of the perfection of wisdom that accords with the voice of all Tathāgatas— for that Mañjuśrī—
He likewise bestowed that Vajra-treasury upon the Mahābodhisattva with both hands;
then, he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name-consecration, "Vajrabuddhi, Vajrabuddhi."
Then that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrabuddhi, striking all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-treasury, uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is the method of the perfection of wisdom of all Buddhas;
it is the supreme destroyer of all enemies and the remover of all evils."
I.1.16 Vajrahetu.

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Dharma-Adhiṣṭhāna Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Sahacittotpāditadharmacakrapravartin, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart of All Tathāgatas called the Samaya of the Wheel of All Tathāgatas: Vajrahetu.
Then, as soon as he had emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became all the maṇḍalas of the Tathāgatas, beginning with the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm;
having emerged and entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he appeared as a single solid mass in the form of a vajra-wheel and took his place in the hand of the Blessed One.

Then, from that form of the Vajra-wheel, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems issued forth; having performed all the miraculous displays of a Buddha’s supernatural powers— such as the turning of the wheel of Dharma immediately upon the arising of the thought of enlightenment— in all world-systems, [they merged] into a single solid mass, the body of the Great Bodhisattva who turns the wheel of Dharma immediately upon the arising of the thought of enlightenment, due to the firmness of the Vajrasattva samādhi and the simultaneous arising of the thought of enlightenment.

Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance: "Aho! I am the vajra-wheel of those who possess the supreme vajra-dharma, by the mere arising of whose thought the wheel of Dharma is set in motion."

Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Sahacittotpāditadharmacakrapravarti, having descended from the heart of the Bhagavān and taken his place upon the lunar mandala to the left of all the Tathāgatas,
again requested his command.
Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi named Sarvatathāgatacakravajra,

for the sake of causing all remaining beings of the realm of sentient beings without exception to enter the commitment (*samaya*) of the great maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas and to experience all happiness and mental well-being through the irreversible wheel,
up to the sign of the supreme accomplishment of setting in motion the wheel of the true Dharma of all Tathāgatas, [entrusted] that vajra-wheel to him.
He likewise bestowed it with both hands upon the Mahābodhisattva Sahacittotpāditadharmacakrapravartin;
then he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name consecration: "Vajramaṇḍa, Vajramaṇḍa!"
Then the Bodhisattva Vajramaṇḍa, together with the assembly of beings, establishing all the Tathāgatas in the state of non-retrogression by means of that vajra-wheel, uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is that which purifies all phenomena for all Buddhas;
it is known as the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), the wheel of non-retrogression. Thus it was said.

I.1.17 Vajrabhāṣa: Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Dharma-Adhiṣṭhāna Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Avāca, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart of All Tathāgatas called the Samaya of the Recitation of All Tathāgatas: *vajrabhāṣa*.
Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, having become the syllables of the Dharma of all the Tathāgatas,
emerged; having entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he appeared as a single mass in the form of the vajra-recitation and was established in the hand of the Blessed One.
Then, from that form of vajra-recitation, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems issued forth;

having performed all the miraculous displays of the supernatural powers of all Buddhas, such as the dharmatā of all Tathāgatas, they became a single solid mass—the body of the Great Bodhisattva Avāca—due to the nature of their own speech and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi.
Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this:
"Aha! I have now remembered the secret, intentional language of the Self-Existent Ones, by which they teach the True Dharma, free from the proliferation of verbal elaboration."
Then that body of the Mahābodhisattva Avāca, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One and taken its place upon a moon disc behind all the Tathāgatas,
once again sought his command.
Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Secret Vajra of Speech of All Tathāgatas,

[bestowed] that vajra-recitation upon the Great Bodhisattva Avāca for the sake of the commitment (*samaya*) of the speech-wisdom of all Tathāgatas, in order to experience the success of speech and all happiness and mental well-being for the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, and for the sake of attaining the supreme accomplishment of the secret speech of all Tathāgatas.
In that very manner, he bestowed it with both hands.
Then, by all the Tathāgatas, he was consecrated with the vajra-name consecration, "Vajravāca, Vajravāca."
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajravāca, conversing with all the Tathāgatas by means of that vajra-recitation, uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is declared to be the vajra-recitation of all Buddhas;
it is the swift accomplishment of the mantras of all Tathāgatas. Thus [he spoke].
the wisdom of the vajra-dharmatā,
the wisdom of the prajñā of all Tathāgatas,
and the wisdom of turning the great wheel;
And the wisdom that turns back the conceptual proliferation of the speech of all Tathāgatas;
these are the Great Wisdom Beings of all Tathāgatas.

I.1.18 Vajrakarma. Then the Blessed One entered the meditative absorption named the Vajra of the Empowerment of Action Arising from the Samaya of the Universal Action Mahābodhisattva of All Tathāgatas, and from his own heart he uttered this heart-essence of all Tathāgatas named the Samaya of the Action of All Tathāgatas: *vajrakarma*.

Then, as soon as he had emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, because of his thorough penetration of the knowledge of the equality of all activities through the samādhi of Vajrasattva, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became the Samaya of the Activities of All Tathāgatas and emerged;
and by those rays of light of the activities of all the Tathāgatas, all world-systems were illuminated.
They became composed of the entire realm of activity of all Tathāgatas;

that whole realm of activity of all Tathāgatas entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana and became a single mass, equal in extent to the convergence of the entire realm of space. Then, from that realm of activity of all Tathāgatas, there emerged the form of Karmavajra.
It was established in the hand of the Blessed One.
Then, from that form of the Karma-vajra, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems issued forth;
having performed all the activities of the Tathāgatas and all the miraculous displays of the supernatural powers of the Buddhas in all world-systems, [they returned].

Because the samādhi of Vajrasattva possesses the infinite activities of all Tathāgatas and is exceedingly firm, he became a single, solid mass—the body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgataviśvakarman—and having stationed himself in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Truly, I am the manifold, unfailing activity of all Buddhas."
That which proceeds as vajra-activity for the effortless benefit of the Buddhas.
Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgataviśvakarma, having emerged from the heart of the Blessed One and taken his place upon a moon disc in front of all the Tathāgatas,
once again sought the command.
Then the Blessed One, having entered the meditative absorption named *Sarvatathāgatāmoghavajra*,

for the sake of initiating the worship of all Tathāgatas and so forth, for the sake of the extensive ritual procedures of all immeasurable and unfailing actions, for the sake of the remaining and non-remaining realms of sentient beings attaining the accomplishment of all actions, and for the sake of experiencing all happiness and mental well-being—
up to the cause of the fruit of the supreme accomplishment of the knowledge and supernormal powers of the vajra-action of all Tathāgatas— he [bestowed] that Vajra of Action upon him.

Having consecrated him as the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgataviśvakarman in the sovereignty over all activities by means of the vajra-consecration of all Tathāgatas, [the Lord] bestowed it upon his two hands.
Thereupon, he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the great vajra-consecration as "Vajraviśva, Vajraviśva."
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśva, having placed that vajra at his own heart and enjoining it toward the state of the activity of all Tathāgatas, uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is the supreme [vajra] of all Buddhas, which performs manifold activities."
"I have placed the universe in my hand; the entire universe is directed by me. Thus [it is said].

I.1.19 Vajrarakṣa: Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Ritual Action Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Duryodhanavīrya, and from his own heart he emitted this heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas called the Samaya of the Protection of All Tathāgatas: VAJRARAKṢA.
Then, as soon as he had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajrapāṇi emerged, having become firm armor;
he entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana and appeared as a single solid mass in the form of a great adamantine armor, and then took his place in the hand of the Blessed One.
Then, from that body of the Vajra Armor, Tathāgata bodies as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems issued forth;
having performed all the extensive rites for the protection of all Tathāgatas and all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas' supernatural powers,
and because of his invincible vigor and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva samādhi, they merged into a single, solid mass, becoming the body of the Great Bodhisattva Duryodhanavīrya.
Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! How firm is this armor consisting of vigor, belonging to those of steadfast self;
for by its firmness, it is supreme in producing a vajra-body for those who are bodiless."
Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Duryodhanavīrya, having emerged from the heart of the Blessed One and taken its place within the lunar mandala to the right of all the Tathāgatas,
once again sought the command.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called Sarvatathāgatadṛḍhavajra, for the sake of the commitment (*samaya*) of the Vīryapāramitā of all Tathāgatas— in order to protect the realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder, to cause them to experience all happiness and mental well-being,
and as a cause for the supreme accomplishment of attaining the vajra-body of all Tathāgatas— bestowed that vajra-armour upon Duryodhanavīrya.
He bestowed [the vajra] with both hands upon the Mahābodhisattva.
Then, all the Tathāgatas consecrated him with the vajra-name-consecration: "Vajramitra, Vajramitra!"
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramitra, armor-clad with that adamantine armor (*vajravarma*), while armoring all the Tathāgatas, uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*):
"This is the supreme armor of loving-kindness (*maitrī-kavaca*) of all Buddhas;
it is proclaimed as the great friend, a mighty protection of firm vigor. Thus [he spoke].

I.1.20 Vajrayakṣa. Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra Empowerment of the Activity Arising from the Samaya of All Great Bodhisattvas who Crush All Māras, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart of All Tathāgatas called the Samaya of the Skillful Means of All Tathāgatas: Vajrayakṣa!
Then, as soon as he had emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara, having become great fang-weapons and issued forth,
entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana; appearing there as a single solid mass in the form of a vajra-fang, he established himself in [Vairocana’s] hand.
Then, from that form of Vajradaṃṣṭra, there issued forth Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems;
having performed all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas, such as the fierce subduing of all Tathāgatas,
and because of the complete crushing of all Māras and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, they merged into a single solid body, the Great Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardin.
Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
Oh, what a great skillful means of the Buddhas, whose very nature is compassion!
That for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, they who are themselves peaceful even manifest ferocity.
Then that body of the great bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardinī emerged from the heart of the Blessed One,
took its place upon the lunar mandala to the left of all the Tathāgatas,
and once again awaited further instructions.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called Sarvatathāgatapracaṇḍavajra, for the sake of subduing the wicked of all Tathāgatas, for the purpose of experiencing the entire realm of beings without exception— free from fear and endowed with all happiness and mental well-being—
and for the cause of attaining the fruit of the supreme siddhi consisting of the great skillful means, knowledge, and supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas, [manifested] that vajra-tusk weapon.
He likewise bestowed it with both hands upon that great bodhisattva, the crusher of all Māras;
then he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name-consecration: "Vajracaṇḍa, Vajracaṇḍa!"
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajracaṇḍa, having placed that weapon of vajra-fangs in his own mouth and terrifying all the Tathāgatas, uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is that which subdues all the wicked among all the Buddhas."
"The sharp weapon of the adamantine fangs is the skillful means of those whose nature is compassion. Thus it is said.

I.1.21 Vajrasandhi: Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra Empowerment of the Ritual Action Arising from the Samaya of the Fist of All Tathāgatas, the Great Bodhisattva; [he then uttered] this heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas called the Samaya of the Vajra-Bond of the Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas.
He issued forth from his own heart as Vajrasandhi.
Then, as soon as he had emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara, having become the binding of all the mudrās of all the Tathāgatas,
emerged; having entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he appeared as a single solid mass in the form of a vajra-binding and settled upon [Vairocana’s] hand.

Then, from that body of the vajra-binding, as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems issued forth; having performed all the miraculous displays of the supernatural powers of all Buddhas, such as the knowledge of the mudrās of all Tathāgatas in all world-systems, they merged into a single solid mass— the body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi— due to the firmness of the Vajrasattva samādhi and the state of being well-bound by the great fist of all Tathāgatas.
Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! How firm indeed is the bond, the pledge of those whose nature is firm—that which, for the sake of accomplishing all hopes, is a binding even for those who are already liberated."
Then the body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi emerged from the heart of the Blessed One,
took his place upon a moon disc behind all the Tathāgatas,
and once again awaited further instructions.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Pledge of All Tathāgatas, for the sake of the manifestation of the presence of all Tathāgata deities within the entire realm of sentient beings without exception through the pledge of binding the mudrās of all Tathāgatas,

and for the purpose of experiencing all accomplishments, bliss, and mental well-being— up to the cause of the fruit of the supreme accomplishment of sovereignty over the mudrās of the omniscience of all Tathāgatas— he [taught] that vajra-binding.
He bestowed [the seal] with both hands upon that Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi in the same manner.
Thereupon, he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name consecration: "Vajramuṣṭi, Vajramuṣṭi!"
Then that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramuṣṭi, binding all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-bind, uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is the very firm binding of the mudrā of all Buddhas, which is the samaya difficult to transgress for the sake of the swift accomplishment of all Buddhas. Thus it was said.
The extensive ritual procedure for the worship of all Tathāgatas,
the firm armor of great heroism,
and the great skillful means of all Tathāgatas.
And this is the knowledge of all mudrās;
these are the Great Karma-beings of all the Tathāgatas.
I.1.22 Sattvavajri. Then indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, having brought forth all the gnoses of the Tathāgata Vairocana,
entered the meditative absorption named "Vajra-Adhiṣṭhāna Arising from the Samaya of the Vajra-Pāramitā" for the purpose of sealing all the gnoses of the Tathāgatas.
Having entered this seal of all Tathāgatas named "The Vajra-Samaya of All Tathāgatas," Sattvavajrī issued it forth from her own heart.
Then, as soon as this had issued forth, vajra-rays streamed out from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.
And from those vajra-rays, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems;
having done so, he sealed the gnoses of the vajra-perfection of all the Tathāgatas.
Once again, having manifested as a single solid mass in the form of a great vajra, equal in measure to the convergence of all world-systems,
he took his place upon a moon disc in front of the Blessed One Vairocana and uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Indeed, among all Buddhas, I am the firm Vajra of sentient beings;
because of that firmness, though bodiless, I have attained the state of a vajra-body. Thus it is said.
I.1.23 Ratnavajrī. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, for the purpose of sealing the wisdom of all Tathāgatas of the Blessed One Vairocana,
entered the meditative absorption named "Vajra-empowerment arising from the commitment of the Jewel Perfection," and [manifested] this Vajra-jewel commitment.
The one named Ratnavajrī caused her own mudrā to issue forth from her own heart.
Then, as soon as this [mantra] had issued forth, jewel-rays radiated from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.
From those jewel-rays, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems,
and having sealed all the gnoses of all the Tathāgatas,
Once again, becoming a single mass as vast as the extent of all world-systems, he manifested as a great body of diamond-jewel,
and resting upon a moon disc at the right side of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Indeed, I am remembered as the Ratnavajra of all Buddhas, for I am the firm method of consecration for all mudrās. Thus it is said.
I.1.24 Dharmavajrī. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja, in order to seal the gnosis of all Tathāgatas of the Blessed One Vairocana,
entered the meditative absorption named "The Vajra Empowerment Arising from the Samaya of the Perfection of Dharma," and [manifested] this Dharmasamaya.
Then Dharma-vajrī uttered his own name-seal from his own heart.
Then, as soon as this had issued forth, lotus-rays of light streamed out from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.
From those lotus-rays, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all the world-systems;
having done so, he sealed all the gnoses of all the Tathāgatas.
Once again, becoming a single mass as vast as the convergence of all world-systems, he manifested as the great vajra-lotus body;
resting upon a moon disc behind the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am the pure Dharma-vajra of all Buddhas."
For by the very purity of its intrinsic nature, even passion is indeed utterly stainless.

I.1.25 Karmavajri: Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, for the purpose of sealing the gnosis of all Tathāgatas of the Blessed One Vairocana, the Tathāgata, entered the meditative absorption named "Vajra-Adhiṣṭhāna Arising from the Perfection of Action," and [manifested] this Samaya of the Action of All Tathāgatas.
Then Karmavajrī, uttering her own name, brought forth her own mudrā from her heart.
Then, as soon as this [light] had issued forth, rays of all activities emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.

And from those rays of the activity of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems; having thus sealed the gnoses of all the Tathāgatas, he—
Once again, becoming a single mass equal in measure to the convergence of all world-systems, a great vajra-form of karma facing in every direction, he manifested and,
taking his place upon a moon disc at the left side of the Blessed One Vairocana, uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Indeed, I am the great Vajra of Action of all the Buddhas, since, though being one, I perform virtuous deeds for the entire realm of sentient beings without exception."
The pledge of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas,
the great consecration,
the vajra-nature of phenomena.
And "all offerings" refers to the perfections of all Tathāgatas.
I.1.26 Vajralāsyā.

Then the Blessed One Vairocana again entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Samaya of the Worship of Delight of All Tathāgatas, and from his own heart he brought forth this Great Goddess of the Family of All Tathāgatas:
Vajralāsyā.
Then, as soon as she had emerged, vajra-mudrās issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.
From the faces of those vajra-mudrās, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems.

These then merged once more into a single mass, becoming the Great Goddess whose physical form resembles Vajrasattva, possessing diverse colors, forms, marks, and modes of deportment, adorned with every ornament, embodying the gathering of all the Tathāgata families, and beloved by Vajrasattva.
Having taken her place upon a moon disc to the left side of the Blessed One Akṣobhya’s maṇḍala, she uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aha! There is indeed no other worship equal to that of the Self-Existent Ones."
"By means of desire, pleasure, and worship, all worship is set in motion. Thus it is said.

I.1.27 Vajramālā. Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called Vajra Born from the Samaya of the Empowerment of the Jewel Garland of All Tathāgatas, and he brought forth me, the Great Goddess of the Family of All Tathāgatas, from his own heart:
"Vajramāle!"
Then, as soon as she had emerged, the Great Jewel Seals issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.
From those Great Jewel Seals, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems;
having thus become one solid mass, he manifested as the Great Goddess Vajramālā.
Having taken her place upon a full moon disk on the left side of the Blessed One’s Ratnasaṃbhava maṇḍala, she uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Truly, I am peerless, for I am celebrated as the 'Worship of Jewels' (Ratnapūjā). Being fully honored, I cause them to govern the supreme sovereignty over the three realms."

I.1.28 Vajragīta: Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Samaya of the Chanting of All Tathāgatas, and from his own heart he brought forth this Great Goddess of the Family of All Tathāgatas. As soon as she had emerged, the Dharma-mudrās of all Tathāgatas issued forth from the hearts of all Tathāgatas.

And from all those seals of the Dharma of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems; then, having again become the single-mass Great Goddess Vajragītā, she took her place upon a moon disk at the left side of the Blessed One’s Lokeśvararāja maṇḍala and uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aha! I am indeed a worship consisting of song for all-seeing ones, since they are pleased by such offerings even though they are like echoes."

I.1.29 Vajranṛtyā: Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Pledge of the Worship of the Dance of All Tathāgatas, and from his own heart he brought forth this Great Goddess of the Family of All Tathāgatas,
Vajranṛtyā.
Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, the extensive rituals for the dance-offering of all the Tathāgatas emerged.
And from those extensive rituals for the dance-offerings of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms within all world-systems;
these, in turn, coalesced once more into the single, solid mass of the Great Goddess Vajranṛttamahādevī.
Having taken her place upon a full moon disc on the left side of the mandala of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, she uttered this inspired utterance:
"O, how sublime is my worship! For I perform the purpose of all forms of worship, in that the worship of the Buddha is accomplished through the ritual of the Vajra Dance."
The pledge of the supreme bliss and mental joy of all Tathāgatas,
the garland of all Tathāgatas,
and the verses of all Tathāgatas.
And she is the performer of the unsurpassed worship-activity for all Tathāgatas;
these are the secret worships of all Tathāgatas.
I.1.30 Vajradhūpa. Then again, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, for the sake of returning the worship to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana,
entered the samādhi named Vajra Arising from the Samaya that Delights All Tathāgatas, and [manifested] this courtesan of all Tathāgatas.
He issued forth from his own heart as Vajradhūpā.

Then, as soon as this [mantra] had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became various kinds of arrays of clouds of incense offerings (*dhūpapūjā*) that pervaded the entire vajra-realm and streamed forth.
And from those oceans of clouds of incense offerings, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms of all world-systems emerged.

Once again, having become a single solid mass as the body of the Vajra Incense Deity, she took her place upon a moon disc in the corner on the left side of the Blessed One’s peaked pavilion of the Vajra-jewel-summit, and uttered this inspired utterance:
"O, how wonderful! This great worship is auspicious and brings supreme refreshment!"
For by means of the yoga of entering into sentient beings, awakening is swiftly attained. Thus it is said.
I.1.31 Vajrapuṣpa: Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, for the sake of performing a reciprocal worship to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana,
entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Pledge of Worship with Jewel Ornaments, [and manifested] this female attendant of all the Tathāgatas.
From his own heart, he uttered the mantra "Vajrapuṣpe."

Then, as soon as this [mantra] had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became arrays of all flower-offerings that pervaded the entire realm of space and issued forth; and from those arrays of all flower-offerings,
Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms of all world-systems issued forth.

Once again, having become a single mass as the body of the deity Vajrapuṣpa, she took her place upon a moon disc in the left corner of the Blessed One’s gabled chamber at the peak of the Vajramaṇiratna, and uttered this inspired utterance:
"O, how wonderful! I am the Flower-Worshipper, the creator of all ornaments!"
By worshipping that which is the jewel-nature of the Tathāgata, it is swiftly attained. Thus it is said.
I.1.32 Vajraloka:
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja, in order to perform a reciprocal worship for the Blessed Tathāgata Vairocana,
entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Pledge of the Worship of the Light of All Tathāgatas, [and manifested] this messenger of all Tathāgatas.
He issued forth from his own heart as Vajrāloka.

Then, as soon as she had emerged, that very Blessed One Vajradhara, having become the arrays of all-light offerings that pervade the entire *dharmadhātu*, issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.
And from those arrays of all-light offerings, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms of all world-systems issued forth.
Once again, having become a single solid mass as the body of the deity Vajrālokā,
she took her place upon a moon disc in the left corner of the Blessed One’s peaked pavilion with its crest of vajra-jewels, and uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! How truly sublime is this auspicious lamp-offering, by which one may swiftly obtain the vision of all Buddhas, possessed of light! Thus it is said.
I.1.33 Vajragandhā. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, for the sake of performing a reciprocal worship to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana,
entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Pledge of the Worship of Incense of All Tathāgatas, and [emanated] this female servant of all Tathāgatas.
She emerged from her own heart, saying: "Vajragandhe!"

Then, as soon as she had emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara manifested as arrays of offerings of all perfumes, pervading all world-systems, and issued forth.
From those arrays of perfume offerings, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms of all world-systems emerged; these then merged into a single solid mass in the form of the deity Vajragandhā.
She took her place upon a moon disc in the left corner of the Blessed One’s peaked pavilion of vajra-jewel-summits and uttered this inspired utterance:
"Oh, what a divine and delightful worship consisting of fragrance!
For the scent of the Tathāgata indeed pervades the entire body. Thus it is said.
The penetration of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, the accumulation of the factors of great enlightenment, and the illumination of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas.
And [it consists of] the perfumes of ethical discipline, meditative concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation;
it carries out the commands of all Tathāgatas.

I.1.34 Vajrāṅkuśa: Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Being Arising from the Samaya of the Great Being Kuśa, which is the Samaya of all Tathāgatas; he then brought forth from his own heart Vajrāṅkuśa, the Lord of the Multitude of All Mudrās of all Tathāgatas. Vajrāṅkuśa!
Then, as soon as he had emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara emerged, having become the entire host of seals (mudrā) of all the Tathāgatas.
And from that host of seals of all the Tathāgatas, there emerged forms of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all world-systems;
these, once again, coalesced into a single, solid mass, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrāṅkuśa.

Having taken his place upon a moon disc in the center of the vajra gate of the Blessed One’s gabled chamber with its peak of vajra-jewel gems, and drawing in the commitments (*samaya*) of all the Tathāgatas,
he uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*).
"Aho! Indeed, my power of summoning all Buddhas is firm;
for by me they are summoned and they attend to the entire maṇḍala. Thus it is said.
I.1.35 Vajrapāśa.

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra Being Born from the Samaya of the Great Being Who Enters the Samaya of All Tathāgatas, and from his own heart he brought forth the gatekeeper who causes entry by means of the mudrās of all Tathāgatas: Vajrapāśa.

Then, as soon as he had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara emerged in the form of the multitudes of mudrās for entering the samaya of all the Tathāgatas.
And from those multitudes of mudrās for entering the samaya of all the Tathāgatas, there issued forth forms of the Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all world-systems;
these then merged once more into a single, solid mass, becoming the body of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāśa.
Resting upon a moon disc in the midst of the jewel door of the Blessed One’s peaked pavilion of the Vajra-jewel-summit, causing all the Tathāgatas to enter, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am the firm Vajra-noose of all the Buddhas."
"Though it has already entered all atoms, it is entered by me once again. Thus [it is said].
I.1.36 Vajrasphoṭa:
Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi named *Vajrasattva-vajra*, which arises from the great being-samaya of the Samayasphoṭa of all Tathāgatas;
and from his own heart, he emitted this messenger of all Tathāgatas named *Sarvatathāgatasamayabandha*: Vajrasphoṭa!
Then, as soon as he had emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara manifested as the multitudes of mudrās for binding the samaya of all the Tathāgatas;
and from those multitudes of all the mudrās for binding the samaya of all the Tathāgatas, there emerged Tathāgata-forms equal in number to the atoms of all world-systems,
which then coalesced into a single, solid mass, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrasphoṭa.
Having taken his place upon a moon disc in the center of the Dharma-gate of the Blessed One’s gabled pavilion with its peak of vajra-jewels,
and binding all the Tathāgatas,
he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Indeed, I am the firm Vajra-fetter of all Buddhas, since for those who are liberated from all bonds, bondage is desired for the sake of sentient beings. Thus it is said.
I.1.37 Vajrāveśa:

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called Sarvatathāgatāveśamahāsattvasamayasambhavasattvavajra, and from his own heart he brought forth this servant of all the seals (mudrā) of all the Tathāgatas:
Vajrāveśa.
Then, as soon as he had emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara issued forth, having become the entire host of all the Tathāgatas' mudrās.

And from that entire host of all the Tathāgatas' mudrās, there issued forth Tathāgata-forms equal in number to the atoms of all world-systems; these then manifested as a single, solid mass in the form of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrāveśa.
Having taken his place upon a moon disc in the center of the ritual entrance of the Blessed One’s peaked pavilion topped with a diamond-jewel crest, and causing all the Tathāgatas to enter [him],
he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Indeed, I am the firm vajra-entrance of all Buddhas, since, having become the lords of all, they indeed become even servants. Thus it is said.
The summoning of all Tathāgatas, their entry, and their binding.
And subjugation; these are the executors of the commands of all Tathāgatas.
Then the Blessed One made the gesture of snapping his fingers to empower the assembly of all Tathāgatas.
He spoke this heart-mantra for the empowerment of the assembly of all Tathāgatas: "Vajrasamāja!"

Then, at that very moment of the *kṣapālava* muhūrta, all the Tathāgatas—equal in number to the atoms within all the world-systems—in oceans of clouds throughout the expanse of all world-systems, being exhorted by the sign of the snapping of fingers from all the Tathāgatas, assembled together with their circles of assemblies of Bodhisattvas.

They approached the Blessed One’s jeweled gabled pavilion with its peak of vajra-jewels, and where the Blessed One Vairocana was, they drew near; having arrived, they said: "Oṃ! I perform prostration at the feet of all the Tathāgatas."

Having thus performed a prostration at the feet of all the Tathāgatas by reciting this mantra—which is established by its very nature—according to their inclination, they uttered this inspired utterance:
Oh, how great is the honor shown to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra,
that the Tathāgata shines forth in the midst of the Tathāgata’s wheel!

Then, having spoken this, all those Tathāgatas who had assembled from all the world-systems of the ten directions, through the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all the Tathāgatas, entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana together with their circles of assemblies of Bodhisattvas.
And from the hearts of all those Tathāgatas, their respective circles of assemblies of Bodhisattvas emerged.
Having formed circles on all sides of the Lord’s peaked pavilion with its crest-jewel of diamond, they remained there in meditative equipoise and uttered this inspired utterance:
"Oh, how truly great is the magnanimity of all Buddhas, born of no beginning!"
For all atoms, when enumerated, have indeed attained oneness in the Buddhas.

Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, having again assembled in a gathering, for the sake of empowering this great maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm, for the protection of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, for the attainment of all benefit and happiness, and for the supreme accomplishment of the perfect awakening to the knowledge and super-knowledges of the equality of all Tathāgatas, [uttered] the hymn of the one hundred and eight names of Mahāvajradhara.
They entreated the Blessed One, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, their own Vajrasattva, the beginningless and endless Great Vajra-holder, with these one hundred and eight names.
O Vajrasattva, Great Being, Vajra of all Tathāgatas, Samantabhadra, Primordial Vajra, Vajrapāṇi—homage be to you! (1)
O Vajrarāja, supreme among the truly wise, Tathāgata Vajrāṅkuśa;
O Amogharāja, foremost of vajras, Vajrākarṣa, homage be to you! // 2 //
O Vajrarāga, great bliss; O Vajra-arrow, who brings all under control;
O Bhāra-kāma, great vajra; O Vajra-bow, homage be to you! // 3 //
O Vajrasādhu, supreme among beings, O Vajratuṣṭi of great delight, O Prāmodyarāja, foremost of Vajras, O Vajraharṣa, homage be to you! // 4 //
O Vajraratna, O you whose meaning is the supreme vajra, O Vajrākāśa, O Great Maṇi!
O Ākāśagarbha, O you enriched by the vajra, O Vajragarbha, homage be to you! // 5 //
O Vajra Splendor, Great Flame, Vajra Sun, Light of the Victors, Vajra Ray, Great Brilliance, Vajra Radiance—homage be to you! // 6 //
O Vajraketu, who acts for the benefit of beings; O Vajradhvaja, who is easily pleased;
O Ratnaketu, Great Vajra; O Vajrayaṣṭi, homage be to you! (7)
O Vajrahāsa, Great Laughter; O Vajrasmita, Greatly Wondrous One; O Supreme Vajra of Joy and Delight; O Vajraprīti, homage be to you! // 8 //
O Vajradharma, you who realize the meaning of reality; O Vajrapadma, you who purify perfectly;
O Lokeśvara, O Suvajrākṣa, O Vajranetra—homage be to you! 9.
O Vajra-sharp one, Great Vehicle, Vajra-treasury, great weapon!
O Mañjuśrī, Vajra-profundity, Vajra-buddhi—homage be to you! 10.
O Vajra-Cause, Great Mandala! O Vajra-Wheel, Great Method! O Well-Revolved One, arisen from the Vajra! O Vajra-Mandala, homage be to you! // 11 //
O Vajra-Speech, supreme among excellent vidyās; O Vajra-Japa, bestower of perfect accomplishment;
O Speechless One, supreme vajra-accomplishment; O Vajra-Voice, homage be to you! 12.
O Vajrakarma, O Suvajrājñā, O Karmavajra who pervades all, O Amoghavajra of great magnanimity, O Vajraviśva, homage be to you! // 13 //
