O Vajrarakṣa of great fortitude, O Vajravarma most firm, O Duyodhana of foremost heroism, O Vajravīrya, homage be to you! // 14 //
O Vajrayakṣa, of great skillful means; O Vajradaṃṣṭra, of great terror; O Bhārapramardin, O fierce Vajra, O wrathful Vajra—homage be to you! // 15 //
O Vajra-joint, you who are well-near, O Vajra-bind, the liberator;
O Vajra-fist, the supreme commitment—homage be to you, O Vajra-fist! 16.
Whoever should maintain these eighteen auspicious names, he is consecrated with all the supreme [consecrations], such as the vajra-name consecration and others. (17)
But whoever should constantly sing the praises of this secondary name of the Great Vajradhara, he too shall become equal to Vajradhara. (18)
Praised by us with these one hundred and eight names, expand this great system, the realization of the Mahāyāna. (19)
"O Protector, we entreat you: please speak the supreme method, the great wheel of all Buddhas, the most excellent great maṇḍala. (20) Thus.

The delineation of the maṇḍala: Then the Blessed One Vajradhara, having heard the words of the exhortation from all the Tathāgatas, entered the samādhi called "Vajra-empowerment arising from the commitment of all the Tathāgatas" and proclaimed the great maṇḍala called the Vajradhātu.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme great maṇḍala, which resembles the Vajradhātu and is known as the Vajradhātu. (1)
Having sat down in the center of this mandala, one should meditate upon and empower the Great Being’s Great Seal (mahāmudrā). // 2 //
Rising in that very manner and remaining in the mudrā, one should look out in all directions; one should circumambulate with pride, uttering the mantra of Vajrasattva. // 3 //
The wise one should delineate the mandala with a beautiful thread that is new, well-prepared, of the correct measure, and as far as possible.
It is square, with four gates, adorned with four archways, provided with four boundary lines, and decorated with silk bands and garlands of flowers. // 5 //
In all the corner sections and at the junctions of the doors and projections,
one should trace the outer maṇḍala, inlaid with vajra-jewels.
Having entered its inner city, which resembles a wheel, is encircled by a vajra-thread, and is adorned with eight pillars. // 7 //
Adorned with a moon mandala situated upon the tip of a vajra pillar, one should place the image of the Buddha in the center of the central mandala. // 8 //
On all sides of the Buddha, in the center of the mandalas,
one should indeed draw the four supreme samayas in successive order.
Having entered with vajra-velocity into the fourfold mandalas, one should establish the four Buddhas, beginning with Akṣobhya, within them. (10)
One should construct the Akṣobhya maṇḍala together with Vajradhara and the others;
the Ratnasaṃbhava maṇḍala is filled with Vajragarbha and the others.
The mandala of Amitāyus, purified by Vajranetra and the others, and the mandala of Amoghasiddhi beginning with Vajraviśva, should be drawn. Thus [ends verse 12].
One should draw the Vajra goddesses situated in the corners of the wheel;
one should draw the offerings to the Buddhas in the corners of the outer maṇḍala. (13)
In the middle of all the doors, one should place the four door-keepers;
and among those situated on the outer mandala, one should install the great beings.
Then, having properly bound the mudrā of the fire according to the ritual procedure, the Vajrācārya, having entered, should release the mudrā and enter [the mandala]. 15.
In this regard, the heart-mantra for all types of possession is as follows: AḤ.

Having sought permission exactly as prescribed, and having likewise performed the self-consecration (*svādhiṣṭhāna*) and so forth, one should utter one's own name and then accomplish it with the *vajra*. // 1 //
Then, having bound the Sattvavajrāṅkuśī mudrā, the Vajrācārya, further making the sound of snapping the fingers together, should assemble all the Buddhas. // 2 //
At that very moment, all the Buddhas, accompanied by Vajrasattva and complete with all the mandalas, proceed to the assembly within the mandala. (3)
Then, having quickly formed the Mahāmudrā of Vajradhara,
one should recite the supreme eight hundred names once at each gate.
Then, being satisfied by the assembly, the Tathāgatas proceed firmly;
Vajrasattva, having attained self-perfection, remains present as a friend. // 5 //
Then, having performed the ritual at all the gates with the hook and other implements,
one should establish the pledges by means of the supreme mudrās of great action.
The Great Being should accomplish [the goal] by means of the supreme samaya-mudrās, such as Sattvavajrī and the others, while uttering "jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ. // 7 //
Then all the great beings, beginning with the Buddhas, being drawn together as a complete assembly,
having entered well and been bound, go under their control.
Then, having been satisfied by that high-souled one with secret worship, he should be requested: "For the sake of all sentient beings, act for the attainment of all siddhis. (9) Thus it is said.
Thus, in all maṇḍalas, this is the activity of the Vajrācārya.
Now, herein follows the detailed procedure for the entry of the vajra-disciple and other rites within this Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.

In this regard, first of all, there is entry for the purpose of performing the task of achieving the supreme accomplishment of all benefit and happiness, which protects the entire realm of sentient beings without exception.
In this entry into the great maṇḍala, no examination of whether one is a worthy vessel or not should be performed.
For what reason?
"O Blessed Ones, there are certain beings who have committed great evils; yet, upon seeing and entering this Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm, they shall become free from all states of woe.

Furthermore, O Blessed Ones, there are beings who are greedy for all kinds of food, drink, and sensual pleasures, who are hostile toward the commitments (samaya), and who are incapable of the preliminary practices and so forth.
Even for them, by entering here according to their own desires, there shall be the fulfillment of all their hopes."

There are, Blessed Ones, beings who, out of a fondness for dancing, singing, laughter, performance, food, and recreation, and because they do not understand the reality (*dharmatā*) of the realization of the Mahāyāna of all Tathāgatas, enter the maṇḍalas of other deities;

yet, being terrified by the fear of the precepts, they do not enter the maṇḍalas of all the Tathāgata families—which are the perfection that fulfills all hopes and which produce unsurpassed delight, joy, and exhilaration.
For them—who dwell facing the path toward entry into the maṇḍalas of the miserable states—there is nevertheless entry into the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.

It is appropriate for the purpose of experiencing all forms of delight, joy, supreme accomplishment, bliss, and mental well-being, and for turning back from the path leading toward entry into all the lower realms of existence.

Furthermore, there are righteous beings, O Blessed Ones, who, seeking the awakening of a Buddha through the means of the supreme accomplishments of the ethical discipline, meditative concentration, and wisdom of all Tathāgatas, undergo hardships while proceeding through the stages beginning with the dhyānas and liberations.
For them, by merely entering this very Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm, even the state of all Tathāgatas is not difficult to attain; how much less so, then, any other siddhi?
In that regard, first of all, one should perform the fourfold prostration to all the Tathāgatas. As follows:
with the entire body and the vajra-añjali gesture extended, one should prostrate with this mantra:
*Oṃ, for the purpose of worshiping and attending upon all the Tathāgatas, I offer myself; O Vajrasattva of all the Tathāgatas, please empower me!*

Remaining in that same posture, having placed the vajra-añjali at the heart, one should prostrate with the forehead while reciting this mantra: *oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjābhiṣekāyātmānaṃ niryātayāmi, sarvatathāgatavajraratnābhiṣiñca māṃ*.

Then, having likewise arisen, one should bow with the head and face in the vajrāñjali gesture with this mantra: *oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjāpravartanāyātmānaṃ niryātayāmi sarvatathāgatavajradharma pravartaya mām*.

Then, remaining in that same posture, having lowered the vajra-añjali from the head and placed it at the heart, one should prostrate with the head using this mantra: *oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjākarmaṇe ātmānaṃ niryātayāmi sarvatathāgata-vajrakarma kuru mām*.
Then, wearing a red upper garment and having one's face covered with a red cloth, one should bind the *sattvavajrī* mudrā with this heart-mantra: *samayas tvam*.
Then, having tied the rosary with the two middle fingers, one should insert it with this heart-mantra: *samaya hūṃ*.
Then, having caused [the candidate] to enter, one should speak thus:
"Today you have entered the family of all the Tathāgatas;
therefore, I shall generate in you the vajra-wisdom."
By means of this knowledge, you will attain even the accomplishment of all the Tathāgatas,
let alone other accomplishments;
furthermore, you must not speak of it to anyone who has not seen the great maṇḍala.
“May your pledge not be violated.
Then the Vajrācārya himself, having bound the Sattvavajra mudrā facing upward and placing it upon the head of the Vajra-disciple, shall speak thus:
“This Samayavajra of yours shall split your head asunder [if you break your vow].”
If you should speak to anyone,
then, having consecrated the water once with that very *samayamudrā* and the *śapathahṛdaya*,
you should have that disciple drink it.
In this regard, the heart of the oath is as follows:
"Vajrasattva himself is now established within your heart;
he would depart at that very moment, having pierced through it, were you to speak of this method."
Vajrodaka ṭhaḥ.
Then he should say to the disciple:
"From this day forward, I am Vajrapāṇi to you; whatever I tell you to do, that must be performed, and you must not disregard me."
"May it not happen that, by failing to avoid poison, you should meet your end and fall into hell," he said;
then one should say what must be said: "May all the Tathāgatas empower me; may Vajrasattva enter me!"
Then, the Vajrācārya, acting with haste, should form the Sattvavajrī mudrā and utter this:
"This is that samaya, the vajra known as Vajrasattva;
may it cause you to enter today itself into unsurpassed vajra-wisdom."
"Vajrāveśa aḥ!
Then, having formed the wrathful fist, one should snap the Sattvavajrī mudrā and recite the Mahāyāna-abhisamaya with vajra-words according to one's preference.
Then he enters; as soon as he has entered, divine knowledge arises.
By that knowledge, he understands the minds of others and knows all matters—past, future, and present.
His heart becomes firm in the teaching of all the Tathāgatas;
all sufferings are utterly destroyed,
and he becomes free from all fears.
He is invulnerable among all sentient beings;
all Tathāgatas empower him, and all accomplishments manifest before him.
Furthermore, unprecedented pleasures arise for him that produce joy, delight, and affection without cause;
through those pleasures, meditative concentrations (*samādhi*) are accomplished for some, and mnemonic retentions (*dhāraṇī*) for others.
For some, all their aspirations are fulfilled; for others, even the state of a Tathāgata is accomplished.
Then, having bound that mudrā, one should release it at one's own heart with this heart-mantra:
"Abide, O Vajra; be firm for me; be eternal for me."
Preside over my heart,
and bestow upon me all accomplishments;
hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ!
Then, one should cast that garland into the great mandala with this heart-mantra: *pratīccha vajra hoḥ*.
Then, wherever it falls, that [being] of his becomes accomplished.
Thereupon, having taken that garland, one should bind it upon his head with this heart-mantra: Oṃ, may you accept this being, O Great Powerful One!
He is accepted by that bond and by that Mahāsattva, and his [mantra] is swiftly accomplished.
Then, while he remains thus possessed, one should release the binding of his face with this heart-mantra: *Oṃ Vajrasattvaḥ svayam adya cakṣūddhāṭanatatparaḥ uddhāṭayati sarvākṣo vajracakṣuḥ*.
The unsurpassed.
O Vajra, behold!
Then, one should show the great maṇḍala in its proper sequence.
Upon merely seeing the great maṇḍala, he is empowered by all the Tathāgatas,
and Vajrasattva dwells within his heart.
He beholds the miraculous manifestations of the *prātihāryas*, such as the vision of various circles of supreme rays,
because he is sustained by the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all the Tathāgatas.
At times, the Blessed One Mahāvajradhara grants a vision in his own form.
The Tathāgata said:
"From that time forward, all objectives, all activities desired by the mind, and all accomplishments shall be attained," and so forth.
"Whether it be the state of a Vajradhara or the state of a Tathāgata," [he said].
Then, having shown the great maṇḍala, one should consecrate him with scented water from a flask empowered by the vajra, reciting this heart-mantra: "Vajrābhiṣiñca."
Then, having tied a single mudrā or garland and placed his own insignia upon the hand, he should speak thus:
"Today you are consecrated by the Buddhas through the vajra-consecration.
Take this, which is the state of all Buddhas; grasp the vajra for the sake of perfect accomplishment."
Oṃ, I consecrate you as the Vajra Lord; remain firm, O Vajra, for you are the Samaya.
Then one should consecrate [the disciple] with the Vajra-name consecration by means of this heart-mantra:
Oṃ, I consecrate you, O Vajrasattva, through the Vajra-name consecration; O Vajra, [your] name!
Whichever name one may employ for someone, the word "he" (he-śabda) should be used for that person.
The detailed procedure for entering all maṇḍalas.
Then one should say:
"Which do you prefer: the knowledge of the accomplishment of the arising of wealth, or the knowledge of the perfection of the accomplishment of supernatural powers?"
"Whether it be the knowledge of accomplishing the siddhis of the vidyādharas,
or even the knowledge of accomplishing the supreme siddhi of all the Tathāgatas."
Then, whatever is pleasing to each person, that should be recited for them.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the seal for the accomplishment of the attainment of the goal;
one should meditate upon the vajra-form situated as a treasure within the heart.
Meditating thus, he beholds the treasures situated within the earth. // 1 //
Having drawn the vajra-image, one should meditate upon it in the sky;
wherever one sees it fall, there one should indicate that a treasure-trove exists. // 2 //
A wise person should visualize a vajra-image upon the tongue;
by means of this, one personally utters speech from the perspective of ultimate reality. (3)
"Meditating upon one's own entire body as consisting of the vajra-image, wherever one falls while thus possessed, there one should indicate a treasure-trove. Thus [ends verse] 4.
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
Vajra-treasure.
The treasure of delight.
The treasury of Dharma.
Treasury of karma.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrā for accomplishing the siddhi of vajra-ṛddhi:
"When the vajra-entrance has arisen, one should meditate upon water consisting of vajra-images; having quickly attained siddhi through this meditation, one may walk upon the surface of the water. (1)
In that very way, having generated the state of possession, whatever form one contemplates for oneself, that indeed becomes the form of a Buddha for oneself. // 2 //
In that very same way, by personally contemplating oneself as possessed [by that state], thinking "I am space," one shall attain invisibility for as long as one desires.
Having himself become possessed by the vajra and contemplating, "I am the vajra," as long as he ascends to that place, for that long he shall travel through the sky. Thus [it is said]. // 4 //
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
Vajrajala.
Vajra-form.
Vajra-space.
I am the Great Vajra.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrā for accomplishing the siddhi of the Vajra-Vidyādhara:
having drawn the orb of the moon, one should ascend upon its surface;
manifesting a vajra in one's hand, one becomes a Vajra-Vidyādhara. // 1 //
Having ascended the lunar disc, one should visualize the vajra-jewel;
as long as the pure-souled one desires, so long does he fly up in an instant. // 2 //
Mounted upon the lunar disk and visualizing a vajra-lotus held in his hand, he who possesses the vajra-eye shall bestow the station of the Vidyādharas. // 3 //
Standing in the center of the lunar disc, one should meditate upon the Action-Vajra;
by swiftly holding the Vajra of Universal Power, one shall become a master of all vidyās. Thus [it is said]. (4)
Now, O Vajradhara, follow these heart-mantras.
O Holder of Jewels!
Holder of the lotus.
Karmadhara (the holder of the task)
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrās for accomplishing the supreme siddhi of all Tathāgatas:
"Having entered into the samādhis of all vajras within the realms of space, the Vajra-being flies up in an instant for as long as he desires. (1)
By meditating upon all pure samādhis as well as the supreme ones, one who accomplishes gnosis swiftly attains the five superknowledges. // 2 //
Pervading all space as consisting of Vajrasattva, one who possesses firm recollection will swiftly become Vajradhara himself. // 3 //

Having resolved with conviction that everything within the realms of space consists of the image of the Buddha, one will become a Buddha through all the meditative absorptions of the Buddhas. Thus, [verse 4].
Now, the heart-mantras for this are:
*vajra vajra*.
Pure, pure!
Beings, beings!
Buddha Buddha.
The accomplishment of all siddhis and gnoses.
Then he becomes capable of upholding the secret teachings.
First of all, let there be this heart-mantra of the oath:

*Oṃ vajrasattvaḥ svayaṃ te 'dya hṛdayaṃ samavasthitaḥ / nirbhidya tatkṣaṇaṃ yāyādyadi bhūyādidannayam //* (Oṃ, Vajrasattva himself is now established within your heart; he would depart at that very moment, piercing through it, were you to act otherwise.)
Then he should speak thus: "You must not transgress this Heart of Oaths;
lest you suffer an untimely death by failing to avoid poison, and fall into hell with this very body."
Then one should teach the knowledge of the secret mudrā:
having generated the vajra-entrance, one who is concentrated should perform the clapping;
by means of the subtle claps of the vajra-añjali, even a mountain may be brought under control. // 1 //
The vajra-clapping mudrā.
Having applied the ritual procedure for the vajra-entrance, one should strike with the palms in the vajra-binding gesture;
by means of the practice of subtle *tāla* rhythms, one may enter even a mountain. // 2 //
In the same way, by means of the rite of possession, when the vajra-bond is extended and the fingertips are clapped together, one may destroy a hundred lineages in an instant. // 3 //
Through the application of the method for the subtle penetration, [the breath] is concentrated on all the fingers;
released from the vajra-bind, it is the supreme remover of all suffering. Thus, [verse] 4.
Now follows their secret practice:
one should enter the body of a woman or a man through the *bhaga*.
Having entered, one should mentally cause all its activity to radiate forth equally. Thus it is said.
In this regard, these are the *tālahṛdaya* mantras:
*vajra vaśa*.
O Vajra, enter!
Vajra, destroy!
Vajra-hara!
Then, having given the heart-mantra, one should instruct [the disciple] in the knowledge of the four mudrās of their own family deity.
By this procedure, it should be said:
"You must not show even a single one of these mudrās to anyone else who is unskilled in them."
For what reason?
Because those beings, having not seen the great maṇḍala, employ the binding of mudrās; then, they will not attain success in that way.
Consequently, overcome by doubt and failing to avoid calamity, they will quickly die and fall into the great Avīci hell.
"And you would go to an evil rebirth."
Now follows the knowledge of the great mudrā for accomplishing the being of all Tathāgatas:
Beginning with the knowledge of the mind, one should meditate upon the Vajra-Sun, manifesting oneself as the Buddha-form, the Vajradhātu. (1)
Others, however, attain merely the accomplishments (siddhi), as well as knowledge, longevity, strength, and splendor;
they achieve the power to go everywhere, and even Buddhahood is not difficult for them to obtain. // 2 // Thus it is said.
The seal of the perfect awakening of all Tathāgatas.
Now follows the binding of the mahāmudrā for the sādhana of Vajrasattva:
Raising the vajra with pride and maintaining the pride of the vajra, one becomes Vajrasattva himself through the vajras of body, speech, and mind. (1)
Any other person who goes everywhere, becomes the lord of all desires, and is happy;
through [this practice], they shall become foremost in miraculous power, longevity, strength, and form, equal to Vajrasattva. Thus [it is said]. // 2 //
By means of the vajras of body, speech, and mind, one should accomplish the Great Beings together with their symbolic seals (cinhamudrā), according to the manner of the drawing. // 3 //
Now, I shall explain in due order the accomplishment and the very success of all ritual manuals (kalpa) herein, as well as the great rites of those who have attained success.
Every day, first performing the self-consecration and so forth at the appropriate time, one should accomplish everything; thereafter, one may proceed as one pleases. Thus [it is said].
In this regard, the detailed procedure for the accomplishment of Mahāmudrā is as follows:
Having generated the vajra-possesion and having bound the Mahāmudrā according to the ritual rule, one should thereafter manifest that Great Being. // 1 //
Having seen that Jñānasattva, one should manifest him within one's own body;
having drawn him in, caused him to enter, bound him, and brought him under control, one should accomplish the practice.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows: Vajrasattva, Aḥ.
The Heart-mantra of Vajrāveśa.
Vajrasattva is the visible [reality].
The Heart of the Recollection of the Mahāsattva.
jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ //
The heart-mantra for attracting, entering, binding, and subjugating great beings.
When it is proclaimed, “You are the pledge,” the moon should enter from behind;
there, while saying, “I am the pledge,” one should contemplate oneself as the being (sattva). // 1 //
Whatever mudrā belongs to whichever sentient being, one should visualize that as oneself;
one shall accomplish the realization of all mudrās through vajra-recitation. // 2 //
Uttering "JAḤ HŪṂ VAṂ HOḤ," one should cause all the Buddhas to enter the body;
this is another great accomplishment through the mental yoga of the adept. Thus [ends verse 3].
Now I shall explain their ritual activity, the unsurpassed vajra-activity;
one who has attained perfection through the recollection of the Buddha will swiftly attain Buddhahood. // 4 //
One who has attained perfection through the Sattvavajrī becomes the sovereign of all mudrās;
through the Sattvavajrā mudrā, one becomes the sovereign of all jewels. 5.
One who is perfected in Dharmavajrī shall indeed become a bearer of the Buddha-dharma; through the mudrā of Karmavajrī, one shall become a performer of vajra-activities. // 6 //
Vajrasattva is accomplished by binding with the Sattva-mudrā;
one should attract Vajradhara through the application of the Vajra-attraction rite. // 7 //
The great mudrā of Vajrarāga shall cause all Buddhas to experience passion;
through the application of the Vajra-sādhana, one shall satisfy all Buddhas. // 8 //
One should bestow the empowerments of the Buddhas and likewise the ritual of the jewel-seal;
through the application of the Vajra-Tejas, one will quickly become Vajra-Tejas. // 9 //
By serving the Holder of the Vajra Banner, one shall become a fulfiller of all hopes;
by applying the ritual of the Vajra Laughter, one shall laugh together with all the Buddhas. (10)
May he become a bearer of the Vajra-Dharma through the application of the Vajra-Dharma;
may he be the foremost in wisdom among all Buddhas through the application of the Vajra-Sharp. (11)
Having served the Holder of the Vajra-Wheel, he shall turn the Wheel of Dharma;
through the application of the Vajra-Speech, he attains the accomplishment of the Buddha’s speech. // 12 //
Through the swift accomplishment of the supreme Vajrakarma, one who has entered the state of Vajrakarma shall, having bound on the Vajra-armour, attain the nature of a Vajra-body. // 13 //
By accomplishing Vajrayakṣa, one indeed becomes equal to Vajrayakṣa;
and by binding the vajra-fist, one achieves success with all mudrās. (14)
By accomplishing Vajralāsyā, one indeed attains great vajra-joy;
Vajramālā, when bound, bestows the empowerment of all Buddhas. (15)
One should apply the Vajra Song through the practice of the Vajra Song;
by performing the Vajra Dance, one is honored by all the Buddhas. (16)
By the application of vajra-incense, one shall gladden the entire world;
and by employing vajra-flowers, one shall bring the world under one's control. 17.
By worshipping the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) of the Vajra-Illumination, one shall be granted vision;
through the application of vajra-fragrance, one shall become the remover of all suffering. (18)
Through the drawing-in with the vajra-hook, one becomes the supreme performer of all summonings;
through the application of the vajra-noose, may one become the bringer of all [beings] into subjection. // 19 //
By joining the vajra-sphoṭa, there shall be the destruction of all bonds; by applying the procedure for vajrāveśa, one accomplishes all types of possession. Thus [it is said]. (20)
Now follows the knowledge of the vajra-samaya-mudrā of all Tathāgatas:
Having firmly formed the añjali with all the fingers bound together, it is called the Vajrāñjali; it is the Vajrabandha because of its excellent binding. // 1 //
All the samaya-mudrās arise from the vajra-bind;
I shall now explain their binding, the unsurpassed vajra-bind. // 2 //
Having made the *sattvavajrā* firm, with the middle finger raised like a sprout, the second [mudrā] is praised by the Buddhas through the contraction of the space between the middle fingers. (3)
The middle finger and thumb joined like a jewel, with the middle fingers contracted like a lotus—this fifth is the Buddha-mudrā, likewise with the tips well-curved. // 4 //
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the binding of the mudrās that take up the samaya, as well as their accomplishment and activity, belonging indeed to the Tathāgata family. // 5 //
In the moon formed by both hands with the middle fingers excluded,
the vajra is indeed joined by the tips of the outer fingers with the Sattvavajrā.
Through the contact of the tips of the supreme hooks, she bestows the cry of "Well done!";
for this is the host of the mudrās of accomplishment belonging to the four Vajrasattvas. 7.
Ratnavajrā is formed by joining the tips of the thumbs and index fingers; that same [mudrā] has the middle, ring, and little fingers well extended. (8)
The *patākā* mudrā is formed by joining the thumbs and little fingers together;
when that same [mudrā] is rotated, it is situated in the position of laughter.
With the thumbs extended and touching, the index fingers are bent; that same [mudrā], when the middle fingers are joined at their tips like a bud, is the *vajramuṣṭi* (vajra-fist).
That same [mudrā], when placed at the level of the forehead and designated as the "wheel," with the thumbs bound and the palms extended upward, is called Akaniṣṭhā. // 11 //

From the joining of the tips of the little finger and the thumb, it is devoid of ritual action; that same [mudrā], however, when joined with the tips of the index fingers and extended well, is situated at the heart.
With the tips of the index fingers curved and the little fingers released from their joints,
one should press the thumbs against the inner side of the little fingers using the curved tips.
At the heart, however, with the thumbs level and the fingers well extended like a garland, the tips of the fingers are turned upward; when joined above the head, it is the mudrā of the dancing one.

The Vajrabandha mudrā is formed by giving [the hands] downwards; the Svāñjali is given upwards; the Samā is the pressing together of the thumbs; and the Suprasārita is the spreading out [of the fingers] like an ointment. // 15 //
With one index finger contracted, the two thumbs bound together in a knot, the tips of the thumbs joined in a forehead-binding [mudrā], and the tips of the vajra-fists joined—thus it is said. (16)
Now I shall explain their means of accomplishment, the supreme Vajra-accomplishment, by means of one's own mudrā abiding in the heart through the *sattvavajra-samādhi*. (17)
Now I shall explain their ritual activity, the unsurpassed Vajra-activity;
through the mudrās of the Vajradhātu and others, the Tathāgatas are united by means of the assembly. (18)
At that very moment, they shall empower the mandala master and his disciples;
when the Sattvavajrī mudrā is bound, one becomes equal to Vajradhara. // 19 //
As soon as Vajrāṅkuśī is bound, one should summon all the Buddhas;
through the application of Rāgavajra, one may cause even the Buddhas to feel passion.

By means of the Vajrasādhu-bond, one attains the satisfaction of the Buddhas’ generosity; through Vajra-satisfaction, one is praised by all the Victors with shouts of "Excellent! (sādhukāra). // 21 //
When the Ratnavajrī is bound, one is consecrated by the Buddhas;
indeed, by binding the Vajrasūryā, one becomes like the radiance of a Buddha. (22)
Becoming a bearer of the Vajra-banner, he shall fulfill all hopes;
through the application of the Vajra-laugh, he shall laugh together with all the Buddhas. // 23 //
Having attained the Dharmavajrā [mudrā], one becomes like Vajradharma;
and by grasping the Vajrakośā, one cuts through all afflictions. // 24 //
Having made the vajra-wheel firm, one becomes the sovereign of the maṇḍala;
through the application of vajra-speech, the supreme accomplishment of vajra-voice is attained. // 25 //
By focusing upon Karmavajrā, one becomes equal to Vajrakarma;
by making Vajravarmā firm, the body becomes composed of vajra. // 26 //
With the Vajradaṃṣṭrāgra mudrā, he shatters the wicked Māras;
having firmly bound the Vajramuṣṭi, he shall bring all mudrās under his control.
Through *lāsya* one obtains divine delights; through *mālā*, ornaments;
through *gīta*, constant eloquent speech; and through *nṛtya*, one receives worship. (28)
One should gladden the world with incense, beautify it with the splendor of flowers, purify the world with light, and [attain] divine fragrance through perfume. // 29 //
The Vajrāṅkuśa shall draw [them] forth; the Vajrapāśa shall cause them to enter;
the Vajrasphoṭā shall bind them; and the Vajraghaṇṭā shall cause them to enter completely. Thus it is said. (30)
Now follow the Dharma-mudrās:
Vajra-wisdom is that which makes the Vajradhātu of the Buddhas firm.
Hereafter, I shall explain the Dharma-mudrās according to the ritual procedure. (1)
When "You are the pledge" (*samayas tvam*) is uttered, one becomes the lord of all mudrās; when "Of another" (*anyasya*) is indeed uttered, one will certainly summon the Buddhas. // 2 //
When he utters "Aho! What bliss!", he would cause even the Buddhas to feel passion;
by exclaiming "Excellent! Excellent! and offering words of praise, he would satisfy them.
When "sumahattvam" is uttered, there is the consecration by all the Buddhas;
when "rūpodyote" is indeed uttered, there will be the splendor of the Dharma. // 4 //
When "Arthaprāpti" is uttered, it fulfills all hopes;
when "Ha Ha Hūṃ He" is uttered, one attains the laughter of the Buddhas. // 5 //
When "sarvakāri" is uttered, one purifies even that which should not be done;
when "duḥkhaccheda" is uttered, he cuts through all sufferings.
When "Buddha Bodhi" is uttered, one becomes the sovereign of the mandala;
when "Pratiśabda" is uttered, one converses with the Buddhas simultaneously. (7)
When "Śubhasiddham" is uttered, mastery over all things shall arise;
when "Nirbhayastvam" is uttered, one shall become fearless at that very moment.
When "Śatrubhakṣa" (Devourer of Enemies) is uttered, he shall devour all enemies;
when "Sarvasiddhiḥ" (All Accomplishment) is uttered, all accomplishments will come to pass. // 9 //
May "Great Delight" grant divine pleasure, and likewise "Beauty of Form" grant that very same;
may "Bliss of the Ear" bestow happiness, and "All Offerings" grant perfect worship. 10.
“O Gladdening One,” [grant] happiness of mind; “O Bearer of Fruit,” [grant] the attainment of fruit;
“O Radiant One,” [grant] great splendor; “O Fragrant-Limbed One,” [grant] fragrance. 11.
“*Ayāhi jaḥ*”: the summoning; “*Ahi hūṃ hūṃ*”: the entry; “*Hesphoṭa vaṃ*”: the great binding; “*Ghaṇṭā aḥ aḥ*”: the shaking. // 12 //
Now, their auspicious Dharma-seal practice (*dharmamudrā-sādhana*) will be explained: one should visualize Vajrā upon the tongue; she performs all ritual actions. (13)
Now follows the binding of the action-seal (karmamudrā).
Having firmly formed the vajra-fist, one who is composed should divide it into two;
thus there shall be two vajra-mudrās, and thereafter the binding will be explained. // 1 //
The left vajra-finger should be grasped by the right hand raised up;
this mudrā is named Bodhyagrī, the bestower of the enlightenment of the Buddhas. // 2 //
Akṣobhya’s [mudrā] is the earth-touching; likewise, that of Ratna is the boon-granting;
Amitāyus’s is the supreme meditative concentration; and that of Amogha is the fear-dispelling. // 3 //
Hereafter, I shall explain in brief the action seals (karmamudrā), which set in motion the vajra activities of the beings such as Vajrasattva and the others. // 4 //
With pride, she performs the gesture of uplifting with two hands;
she stands in the posture of grasping a goad, and through the application of the arrow and bell, she is established in the heart as the one who utters "Well done! (Sādhukārā).
In the consecration, however, there is the display of the double-vajra at the heart, the left arm-staff, and likewise its placement in the mouth. (6)
Blossoming to the right and left, [the rays] from the heart and the left [hand] brandish a sword and a mallet;
whirled like a circle of fire, they emerge from the two mouths of the vajra. // 7 //
Released from the whirling of the vajra-dance, [the hands] are placed upon the cheeks and the uṣṇīṣa;
the armor [mudrā] consists of the tips of the little fingers and the fangs, pressed together by the two fists. // 8 //

Through the application of vajra-pride, with gestures that bend the body and cause it to tremble, [the offering] is bound like a garland, emitted from the mouth, and performed through the dance of the vajra. // 9 //
One should offer incense and the other offerings using the vajra-fist gesture;
these are prescribed as the offering mudrās for the worship of all Buddhas. // 10 //
By forming the hook-bond with the index fingers, the little fingers become the Great Hook;
they are pressed against the backs [of the hands] by the two ends of the arm-knots. Thus [ends verse 11].
Now I shall explain their means of accomplishment, equal to that performed by the Vajrakarmakṛt:
one should visualize a vajra consisting entirely of vajras within the heart. Thus [ends verse 12].
Now, regarding these action seals (karmamudrā), the various vajra-activities are manifold; however, when the wisdom-fist (jñānamuṣṭi) is bound, the wisdom of the Buddha enters [the practitioner]. 13.
When there is the binding of Akṣobhya, the mind becomes Akṣobhya;
with the mudrā of Ratnasaṃbhava, one becomes possessed of supreme grace for others. // 14 //

In the seal of the wheel of the true Dharma, one should turn the wheel of Dharma; with the foremost gesture of fearlessness, one will swiftly become the bestower of health upon all sentient beings. (15)
Having strengthened one's pride, one attains the bliss of Vajrasattva;
with Vajrāṅkuśī, one should summon all the Tathāgatas in an instant. 16.
One should cause even one's own Vajra-consort to experience passion with the Vajra-arrows;
indeed, through the Vajra-delight, all the Victors bestow words of approval. 17.
Having bound the great vajra-jewel, he is consecrated by the Teachers;
having attained the vajra-sun samādhi, he becomes equal to Vajrasūrya. 18.
Having raised the Vajradhvaja, he should cause a rain of jewels to fall;
having attained the Vajrasmitā [samādhi], he should laugh quickly together with the Buddhas. (19)
Having assumed the Vajrapuṣpā mudrā, he beholds Vajradharma;
having firmly bound the Vajrakośā mudrā, he cuts through all sufferings. // 20 //
Having stabilized the vajra-wheel, one should turn the wheel of Dharma;
indeed, all the words of the Buddha are accomplished through vajra-recitation. // 21 //
Through the worship of the vajra dance, even a Buddha may be brought under one's control;
by binding the vajra armor, one shall attain the state of vajra-essence. // 22 //
Having firmly grasped the Vajra-fang [mudrā], one may destroy even the state of a Vajra;
with the Vajra-fist, one may seize everything—the perfection of the mudrā is thereby attained. // 23 //
Vajralāsyā bestows delight; Vajramālā, beautiful form;
Vajragītā, excellent song; and Vajranṛtyā, she shall bring [all] under control. (24)
Through incense, one attains delight of mind; through flowers, ornaments;
through the lamp-offering, great radiance; and through vajra-fragrance, a sweet scent. (25)
One should attract with Vajrāṅkuśī, cause entry with Vajrāśā, bind with Vajranigaḍā, and cause to move with Vajraghaṇṭā. Thus [it is said]. // 26 //
Now follows the detailed procedure for binding the common seal of all mudrās.
Therein, at the very beginning, having formed the *vajrabandha* with the fingers and placed it at the heart, one should recite this heart-mantra: *vajrabandha traṭ*.
Then all the binding of mudrās come under one's control within the vajras of one's own body, speech, and mind.
Then, having bound the Vajrāveśa-samayamudrā, one should utter this heart-mantra: AḤ.
Then, having entered [the body], they remain present as friends.
Then, having recollected the great beings of the mudrā-samaya, one should utter this heart-mantra: "I am the Great Being of the Samaya."
By this, all mudrās are accomplished.
This concludes the detailed procedure for all mudrās.
Now follows the general detailed procedure for the means of accomplishment (*sādhana*).
Therein, at the very outset, having bound one's own mudrā, one should meditate upon oneself as the being of one's own mudrā by means of this heart-mantra: *samayo ’ham*.
Then, having visualized oneself as the being of one's own mudrā and having empowered oneself with this mantra— "May the Samayasattva empower me"—
one should then accomplish [the goal].
This is the detailed procedure for the method of accomplishment.
Now follows the detailed procedure for the accomplishment of success (*siddhi*).
In that regard, at the very outset, one who desires the accomplishment of a specific aim should achieve that aim by means of this heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*).
By this, the accomplished mudrā brings about the arising of the great purpose.
Now, if one desires the accomplishment of the vajra, there is the vajra-accomplishment through this heart-mantra.
By this, one becomes a Vajra-siddha according to one's own preference.
Now, O Vajra-vidyādhara, if one should desire the accomplishment of a vidyādhara, [one should do so] with this heart-mantra.
By this, one attains the accomplishment of a Vidyādhara according to one's preference.
Now, if one should desire the supreme accomplishment, it is by means of the heart-mantra of one's own mudrā.
This is the detailed procedure for the rites of accomplishment.
Now follows the detailed procedure for the general consecration into the vajra of one's own body, speech, and mind for all mudrās.
When the empowerment of the mudrā becomes lax, or when one desires to release it oneself, [this rite is performed].
Then, one should strengthen this with the following heart-mantra:
Oṃ, protect the samaya of Vajrasattva;
abide as Vajrasattva.
Be firm for me,
be well-pleasing to me, be devoted to me,
be easy to nourish for me.
Grant me all accomplishments, and bring about the excellence of my mind in all activities! HŪṂ HA HA HA HA HOḤ! O Blessed One, Vajra of all Tathāgatas, do not abandon me!
O Great Samayasattva, become the Vajra-holder! ĀḤ!
“By this, even those who have committed the immediate transgressions (*ānantarya*), those who reject the true Dharma, and those who have performed every kind of evil deed—

even if they are practitioners of the seals (*mudrā*) of all Tathāgatas— by means of the firm realization of Vajrasattva, shall in this very life attain whatever siddhi they desire: whether it be the common siddhi, the supreme siddhi, the Vajra-siddhi, the Vajrasattva-siddhi, or even the Tathāgata-siddhi.”
"Or they shall attain [it]," said the Blessed One, Sarvatathāgatavajrasattva.
Now follows the detailed general procedure for the release of one's own mudrās.
Therein, from the very beginning, one should release each mudrā at the very place from which it arose by means of this heart-mantra: *vajra muḥ*.

Then, having been consecrated by the Jewel-Vajra mudrā arising from the heart, which remains at the place of one's own consecration, one should wrap and tie the garland with the two index fingers; likewise, one should bind the armor with this heart-mantra: *oṃ ratnavajrābhiṣiñca sarvamudrā me dṛḍhīkuru varakavacena vaṃ*.
Then again, having performed the binding of the garland up to the armor, one should satisfy [the deity] with the equal-syllable heart-mantra: *vajra tuṣya hoḥ*.
By this method, the mudrās—whether released or bound—will be satisfied;
they will attain the state of a Vajra, or else that of Vajrasattva.
Vajrasattva, when recited even once according to one's desire with a joyful mind,
is accomplished by mere recitation, just as Vajrapāṇi has said.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Samantabhadra.
In all ritual activities for the accomplishment of Vajrasattva and other beings, recitation (jāpa), even when performed according to one's preference,
bestows success in all tantras.

"In this [tantra], the sādhana for the heart-mudrās, mantras, and vidyās is performed in every respect according to whichever methods one prefers—whether those declared in the Kalpas or those composed by oneself. Thus it is said.
Then, proclaiming the secret mudrā of worship,
one should perform the fourfold secret worship while singing this vajra hymn of praise.
Oṃ! Through the gathering of Vajrasattva, through the unsurpassed Vajraratna, and through the songs of Vajradharma, become a performer of Vajra-activity.
Then, in the inner maṇḍala as well, one should perform worship with incense and other offerings, while holding them with the vajra-dance hand-gesture accompanied by this very song of vajra-praise.
Then, having performed worship with vajra-incense and so forth in the outer maṇḍala, one should place those offerings in their respective positions.

Then, having requested all the Tathāgatas, saying, "May everyone worship according to their ability," and having caused worship with incense and other offerings as desired, one should satisfy those who have entered the great maṇḍala with all flavors, food, amusements, and so forth, as well as all requisites offered according to one's wealth; this is the vajra-vow of the accomplishment of all Tathāgatas.
One should give [it], saying:
"This is that state of omniscience, which resides in the hand of Vajrasattva;
you too must always uphold it, O Vajrapāṇi of firm vows."
Oṃ, the accomplishment of all Tathāgatas, vajra-samaya, abide!
I maintain you; O Vajrasattva, hi hi hi hi hūṃ!
Then, the core of the oath—"This must not be told to anyone else"—should be declared.
Thereafter, having dismissed those who have entered as they came, one should inform all the Tathāgatas; having formed the *sattvavajrī* mudrā, one should release it upward.
And one should recite this heart-mantra:
*Oṃ, you have accomplished the welfare of all sentient beings; the success has been granted according to [your] capacity.
Go now to the realm of the Buddhas, so that you may return again.*
Vajrasattva muḥ.
In this manner, it should be performed in all maṇḍalas;
it is said that [this applies] to the supreme samaya mudrās as well.
The detailed procedure for the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm from the *Sarvatathāgata-mahāyānābhisamaya-mahākalparāja* is completed.
Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Samaya of All Tathāgatas’ All-Vajra Dhāraṇīs. Immediately upon entering it, from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas,
that very Blessed One Vajrapāṇi emerged, having become the deity of the Vajra-Dhāraṇī-Samaya-Mudrā, assuming the forms of the Vajra-holders and possessing a core of universal blazing light.
Having perfected the gnoses of the *vajradhāraṇīs* of all the Tathāgatas of all world-systems,
and having become the reflected images of the *samayamudrās* of all the Tathāgatas,
he, by means of the yoga of entering the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu of all the Tathāgatas, took recourse upon moon-maṇḍalas and uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*).
Oh, how the aspiration for awakening desires the welfare of all sentient beings,
such that the steadfast ones even assume the form of women for the sake of discipline!
The Emanation of Deities from Samādhi:
Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Vajra Realm, the Samaya of the Wisdom-Seals of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme self-mantra: OṂ VAJRADHĀTVĪŚVARĪ HŪṂ.
Then the Tathāgata Akṣobhya entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Wisdom-Seals of the Samaya of Vajrasattva of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme self-mantra: OṂ...
Vajra-vajriṇi hūṃ.

Then the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Wisdom-Mudrās of the Vajra-Jewel Samaya of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme personal vidyā: Oṃ ratnavajriṇi hūṃ.

Then the Tathāgata Amitāyus entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Wisdom-Seals of the Samaya of the Vajra-Dharma of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme personal vidyā: Oṃ dharmavajriṇi hūṃ.

Then the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Samaya-Jñāna-Mudrā of the Vajra-Ear of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme personal vidyā: OṂ KARMAVAJRIṆI HŪṂ.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke the fourfold samaya-mudrās of the great dhāraṇīs of all the Tathāgatas.
Oṃ, in the secret samaya of Vajrasattva, hūṃ!
Oṃ, Guhyavajrāṅkuśī, hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Vajra Secret Passion, arouse passion! Hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Mistress, the virtuous one of the secret vajra, hūṃ!
Samantabhadrā,
Tathāgatāṅkuśī, and Ratirāgā.
And Sādhumatī. These are the Vajra-dhāraṇīs: Oṃ vajraguhyaratnasamaye hūṃ.
Oṃ, Vajraguhyaprabhe, hūṃ!
Oṃ, at the secret tip of the Vajra Banner, hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Vajrī of Secret Laughter, hūṃ!
Ratnottamā, Ratnolkā, Dhvajāgrakeyūrā,
And Hāsavatī;
these are the Ratnadhāraṇīs.
Oṃ, at the secret samaya of Vajradharma, hūṃ!
Oṃ vajrakośaguhye hūṃ.
Oṃ vajraguhyamaṇḍale hūṃ.
Oṃ, at the time of the secret vajra recitation, hūṃ.
Vajrāmbujā, Ādhāraṇī,
Sarvacakra.
And there are the thousand-fold revolutions and the dhāraṇīs for upholding the Dharma.
Oṃ vajra-guhya-karma-samaye hūṃ.
Oṃ, vajra-secret armor, hūṃ!
Oṃ, you who bear the secret vajra-fangs, hūṃ!
Oṃ vajraguhyamuṣṭi hūṃ.
Siddhottarā,
Sarvarakṣā,
and Tejaḥpratyāhāriṇī.
And the Dharaṇī-mudrā;
these are called "all dhāraṇīs."
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again spoke the fourfold secret samaya-mudrās of all the Tathāgatas:
Oṃ guhyasatvavajri hūṃ.
Oṃ guhyaratnavajri hūṃ.
Oṃ Guhyadharmavajri Hūṃ.
Oṃ, O Vajra of Secret Activity, hūṃ!
These very [deities], beginning with Vajrapāramitā, are the samaya-mudrās of the compendium of the dhāraṇīs of the secret vajra-samaya of all Tathāgatas;
they should be placed within the great maṇḍala of Vajradhātveśvarī, blazing and resting upon moon discs.
Then Vajrapāṇi again proclaimed the fourfold mudrās of the secret worship-samaya of all the Tathāgatas:
OṂ VAJRA-GUHYA-RATI-PUJĀ-SAMAYE SARVA-PUJĀM PRAVARTAYA HŪṂ.
Oṃ, at the time of the secret vajra empowerment and worship, set forth all offerings! Hūṃ!
Oṃ, at the time of the secret vajra song offering, set forth all offerings, hūṃ!
Oṃ, at the time of the secret vajra dance offering, set in motion all offerings! Hūṃ.
Those very same [deities], Vajralāsyā and the others, blazing and bearing their own emblems as mudrās, should be placed in the four corners of the wheel-maṇḍala.
The delineation of the maṇḍala:
Then Vajrapāṇi again spoke this great vajra-maṇḍala named the Vajra Secret.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme vajra-maṇḍala.
Resembling the Vajra-dhātu, it is known as the Vajra-guhya. // 1 //
By means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala, one should draw all the maṇḍalas;
in the centers of all the maṇḍalas, one should draw the mudrās of the Buddhas. // 2 //
The Caitya well-established in the paryanka posture is known as Vajradhātvīśvarī;
in the paryanka posture, Vajrā is proclaimed as Vajracintā. (3)
The Vajra-jewel in the cross-legged posture is proclaimed as "Self-Consecration";
the Vajra-lotus in the cross-legged posture is proclaimed as the "Weapon. // 4 //
The Karma-vajra is in the paryaṅka posture; she is celebrated as Sarva-vajrā.
They should be painted seated upon lotuses, established within circles of light. (5)
In the center of the seat, one should draw a raised vajra, as well as two hooks;
likewise, a vajra joined with another vajra, and two "well done" (sādhukāra) gestures. // 6 //
One should fashion a jewel blazing with light, as well as the sun-seal;
likewise, the tip of a banner with flames, and two vajras within the row of teeth.
In the center of the vajra, one should draw a lotus and a sword with flames;
likewise, the spokes of the vajra, the vajra-wheel, and a tongue blazing with rays of light. (8)
The vajra, however, has faces on all sides; the armor is joined with vajras;
likewise, the two vajra-fangs are to be drawn, and the fist-mudrā is formed with both hands. (9)
Satvavajrā and the others should be drawn according to the rules in the Dhātumaṇḍala;
the insignia-mudrās of Vajralāsyā and the others should likewise be drawn in the Maṇḍala.
And from the outside, one should draw their respective emblems as appropriate; one should draw the emblems of Maitreya and the others according to one's preference. Thus [it is said]. (11)
Regarding the initiation into the mandala:
now, in this Vajra-Guhyamandala, there is a detailed account of various procedures beginning with the entry.
In that regard, first of all, the Vajrācārya himself, having bound the Sattvavajrī mudrā, should enter.
Having entered and performed a single circumambulation,
having offered that mudrā to the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, and having released it properly upon one's own heart,
Having performed the ritual actions appropriately at the four gates by means of the vajra-hook, the karma-mudrās, and so forth, one should exit;
having exited, one should cause the disciples to enter by means of the yoga of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.
Then, having caused them to enter and covered their eyes with the fist, one should give them the secret vajra-sign of accomplishment.
One should teach the knowledge of the Vajra-guhyamudrā.
Regarding the mudrās, one should first teach the knowledge of the Vajraguhyakāya-mudrā:
within a moon mandala, [one forms] the hands and feet in añjali and the face [in its proper place].
While yawning, one should visualize the vajra and cause the Vajriṇī to feel passion. // 1 //
One should visualize a goad and a contraction of the arms, and a vajra upon the head;
while summoning with the hand, one should likewise bring forth Aṅkuśī.
By means of the application of discharging an arrow, one should strike the heart while yawning;
by means of the yoga of passion, one may even personally arouse Rativajrā. // 3 //
One should bind one's own heart with the "arm-binding" [mudrā]; by means of the application of the "vajra-armor," one may protect even a Buddha oneself. Thus, [verse] 4.
In that regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
VAJRA RĀGAYA HOḤ.
Vajrāṅkuśa Jaḥ!
Kill, kill, phaṭ!
Bind, protect, and deliver me!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the Vajra-secret gaze-mudrā:
"The vajra-gaze has eyes wide open with intense passion and great joy; by gazing with it, a woman becomes eternally submissive. (1)
With eyes darting and flickering, and eyelashes drawn together, this is called the "Blazing Attraction" (Dīptakṛṣṭi); it shall attract the entire world. // 2 //
With his eyes narrowed by anger and his frown completely destroyed, and having fixed his gaze with wrath, he could destroy even the three worlds. // 3 //
"The unblinking gaze, as firm as the stone that crushes Mount Meru, is known as the 'Gaze of Loving-kindness' (maitrīdṛṣṭi); it removes fevers, seizing spirits, and poisons. Thus [it is said]. (4)
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows: Vajradṛṣṭi, maṭ.
He who is born from the blazing gaze and the goad.
The gaze of anger is hrīḥ.
O you of firm vision, *traṭ*!
Then one should teach the knowledge of the secret speech-mudrā of Vajra:
"When 'hoḥ hoḥ hoḥ ho' is uttered, by means of the turning of speech, in an instant he shall arouse passion in all sentient beings through his perfectly clear vajra-speech. (1)
When "JJAḤ JJAḤ JJAḤ JJA" is uttered with a voice clearly expressive of wrath, one may summon even the entire world, including those equal to the Holder of the Vajra. // 2 //
Having concentrated with the utterance of the sound *huṃ huṃ huṃ huṃ*, which is perfectly clear, he may slay all beings, even those as firm as Mount Meru. // 3 //
When "haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ" is uttered with subtle speech, clearly articulated, one should protect all this—the eye, and even the Victor whose nature is vajra. Thus [it is said]. //4//
In this regard, these are the heart-mantras:
Vajra Hoḥ.
Vajra jjaḥ.
Vajra hūṃ.
Vajra haṃ.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the secret mind-mudrā of Vajra:
while personally meditating upon oneself as endowed with the excellence of all forms, one shall bring Vajrapāṇi and all the Buddhas under one's control. // 1 //
Meditating upon himself as Vajragarbha, endowed with the excellence of all aspects, he should personally summon his own self as Vajrapāṇi. // 2 //
Meditating upon himself as Vajranetra, endowed with the excellence of all aspects, he himself shall slay all phenomena. (3)
Meditating upon himself as the Vajra-Universal (Vajraviśva) endowed with the excellence of all aspects, he protects himself as the All-Vajra. Thus, [verse 4].
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
VAJRAPĀṆI VAŚAMĀNAYA SARVABUDDHĀN HOḤ.
O Vajragarbha, quickly summon Vajrapāṇi! HŪṂ JJAḤ!
O Vajranetra, slay all phenomena! Hūṃ phaṭ!
O Vajraviśva, protect all vajras! Haṃ!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the Vajra-secret-mudrā:
Having placed the Satvavajrā at one's own heart, and gazing with the vajra-vision, one shall indeed cause the entire world to enter [into the state of absorption]. (1)
Having established the Jewel-Vajra within his own heart, and gazing with a blazing look, he indeed brings everything under his control. // 2 //
Having placed the Dharma-vajrā at his own heart, he should indeed slay the entire world by gazing upon it with a wrathful look. // 3 //
Having established the Action-Vajra within one's own heart, and gazing with a compassionate eye, one should indeed protect this entire world. Thus [it is said]. (4)
Now, the heart mantras of these Vajra Secret Knowledge Mudrās are as follows:
*vajraguhyasamaya aḥ*.
Vajra-guhyasamaya hoḥ!
Vajra-guhyasamaya hūṃ.
Vajra-guhyasamaya haṃ.
Then, one should teach the binding of the Vajra-secret-mudrās:
"The great secret mudrās are proclaimed to arise from the vajra-añjali;
their binding as the great mudrās shall now be explained in brief. (1)
With her two big toes forming a cross-legged posture, the tips of her fingers curved against each other, and her waist and head held perfectly straight—she is known as Vajradhātvīśvarī. // 2 //
That same gesture is Madhyavajrā when the two middle fingers are joined at the tips; it is also Madhyānāmāntyapadmā when the fingers of the outstretched hand are extended. (3)
The foremost Vajra, the supreme among divine vajras, is concealed by both thumbs;
it is the foremost jewel of the "Well Done" gesture, blazing with the supreme source of jewels.
The same [mudrā], with the final jewel [finger] equalized and thus rotated, with all fingertips well-extended and the thumbs positioned between them, is [the next]. (5)
But that same circle of extended fingers, when raised to the mouth, covered by the thumb-vajra and with the tips joined together inside, [is the seal]. // 6 //
With the two thumbs spread apart, that is the *abhyantaravajriṇī* [mudrā];
furthermore, these are the *vajraguhyā* [mudrās], which arise from the *vajrabandha*. (7)

Furthermore, the secrets of the Dharma are revealed by means of signs meditated upon within the *saṃpuṭa*; the secrets of activity are revealed by means of signs situated within the interior of the secret of activity. (8)
Hereafter, I shall explain the Dharma-mudrās in brief:
ĀḤ JJAḤ HOḤ SAḤ,
UṂ ĀṂ TRAṂ HAḤ.
Hrīḥ dhaṃ bhaṃ raṃ, kaṃ haṃ huṃ vaṃ. // 1 //
Having divided the secret mudrā into two, one should fashion it among the action mudrās;
likewise, having divided each of the supreme pledges into two as well. // 2 //

Now I shall explain their means of accomplishment: saying "You are the pledge" (samayas tvam), they themselves bind [the mudrās], and those whose nature is the bliss of passionate desire attain success. (1)
However, among these, a wise man should never employ one particular [mudrā] at all times; rather, he should employ it in secret or for a great purpose. // 2 //
For these wives of the self-born ones have been established by the Self-existent as being firmly devoted to all souls;
being steadfastly attached to their practitioners, they shall not abandon their own husbands. Thus [it is said].
Now, from the binding of all these mudrās, the following rites arise:
having generated the Vajra-penetration upon oneself or another,
one should bind or cause [the other] to be bound by means of this heart-mantra.
Vajra hūṃ bind!
Now follows the release:
from whichever [place] all the mudrās have arisen, in brief,
one should release them there, with this heart-mantra.
Oṃ vajra muḥ.
Then there is the act of stabilization:
having stabilized the jewel-vajra, it is released from the heart to the crown of the head;
one should bind the armor with the tips of the fingers while reciting this heart-mantra.
Oṃ, firm vajra armor, be steadfast!
Now follows the procedure for binding:
just as pearls in their settings are made firm by a casing,
one should bind them all with this very heart-mantra.
Oṃ, the clapping of the secret samaya: saḥ.

"Vajrasattva, when recited according to one's preference, should be employed here in this ritual procedure for all mandala activities; he is the supreme bringer of all accomplishments. Thus it is said.
The detailed ritual procedure for the Vajra-secret Vajra-maṇḍala from the *Sarvatathāgata-mahāyānābhisamaya-mahākalparāja* is completed.
The Emission of Deities from Samādhi:

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Pledge of the Subtle Vajra-Wisdom Seal of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme personal vidyā: OṂ SŪKṢMAVAJRAJÑĀNASAMAYA HŪṂ.

Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Subtle Wisdom Samaya of All Tathāgatas Vajrasattva," and spoke this supreme self-knowledge mantra:
OṂ VAJRASATTVA SŪKṢMAJÑĀNASAMAYA HŪṂ //

Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Pledge of Subtle Wisdom of the Vajra-Jewel of All Tathāgatas" and spoke this supreme personal vidyā: OṂ VAJRARATNA SŪKṢMAJÑĀNASAMAYA HŪṂ.

Then the Tathāgata Amitāyus entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Subtle Wisdom Samaya of the Vajra Dharma of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge: Oṃ vajradharma sūkṣmajñānasamaya hūṃ.

Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Samaya of Subtle Wisdom of the Vajra-Action of All Tathāgatas" and spoke this supreme personal vidyā-mantra:
Oṃ vajrakarma sūkṣmajñānasamaya hūṃ.

Then the Blessed One Vairocana entered the samādhi called the "Subtle Wisdom Vajra of All Tathāgatas. As soon as he had entered it, rays of light from the subtle wisdom vajras issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas,
illuminating all world systems and all sentient beings.

Having stabilized the attainments of the vajra-samādhis of the subtle wisdom of all Tathāgatas, and having again become one, he focused upon the state of the vajra-body of samādhi-wisdom; then, having arisen as the single mass of Tathāgata-wisdom,
he entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana.
Then Vajrapāṇi, having entered into the hearts of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, spoke this subtle-vajra of the great samaya of the subtle wisdom of all Tathāgatas: "Subtle-vajra!"
Then, as soon as this was spoken, Vajrapāṇi emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas;
having empowered himself as the subtle wisdom-vajra-image of all the Tathāgatas,
he stood upon the tips of the noses of all the Tathāgatas and uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Indeed, the subtle vajra of all the Buddhas is great;
because of its greatness, though it is subtle, it can pervade even the triple world. Thus it is said.

Then, having spoken this, the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, for the sake of the radiation of the signs of the extremely subtle vajra-wisdom from the tips of the noses of all Tathāgatas, and by means of the yoga of the radiation of the entire *dharmadhātu* from the bodies of all Tathāgatas, pervaded the entire realm of space with the signs of the extremely subtle vajra-wisdom;
and having empowered himself as the vajra-image of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas pervading the entire realm of space, he remained there.
Then, at that very moment, all the Tathāgatas, having focused upon the essence of the vajra-nature within the vajra of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas,
remained absorbed in the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Vajra of the Subtle Wisdom of All Tathāgatas."
Then, from that Vajra of the Wisdom of all Tathāgatas, the Heart-mantra of the Samādhi-wisdom of all Tathāgatas issued forth: "Vajranābhi Tathāgata HŪṂ."
Then, as soon as this had issued forth, the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi again entered the bodies of all the Tathāgatas by means of the yoga of entering subtle gnosis;
having done so, he remained within their hearts as vajra-images.
Then, from those vajras of the beings of all the Tathāgatas, this fourfold heart-mantra of great gnosis issued forth.
O you whose nature is vajra.
Heart-vajra-hook.
Abide, O Rāgavajra; enter the heart!
Oh, Vajra-joy!
the wisdom-seal of Vajrasattva;
the wisdom-seal of the empowerment of the assembly of all Tathāgatas;
the wisdom-seal of the passion of all Tathāgatas;
And the Great Joy Wisdom Seal;
these are the great vajra samādhis of all the Tathāgatas.

Then Vajrapāṇi, the heart of all Tathāgatas, again entered his own heart by means of the yoga of entering subtle gnosis; having entered the heart, he remained there, empowering himself as a vajra-image within the heart.
Then, from that adamantine body, this fourfold heart-mantra issued forth:
*Vajraratnātmaka*.
Heart Vajra-sūrya.
O Vajradhvaja, remain at the summit! Vaṃ.
The vajra-laugh of the heart.
The wisdom-seal of the vajra-consecration of all Tathāgatas; the wisdom-seal of the array of the great mandala of light;
the wisdom-seal that fulfills the aspirations of all Tathāgatas.
This is the "Wisdom-Seal of the Great Laughter of All Tathāgatas";
it is the samādhis of the jewels of all Tathāgatas.
Then Vajrapāṇi, once again through the yoga of entering the subtle vajra-wisdom, entered his own heart—the vajra-heart—and remained there, having empowered himself as the vajra-image.
Then, from that vajra-image, this fourfold heart-mantra issued forth:
"Vajrapadmātmake."
The adamantine treasury of the heart.
Stay, O Vajracakra; enter the heart!
Vajra-tip of the tongue, heart!
The seal of the knowledge of the equality of all phenomena,
the seal of the wisdom-knowledge of all Tathāgatas,
and the seal of the knowledge of entering the great wheel.
The seal of non-conceptual gnosis, which is the speech of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas;
these are the samādhis of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas.
Then Vajrapāṇi once again, having entered that Vajra-heart by means of the yoga of entering the extremely subtle gnosis from the Vajra-heart at his own heart,
remained there, having empowered himself as a subtle vajra-image.
Then, from that subtle vajra-form, this fourfold heart-mantra issued forth:
"Sarvavajrātmaka."
The heart-vajra armor.
Stay, O Vajrayakṣa, O Heart!
Vajramuṣṭihṛdaya!

The wisdom-seal of the all-encompassing diverse activities of all Tathāgatas; the wisdom-seal of the valor that is difficult to overcome; the wisdom-seal of the destruction of the entire mandala of Māras.
This is called the "Knowledge-Seal of the Bond of All Tathāgatas";
it consists of the meditative absorptions of the activities of all Tathāgatas.

Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, once again, through the yoga of the radiation of the signs of extremely subtle gnosis, emerged from the bodies of all the Tathāgatas; having manifested as the body of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, he further assumed the forms of the Great Bodhisattvas such as Vajrasattva and others.
Having established their respective insignia within their hearts,
and relying upon moon-mandalas through the yoga of the arrangement of the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, they remained absorbed in the meditative concentrations of their own hearts.
The delineation of the maṇḍala:
Then Vajrapāṇi, once again for the sake of accomplishing the samādhi, gnosis, and superknowledges of all the Tathāgatas, spoke this Vajra-subtle-gnosis maṇḍala.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme Dharma-maṇḍala.
Resembling the Vajra-realm, it is known as the Subtle Vajra. // 1 //
One should establish the Great Beings through the yoga of the great maṇḍala;
one should draw the Buddha in the center of the vajra, and also within the circles of the Buddha-maṇḍalas. // 2 //
The Great Beings (mahāsattvas) should be depicted with their own seals and heart-mantras; they are seated in meditative absorption, with both hands in the vajra-bond gesture. Thus [it is said].
Next, regarding the mudrās here, the detailed procedure for the summoning and so forth in the Vajrasūkṣmadharmamaṇḍala,
and the detailed procedure for the entry and so forth according to the yoga of the great maṇḍala: having bestowed the insignia of gnosis with both hands,
One should teach the knowledge of Mahāmudrā for the purification of one’s own mind:
having placed the tongue against the palate, one should focus on the tip of the nose;
through the touch of the bliss of the subtle vajra, the mind becomes concentrated. (1)
When the sign of the touch of subtle vajra-bliss arises, one should cause that sign to expand; one should cause that mind to radiate everywhere. // 2 //

Just as the mind radiates throughout the triple world by means of its expansive diffusion according to one's wish, so too should it withdraw [the radiation] back again until it has returned to the tip of the nose. (3)
From that time forward, whatever one should meditate upon with a well-concentrated mind, all of this should be made firm, being fashioned by the knowledge of meditative absorption. // 4 //
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows:
*sūkṣma vajra*.
Sphara vajra.
Withdraw, O Vajra!
O Vajra, remain firm!
Whichever sentient being possesses great and firm loving-kindness, one should extend that [loving-kindness] toward all sentient beings through the yoga of mental pervasion. // 1 //

Through the practice of pervading with loving-kindness, one should indeed radiate compassion toward whoever it may be, being engaged for the sake of all sentient beings through actual application. // 2 //
All things are naturally luminous, primordially pure, and equal to space; whether it be non-dharma or dharma, it is satisfied by its own being as it radiates forth. // 3 //
"Those who are like the foremost of the wicked and who have no share in the awakening of a Buddha—one should cultivate great equanimity for the sake of purifying them. (4)
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
"Pervade with great loving-kindness."
Pervade with great compassion.
O all-pure one, radiate joy!
Awaken all sentient beings!
Then, one should train in the knowledge that recollects all the Tathāgatas:
whether in space or in another location, through the application of the subtle vajra, one should meditate upon the vajra-form while either standing or sitting. (1)
In the same way, in all places, through the application of the subtle vajra, one who is well-composed should meditate upon the Bodhisattva Heart-Vajra. // 2 //
One should meditate upon the great image of Vajrapāṇi in all locations, by means of the subtle vajra-application, correctly and in successive order. (3)
One who is well-composed should meditate, in due order and according to the instructions, upon the form of the Buddha, endowed with the excellence of all aspects, in every respect. Thus, [verse 4].
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
*vajrāmukhībhava*.
Enter, O Great Bodhisattva!
Vajrapāṇi, show your own form!
Enter by means of the recollection of the Buddha.
By means of the subtle vajra application, one should meditate upon oneself by oneself;
the meditation on the lunar disc as one's own self is the cultivation of the bodhicitta. // 1 //
One should visualize oneself by means of one's own self within the center of the lunar disk as the Vajra-form; this is the meditation on Sattvavajra. (2)
Having applied the subtle vajra method, one should meditate upon oneself by means of one's own self;
this is the meditation on Vajrasattva, with oneself as the heart of Sattvavajra. (3)
"One should personally meditate upon one's own self as the form of the Buddha, endowed with the excellence of all aspects; this is the meditation for the sake of the awakening of a Buddha. (4)
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
"O Samantabhadra, enter!"
Enter the Being-Vajra!
Enter into the samādhi-wisdom of Vajrasattva!
I am the Tathāgata.
Then, one should teach the secret gnosis of the mudrā of the dharmatā of all Tathāgatas:
"By speaking once with vajra-words, 'I am indeed equal to the Tathāgata,' one should slay all sentient beings through the union of the two organs. (1)
For I am indeed equal to the Great Vajra; by speaking once with vajra-words, one will certainly attract the world through the union of the two organs. // 2 //
For I am indeed equal to Vajradharma; by speaking once with vajra-words, he may destroy the entire world through the union of the two organs. // 3 //
"For I am indeed equal to the universal vajra; by speaking once with vajra-words, one shall accomplish all activities through the union of the two organs. // 4 //
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the samādhi-mudrā of the empowerment of the vajra of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas:
"By means of the application of the subtle vajra, one should meditate on the image of a Buddha within the center of the vajra; for he shall indeed attain Buddhahood as his own self. Thus it is said.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the samādhi-mudrā of Vajrasattva:
"By applying the subtle vajra-method, the hosts such as Vajra and the others are within the heart;
by meditating upon Vajrasattva and the rest, they grant their own accomplishments. Thus it is said.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the samaya-mudrās of the samādhi of the family of all Tathāgatas:
"Those arising from the vajra-bind are proclaimed to be sixteen; the binding of those foremost samayas of samādhi shall now be explained. (1)
Seated in the paryanka posture, fully reclined, likewise twisted and inverted, and the fourth, situated at the heart—these are [the positions] in the maṇḍala of Vajrasattva and the others. // 2 //
Situated on the forehead, on the back of the head, and on the shoulder, she is employed with laughter;
she is the nourisher of the face, the sword in the heart, the blooming of the heart, and she resides in the mouth. // 3 //
Located on the crown, the chest, and the face, as well as in the position of Jyeṣṭha and in front;
beyond this, one should teach the Dharma-mudrās in brief. Thus [it is said]. //4//
dṛ kki / gra gra / ma ṭaḥ / a gra / traṃ traṃ / aṃ aṃ / caṃ caṃ / tra ṭaḥ /
Dhṛtaḥ / Bhṛtaḥ / Kra saḥ / Ha haḥ / Va va / Vaṃ vaṃ /
phaṭ gra saḥ.
Then, one should instruct the subtle Vajrin in the foremost rites of Dharma; having formed the Fist of Knowledge (jñānamuṣṭi) in union, one should employ it in two ways. Thus [it is said].
The detailed ritual procedure for the Dharma-maṇḍala of Vajra-jñāna from the *Mahākalparāja*, which is the realization of the Mahāyāna of all Tathāgatas, is hereby completed.
I.4 Emanation of Deities from Samādhi:

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Empowerment of the Ritual Action of the Pervasive Expansion of the Extensive Procedures for the Supreme Worship of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme mantra of his own vidyā: OṂ SARVATATHĀGATA VAJRADHĀTVANUTTARAPŪJĀSPHARAṆA SAMAYE HŪṂ.

Then, indeed, the Tathāgatas Akṣobhya entered the samādhi called the Vajra Empowerment of the Samaya of the Karma of the Pervasive Expansion of the Extensive Ritual for the Unsurpassed Worship of All Tathāgata Vajrasattvas, and spoke this supreme mantra of his own vidyā: OṂ SARVATATHĀGATAVAJRASATTVĀNUTTARAPŪJĀSPHARAṆASAMAYE HŪṂ.

Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Empowerment of the Ritual Procedure for the Extensive Pervasion of the Supreme Vajra-Jewel Worship of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme mantra of his own wisdom: OṂ SARVATATHĀGATAVAJRARATNĀNUTTARAPŪJĀSPHARAṆASAMAYE HŪṂ.

Then the Tathāgata Amitāyus entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Empowerment of the Ritual Procedure for the Extensive Pervasion of the Supreme Worship of the Vajra Dharma of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge: OṂ SARVATATHĀGATAVAJRADHARMĀNUTTARAPŪJĀSPHARAṆASAMAYE HŪṂ.

Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Empowerment of the Samaya of the Pervasive Activity of the Extensive Ritual for the Unsurpassed Vajra-Action Worship of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme mantra of his own wisdom: OṂ SARVATATHĀGATAVAJRAKARMĀNUTTARAPŪJĀSPHARAṆASAMAYA HŪṂ.

Then the Blessed One Vairocana again entered the samādhi called the Vajra-Samaya of the Ritual for the Extensive Worship of All Tathāgatas that Pervades the Entire Dharmadhātu. As soon as he had entered it, at that very moment, from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that same Blessed One Vajradhara emerged,
having become deities of oceans of clouds of the extensive ritual arrays of all various kinds of worship, pervading the entire dharmadhātu and converging within the entire expanse of space.

In all the ocean-like clouds of the expanse of world-systems, within the circles of the assemblies of all Tathāgatas, [they perform] the generation of the unsurpassed great mind of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas, the accomplishment of the conduct of Samantabhadra through the gathering of the families of all Tathāgatas, the descent upon the great seat of enlightenment, the subduing of all Māras, the manifest awakening to the equality of all Tathāgatas, the production of the great maṇḍalas of all Tathāgatas, the turning of the wheel of the true Dharma that conquers the entire three worlds, and the performance of the welfare of the realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder, and so forth.
They remained there, manifesting all the miraculous transformations of the supernatural powers of the Buddhas.

And those deities of the ocean-like clouds of offerings, their two hands occupied with their respective mudrās, having worshipped all the Tathāgatas according to the ritual, and having become established upon moon-maṇḍalas through the yoga of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm, uttered this inspired utterance:
"O, how wonderful! I am the worship of the Buddhas, the initiator of all worship!"
For they indeed bestow that greatness of Buddhahood, which belongs to all Buddhas.
Then Vajrapāṇi again spoke the extensive ritual procedure for the activities of worship and so forth of all the Tathāgatas, the activity maṇḍala named Vajrakārya:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatasarvātmaniryātanapūjāspharaṇa karmavajri aḥ!
Oṃ sarvatathāgatasarvātmaniryātanākarṣaṇapūjāspharaṇa karmāgri jjaḥ!
Oṃ, O arrow of activity that radiates the worship of affectionate dedication of all selves of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ hoḥ!
Oṃ! May there be satisfaction through the rite of the pervasive offering of "Well Done" (sādhukāra), which is the total self-surrender of all Tathāgatas; aḥ!
The blissful bliss of all Tathāgatas,
the attractor of all Tathāgatas, and the one who inspires passion in all Tathāgatas.
And [the goddess] Sarvatathāgata-saṃtoṣaṇī; these are the great offerings to all Tathāgatas.
Oṃ, homage to the jewels of the empowerment of the bodies of all Tathāgatas; Oṃ Vajramaṇi! Oṃ!
Oṃ, homage to all the Tathāgata-suns; O Vajratejinī, Jvālā Hrīḥ!
Oṃ, homage to those who are at the tip of the wish-fulfilling jewel banner that fulfills the hopes of all Tathāgatas; Oṃ Traṃ, at the tip of the Vajra-banner!
Oṃ, homage to those who produce great joy and rapture for all Tathāgatas; O Vajrahāsa, Haḥ!
Mahādhipatinī, Mahodyotā,
Mahāratnavarṣā.
And [the goddess] Mahāprītiharṣā; these are the offerings for the consecration of all Tathāgatas.
Oṃ! With the samādhis of the vajra-nature of all Tathāgatas, I praise you, the great supreme Dharma, Hrīḥ!
Oṃ, with the emanations of the Prajñāpāramitā of all Tathāgatas, I praise you, O Dhaṃ, who follows the Great Sound!
Oṃ, with the methods of all the sūtras beginning with the *Sarvatathāgatacakrākṣaraparivarta*, I praise [you] in all maṇḍalas; hūṃ!
Oṃ, with the songs of the communal chanting of the Buddhas, which is the intentional language of all Tathāgatas, I praise you, O Vajrāvācī; vaṃ!
The Song of Great Wisdom,
following the great resonance,
the entry into all mandalas.
And the practice of mantra;
these are the dharma-worships of all the Tathāgatas.
Oṃ, perform, perform the ritual action of the offering that radiates clouds of incense from all the Tathāgatas!
Oṃ, for the ritual action of the pervasive emanation of the blossoming flowers of all Tathāgatas, kiri kiri!
Oṃ, for the rite of worship consisting of the pervasive radiance and blazing light of all Tathāgatas, fill, fill!
Oṃ, perform, perform the rite of worship that radiates oceans of fragrance from all the Tathāgatas!
They are Satvavatī, Mahābodhyaṅgavatī,
Cakṣuṣmatī,
and Gandhavatī.
The ritual offerings of the activities of all Tathāgatas.
The delineation of the maṇḍala:
