Now, herein is the Vajrakāryakarma-maṇḍala, which initiates the worship of all Tathāgatas without exception or remainder.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme *karma-maṇḍala*,
which resembles the Vajra-realm and is known as the "Vajra-Action."
One should cause the image of the Buddha to be established by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala;
one should draw the deities together with their mudrās by means of the yoga of Vajrasattva and the others. Thus it is said.
Now follows the detailed procedure for the entry into the Vajrakārya-karma-maṇḍala and other rites within this [tantra].
There, at the very beginning, one should cause [the disciple] to enter by means of the yoga of entering the Vajradhātu.
Having caused them to enter, one should speak thus:
"This is the samaya of worship for all Tathāgatas."
"Therefore, you must perform these sixteenfold worship rites day after day according to your capacity."
Then, having released the binding of the face and shown the ritual maṇḍala,
[he should place] the universal insignia with both hands.
One should give.
Consequently, he is honored even by all the Tathāgatas, let alone by others.
Then, one should teach the mudrā of the knowledge of the worship consisting in the accomplishment of the great bodhicitta:
"By generating a firm resolve for bodhicitta, one should think, 'I am a Buddha.'"
But by worshipping oneself as a jewel, one may even obtain the bliss of a Buddha. // 1 //
Having generated the firm resolve for awakening and thinking, "I am the Buddha," one worships with offerings such as the cleansing of impurities and so forth, and then consecrates oneself. // 2 //
Having generated the firm resolve for awakening and thinking "I am the Buddha," one should worship oneself with songs, pleasures, and offerings, and thus arouse passion.
Thinking "I am a Buddha" through the firm generation of the thought of awakening (bodhicitta), he who dances while making offerings is honored even by the Buddhas. // 4 // Thus it is said.
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
"I am the self of the Buddha."
I consecrate the Buddha.
I offer praise to the Buddha.
I perform an offering to the Buddha.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrās for worshipping all Buddhas;
likewise, by means of the supreme applications of the vajras of body, speech, and mind, one who worships all Buddhas will certainly become worthy of homage. // 1 //
One whose self is the worship through rejoicing, born from the vajras of body, speech, and mind of the great merit of all Buddhas, shall swiftly attain Buddhahood. // 2 //
Through the self-determination of the vajras of divine body, speech, and mind, one is honored with the thought: "I worship all the perfectly awakened ones with all forms of worship. // 3 //
Through the dedication and offerings of all accumulations of merit arising from the vajra of body, speech, and mind, one shall become equal to all Buddhas. Thus [it is said]. 4.
In this regard, there are these [verses]:
"I prostrate."
I rejoice.
Worship of the Buddha.
Transformation.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrā for the worship of the Dharma:
"All phenomena are luminous by nature, for they are pure from the beginning by their very essence.
By worshipping with this Dharma, one shall indeed obtain the joys of delight. (1)
The syllable *a* is to be declared as the mouth in the compendium of all phenomena;
by means of this Dharma-seal, one cuts through all sufferings. (2)
The Tathāgata is the cause of all phenomena;
by worshipping him with the worship of the Wheel of the True Dharma, one shall become a bearer of the Dharma. // 3 //
Having stated that all phenomena are by nature like echoes,
one should worship with this offering of Dharma and thereby attain the state of self-mastery.
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
Sarvaśuddha.
Samantabhadra!
The Wheel of Dharma.
Free from conceptual proliferation.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrās for the worship of samādhi:
"By meditating on one's own atoms within the vajras of body, speech, and mind as the forms of vajras, one who is of the nature of vajra will swiftly become [a Vajra-being]. (1)
Meditating upon one's own atoms within the vajras of body, speech, and mind as all the Buddhas, one will swiftly become the Dharmakāya. // 2 //
By meditating upon the vajra-sattvas within the atoms of one's own body, speech, and mind-vajras, one becomes equal to Vajrasattva. // 3 //
"By meditating on the forms of the Buddhas within the vajras of one's own body, speech, and mind—each composed of its own atoms—one shall attain the state of perfect Buddhahood. (4)
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
Vajrakāya.
The Dharma-body.
The body of sentient beings.
The Buddha-body.
Then one should teach the secret worship and the knowledge of the mudrās:
"The self-arisen one performs the worship of the bliss of embracing all bodies; by offering this, one will quickly become equal to Vajrasattva. (1)
But by bestowing the pleasures of seizing the hair in firm union with intense passion upon the Buddhas, one becomes equal to a vajra-jewel. // 2 //
But by offering up those supreme pleasures kissed by the attachment to the bliss of firm conviction, one becomes equal to Vajradharma of the Buddhas. // 3 //
By offering the bliss arising from the union of the two organs in every respect as an act of worship, one becomes equal to Vajrakarma. Thus [ends verse 4].
In this regard, these are the heart-mantras of the secret mudrās:
Rativajra.
Rāgavajra.
Prītivajra.
Kāmavajra.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the great mudrās for the ritual of worshiping all the Tathāgatas:
"By means of yoga, [the hands] are placed on the heart, the sides, and the back, as well as on the forehead and so forth;
they rest upon the mouth, the ears, the head, the back, the crown of the head, the nose, and the hips."
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the samaya-mudrās for the ritual of worship of all Tathāgatas:
"Having made the vajra-bind firm through the application of the mahāmudrā, one should worship the Jinas by placing [the mudrās] at the heart and other locations. Thus it is said.
Then, one should teach the dharma-knowledge for the worship of all Tathāgatas:
Oṃ grayaḥ yyaḥ sā / tri raṃ haṃ naḥ /
Khaṃ ṣaṃ hūṃ hi / Śa ṇa siḥ saṃ / The action seals (karmamudrā) are, in brief, the action seals made twofold. Thus it is said.
The detailed ritual procedure for the maṇḍala of vajra activities from the *Mahākalparāja*, the realization of the Mahāyāna of all Tathāgatas, is hereby completed.
1.5 The Emanation of Deities:

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, having generated the family of all Tathāgatas through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, spoke this heart-mantra of the seals of all Tathāgatas for the sake of gathering all accomplishments within this extensive ritual procedure of the Great Kalpa of the Family of All Tathāgatas: OṂ SARVATATHĀGATAMUṢṬI VAṂ.
Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, having generated the family of all Tathāgatas through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas,
spoke this seal of all Tathāgatas for the sake of gathering all accomplishments within this extensive ritual procedure of the great kalpa of the family of all Tathāgatas:
Oṃ vajrasattvam-uṣṭi aḥ.

Then the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, having generated the family of all Tathāgatas through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, spoke this seal of all Tathāgatas for the purpose of gathering all accomplishments within this extensive ritual procedure of the Great Kalpa of the Family of All Tathāgatas: Oṃ vajraratnamuṣṭi traṃ.

Then the Tathāgata Amitāyus, through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, having generated the family of all Tathāgatas, spoke this seal of all Tathāgatas for the sake of encompassing all accomplishments within this extensive ritual procedure of the Great Kalpa of the Family of All Tathāgatas: Oṃ vajradharmamuṣṭi khaṃ.

Then the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, having generated the family of all Tathāgatas through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, spoke this seal of all Tathāgatas for the purpose of gathering all accomplishments from this extensive ritual procedure of the Great Kalpa of the Family of All Tathāgatas: Oṃ vajrakarmamuṣṭi hāṃ.
The delineation of the maṇḍala:

Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, through his own empowerment, having generated the family of all Tathāgatas of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, [proclaimed] this for the sake of gathering all accomplishments from this extensive ritual procedure of the great kalpa of the family of all Tathāgatas.
He spoke the maṇḍala of the four mudrās named Vajrasiddhi.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme maṇḍala of mudrās, which resembles the Vajradhātu and is known as Vajrasiddhi. (1)
The wise one should trace the lines by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala;
having first established the image of the Buddha, he should draw the four mudrās. // 2 //
Within the centers of the moon-maṇḍalas, one should draw the vajra-mudrā and so forth. Thus, [verse] 3.
Regarding initiation into the maṇḍala:
having performed here, in this Vajrasiddhi-mudrā-maṇḍala, the detailed ritual for summoning and so forth, and having caused [the disciple] to enter in that same manner, one should speak thus:
"You must not reveal this secret chapter to anyone."
For what reason?

There are beings of wrong views, performers of evil deeds, lacking in vigor, and devoid of skill; they are unacquainted with the art of painting, and because they consider the great maṇḍalas of all the Tathāgata families, such as the Vajradhātu and others, to be too vast, they do not enter them due to their lack of vigor.

For their sake, this Vajrasiddhi-mudrā-maṇḍala— which is the pledge (*samaya*) of the maṇḍala of the families of all Tathāgatas— is empowered as the sign of the supreme vajra-siddhi of all Tathāgatas, for the purpose of protecting the entire realm of sentient beings without exception and for the experience of all benefit, happiness, and mental well-being.
You must not lack faith in these secrets of the pledge-mudrās of the families of all Tathāgatas.

Having said, "May there not be for you rebirth in the hells, the animal realm, or as a preta; may there not be untimely death through the failure to avoid dangers," one should release the binding of the mouth and show the mandala.
Then, one should proclaim the seal-commitment (mudrā-samaya) of all the Tathāgatas:
"Whichever seal one should bind for whichever great being,"
While reciting the mantra, one should contemplate that [deity] with one's own mind through the meaning of the heart-mantra.
By means of this yoga of knowledge belonging to the great-souled ones, all mudrās for everyone attain accomplishment, according to the word of Vajrapāṇi. // 2 //
Then one should explain the secret of all mudrās:
having opened one's own organ, one should grasp it with the vajra-fist;
whichever mudrā one touches with that, she comes under one's control at that very moment.
Then one should speak of the dharmatā of all mudrās;
having applied the subtle vajra method, one should bind the jñānamudrā.
By means of this application of the method, one shall bring the jñānamudrā under control.
Then one should explain all the rites of the mudrās:
"But by offering songs, dances, aesthetic delights, food, recreation, and other pleasures to the Buddhas, one should bring [the practitioner] under the power of the karma-mudrā. Thus it is said.
Then, one should teach the secret knowledge of the mudrās for the mastery of all maṇḍalas:
"Having become a self-arisen one with an erect *liṅga*, one should sit upon a white cloth;
having empowered the *liṅga* as a *caitya*, [one should think] 'I myself am the Vajradhātu. (1)

Having made the vajra-bind firm, with the middle fingers raised like sprouts and the little and index fingers extended from the mouth—this is the pledge (*samaya*) of those who hold the foremost pledges. // 2 //
Concentrated in meditative absorption, he should visualize the mandala through the application of the subtle vajra, leading it to the mastery of samādhi by means of the subtle vajra. (3)

Having formed the pair of vajra-mudrās, one should firmly grasp the vajra between them; by binding the tips of the little fingers, this is the foremost mandala for vajra-activities. (4) Thus it is said.
Then, having instructed [the disciple] in the fourfold binding of the great mudrās of Vajrasattva and the others as they truly are,
according to the detailed procedure for the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu,
one should likewise draw all the maṇḍalas beginning with Akṣobhya using the yoga of the four-mudrā maṇḍala, just like the maṇḍala of the four mudrās of Vajrasiddhi.
By means of their respective mudrās, they grant all siddhis;
likewise, when painted upon cloth, walls, or in space—in short, in any location—they grant all siddhis.

From the time of the construction of the mandala onwards, for some, accomplishment is attained within that very entry into the mandala according to their preference; for others, it begins from that point after one day; and for others, after four days.
For some, it takes sixteen days; for others,

even those who have committed the five acts of immediate retribution, it takes one year— provided they perform all their tasks at will with ease, experiencing all forms of affection, all flavors, and the pleasures of food and recreation— and thus the Blessed One has declared that the supreme accomplishment is attained.
1.6 The Emanation of the Deity from Samādhi:

Then the Blessed One Vairocana again entered the samādhi called *Sarvatathāgatottamasiddhisamayavajra* (the Vajra of the Pledge of the Supreme Accomplishment of All Tathāgatas), and from his own heart he emitted this heart-essence of all Tathāgatas called *Sarvatathāgatamahāyānābhisamaya* (the Great Vehicle Realization of All Tathāgatas): "Vajrasattva!"

The delineation of the maṇḍala: Then the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, for the sake of protecting the realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder, and for the experience of all benefit, happiness, and mental well-being, up to the attainment of the supreme siddhi of all Tathāgatas, spoke this maṇḍala of the realization of the Mahāyāna.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme *sattvamaṇḍala*, which resembles the *vajradhātu* and is known as *Vajrasattva*. (1)
One should delineate the outer maṇḍala by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala;
one should then place Vajrasattva in the center of the moon-maṇḍala. Thus it is said.
Then, having performed the summoning, entry, and so forth into the maṇḍala according to the rules, one should generate the gnoses of the accomplishments of all the Tathāgatas.
In this regard, first of all it must be said: "This should not be spoken by you to anyone who has not seen the ritual convention (*samaya*) or who is unskilled in these secrets;
lest they be reborn in any of the miserable realms (*apāya*), or suffer untimely death through the failure to avoid danger."
Then, one should teach the knowledge for accomplishing the supreme siddhi of Vajrasattva:
"Mounted upon the orb of the full moon and embracing the Mahāmudrā, by meditating on oneself as Vajrasattva, one quickly attains accomplishment. Thus it is said.
Then, one should instruct [the disciple] in the secret samaya-knowledge of all mandalas:
"There is no other evil in the three realms equal to dispassion;
therefore, you must never again become dispassionate toward desire."
Great pledge: *han phaṭ*!
Then one should give the Heart of the Oath in this manner:
"In all the mandalas of the families of all the Tathāgatas, throughout the detailed rituals, the commitment of the samaya must be bestowed."
Then, one should teach the fourfold binding of the great mudrās and so forth of Vajrasattva; likewise, the accomplishments [are attained].
Thus, on cloth paintings and all other images, all accomplishments are granted according to the desired procedure.
Thus, it is as described in the *Vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalavidhivistara*.

Excellent for you, Vajrasattva; excellent for you, Vajraratna;
excellent for you, Vajradharma; excellent for you, Vajrakarman! (1)
This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna, the secret of all Tathāgatas, and the compendium of the Mahāyāna. // 2 //
Even the name of Vajrasattva is the supreme bringer of all accomplishments;
indeed, when practiced with purity, one shall attain Buddhahood through bliss. // 3 //
"By means of the application of Vajradharma, one shall accomplish happiness through all the pleasures of the senses;
in this very life, one shall achieve inexhaustible and imperishable bliss.
Thus ends the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha*, the great king of ritual manuals titled "The Mahāyāna Abhisamaya of All Tathāgatas."
Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, having again assembled in a great assembly, entreated the Blessed One, the Great Cakravartin of all Tathāgatas, with this hymn of one hundred and eight names.
Homage to you, Vajrasattva, Great Vajra, Lord of Vajras, Excellent Accomplisher, Vajra Consecration, Vajra Radiance, Vajra Banner! // 1 //
O Laughing Vajra, Great Dharma, Vajra Treasury, Great Excellence, Sovereign King of all Maṇḍalas, free from conceptual proliferation—homage be to you! // 2 //
O Vajrakarma, great protector, fierce yakṣa, great graha, vajra-fist, great mudrā, you who are all mudrās, homage be to you! // 3 //
O Bodhicitta, O Great Enlightenment, O Buddha, O All-Tathāgatas! O Vajrayāna, O Great Wisdom, O Mahāyāna, homage be to you! // 5 //
O you who are all-purpose, the purpose of all reality, the purpose of great beings, and all-knowing;
O omniscient one, the doer of all, the all, the seer of all—homage be to you! // 5 //
O you whose nature is the vajra, supreme among the excellent vajras, vajra-valiant, bearer of the excellent vajra; O great pledge, essence of reality, great truth—homage be to you! // 6 //
O Vajrāṅkuśa, great desire, most radiant in the divine sport, O Vajraprabha, illuminating light, light of the Buddhas—homage be to you! // 7 //
O Supreme Vajra King, O Supreme Vajra, O Foremost among the Foremost of Sciences, O Best of Men!
O Supreme Vajra, O Foremost among the Great Foremost, O Supreme Science, homage be to you! // 8 //
O Vajradhātu, Great Secret, Vajra-secret, Holder of the well-guarded secret; O Vajrasūkṣma, Great Meditation, Vajra-activity—homage be to you! // 9 //
O supreme Buddha, O supreme Vajra-Buddha, O great wise one in the awakening of the Buddhas, O great Buddha of Buddha-knowledge, O Buddha of Buddhas—homage be to you! // 10 //
O worship of the Buddhas, great worship, worship of sentient beings, O excellent worshiper!
O great skillful means, O great accomplishment, O Vajra-accomplishment, homage be to you! 11.
O Great Body of the Tathāgata, O Sarasvatī of the Tathāgata, O Great Mind of the Tathāgata, O Vajra-mind, homage be to you! 12.
O Lord of Buddhas, you who carry out the commands of the Victors, O Buddha-mitra, elder brother of the Victors, O pervasive Mahāvairocana, Teacher, both peaceful and fierce—homage be to you! (13)
O Great Reality of the Tathāgata, O Great Method of the limit of existence, O Wisdom of all perfections, O Ultimate Truth—homage be to you! (14)
Samantabhadra, supreme in conduct, O Māra, subduer of Māra! O you who possess the knowledge of universal equality, the foremost of all, who go everywhere—homage be to you! 15.
O Buddha-huṃkāra, Huṃkāra, Vajra-huṃkāra, Dāmaka;
O you whose limbs are the universal vajra, O fierce vajra, O Vajrapāṇi—homage be to you! 16.
To be saluted, worshipped, honored, and likewise revered by the Tathāgatas—you are called Vajrasattva because your mind is as firm as a vajra. // 17 //
For perfect enlightenment depends upon you; you are the father of all who see.
Having encountered you, Tathāgatas have arisen and will arise. (18)
Whoever should praise with this king of hymns with true devotion, and who should praise while singing it, he too shall become equal to the Holder of the Vajra. (19)
We entreat you, O Protector, who brings all Buddhas under your power:
for the sake of the purposeful activity for the benefit of all sentient beings, manifest your own family. (20) Thus it was said.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the sovereign of all Tathāgatas, having heard the words of entreaty from all the Tathāgatas,
established that vajra within his own heart.
Having summoned all those Tathāgatas, he spoke thus:
"O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, I do not comply."
All the Tathāgatas asked:
"What is the cause?"
Vajradhara said:
"O Blessed Ones, there are beings such as Maheśvara and other wicked beings who cannot even be converted by all you Tathāgatas."
"How should I conduct myself toward them?"
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, through the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas, entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Great Skillful Means Wisdom of All the Tathāgatas.

Immediately upon his entering it, all the Tathāgatas, for the sake of pervading the entire realm of space as far as the atoms of dust, gathered once again on the summit of Mount Sumeru in the jeweled gabled palace of vajra-maṇi-ratnas.
Having focused upon the equality of all Tathāgatas,

they entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, which bears the Śrīvatsa mark. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, having empowered himself as the heart of all Tathāgatas, through the equality of all vajras, for the sake of the supreme accomplishment of the welfare and happiness of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, [remained there].
And for the sake of disciplining all the wicked,
having taken hold of the middle of the knowledge of the samādhis and skillful means of the great compassion of all Tathāgatas,
he entered the samādhi named "The Vajra of the Samaya of the Wrathful Skillful Means of the Great Compassion of All Tathāgatas."

And immediately upon his entering [this samādhi], at that very moment, from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, there issued forth the heart-mantra of all the Tathāgatas called "The Pledge of All the Tathāgatas": HŪṂ.
Then, as soon as this had issued forth from the heart-vajra of Vajrapāṇi, that very Blessed One Vajradhara manifested as many forms of Vajrapāṇi, whose bodies were filled with flames on all sides;

who possessed knitted brows, furrowed foreheads, and mouths made terrifying by curved fangs; whose hands were busily occupied with weapons blazing with vajra-flames, such as vajra-hooks, nooses, and maces; and who wore various colorful ornaments and diverse garments. Having thus emerged, they appeared.

Having subdued all malevolent beings in all world-systems, they took their places upon moon-maṇḍalas through the yoga of the great maṇḍala of the Vajra-realm surrounding the Blessed One Vairocana, and uttered this inspired utterance:
"Oh, how wonderful is the discipline of skillful means for those possessed of great skillful means!
For through the disciplining of beings by skillful means, even the stainless ones undergo the state of wrath."
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, having focused upon the non-conceptual nature of reality (*dharmatā*) of all Tathāgatas,

entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Empowerment of the Great Wrathful Vajra-Samaya of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra, the heart-essence of all Tathāgatas, called "The Vajra Huṃ of All Tathāgatas":
Oṃ sumbha niḥsumbha hūṃ!
Seize, seize, hūṃ!
Cause to be seized, hūṃ!
Bring here, hoṃ, O Blessed One!
Vajra hūṃ phaṭ!
Then, as soon as this had issued forth, the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas;
having empowered and drawn in all the Tathāgatas, together with their circles of bodhisattva assemblies, from as many oceans of clouds spreading through all world-systems as there are,
he caused them to enter the great maṇḍala of the Vajra-samaya.
Having bound himself with the samayas, he again became a single, solid mass as the body of the Great Vajra Wrathful One;
then, remaining in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
Oh, how entirely auspicious and faultless is the mental state of awakening! For through it, even anger becomes delightful when employed for the sake of disciplining sentient beings.
Then that body of the Great Vajra Wrathful One, having emerged from the heart of the Blessed One and come to rest upon a moon disc in front of all the Tathāgatas,
once again sought his command.

Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Vajra that Attracts the Samayas of All Tathāgatas, and from his own heart he emitted this heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas called the Hook of the Samaya of All Tathāgatas: *huṃ ṭakki jjaḥ*.

Then, as soon as this had issued forth, all the lords of the triple world, such as Maheśvara and others, throughout the ocean-like clouds of the expanse of all world-systems— surrounded by their entire retinues of worldly inhabitants and drawn in without exception by the vajra-hook of the samaya of all Tathāgatas— approached the summit of Mount Sumeru and the gabled pavilion at the peak of the Vajra-jewel mountain.
They stood surrounding the Bhagavat on all sides, encircling the peaked gabled palace with its crest of vajra-jewels.
Then Vajrapāṇi, taking that vajra from his own heart and brandishing it, surveyed the entire wheel of the three worlds within the whole triple realm and spoke thus:
“Follow, O sirs, the teaching of all the Tathāgatas, and carry out my command!”
Then they spoke thus:
"How should we proceed?
The Blessed One Vajrapāṇi replied:
“Go for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha through practice; strive, O friends, for the attainment of the knowledge of the Omniscient One! Thus [he said].
Then, Mahādeva—the sovereign of the entire triple world in this universe, who was arrogant due to his lordship over all the three worlds—displaying great wrath, spoke thus:

"O Yakṣa, I am the sovereign of the triple world, the Lord, the creator and transformer, the Lord of all beings, the God beyond gods, the Great God! So how could I act according to your command, O Yakṣa?"
Then Vajrapāṇi, brandishing his vajra once more, commanded:
"O wicked being, enter the maṇḍala quickly and abide in my samaya!"
Then the god Mahādeva said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, who is this being who issues such a command to Īśvara?
Then the Blessed One summoned the entire host of the three worlds, beginning with Maheśvara, and spoke thus:
“Friends, proceed to undertake the vow of the commitment to going for the three refuges!
Lest this yakṣa Vajrapāṇi—cruel, wrathful, fierce, and a great bodhisattva—should destroy the entire triple world with his blazing vajra.
Then Maheśvara, by virtue of his sovereignty over the entire triple world and through the power of his own gnosis, [acted] in order to manifest fear before the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi.
Displaying his state of great fierce wrath, his form of great terror, his emission of great flames, and his great, violent laughter together with his retinue, he spoke thus:
"O sir! I am the sovereign of the entire triple world; you must carry out my command!"
Then Vajrapāṇi, brandishing that vajra with pride and laughing, spoke thus:
"O you who feed on the flesh of humans and kaṭapūtanas, who consume the ashes of funeral pyres as food and drink, and who use them for bedding, seating, and clothing—obey my command!
Then Maheśvara, the Great God, having empowered the entire triple world so that it was possessed by the Great Wrath, spoke thus.
“You too must obey my command and undertake [this practice] at the proper time.”
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Great Wrathful King, said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, this great god Mahādeva, out of pride in the power of his own knowledge and due to his sovereignty and lordship, does not bow before the teaching of all the Tathāgatas.
How, then, shall this be dealt with?"
Then the Blessed One causes [the practitioner] to recollect the Great Vajra-Samaya, which has arisen from the hearts of all Tathāgatas: Oṃ nisumbha vajra hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi uttered his own Vajra-heart mantra: HŪṂ.

Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the lords of the three worlds, beginning with Mahādeva, who had assembled from the entire triple realm, fell face-downward; crying out in piteous tones, they went for refuge to the Blessed One and Vajrapāṇi.
And that god Mahādeva, having fallen to the ground, became motionless and died.
Then the Blessed One, though already knowing [the situation], spoke thus to Vajrapāṇi:
“Proceed, Vajrapāṇi, for the sake of the safety of this entire wheel of the three worlds;
do not cause its destruction.”
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Great Wrathful King, having heard the words of the Blessed One, summoned all those beginning with the gods and spoke thus:
"Take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, and act according to my command."
“If you desire your own lives,” they said.
Then they replied,
“We go for refuge to the oceans of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.”
"We do not know the command of your teaching."

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, having summoned them, spoke thus: "O gods, this Blessed One, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, is the sovereign of all Tathāgatas, the father of all Tathāgatas, the executor of the commands of all Tathāgatas, and the eldest son of all Tathāgatas; he acts for the sake of disciplining all sentient beings."
He was consecrated as the Great Wrathful King by virtue of his capacity for action.
For what reason?
Because among you there are wicked hosts such as Mahādeva and others, who cannot be turned away from their evils even by all the Tathāgatas through peaceful means.
"For the sake of subduing those evil beings, I have empowered [this rite]; therefore, you must abide by this agreement"—such was the command.
They replied thus:
"O Blessed One, protect us from this loss of life!"
"Whatever command he shall give, that we will do.
The Blessed One said, "O friends, go for refuge to him alone; he alone will protect you, and no other."

Then those lords of the three worlds, having assembled from the entirety of the triple realm of the three worlds, turned toward where the Blessed One Vajradhara was and, with one voice, uttered cries of great distress, saying:
“Save us, O Blessed One! Save us from this suffering of death!”
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having summoned those gods and others, spoke thus: "Ho! You wicked ones, submit to my teaching!
Lest I reduce you to a single flame with this blazing vajra,"
"I shall reduce them all to ashes.
They replied thus:

"O Blessed One, you are Samantabhadra; you are the arousal of the mind of all Tathāgatas, peaceful and disciplined, seeking the welfare of all sentient beings, and bestowing fearlessness upon all sentient beings."
“Then, Blessed One, how will it burn us?
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Great Wrathful King, said this to them:
“O noble ones, I am Samantabhadra; because I carry out the commands of all the Tathāgatas, I have come for the sake of purifying those like you—beings of a wicked nature with sinful minds.”
"If you do not abide by my command, I shall destroy you.
They replied, "So be it."

Then Vajrapāṇi, the Great Wrathful King, having released Maheśvara and comforted the other gods, spoke this heart-mantra of all the Tathāgatas called "Vajra Arising" (*vajrottiṣṭhan*) for the purpose of raising them up: "Vajra, arise! As soon as this was spoken, with the exception of Maheśvara, all those lords of the three worlds assembled in the triple realm, together with their retinues, became fully revived; their hearts were comforted, and they experienced divine pleasures.
Free from fear, anxiety, and horripilation, they arose while gazing at the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi.
Then the Blessed One addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
“This great being, this great god, the lord of gods, has not been raised up;
so what is the use of destroying his life?”
“Bring him back to life;
he shall become a virtuous man.
Then Vajrapāṇi, saying “So be it,” recited this Heart-mantra for Reviving the Dead, the Vajrāyus: *Oṃ vajrāyur-jīvaya jīvaya saṃjīvaya saṃjīvaya svāhā.*
Then, as soon as this was spoken, the god Mahādeva, though dead, desired to revive and rise up;
yet he was unable to rise.
Thereupon, he said this to the Blessed One:
“What shall I say to him as instructed by the Blessed One?
The Blessed One said,
“Do not act in such a way as to carry out the command of this Great Being.”

“This one alone instructs him; it is not I,” Maheśvara said. [The Buddha asked: “Lord, are you not able to rescue these beings whom you have seen? Maheśvara replied: “I am indeed able. The Buddha said: “If you are able, why do you not rescue them? Maheśvara said: “I am indeed able, but they do not wish to be rescued by me. The Buddha said: “Why is that? Maheśvara said: “Because they do not believe in me. The Buddha said: “If they do not believe in you, how can they be saved? You should teach them so that they may develop faith in you. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I am now able to teach them so that they may develop faith in me. The Buddha said: “Well done, well done! Maheśvara, you should now teach them so that they may develop faith in you. At that time, Maheśvara, having received this instruction from the Buddha, immediately went to where those beings were and taught them as follows: “Friends, you must abandon all evil deeds and practice all wholesome deeds. Why is that? Because when one abandons all evil deeds and practices all wholesome deeds, one will surely attain birth in my realm. Those beings, having heard his teaching, developed faith in him and practiced accordingly. Because of this, they were reborn in his realm. The Buddha said: “Maheśvara, you have now accomplished what was entrusted to you. You should again go to where those beings are and teach them as before. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I have already taught them once, yet they still do not believe in me. How can they be saved? The Buddha said: “Maheśvara, you should teach them with skillful means so that they may develop faith in you. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I am now able to teach them with skillful means so that they may develop faith in me. The Buddha said: “Well done, well done! Maheśvara, you should now teach them with skillful means so that they may develop faith in you. Why is that? Because when one abandons all evil deeds and practices all wholesome deeds, one will surely attain birth in my realm. Those beings, having heard his teaching, developed faith in him and practiced accordingly. Because of this, they were reborn in his realm. The Buddha said: “Maheśvara, you have now accomplished what was entrusted to you. You should again go to where those beings are and teach them as before. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I have already taught them twice, yet they still do not believe in me. How can they be saved? The Buddha said: “Maheśvara, you should teach them with further skillful means so that they may develop faith in you. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I am now able to teach them with further skillful means so that they may develop faith in me. The Buddha said: “Well done, well done! The Buddha said: “Maheśvara, you have now accomplished what was entrusted to you. You should again go to where those beings are and teach them as before. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I have already taught them three times, yet they still do not believe in me. How can they be saved? The Buddha said: “Maheśvara, you should teach them with even greater skillful means so that they may develop faith in you. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I am now able to teach them with even greater skillful means so that they may develop faith in me. The Buddha said: “Well done, well done! Maheśvara, you should now teach them with even greater skillful means so that they may develop faith in you. Why is that? Because when one abandons all evil deeds and practices all wholesome deeds, one will surely attain birth in my realm. Those beings, having heard his teaching, developed faith in him and practiced accordingly. Because of this, they were reborn in his realm. The Buddha said: “Maheśvara, you have now accomplished what was entrusted to you. You should again go to where those beings are and teach them as before. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I have already taught them four times, yet they still do not believe in me. How can they be saved? The Buddha said: “Maheśvara, you should teach them with yet more skillful means so that they may develop faith in you. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I am now able to teach them with yet more skillful means so that they may develop faith in me. The Buddha said: “Well done, well done! Maheśvara, you should now teach them with yet more skillful means so that they may develop faith in you. At that time, Maheśvara, having received this instruction from the Buddha, immediately went to where those beings were and taught them as follows: “Friends, you must abandon all evil deeds and practice all wholesome deeds. Why is that? Because when one abandons all evil deeds and practices all wholesome deeds, one will surely attain birth in my realm. Those beings, having heard his teaching, developed faith in him and practiced accordingly. Because of this, they were reborn in his realm. The Buddha said: “Maheśvara, you have now accomplished what was entrusted to you. You should again go to where those beings are and teach them as before. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I have already taught them five times, yet they still do not believe in me. How can they be saved? The Buddha said: “Maheśvara, you should teach them with even more profound skillful means so that they may develop faith in you. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I am now able to teach them with even more profound skillful means so that they may develop faith in me. The Buddha said: “Well done, well done! Maheśvara, you should now teach them with even more profound skillful means so that they may develop faith in you. At that time, Maheśvara, having received this instruction from the Buddha, immediately went to where those beings were and taught them as follows: “Friends, you must abandon all evil deeds and practice all wholesome deeds. Why is that? Because when one abandons all evil deeds and practices all wholesome deeds, one will surely attain birth in my realm. Those beings, having heard his teaching, developed faith in him and practiced accordingly. Because of this, they were reborn in his realm. The Buddha said: “Maheśvara, you have now accomplished what was entrusted to you. You should again go to where those beings are and teach them as before. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I have already taught them six times, yet they still do not believe in me. How can they be saved? The Buddha said: “Maheśvara, you should teach them with the most profound skillful means so that they may develop faith in you. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I am now able to teach them with the most profound skillful means so that they may develop faith in me. The Buddha said: “Well done, well done! At that time, Maheśvara, having received this instruction from the Buddha, immediately went to where those beings were and taught them as follows: “Friends, you must abandon all evil deeds and practice all wholesome deeds. Why is that? Because when one abandons all evil deeds and practices all wholesome deeds, one will surely attain birth in my realm. Those beings, having heard his teaching, developed faith in him and practiced accordingly. Because of this, they were reborn in his realm. The Buddha said: “Maheśvara, you have now accomplished what was entrusted to you. You should again go to where those beings are and teach them as before. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I have already taught them seven times, yet they still do not believe in me. How can they be saved? The Buddha said: “Maheśvara, you should teach them with the ultimate skillful means so that they may develop faith in you. Maheśvara said: “World-Honored One, I am now able to teach them with
The Blessed One said,
"I am not able to protect him from this.
He replied:
“For what reason?
He replied:
“Because he is the sovereign lord of all Tathāgatas.”
He said:
“Lord, I do not understand the meaning of what the Blessed One has spoken.
However, as for this one who is indeed the sovereign over even the Tathāgatas—the sovereigns of all the three realms—I do not know who he is.”
Then the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having again summoned Mahādeva, spoke thus:
"O wicked being, why do you not carry out my command?
Then Mahādeva, having heard the words of Vajrasattva, became enraged and fierce; remaining in that very fallen state, he displayed once more his most terrible form and spoke as follows:
“I am prepared even for death, but I will not carry out your command.”
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, manifesting great wrath, stepped forth from his own stride and uttered this mantra: Oṃ pādākarṣaṇa vajra hūṃ!

Then, from the soles of the Blessed One’s feet, there emerged Vajrānucara, whose great mouth was formidable with fangs and a frown formed by eyebrows containing flames on all sides; standing before the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, he awaited his command.
Then Vajrapāṇi, for the purpose of purifying Maheśvara, spoke thus: "Oṃ! O you who draw [him] toward the feet, follower of all Vajradharas, kaṇḍa kaṇḍa vajra hūṃ jaḥ!"

Then, when this had been said, Mahādeva— accompanied by the goddess Umā, with his feet upward and naked, being mocked by all the world— was placed by the attendant Vajra, who was pulling at his feet, upon the soles of the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi’s feet. Then the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Blessed One as follows:
“Blessed One, what shall I do with this wicked being and his wife?
The Blessed One said: *Oṃ vajrākrama hoḥ*.

Then, when this had been said, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having trampled Mahādeva with his left foot and pressing Umā’s breasts with his right, uttered this heart-mantra: Oṃ vajrāviśa hanaya traṃ traṭ!
Then, as soon as this had been spoken, Mahādeva entered [the state of possession] and struck his thousand faces with his thousand hands.
Then, from the exterior of the gabled hall whose pinnacle was adorned with vajra-jewels, a great roar was let forth by all the inhabitants of the three worlds.
“This is our sovereign; he shall be disciplined by this Great-Souled One.”
Then the Blessed One, having generated great compassion for Mahādeva, spoke this Heart of Universal Buddha-Love: Oṃ buddha maitrī vajra rakṣa haṃ.
Then, as soon as this was spoken, Mahādeva’s suffering from that possession subsided.

And that touch of Vajrapāṇi’s palm became the means for attaining the state of a Tathāgata, up to the point of achieving the knowledge, superknowledges, dhāraṇīs, liberations, samādhis, and the consecration of unsurpassed accomplishment.
Then, Mahādeva, experiencing the bliss of all the Tathāgatas’ samādhis, dhāraṇīs, and liberations through the touch of the Blessed One’s palm, cast his body down at the feet of Vajrapāṇi.

Below, after passing through as many world-systems as there are atoms in thirty-two world-systems equal to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system named Bhasmacchatrā; there, a Tathāgata named Bhasmeśvaranirghoṣa has appeared.
Then, from that assembly of great gods, this inspired utterance issued forth:
"Oh, how indeed the unsurpassed Buddha-knowledge of all Buddhas, having caused [beings] to fall away from the state of syllables and words, establishes them in nirvāṇa! Thus it is said.
Then the great bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke thus to Nārāyaṇa and all the other lords of the three worlds:
“Enter, sirs, into this great maṇḍala of the vajra-samaya of all the Tathāgatas;
having entered, observe the samaya of all the Tathāgatas.”
They spoke thus:
"We shall do exactly as you instruct."
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having summoned those inhabitants of the three worlds, spoke thus:
“Accept once more, sirs, the training and the vow of the commitment for going for the three refuges, and abide in my commitment.”
They said, "So be it;
however, we are unacquainted with your pledge.
Then Vajrapāṇi bestowed his own pledge upon them.
Having generated the thought of awakening, strive with great composure according to your strength, following the supreme sequence for the sake of enlightenment.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, addressing those gods and others, saying, "Bind the great samaya-mudrā of entry," they bound it.
With this heart-mantra of the Great Samaya-mudrā:
Oṃ vajra samaya gṛhṇa bandha samayam, Vajrasattva, remember the samaya; you are the samaya of all Tathāgatas.
Be firm for me,
be stable for me, be unshakable for me.
Be unassailable by me, and bring about the excellence of my mind in all activities! Ha ha ha ha hūṃ!

Then, as soon as this was uttered, the entire assembly of beings in the three worlds of the triple realm was entered by the two hands of Vajrakrodha holding the terintiri mudrā, and it became firmly bound.
Then Vajrapāṇi, having caused [them] to enter according to the proper method and having taught the entire great maṇḍala in due order, [proceeded to] the new names of all the deities.
Having consecrated them with the vajra-jewel empowerments,
having bestowed the vajra symbols upon their hands,
and having consecrated them with the vajra-name empowerments,

He established them in the service of all Tathāgatas for the benefit of sentient beings. Then, the activity of the lords of the entire triple world occurs as follows: for Maheśvara, there is Krodhavajra;
To Nārāyaṇa, the Māyā-vajra; to Sanatkumāra, the Vajra-ghaṇṭā;
to Brahmā, the Mauna-vajra.
"To Indra, [he gave] Vajrāyudha"—
thus they were consecrated as the kings of the vidyās.
Then he bestowed them upon all the lords of the gods who roam the intermediate space.
Namely: for Amṛtakuṇḍala, Vajrakuṇḍalin; for Indu, Vajraprabha;
for Mahādaṇḍāgra, Vajradaṇḍa.
To Piṅgala he gave Vajrapiṅgala; having thus taken them up, they were consecrated as the Vajra-krodhas.
Then he bestowed them upon all the lords of the gods who roam through the sky.
Namely: Vajraśauṇḍā for Madhumattā, Vajramālā for Madhukarā,
and Vajravaśī for Jayā.
"Jayāvaha, Vijayavajra," and so forth— these were consecrated as the lords of the Gaṇas.
Then he bestowed [the leadership] upon all the terrestrial lords of the gods.
Namely: for Kośapāla, a thunderbolt-mace;
for Vāyu, a thunderbolt-wind;
for Agni, a thunderbolt-fire.
Vajrabhairava was consecrated as the messenger for Kubera; these and others were thus consecrated as messengers. Then he bestowed them upon all the gods who are lords of the netherworld (pātāla).
Namely: Vajrāṅkuśa for Varāha,
Vajrakāla for Yama,
and Vajravināyaka for Pṛthvīcūlika.
Varuṇa was consecrated as Nāgavajra; these and others were thus consecrated as ceṭakas.

Then, having consecrated the Śaiva goddesses as sovereigns of the three worlds with the vajra-jewel consecration, and having empowered them with vajras from their own insignia, [he established new names for them].
Having consecrated him with the Vajra-name empowerment,
he established him in the service of all Tathāgatas for the benefit of sentient beings;
namely, Krodhavajrāgni for Umā.
To Rukmiṇī, Vajrasauvarṇī; to Ṣaṣṭhī, Vajrakaumārī; to Brahmāṇī, Vajraśānti.
"Indrāṇī’s is the Vajramuṣṭi," and so forth; thus they were consecrated as the Vajrarājñīs.
Then he bestowed [the empowerments] upon all the Mothers who roam the intermediate space.
Namely: for Amṛtā, Vajrāmṛtā; for Rohiṇī, Vajrakānti;
for Daṇḍahāriṇī, Daṇḍavajrāgrā.

Vajramekhalā was consecrated as the destroyer of those who have taken birth, and others such as these were consecrated as the Vajra-krodhinīs (Vajra Wrathful Goddesses). Then he bestowed [the consecration] upon all the Mothers who move through the sky (Khecarīs).
Namely: Vajravilayā for killing,
Vajrāśanā for eating,
and Vajravasanā for clothing.
For the sake of pleasure, Vajravaśā and others were consecrated as courtesans;
thereafter, he bestowed [the office] upon all the Mothers who roam the earth.
Namely: Vajradūtī for Śivā, Vegavajriṇī for Vāyavī,
and Vajrajvālā for Āgneyī.
To Kuberī he gave Vajravikaṭā; thus were these and others consecrated as Vajradūtīs.
Then he bestowed them upon all the Mothers who dwell in the netherworld (pātāla).
To Vārāhī, Vajramukhī; to Cāmuṇḍā, Vajrakālī; to Chinnanāsā, Vajrapūtanā.
Vajramakarī for Vāruṇī— these and others were consecrated as the Vajraceṭīs.

Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having brought to fulfillment the Buddha-knowledges of all those who had entered therein, and having instructed them in the binding of all mudrās, bestowed upon them the Vajra-samayas with this heart-mantra of oath:
This vajra is the great vajra empowered by all the Buddhas;
through the transgression of the samaya, it shall swiftly reduce one's kinsmen to ashes.
Oṃ hana samaya hūṃ phaṭ!
Then he bestowed the mudrā for seizing the heart.
One who contemplates the accomplishment of their purpose should form the double vajra-mudrā, bind the two index fingers like hooks, and perform the circling and counter-circling. // 1 //
You must stand before him for the accomplishment of your purpose;
for this may be the moment that brings about the loss of your lives.
Having made the vajra-bind firm and well-restrained with the tips [of the fingers] bent, one should join the pair of thumbs and press them against the pair of middle fingers. (3)
This is your pledge; may it destroy anyone who should transgress it—the bond of the Samayamudrā of the Vajra-Vidyādhara. 4.
The binding of the little fingers is that of the two Vajra-mudrās; having turned them so that the tips of the fingers are tucked behind, they rest upon the head. (5)
This is the samaya of the Great Being, the binding of the Vajra-Vidyadhara;
whoever looks upon him with wrath should likewise remain before him.
Having firmly bound the vajra-protection, one should press the vajra-bind; for this is the samaya of the terrestrial spirits, the protector of all sentient beings. // 7 //
But whoever, filled with wrath, should bind [an enemy] for the sake of protection—whichever being it may be—one must stand behind that being for its defense. (8)
Having formed the double vajra-mudrā, with the tips of the left [hands] pressed together, one should perform the twisting and unwinding motion and snap the little fingers. // 9 //
"If he should be overcome by anger, you must employ the *samaya* [oath]; you all must stand before him for the sake of all supreme accomplishments. Thus [it is said]. (10)
Having knotted the ring fingers firmly with the vajra-bind, one should encircle the vajra-mudrā formed by the tips of the middle fingers and thumbs. // 11 //
Having turned [the hand] over and placed it upon the forehead, whoever should summon [him], one must always remain before him, provided that he preserves his life. (12) Thus.
Now, these are the heart-mantras for grasping the pledge (samaya) of these seals (mudrā) that captivate the hearts of the entire triple world:
Oṃ valitodvalita vajrākarṣaya hūṃ jjaḥ.
The heart mantra for summoning the deities with the Vajravalita mudrā:
HŪṂ VAJRĀGRA PĪḌAYA SAMAYA HŪṂ.
Of those who move through the atmosphere.
Oṃ vajramālāgra vaṃ.
For those who wear garlands:
Oṃ vajrabandha haṃ.
For those who move upon the earth: Oṃ vajra pātāla bhañja bhañja hūṃ phaṭ!
To those dwelling in the netherworld:
Oṃ Heruka Vajra Samaya, you who shatter the seal of all the wicked, hūṃ phaṭ!
"Of all the Mothers."
Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, I have been consecrated by all the Tathāgatas as the Subduer of the Wicked.
Therefore, please grant me your command: how should I proceed regarding these bondages of all the wicked maṇḍalas?"
Then the Blessed One, having heard this, spoke as follows:
Oṃ vajra suṃbha niḥsuṃbha hūṃ phaṭ.

Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, for the sake of protecting all sentient beings, spoke this heart-mantra for summoning all maṇḍalas: Oṃ vajra, summon the samayas of all maṇḍalas; O Vajradhara, do not transgress the truth! Hūṃ phaṭ!
The two vajra-hooks are rotated at the heart;
the two outer hooks perform the supreme summoning of the external maṇḍala.
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the maṇḍalas from every direction surrounded and took their positions on the summit of Mount Sumeru.
Then the Blessed One, Vajrapāṇi, having summoned those who were arranged in all the maṇḍalas, spoke thus:
"O sirs, undertake the observance of the samaya of abstaining from taking life."
Thus it was said.
Then those outer maṇḍala samaya-beings addressed the Blessed One:
"O Blessed One, we are meat-eaters; seeing living beings, we sustain our lives by taking away their vital essence."
“Therefore, may the Blessed One command how we are to live.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this to the wicked Vajrakrodha:
“Oṃ! Wicked Vajrakrodha, strike, burn, cook, destroy, scatter! Smash, smash all the maṇḍalas of the wicked samaya-seals! Crush, crush! Devour, devour the mantras of others! Vajra!”
Samaya hūṃ phaṭ.
With the fingers of the Vajra-krodha [mudrā] properly interlaced and the nails joined, one should firmly join them at the tips; this is the mudrā that destroys the wicked. Thus it is said.
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the mandalas of the wicked gathered together and were destroyed and scattered in their multitudes;
the binding of their pledge-mudrās (samayamudrā) burst apart.
And those wicked beings of the pledge, being burned and cooked, let out great cries of lamentation reaching to the very depths of the Mahāraurava hell.
Joining their palms toward where the Blessed One Mahāvajradhara was, they spoke thus:
“Protect us, Blessed One,
so that we do not abandon our lives!”
Then Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Blessed One in this way:
"Command me, Blessed One, how I am to proceed against these wicked maṇḍalas.
Then the Blessed One spoke this: Oṃ niṣumbha hana daha paca gṛhṇa bandha huṃ phaṭ!

Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this Vajra-Cruel-Anger mantra: Oṃ, Great Vajra-Cruel-Anger! Strike down all evil maṇḍalas; destroy all evil samayas; scatter, shatter, burst asunder, and break all evil samaya-seals and bonds!
Seize! Strike! Burn! Cook all wicked beings who have violated the samaya! Vajrasamaya hūṃ phaṭ!
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the mandalas of the seals of the wicked samayas once again became unified and fell into the great ocean.

Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Blessed One in this way: “I have been requested by the Blessed One to subdue all malevolent beings; how, then, should I proceed against these ḍākinīs, grahas, and all other seizing spirits?”
Then the Blessed One spoke this: Oṃ hana hana vajra huṃ phaṭ!
Then the great bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again spoke this heart-mantra for summoning all the wicked grahas, such as the ḍākinīs: OṂ VAJRĀKARṢAYA ŚĪGHRAṂ SARVADUṢṬAGRAHĀN VAJRADHARASATYENA HUṂ JAḤ.
Then, as soon as this was spoken, the ḍākinīs and all other malevolent grahas gathered around the summit of Mount Sumeru and remained there, forming a circle on the outside.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having summoned those ḍākinīs and all the malevolent grahas, spoke thus:
"Observe, sirs, the vow of the samaya precept regarding abstinence from taking life;
lest I consume your families with my vajra, blazing, aflame, and become a single mass of fire."
Then those ḍākinīs and all the other malevolent grahas joined their palms toward where the Blessed One was and addressed the Blessed One:
“O Blessed One, we are eaters of flesh;
therefore, please command us how we should proceed.”

Then the Blessed One spoke thus to Vajrapāṇi: "Vajrapāṇi, proceed to generate great compassion for all these beings and grant them the means [of deliverance]. Then Vajrapāṇi, the Great Compassionate One, recited this Heart-Mantra of the Knowledge-Seal for discerning the signs of death for all sentient beings: Oṃ vajra pratigṛhṇa hṛdayam ākarṣaya; if this being is about to die because of being a meat-eater, [then draw forth their heart].
May his heart emerge! Samaya huṃ jjaḥ!
Now follows the binding of its mudrā: having formed the vajra-bind with both arms at the heart of a friend, one should pull up one's own armpits with the tips of the vajra-fingers. Thus it is said.
"By means of this mudrā, you must extract the hearts of all sentient beings and consume them.
Then those ḍākinīs and others, along with all the malevolent grahas, let out "hulu-hulu" roars and departed for their own abodes.

Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Blessed One in this way: “I have been empowered by all the Blessed Tathāgatas as the subduer of all the wicked. Therefore, may the Blessed One command me: what shall I do regarding diseases such as fevers?”
Then the Blessed One said: Oṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi uttered the heart-mantra for summoning all fevers and the like: Oṃ vajra samayānaya sarvaduṣṭajvarādīn nāśayaṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the fevers and other afflictions surrounded Mount Sumeru from the outside and took their positions upon its summit.
Then Vajrapāṇi, having summoned those fevers and others, spoke thus:
"O worthy ones, enter into the vow of restraint by undertaking the training in abstaining from harming sentient beings."
Then they spoke thus:
“Blessed One, we make our living by abducting two beings.
Therefore, it would be well if the Blessed One would command us: how should we proceed?”
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi uttered this heart-mantra of the seal of knowledge for the purification of one’s own karma: *oṃ vajrakarma viśodhaya sarvāvaraṇāni buddhasatyena samaya hūṃ*.
Now follows the binding of its seal:
having made the vajra-añjali firm, the two index fingers are bent inward.
"With the big toes firmly bound together and restrained, it removes all evil. Thus it is said.
"Whosoever is afflicted by any disease such as fever, if you show this mudrā through ritual action,
you must depart from him; lest there be the destruction of your lives."
Then, having said, "So be it," they departed.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke thus to all the Tathāgatas:
“I have been sent forth from my own heart by the Blessed Ones for the sake of purifying all obscurations, hindrances, and karmic veils.
Therefore, may the Blessed Ones command me: how should these hells and all other states of woe be treated?”
The Blessed One said: Oṃ kṣapaya vajra svāhā.

Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this heart-mantra for drawing forth [beings] from the entire cycle of rebirths in the miserable states, such as Raurava: Oṃ sarvāpāyakarṣaṇa viśodhana vajrasamaya hūṃ phaṭ.
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the abodes of the lower realms, beginning with Raurava and Mahāraurava, surrounded and remained outside upon the summit of Mount Sumeru.

Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi summoned all those sentient beings who had fallen into the states of the lower realms and spoke to them thus: "Take hold, friends, from this peril of not having gone for refuge to the Three Jewels!"
“We, too, go for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, and to you.
Then Vajrapāṇi uttered the heart-mantra that shatters all miserable realms: *Oṃ vajrapāṇi visphoṭaya sarvāpāyabandhanāni pramokṣaya sarvasattvān sarvāpāyagatibhyaḥ sarvatathāgatavajrasamaya traṭ*.
Now follows the binding of its mudrā:
having made the vajra-bind firm, with the two middle fingers joined together and the four remaining fingers attached to the mouth [of the hands], it is proclaimed as "Pāpasphoṭā."
Then all those sentient beings dwelling within the cycle of the three lower realms, having seen this mudrā from the presence of Vajrapāṇi,
passed away from all miserable destinies and were reborn at the feet of the Blessed One Vairocana.
"And those [beings] have fallen into the great ocean of the miserable realms (*apāya*).
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Blessed One as follows:

"O Blessed One, for the sake of protecting the realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder, and for the purpose of experiencing all benefit and happiness, until the attainment of the fruit of the supreme siddhi of all Tathāgatas, [I shall practice] the Vajra of the Siddhi of all Tathāgatas."
He was empowered by all the Tathāgatas.
Then he said, “Therefore, may the Blessed Ones, all the Tathāgatas, please give me their command: what shall I do for these human beings?
Then all the Tathāgatas, having gathered together once more, spoke this: “Oṃ Vajrapāṇi, lead [them] into the great maṇḍala!”
Repel all the wicked and fierce ones;
liberate them from their evils; purify and destroy those who have fallen into wrong views—ha ha ha ha hūṃ!
Then Vajrapāṇi, having heard the command of all the Tathāgatas,

for the sake of protecting the realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder, for the sake of the supreme accomplishment of all benefit and happiness, and as a cause for attaining the fruit of the knowledge and supernormal powers of all the Tathāgatas, spoke this great maṇḍala called Trilokavijaya, which is the embodiment of the great vajra-samaya of all the Tathāgatas.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme great maṇḍala,
which resembles the Vajradhātu and is the highest bestower of all accomplishments.
The pledge named Trilokavijaya, born of the Vajra, which sets in motion the enlightenment of the Buddhas and destroys all that is evil. // 2 //
There, one should mark out the lines with this mantra: Oṃ vajrasamaya sūtraṃ mātikrama.
It is square, with four gates, adorned with four archways, provided with four boundary lines, and beautifully decorated with silk garlands. // 1 //
At all the corners of the mandala and at the junctions of the gates and projections, one should trace the outer mandala with the vajra-jewels of one's own mind. // 2 //
Within that, the wise one [should construct] a square [palace], adorned with vajra-jewels, having four gates, eight pillars, and archways. // 3 //
Upon those [pillars] situated at the tips of the vajra-columns, which are adorned with five mandalas,
one should lay out the lines for the mandala there and fill it with colors.
In that regard, this is the mantra for the colored powders: Oṃ vajracitra samaya hūṃ.
Then, standing in the center and being composed, the Vajrācārya should mentally open the four vajra-doors.
In this regard, the mantra for opening the door is: Oṃ vajrodghāṭaya samaya praveśaya hūṃ.
One should install an image of the Buddha in a vessel made of gold, silver, or well-painted clay, or in a four-cornered brick receptacle.
In this regard, this is the heart-mantra for summoning all Tathāgatas:
Oṃ vajra jvālāgnipradīptākarṣaya sarvatathāgatān mahāvajra samaya hūṃ jaḥ.
One should place a vajra before the Buddha in the midst of flames;
likewise, one should draw a jewel, a lotus, and the double-vajra (viśvāyudha) in the midst of the flames.
Now, the placement-heart mantras for these Vajra-samaya-mudrās are as follows:
HŪṂ SATTVAVAJRA JVĀLĀMĀLA HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Oṃ ratnavajra jvālāmāla hūṃ traḥ.
Oṃ dharmavajra jvālāmāla hūṃ hrīḥ.
HŪṂ KARMAVAJRA JVĀLĀMĀLA HŪṂ HAḤ //
Having emerged with vajra-velocity in that manner before the Buddha,
the wise one should duly draw the maṇḍala of Vajrahuṃkāra.
In this regard, the heart-mantra of Vajravega is as follows: oṃ vajravegākrama hūṃ.
Thus, having stepped upon the thread in all mandalas, such as the Vajradhātu and others,
one should proceed in every direction.
Now, its mudrā is as follows: Having raised the mind from the line, or likewise from the vajra-thread, they enter in succession; he does not stray from the samaya. // 1 //
There, in the center, one should depict the Great Being Vajrapāṇi, possessing the luster of a great blue lotus, who holds the vajra and the syllable HŪṂ. // 2 //
His face is slightly terrifying with bared fangs, his countenance laughing with wrath;
he stands in the pratyālīḍha posture, treading upon [the enemy], with a radiance filled with garlands of flames. (3)
Maheśvara should be depicted with his left foot stepped upon by him [the practitioner], while his right foot should be drawn resting upon the breast of Umā. 4.
There, his heart-mantra is *hūṃ*.
On all its sides, one should place the Vajra-Wrathful Ones,
who have terrifying fangs of anger and whose radiance is filled with garlands of flames.
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows:
[HŪṂ].
Oṃ vajrasattvakrodha hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, Vajra-anger, summon! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajrakāma krodha rāgāya hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, Vajra-joyous wrathful one, well done, well done! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Having proceeded with vajra-impetus to the second supreme mandala,
one should there draw the vajra-consecration surrounded by the wrathful deities.
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows:
*traḥ*.
Oṃ, Vajra-bhṛkuṭi, wrathful one, remove, remove! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, Vajrasūrya, you who possess a great garland of flames, wrathful one, cause all to blaze! Hūṃ Phaṭ!
Oṃ vajra-krodha-ketu dehi hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajrāṭṭahāsa krodha haḥ haḥ haḥ haḥ hūṃ phaṭ!
Having advanced with vajra-impetus to the third circle, which is the most excellent,
one should draw Vajrasena, surrounded by the great-souled wrathful deities.
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows: Hrīḥ.
Oṃ vajradharma krodha, destroy and purify! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, O Vajra-sharp Wrathful One, cut, cut! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, O Vajra-cause wrathful one, enter, cause [them] to enter the maṇḍala; all, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajrakrodha, speak, speak! Vada vada hūṃ phaṭ!
Having entered with vajra-velocity the four-cornered, supreme mandala,
one should draw the vajra-possession surrounded by the hosts of vajra-wrathful deities.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Aḥ.
Oṃ Vajrakarma.
Oṃ vajra armor, wrathful one, protect, protect, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajrayakṣa krodha khāda khāda hūṃ phaṭ!
Hūṃ! O Vajra-wrath Fist, accomplish the commitment! Hūṃ Phaṭ!
In the corners of the mandala, according to the proper sequence,
one should draw the secret worship by means of the application of the Vajradhātu.
Now, their heart mudrās are as follows:
Oṃ vajralāsye rāgaya hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ vajramāle abhiṣiñca hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajragīte gāda gāda hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, Vajra-dancer, bring [him] under control! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Having emerged with the force of a vajra into the supreme outer maṇḍala,
one should establish the four offering goddesses there in the corners.
Now, their heart-seals (hṛdayamudrā) are as follows:
Oṃ vajradhūpapūjāspharaṇasamaye hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, at the time of the radiation of the vajra-flower offering, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, at the time of the radiation of the vajra-light offering, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, at the time of the radiation of the vajra fragrance offering, hūṃ phaṭ!
The goads and so forth should be placed in the four middle sections of the doors;
however, the outer Vajra families are situated within the outer mandala.
Now, their heart mudrās are as follows:
Oṃ vajrāṅkuśa mahākrodha ākarṣaya sarvasamayān hūṃ jjaḥ.
Oṃ, Vajrapāśa, Great Wrathful One, cause all commitments to enter! Hūṃ hūṃ!
Oṃ, Vajrasphoṭa, great wrathful one, bind, bind all samayas! Hūṃ vaṃ!
Oṃ, vajra-entrance! Great wrathful one, cause all samayas to enter! Hūṃ Aḥ!
Now, regarding the detailed procedure for entry into this great maṇḍala of Trilokavijaya:
first of all, the Vajrācārya himself, having bound the *vajrakodhaterintiri* mudrā, should enter.

Having entered, one should address all the Tathāgatas: "O Blessed Tathāgatas, I shall enter the power of wrath; I shall subdue those who are to be subdued and gather in those who are to be gathered in. Therefore, may the Blessed Ones grant me their command."
Thinking, "How should I proceed?",
he should duly place the Vajrakrodha-terintiri mudrā at his own heart,
and perform the ritual actions with the vajra-hook and other implements.

Furthermore, one should bind all the samaya-mudrās; then all [the deities] manifest their presence. Then, having performed the fourfold secret worship as well as with incense and so forth, [one should proceed].

Then the Vajra-Ācārya himself, having bound the Vajra-Krodha-Tirintiri mudrā, should cause the Vajra-disciple to enter by this rite and bind it upon the disciple with this heart-mantra: Oṃ gṛṇha vajra samaya huṃ vaṃ.

Then, having wrapped his head with a blue turban over an inner garment of blue cloth, and having covered his face with a blue-red cloth, he should cause him to enter with this mantra: *oṃ vajra samayaṃ praviśāmi*.
Then, having caused him to enter by means of the Vajrāveśa-samayamudrā, one should produce possession within him with this heart-mantra: *vajrāveśa aḥ*.
Then he enters [into that state].
By means of that entry, he is empowered by all the Tathāgatas;
and he knows everything—past, future, and present—in the mere blink of an eye.
He becomes invulnerable to all sentient beings and unassailable;
by the syllable *huṃ*, he becomes capable of both subduing and favoring all sentient beings;
and Vajrapāṇi constantly accomplishes all his tasks for him.
Then he should give the heart-mantra of the oath.
Then, having properly released the binding of the face,
he should show the great maṇḍala.
Merely by seeing the maṇḍala, one is liberated from all sins and becomes capable of conquering the entire triple world.
And by means of the syllable *huṃ*, one becomes able to attract, cause to enter, bind, subjugate, and strike down all the gods, beginning with Mahādeva.
And through the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas, the great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, who is ever-unfailing, bestows his own accomplishments.
Then, having consecrated him with the vajra-consecration, his own sharp vajra-emblem should be placed in his two hands according to the rule with this mantra: *oṃ vajrapāṇi vajrakarmakaro bhava*.
Then one should bestow the consecration of the Vajra-name with this mantra:
*oṃ vajrakrodha tvām abhiṣiñcāmi vajranāmābhiṣekataḥ hevajra nāma*.
Therefore, whatever name one may give [to a child], the word "he" (he-śabda) should be used for that [name].
Then one should generate the gnoses:
having visualized the vajra-form in the heart, with a radiance like a mass of hair, one should cause the entire world to enter [into it] through the meditative absorption of Vajrakrodha. // 1 //
Having likewise drawn the Vajraratna on the forehead, one should bring all sentient beings under control through the meditative absorption of Vajrakrodha. // 2 //
Placing the vajra-lotus at his throat, with a radiance filled with garlands of flames, he shall destroy all sentient beings through the meditative absorption of Vajrakrodha. // 3 //
Having established the Satvavajra upon the head with its light filled with flames, one should protect this entire world through the meditative absorption of Vajrakrodha. // 4 //
Now, the heart mantras of these wisdom-consorts (jñānamudrā) are as follows:
HŪṂ SATVA VAJRA KRODHĀVIŚA AḤ.
HO RATNA [VAJRAKRODHA] TRAḤ //
Hūṃ! O Dharma-Vajra-Krodha, phaṭ!
Haṃ! O Vajrakrodha, protect my karma!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrā for summoning the deities and others:
having drawn a vajrāṅkuśa (vajra-hook) marked with the syllable HŪṂ on a palm-leaf.
If one moves a finger while enraged, it is the supreme method for summoning the gods. // 1 //
Having drawn a vajra-hook from the center of the sole of one's own foot, and having stepped upon the linga with that very [hook], one will certainly draw in the gods. // 2 //
Having drawn a vajra-hook, when one's own penis has arisen,
by moving it, one shall summon all women, beginning with Umā.
Having drawn a vajra-hook at the anus and likewise at the private parts, whichever deity one thus subjugates, its supreme summoning is accomplished. // 4 //
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ vajra krodhāgrākarṣaya hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ vajra-kramāṅkuśa-krodha ākarṣaya hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajra-krodha-daṇḍāgra ākarṣaya hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, you who sit upon the vajra-anger, come! I summon you; O Vajra, remember your samaya! Hūṃ Phaṭ!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the fourfold mudrās:

"Having assumed the pratyālīḍha stance through the application of the vajra-entrance, one may cause the entire world to enter [into the state of possession] in an instant by means of the mere syllable *hūṃ*. (1)
With adamantine speech, one should correctly utter the heart-mantra of all Buddhas, joined with four *huṃ*s; it will certainly summon everything. (2)
Through the meditative absorption of the Vajra Wrathful One, by means of the supreme gaze of the Vajra Wrathful One, one may slay the entire world through the yoga of the Vajra Hūṃkāra. // 3 //
One should armor one’s own body or that of another with the mind; by means of the application of the great armor, one should protect this entire world. Thus [ends verse 4].
Now, their heart mantras are as follows:
OṂ VAJRA KRODHA KĀYĀVEŚAYA HŪṂ AḤ.
Oṃ vajra vidyottama mahākrodha ānaya ho bhagavan vajra hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajra-krodha-dṛṣṭi! Strike, burn, cook, destroy! With the syllable *huṃ*, cause them to fall! Vajra-samaya *huṃ phaṭ*!
Oṃ! Firm mind, vajra armor, wrathful one, protect! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the seal that seals all sentient beings:
"By means of the meditative absorption of Vajrakrodha, whomever one embraces, that person becomes sealed by the recitation of Vajra-hūṃkāra. (1)
Speaking with a loud voice, one should utter "ṬṬAKKI HŪṂ PHAṬ" once;
whoever [is spoken to] while one is angry shall be struck by a blazing vajra. // 2 //
One should indeed gaze with the vajra-vision through the samādhi of the Vajra Wrath;
whichever sentient being [is thus gazed upon], that very one shall meet with death. // 3 //
Thinking "I shall slay with the mind," one should visualize a vajra at the heart;
by the syllable *hūṃ* alone, one personally seals all [beings] from every side. Thus, [it is said]. (4)
Whichever sentient being seals with whichever mind, having entreated [the deity] with these mudrās, one should accomplish all activities. Thus [it is said]. //5//
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows:
*Ṭakki aḥ*.
Ṭakki Jjaḥ!
Ṭakki hūṃ.
Ṭakki haṃ.
However, with each individual mudrā, one should employ four mudrā-hṛdayas for the four types of ritual actions.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the secret wrathful mudrā:
having embraced him with all one's limbs, one should apply the syllable *hūṃ* to him;
through the union of the two organs, his life shall perish. (1)
Kissing the lips while biting them with the teeth and employing the *huṃ* syllable, through the union of the two organs, the mouth of whomever [one performs this] shall fall off. // 2 //
He who employs the syllable *huṃ* while experiencing pleasure through the union of the two organs shall instead encounter suffering. (3)
Whoever should employ the syllable *huṃ* while pressing with all his limbs through the union of the two organs, his entire body shall fall [to the ground]. Thus, [verse 4].
Now, the heart-mantras for this are: HŪṂ AḤ.
Hūṃ Jjaḥ.
Hūṃ Hoḥ.
Hūṃ haṃ.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrās of the reality of the samaya of the Great Maṇḍala of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds.
Through the application of the Vajradhātu, one becomes possessed of the recollection of the Buddhas;
he who acts for the benefit of sentient beings shall attain Buddhahood. // 1 //
Having likewise drawn Maheśvara and Umā upon the ground, one should proceed in due order and meditate upon the sattva-mudrā according to the drawing. // 2 //
By merely binding this [mudrā], he becomes a conqueror of the three worlds;
his vidyā is swiftly perfected, and he becomes like Vajrahuṃkāra. // 3 //
Standing in the midst of a circle of flames according to the prescribed drawing, one should bind the mudrās of the beings with the vajras of body, speech, and mind. // 4 //
Now I shall explain their activity, the unsurpassed vajra-activity;
one who has attained perfection through the recollection of the Buddha will swiftly attain Buddhahood. // 5 //
Having bound the Trilokavijayā [mudrā], one becomes a conqueror of the three worlds; indeed, like Vajrahuṃkāra, one attains adamantine life and travels everywhere. // 6 //
Through the vajra initiation, she becomes a queen with sovereignty over the world and possesses the excellent Dharma;
as the great wrathful one of the Vajra of Action, she shall be the performer of vajra-activities. // 7 //
The Wrathful Being brings great firmness; one should summon with Krodhāṅkuśī. One should cause passion with Krodharāgā, while Sādhukrodhā bestows satisfaction. (8)
With Bhṛkuṭī one destroys everything; with Krodhasūryā, who possesses fierce radiance, one [destroys all]; Ketukrodhā takes away wealth, while Aṭṭahāsā causes death.
Through the Wrath of Dharma, one should seize dharmas; indeed, one should sever them with the Vajra of Wrath.
Through the Wrath of Cause, one should seize away sufferings; one should seize them away through speech by means of the language of wrath.
One should perform auspicious rites with Karmakrodhā, and protection with Rakṣā;
Krodhayakṣā shall devour the enemy, while Krodhamuṣṭi bestows the attainment of siddhis. Thus [ends verse 11].
Now follows the binding of the Vajrasamaya-mudrās: "Those mudrās arising from the two vajras are proclaimed as the foremost samayas;
I shall explain their binding, the unsurpassed binding of the wrathful ones. (1)
Having formed the *bāhuvajra* [mudrā] and bound the little fingers as hooks, with both index fingers threatening, it is called *Trilokavijayā*. (2)
Likewise, the *agryā* [finger] is bent at the tip due to contact with the mouth;
however, when both the *madhyā* and *agryā* are excluded, it is the *samotthamadhyapadmā*. Thus, [verse] 3.
The two index fingers are vajras, while the right one is bent into a hook; with that very [hook] she seizes the syllable *hūṃ*, and likewise she utters the word "well done" (*sādhu*). 4.
Her form has two peaks [at the ears] and a frown; at her heart is a solar mandala with its tip upward;
her arms are extended above her head, and she smiles with the tips of her threatening fingers. // 5 //
The right hand forms a fist with the index finger nails interlocked;
the middle and tip fingers are held straight, forming a wheel that extends outward from the mouth.
The *tarjanī* and middle fingers form a vajra; the neck is encircled by the *tarjanī*;
the great fangs are formed by the tips being extended further; and the tips are grasped by the vajra-fist. // 7 //

The mudrās of the unions of Vajralāsyā and the others are those very same [mudrās] when uttered with the syllable *huṃ*; furthermore, the dharma-mudrās are those same [mudrās] again when accompanied by the *huṃ* syllables. (8)
Now follow the Dharma-mudrās of the Vajra-samaya:
*huṃ* is for the Buddha-vajrin; *traḥ* is from Vajragarbha;
*hrīḥ* is for Vajrasena; and *aḥ* is for Vajraviśva. Thus it is said.
[From here on, the Dharma-mudrās are as follows in brief:
HŪṂ HEḤ TRĀṂ TAṂ, HI HĪḤ DEḤ HAḤ.
*Dhik khīḥ hūṃ graṃ, kṛ vaṃ dṛ aḥ!
May the Dharma-mudrās of the host of Vajra-krodhas be perfectly accomplished!* Thus it is said.
Then there are the Vajra-Samaya-Karma-Mudrās:
having formed two wrathful fists through the yoga of Vajra-Arrogance and so forth, the Karma-Mudrās are briefly taught in the Great Vajra Family. // 1 //
Whichever side of whichever mudrā corresponds to the ritual action, one should indeed employ that specific mudrā by encircling it in that very manner. // 2 //
The ritual procedure for all mudrās.
Now, here follows the binding of the common mudrās for the Great Maṇḍala of Trilokavijaya:
"The mudrā of Trilokavijaya belongs to the Vajrāgrasamaya;
