it bestows all accomplishments in an instant through the mantra of Vajrahuṃkāra. (1)
One should bind the two vajras, one above and one below, with the tips of the little fingers acting as hooks; this is the Samaya-aṅkuśa mudrā, which instantly attracts everything. // 2 //
Among all the supreme vidyās, Trilokavijayā is remembered as the slayer of everything and likewise the performer of all rites.
Having properly joined the two index fingers of the two vajras while well-composed, one should raise up all who are dead; this is known as the “Vajra Arise” mudrā. 4.
One should properly bind the two index fingers with the supreme vajra-bind; having rotated them, one should place them upon the crown of the head; this increases longevity and health. // 5 //
Having made the vajra-bind firm, with the thumbs joined together, the index fingers are firmly contracted and bent; this is the "drawing-in of the feet" [mudrā]. // 6 //
Having bound the Trilokavijayā [mudrā], whoever should step upon that person's form with his left foot— that being achieves accomplishment within half a month.
Having formed the pair of vajra-mudrās, one should strike them against each other;
indeed, one should strike whichever person’s body has been entered by [the deity]. // 8 //
Having formed the pair of vajra-mudrās, by binding one's own or another's armor with the two index fingers, protection becomes eternal. (9)
Having placed the vajra-bind at the soles and covering them with a mind full of wrath, one should firmly press the thumbs with the vajras; thus the great Vajra family will be accomplished. 10.
Having made the *sattvavajra* firm, with the two middle fingers grasped by the thumbs, one should seize the sharp-tipped *samaya* [pledge] from the vajra-face of the little fingers. 11.
Having formed the pair of vajra-mudrās with the tips of the fingers bent and bound together, by performing the movements of turning and un-turning, one effects the supreme summoning of the deities.

Having made the vajra-bind firm, with the tips [of the fingers] bent and well-restrained, one should join the pair of thumbs and press them in the middle by means of the space-fingers (the middle fingers). 13.
The middle of the little fingers of the two vajra-mudrās should be grasped from behind by the tips of the fingers; this is for the sky-goers. 14.
Having made the vajra-protection firm, one should press the vajra-bind; for this is the samaya of the terrestrial deities, which accomplishes all and is difficult to transgress. // 15 //
Having formed the pair of Vajra-mudrās, with the tips of the left [hands] pressed together and the final fingers snapped, this is the "Attracting by Falling" mudrā. 16.
The two ring fingers are firmly knotted with the vajra-bond; the middle finger and thumb form a vajra, which shatters evil mudrās. (17)
Having formed the two vajra-mudrās and placed them at the heart, one who is composed should press the krodha-muṣṭi; this destroys the outer maṇḍala. 18.
Grasping the left vajra-finger with the tip of the right hand bent, one who is thoroughly enraged should clap; this would cause even Mount Sumeru to fall. (19)
Grasping the left vajra-finger with the tip of the right hook,
one who is well-enraged shall draw in all the planetary spirits and bring them under control.
Having firmly applied the vajra-bind with both arms at the heart,
one should place the tips of the two vajras at one's own belly, while the kuśas remain at the heart.
With a mind full of wrath, one should press the base of the two thumbs with the tips of the index fingers; this is the supreme method for summoning fever. (22)
Having made the vajra-añjali firm, with the two index fingers [bent], and constrained by the well-joined thumbs, this is the mudrā that removes sins. // 23 //
Having formed the two index fingers into the Vajra-mudrā from between the two [hands], one should instantly lift them upward; this is the supreme Patitotkṣepaka. // 24 //
Having firmly established the vajra-bind, with the two middle fingers joined at their tips and the four outer fingers unattached, one shatters evil in an instant. // 25 //
Now follows the binding of the mudrās for the accomplishment of the maṇḍala of all the Tathāgatas:
Having first laid out the maṇḍala while holding the vajra-mudrā, one should subsequently hold the thread; this is remembered as the proper method of laying out the lines. (1)
Having joined the two vajra-mudrās with their tips well-connected, one should summon all the limbs [of the retinue] while gazing with a blazing look. // 2 //
"Having properly joined the two foremost fingers of the two vajras upward and held them firmly, one should open [them] while enraged; this is the supreme opening of the door. // 3 //

Now follows the accomplishment of all mudrās of the entire Vajra family: having assumed the pratyālīḍha posture and employing wrathful speech, one who is thoroughly enraged by the wrathful gaze shall accomplish all rites. Thus it is said.
The detailed ritual procedure for the Great Maṇḍala of Trilokavijaya, from the *Sarvatathāgatavajrasamaya*, the Great Kalparāja, is completed.
The Emanation of Deities from Samādhi:

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Empowerment Arising from the Vajra-dhāraṇī Samaya," and spoke this supreme personal vidyā: OṂ SARVAVAJRIṆI VAJRAMĀTE ĀNAYA SARVA VAJRASATYENA HŪṂ JJAḤ.

Then, as soon as this was spoken, from the heart of Vajrapāṇi, that very Blessed One Vajrapāṇi— having become deities who were the Vajra Wrath Samaya-mudrās, possessing bodies identical to Vajrapāṇi and containing flames all around— emerged and,
having accomplished the purposes of all the Tathāgatas in all the world-systems, [remained].

In order to conceal the secret consort-hood of the Blessed One Vajrasattva, having become the reflected images of the seals (*mudrā*) of the body, speech, and mind of vajra, and having come to rest upon the moon-disc through the yoga of the great maṇḍala of Bhagavān Vairocana’s *Trilokavijaya*, they uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*):
"O, how wonderful! The secret gnosis of all Buddhas is unsurpassed!"
For the sake of the Tathāgata’s happiness, they even take on the state of being his wife.
Hrīḥ.
The delineation of the maṇḍala:
Then Vajrapāṇi again spoke the name of the secret vajra-samaya of the maṇḍala of the mudrās of the samaya of his own family.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme vajra-maṇḍala.
Resembling the Vajra Realm, it is known as the Secret Wrath. // 1 //
One should delineate the entire maṇḍala by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala;
one should install the secret mudrās among those situated within the five maṇḍalas. // 2 //
Within this vajra-maṇḍala, one should place the image of the Buddha;
the wise one should depict the wrathful samayas of the Buddha exactly as they are. // 3 //
Having emerged with the force of a vajra, one should draw the mandala of Vajrapāṇi;
there, in the center, one should depict a transverse trident-vajra firmly established. 4.
Within the midst of the flames, one should draw his [mandala] in due order as follows:
a vajra, a vajrāṅkuśa, an arrow, and likewise Tuṣṭi.
Having entered by means of Vajravega, one should likewise draw the second supreme maṇḍala, the Vajraratna, established in the center of the wheel. // 6 //
In the center of Vajrabhṛkuṭī, one should likewise draw Vajrasūrya and the Banner;
likewise, one should draw rows of teeth made of vajras on its sides. (7)
Having entered with vajra-impetus into the third supreme mandala, one should draw a divine vajra-lotus situated in the center of the lotus. // 8 //
In the midst of the flames, one should draw a lotus, a sword, and likewise a wheel;
and Vajrajihvā according to the rule, on all her sides.
Having entered with the force of a vajra into the fourth, most excellent mandala,
one should draw a vajra upon the horizontal vajra, surrounded by vajras of great radiance.

On all its sides, one should draw the universal vajra (viśvavajra), the excellent armor (sukavaca), the vajra-tusk (vajradaṃṣṭra), and the vajra-fist (vajramuṣṭi), all possessing a radiance filled with every kind of flame.
One should draw this arrangement correctly in the outer corners;
hereafter, I shall explain the vidyās of the mudrās in brief.
[Siḥ]
Oṃ vajrakrodhasamaye siḥ.
Oṃ vajra-roṣāṅkuśi ānaya sarva siḥ.
Oṃ, O Vajra-anger, O Vajra of desire, bring [them] under my control! Hi siḥ!
Oṃ vajratuṣṭikrodhe toṣya sarvāṇi siḥ.
In the Vajrasiṃhāramaṇḍala:
Jiḥ.
Oṃ, O wrathful Vajrabhṛkuṭī, take away all aims! Jiḥ!
Oṃ, O Vajra-flame-garland-radiance, Great Wrathful Fire, blaze forth against all who are hostile! Jiḥ!
Oṃ, O Great Wrathful One with the Vajra Banner and Armlet, grant me everything! Jiḥ!
Oṃ, O Vajra-laugh, laugh! Laugh with the loud, terrifying laughter! [Slay, jiḥ!]
In the Vajra-jihvākāra-maṇḍala.
Diḥ.
Oṃ vajraśuddhakrodhe, strike, slay the wicked, twice!
Oṃ, O Vajra-sharp Wrathful One, cut all [obstacles] twice with the vajra-sheath!
Oṃ, O Great Wrathful One of the Vajra Cause, enter the wheel; cause all to enter! Diḥ!
Oṃ, O Vajra-tongue, speaker of the great wrathful one, release your speech twice!
In the Vajra-Ḍiṃkāra maṇḍala: NHIḤ.
Oṃ, O you who possess the vajra of action in all mouths, O great wrathful one, perform [this] for all: nhīḥ!
Oṃ vajrakavacakrodhe rakṣa māṃ nhīḥ.
Oṃ, O Vajra-Caṇḍakrodha, Great Yakṣiṇī, you with the terrifyingly fierce fangs of a vajra, terrify [them]! NHIḤ!
Oṃ vajrakrodhe muṣṭibandha nhiḥ.
In the *vajra-hīṃ* maṇḍala,
thereupon, in the corner maṇḍalas, there are the heart-mantras of the secret worship vidyās of Vajranṛtya:
*vajra hūṃ rkhne*.
Vajra hūṃ ghūṃ.
Vajra hūṃ rte.
Vajra hūṃ steṃ.
In the outer corners, there are heart-mantras for the offering of musical instruments:
VAJRA TĪ TE.
Vajra ṭaṃ ṭaḥ!
Vajra dhā dhū.
Vajra dhau dhaḥ.
The heart-mantras for the worship of the gatekeepers are as follows:
Vajra jaḥ jjaḥ.
Vajra hūṃ hūṃ.
Vajra vaṃ vaṃ.
Vajra aḥ aḥ.
The initiation into the maṇḍala:
Now follows the detailed procedure for entry into this secret maṇḍala of the Vajra family.
Therein, first of all, one should enter by means of the procedure for entry into the great maṇḍala of Trailokyavijaya.
One should perform an offering of dance for the purpose of worshipping Vajradhara by means of the Vajra-secret, Vajra-family, Samaya, Pratimudrā, Upamudrā, and Jñāna-mudrās.
In this regard, there is this knowledge of the mudrās for the offering of dance, counter-dance, secondary dance, and wisdom-dance.
Therein, at the very beginning, having sung the heart-mantra of the Vajradhātu-collection with a Vajra-song and performed an offering of praise to all the Tathāgatas, one should proceed.

The Vajrācārya should cause the Satvavajrī mudrā to burst open; then they enter by means of the mudrās through which they had previously entered. By means of the application of the Vajra Dance, the two fingers of the Vajra-Krodha [are joined].
One should, however, bind the Vajra-hūṃkāra mudrā at the heart. // 1 //
Then, by means of the ritual of dance and with the Vajra-anger-hook, one should summon all the Buddhas and cast forth the vajra-arrows. // 2 //
One should accomplish [the rite] with Vajratuṣṭi by encircling it with the Vajra-arrow; having released the mudrā, one should bind it again according to the ritual procedure with the Tālī. // 3 //
By this ritual of worship, one should satisfy Vajrapāṇi;
being satisfied and pleased, he shall accomplish all tasks in an instant. (4)
In this regard, these are the *nṛtyahṛdaya* mantras:
*Siddhya vajra*.
Bring the vajra!
Rāgaya vajra.
Excellent, O Vajra!
Then, the offering of the counter-dance should be performed.
Dancing in that same manner, one should grasp the left [hand] with the right fist, turn it over at the forehead, and place the tips [of the fingers] against the face. (1)
In the same way, while dancing, one should summon Sūryā;
raising Vajraketu, one should laugh with the vajra-attahāsa laughter. (2)
By this ritual of worship, having brought under one's control kings and all human beings through power, great splendor, generosity, and hope, one should satisfy them.
In this regard, these are the heart-mantras of the counter-seals:
ĀHI VAJRA.
Enkindle, O Vajra!
Give, O Vajra!
Hāsa hāsa vajra.
In the same manner, having released the dance, one should place the fingertips— joined like closed buds— at the heart and bow with the chest trembling.
In that very manner, one should indeed sever the obstructors with the Vajra-sheath, and whirl the circle of the maṇḍala with the rotation of a firebrand. // 2 //
Indeed, singing with the vajra-voice, one should worship Vajrapāṇi;
by this ritual of worship, everything becomes eternal. // 3 //
In this regard, these are the heart-mantras of the secondary seals (upamudrā).
O Vajra, [protect] desire!
Cut through, O Vajra!
Whirl the vajra!
Speak, O Vajra!
The fingers of the Vajra-krodha [mudrā] are properly joined with their faces turned upward;
having rotated them, the index fingers are positioned at the face upon the uṣṇīṣa. // 1 //
By means of the application of vajra-activity, while displaying the supreme maṇḍala of all deeds through the ritual of dance, one should cause it to dissolve into the heart. // 2 //
In the same way, one should perform the protection with the vajra through the ritual of dance;
having formed the vajra-fangs, one should press them together with the vajra-fist. // 3 //
By this ritual procedure of worship, one shall become capable of performing all activities;
having performed the fourfold worship, one should release the mudrā according to the prescribed rule. Thus [ends verse 4].
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
*Nṛtya vajra*.
Protect, O Vajra!
Eat, O Vajra!
Bind with the vajra!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the Secret Mudrā of Wrath:
"Grasping a vajra with both hands, one with a mind full of anger should snap it; by the name of whomever [it is uttered], the heart of that person shall indeed burst. (1)
Biting his lower lip with his teeth, one should cause [the victim] to suffer by means of the name of whomever [one intends];
if that person transgresses the command, their head shall quickly burst asunder. // 2 //
With the great gaze of the Vajra Wrathful One, one should close one's eyes;
yet, by looking [with wrath] at whoever is named, that person's eyes shall burst asunder. // 3 //
Through the meditative absorption of the Vajra Wrath, one should personally press upon the heart with the vajra-bind; his mind will then burst asunder. Thus it is said. (4)
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
HŪṂ VAJRASPHOṬA ṬHAḤ.
Hūṃ, O Vajra of the Mouth, ṭhaḥ!
Hūṃ Vajranetra Ṭhaḥ!
Hūṃ, mind-vajra, ṭhaḥ!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the secret mudrās of the Great Vajra Family.
In that regard, first of all, there is the binding of the great mudrā:
by forming a hook with the little fingers, one should place the Vajra Wrathful Deities.
On the back of the left trident, however, Trilokavijayā is remembered. // 1 //
With the left forefinger well-extended and likewise with the upturned lotus, having turned [the hand] in that same way, the left vajra is established. // 2 //
Having formed the vajra-bind at the base, one should cover it with a wrathful mind;
pressing firmly with the vajra of the thumbs, this is known as the *krodhaterintiri*. (3)
With the tips of the fingers curled like a hook, she holds a vajra at the mouth with the index fingers;
likewise, she makes the gesture of "well done" (*sādhukāra*) with the two index fingers, and the tip-vajra is placed at the mouth. (4)
The Sūryasaṃdarśā mudrā is formed at the heart; the Samāgrī is situated upon the head.
Having turned it back, the Smitasthā is likewise the Samāgrī, while the Kuḍmalā is formed similarly.
Grasping the hilt of a sword with both hands, the tips of the two index fingers are joined;
the index finger is extended upward from the mouth of the hand. 6.
The index fingers are bound at the throat, and by those two [fingers], the fangs are positioned in the mouth;
with the fists firmly clenched, these are prescribed as the Great Mudrās (mahāmudrā). Thus [it is said]. // 7 //
Now follows the binding of the secret samaya-mudrās of the Vajra family.
Those supreme samayas are proclaimed to arise from the secret fist;
I shall explain their binding, the unsurpassed vajra-binding. (1)
The *vāṇākarṣā* [mudrā] is formed by placing the hands at the heart, turning them toward the sides, and drawing them back from the left;
the *bhṛkuṭī* [mudrā], however, is indeed formed by raising the hands from the heart and turning them around. // 2 //
Displaying the solar disk, with arms extended over the head; having turned [the gaze], she remains smiling, perfectly situated within the face. // 3 //
Having the form of striking with the tips of the fists, displaying the casting down of wheels, and emerging from the mouth, they are the circles of the supreme body upon the head. (4)
Likewise, with the two shoulders at the heart and from the two sides, there is the form of the Vajra-protection;
and by means of the application of the fang-position, it is firmly pressed by the clenched fist. // 5 //
One should bind the mudrās of the outer maṇḍala according to their respective symbols; likewise, one should bind the samaya [mudrā] with the vajra-bind and the vajra-fist. (6) Thus it is said.
Now follow the secret dharma-mudrās of the Vajra family:
phaṭṭaḥ, śaṭṭaḥ, maṭṭaḥ, saṭṭaḥ.
raṭṭaḥ, taṭṭaḥ, ghaṭṭaḥ, haṭṭaḥ, paṭṭaḥ, traṭṭaḥ.
Kaṭṭaḥ, dhaṭṭaḥ, kuṭṭaḥ, riṭṭaḥ, khaṭṭaḥ, vaṭṭaḥ.
Now follows the binding of the secret action-mudrās (karmamudrā) of the Vajra family:
the action-mudrās in brief consist of the vajra-fist made double, which should be placed in the appropriate positions by one who is wrathful and intensely enraged due to malice. Thus it is said.
The detailed procedure for the mandala of the secret wrathful mudrās from the *Sarvatathāgatavajrasamayamahākalparāja* is hereby completed.
The Emanation of Deities from Samādhi:

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Knowledge-Seals of the Samādhi of the Vajra Family of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme vidyā: OṂ SARVATATHĀGATA-SŪKṢMAVAJRA-KRODHA HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Great Wrathful King, spoke the supreme subtle-vajra vidyā for the Conqueror of the Three Worlds: Oṃ sūkṣmavajrakrodhākrama hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme subtle vajra-vidyā for conquering the three worlds: OṂ SŪKṢMAVAJRARATNĀKRAMA HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Then the Bodhisattva Vajranetra spoke this supreme subtle Vidyā-mantra of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds: Oṃ sūkṣmavajrapadmakrodhākrama hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the Bodhisattva Vajraviśva spoke this supreme subtle-vajra vidyā for the conquest of the three worlds: OṂ SŪKṢMAVAJRAKARMAKRODHĀKRAMA HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having again brought forth his own family and established it through the yoga of the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, spoke these heart-mantras:
Oṃ vajrasatva sūkṣmajñāna krodha hūṃ phaṭ // 1 //
Oṃ, O Great Wrathful One, draw in with the subtle vajra-hook, hūṃ phaṭ! // 2 //
Oṃ, O subtle vajra-anger of passion, arouse [him] intensely! Hūṃ phaṭ! // 3 //
Oṃ, subtle vajra, wrathful joy, hūṃ phaṭ! // 4 //
Oṃ, subtle Vajra Bhṛkuṭī Krodha, remove, remove! Hūṃ Phaṭ! // 5 //
Oṃ vajra-sūkṣma-jvālā-maṇḍala-krodha sūrya jvālaya hūṃ phaṭ! // 6 //
Oṃ, O subtle Vajradhvajāgra-krodha, grant me all goals quickly! Hūṃ Phaṭ! // 7 //
Oṃ vajrasūkṣmahāsakrodha ha ha ha ha hūṃ phaṭ // 8 //
Oṃ, subtle Vajra Dharma Wrathful One, purify! Hūṃ Phaṭ! // 9 //
Oṃ, subtle vajra-cutting wrathful one, cut, pierce! Hūṃ phaṭ! // 10 //
Oṃ, subtle vajra-wrathful one, great wheel! Cut! Strike down! Having entered the head, pierce the heart! Hūṃ phaṭ! // 11 //
Oṃ, subtle Vajra-hūṃkāra wrathful one, slay! Strike down! By mere word, hūṃ phaṭ! // 12 //
Oṃ, subtle Vajra-karma-krodha, become the performer of all activities; accomplish all tasks! Hūṃ phaṭ! // 13 //
Oṃ vajrasūkṣmakavacakrodha rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ phaṭ // 14 //
Oṃ, subtle Vajrayakṣa wrathful one, slay and devour all the wicked by the mere thought [of this]; O Vajratoothed one, hūṃ phaṭ! // 15 //
Oṃ, subtle vajra-fist wrathful one, bind, bind! Hūṃ phaṭ! // 16 //
The delineation of the maṇḍala:
Then Vajrapāṇi again proclaimed this maṇḍala of the samaya of subtle gnosis of the Vajra family.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme dharma-maṇḍala.
That which resembles the Vajradhātu is known as the wisdom of wrath. // 1 //
By means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala, one should delineate the entire maṇḍala;
in its center, one should draw the Buddha situated in the middle of the Wisdom-Vajra. //2//
One should draw those very same mudrās on all sides of the Buddha;
having emerged with vajra-velocity, they are placed within the four mandalas.
One should duly install Trilokavijaya and Abhyāṃ;
then, from all sides of them, one should install the Vajra-krodhas according to the ritual rule. (4) Thus it is said.
Now, regarding the initiation into this subtle wisdom maṇḍala of the Vajra family, the detailed ritual procedure is as follows.

Therein, first of all, having caused [the candidate] to enter, one should say: "Today, you have been consecrated by the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi into the state of the Vajra Wrath of all the Tathāgatas; therefore, it is well."

"Engage yourself for the sake of protecting the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, and for the purpose of attaining the fruit of the supreme accomplishment of the welfare and happiness of all Tathāgatas; by means of the Vajra Wrath, purify even all sentient beings, let alone all the wicked.
Having said this, he should release the binding of the mouth.
Then, having shown the entire maṇḍala and having placed the vajra in the hand according to the ritual rule,
one should thereafter instruct [the disciple] in the subtle gnoses of the Vajra-krodha.
Having made the subtle vajra firm through the yoga of the Vajra-hūṃkāra, one should apply the hūṃ-syllable to whomever; that person’s life shall perish. // 1 //
Having made the subtle vajra firm, one should cause it to radiate according to the ritual procedure;
for as long as it radiates, that enemy shall perish. // 2 //
Applying the subtle vajra procedure through the yoga of Vajra-hūṃkāra, the wrathful one should radiate [light] until he has destroyed all sentient beings. // 3 //
In that same manner, the practitioner of yoga should withdraw that [power] as long as he desires;
indeed, he may withdraw everything entirely without remainder, yet he can grant life back once again.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
HŪṂ.
Huṃ, destroy, O Vajra!
Hūṃ! Destroy all, O Vajra!
Oṃ, subtle vajra, bring back quickly! Hūṃ.
If a being possesses a vajra that is co-emergent and exceedingly firm, by means of the yoga of pervading with loving-kindness, one should destroy [the adversary] by pervading with wrath. // 1 //
Through the application of the pervasion of wrath, whoever possesses compassion—by means of that compassionate application—he shall destroy all who are wicked. (2)
Whether they be non-dharmas or dharmas, they are luminous by nature;
meditating thus upon sentient beings, one should destroy them with the syllable HŪṂ.
For those beings who are wicked and unruly, and who are not vessels for the enlightenment of a Buddha, one should destroy them with the syllable *huṃ* for the sake of purifying them. // 4 //
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Vaira-vajra-krodha hūṃ phaṭ.
Karuṇāvajrakrodha hūṃ phaṭ!
HŪṂ! Pure Vajra Wrath, HŪṂ PHAṬ!
HŪṂ! Purifying Vajra-anger, HŪṂ PHAṬ!
Having mentally drawn the Vajra-image of anyone whatsoever, if one causes it to fall into the middle of that person's house, their entire lineage shall perish. // 1 //
In that very same way, one should meditate upon the heart-vajra with subtle methods;
[otherwise] one would cause the great image of the Bodhisattva to fall and destroy one's lineage. // 2 //
Wherever one casts [the ritual substance] while meditating on the great image of Vajrapāṇi, that kingdom, along with the king himself, perishes through various calamities. // 3 //
While meditating on the form of the Buddha endowed with the excellence of all aspects, if one causes it to fall upon a kingdom, that kingdom will certainly perish. Thus [it is said].
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
*huṃ vajra prapāta*.
Hūṃ! Bodhisattva, fall down!
Hūṃ! O Vajradhara, fall down!
Hūṃ! O Buddha, do not fall!
By means of the practice of the subtle vajra, visualizing the lunar disc as oneself, one should cause oneself to fall; wherever it falls, there he shall descend. // 1 //
Visualizing oneself as the Vajra within the moon by means of one's own self, whichever [family] one falls upon while intensely enraged, that family perishes in an instant. // 2 //
Visualizing oneself as Vajrapāṇi by means of one's own self, wherever one should fall, that place will soon be utterly destroyed. // 3 //
If one visualizes oneself as the form of the Buddha by means of one's own self, that kingdom where [the practitioner] falls shall perish before long. Thus it is said.
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
*bodhyagra prapātaya hūṃ*.
O All-Vajra, cause [them] to fall! Hūṃ!
O Vajrasattva, cause [him] to fall! Hūṃ!
Buddha prapātaya hūṃ!
Then, one should teach the secret mudrā-knowledge of the Vajra-family dharma:
by means of the vajra-krodha-samāpatti, one should envelop one's own body.
By whose name he dies, being enveloped by the Vajra-hūṃkṛta. // 1 //
Having entered into the subtle vajra through the subtle nose once, by means of the yoga of the breath and the syllable *huṃ*, one may cause even the three worlds to fall. // 2 //
Applying the subtle vajra method, one who is enraged should gaze with the vajra-vision; by so beholding, the [victim] goes to blindness or even reaches death. // 3 //
"By entering through the *bhaga* with the mind focused on anyone whatsoever, one brings them under one's own control by drawing their heart toward oneself, or even that of Yama. (4)
In that regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
*Hūṃ vajra valita krodha māraya hūṃ phaṭ*.
Oṃ vajra sūkṣma, cause the poison of the breath to fall! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajra-dṛṣṭi, destroy the poison! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Hūṃ! O wrathful one who draws [the heart] to you, enter the body, pierce and split the heart; pull out, pull out! Phaṭ!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the Dharma-mudrās of the Vajra family.
In that regard, first is the binding of the Mahāmudrā:
by means of the application of vajra-knowledge, [one visualizes] those with radiance filled with garlands of flames.
"By visualizing oneself as a Vajra Wrath deity, one attains accomplishment in an instant. Thus it is said.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the Dharma-samaya-mudrā of the Vajra family:

"The samaya of meditative concentration and wisdom, conjoined with two *huṃ* syllables, should be established in its proper places as the most excellent bestower of all accomplishments. Thus it is said.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the Dharma-mudrā of the Vajra-family Dharma-samaya:
*phaṭ saṭ maṭ saṭ raṭ taṭ dhṛṭ haṭ paṭ traṭ ghaṭ bhaṭ kṛṭ riṭ khaṭ vaṭ*.
Thus have the seals of the Dharma been explained in brief.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the action seals (karmamudrā) of the Vajra family’s dharma-samaya:

"Having formed the dharma-fist in two ways according to their respective positions and applications, the action seals attain accomplishment in brief according to the prescribed ritual. Thus it is said.
The detailed procedure for the maṇḍala of the samaya of the wisdom of the Dharma of the Vajra family from the *Sarvatathāgatavajrasamayamahākalparāja* is completed.
The Emanation of Deities from Samādhi:

Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment Arising from the Samaya of the Vajra Activity of All Tathāgatas" and spoke this supreme personal vidyā: OṂ SARVATATHĀGATA KARMEŚVARĪ HŪṂ.

Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge: Oṃ, at the time of the extensive ritual procedure for the great worship that pervades the dharma-realm of all Tathāgatas, you who bring victory over the three worlds, subdue all the wicked, O Vajrīṇī! Hūṃ!

Then the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha again spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge: Oṃ, at the time of the extensive ritual procedure for the great act of worship that gathers all Tathāgatas within the realm of space, Hūṃ!

Then the Bodhisattva Vajranetra again spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge: Oṃ, at the time of the extensive ritual procedure for the great act of worship that pervades the dharma-realm of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!

Then the Bodhisattva Vajraviśva again spoke this supreme mantra of his own vidyā: Oṃ, at the time of the extensive ritual procedure for the various great offerings to all the Tathāgatas in all world-realms, hūṃ!
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again produced from his own heart the deities of the extensive ritual for the worship of his own family;

having performed all the miraculous transformations of the Tathāgatas— such as summoning, subjugating, and enchanting all the Tathāgatas in all world-systems, and enjoining them to perform the activities that accomplish all rites—
he once more remained abiding upon moon-mandalas by means of the yoga of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm of the Blessed One Vairocana.
The delineation of the maṇḍala: Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this extensive ritual procedure for the maṇḍala of vajra-activity, the maṇḍala of rites.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme maṇḍala of rites.
Resembling the Vajra Realm, it is known as the Karma-vajra. // 1 //
One should delineate the entire maṇḍala by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala;
one should install the images of the Buddhas within the central maṇḍala. // 2 //
One should station the foremost samayas on all sides of the Buddha; having stepped forth with vajra-impulses, one should do so within the fourfold mandalas. (3)
One should install the four Vajranātha deities and others in their proper places; on all sides of them, one should install the Great Beings (mahāsattvīs). Thus [it is said]. // 4 //
Now, in this ritual mandala, there are the Vajra-karma mudrās:
Oṃ vajrasattvasiddhijñānasamaye hūṃ jjaḥ. (1)
Oṃ vajrākarṣaṇakarmajñānasamaye hūṃ jjaḥ // 2 //
Oṃ vajraratirāgakarmajñānasamaye hūṃ jjaḥ // 3 //
Oṃ vajrasādhukarmajñānasamaye hūṃ jjaḥ // 4 //
Oṃ vajrabhṛkuṭī, subjugate! Hūṃ. // 5 //
Oṃ, within the vajra-sun mandala, bring [them] under control! Hūṃ. // 6 //
Oṃ, O Vajradhvajāgrakeyūra, bring [them] under control! Hūṃ. // 7 //
Oṃ vajrāṭṭahāse vaśīkuru hūṃ // 8 //
Oṃ vajrapadmarāge rāgaya hūṃ. // 9 //
Oṃ, O Vajra-sharp Passion, inflame [me], hūṃ! // 10 //
Oṃ vajramaṇḍalarāge rāgaya hūṃ. // 11 //
Oṃ, O foremost of vajra-speech, inspire passion! Hūṃ. // 12 //
Oṃ, at the time of the vajra-activity, perform worship! Hūṃ. // 13 //
Oṃ, bind the vajra armor; protect! Hūṃ. // 14 //
Oṃ vajrayakṣiṇi, slay! O you with adamantine fangs, pierce the heart of so-and-so! Hūṃ phaṭ! // 15 //
Oṃ vajrakarmamuṣṭi siddhya siddhya hūṃ phaṭ! // 16 //
Now, having performed the detailed ritual procedure here in the action maṇḍala according to the rules,
one should generate the action-knowledges of the Vajra family.
In that regard, from the very beginning, one should teach the knowledge of rites for pacification and so forth:

having kindled the fire with sweet-smelling sacrificial wood (*samidh*), being well-composed, and through the meditative absorption (*samāpatti*) of Vajrakrodha, one should burn away all evils by offering sesame seeds into the fire. // 1 //
Having kindled the sacrificial fire with those very same fuel-sticks, by constantly offering oblations of rice grains, the prosperity of the household will certainly be secured. // 2 //
Having kindled the fire with fuel sticks and sweet substances, the wise man increases his lifespan by offering young shoots of *dūrvā* grass mixed with clarified butter. // 3 //
"Having kindled the sacrificial fire with those very same fuel-sticks, one who offers oblations of fresh *kuśa* shoots mixed with oil achieves eternal protection. // 4 //
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ, svāhā to the vajra that burns away all sins!
Oṃ, svāhā to Vajrapuṣṭi!
Oṃ, svāhā to the adamantine life-force!
Oṃ, to the unimpeded vajra, svāhā!
First, having kindled the fire with fuel-sticks and *kaḍaka* wood through the *vajrakrodha-samādhi*, it is fanned by means of thorny branches. // 1 //
Having kindled the fire with those very same fuel-sticks, one who is full of great wrath, by offering oblations of red flowers and fruits, causes the world to become impassioned. // 2 //
For even if one is provoked by those who have offered oblations, the practitioner, having kindled the fire and offering iron filings as an oblation, will become bound with a vajra-bond. // 3 //
Having kindled the fire with those very same fuel-sticks, one who is composed should offer bitter fruit out of anger; thus, he shall produce pestilence in an instant.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
HŪṂ VAJRĀKARṢAYA SVĀHĀ.
Hūṃ vajra rāgaya svāhā!
Hūṃ vajra bandhāya svāhā!
Hūṃ vajra māraṇāya svāhā!
Having kindled the blazing fire with pure fuel-sticks, the wise one, having prospered, performs the oblation with sour fruits and flowers; this is the supreme rite of subjugation. // 1 //

Having kindled the fire with those very same fuel-sticks, one who is composed and yet wrathful should offer oblations for the sake of the fruit of desire; he shall attain the power to assume any form at will. // 2 //
Having kindled the sacrificial fire with such very same fuel-sticks, she offered oblations of stalks of invisible flowers; because of her radiance, she could not be seen.
"Having kindled the fire with those very same fuel-sticks, one who is composed, offering flowers from the celestial creeper, shall become a traveler of the sky. Thus [ends verse 4].
In that regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ vajravaśaṃkarāya svāhā.
Oṃ, svāhā to the Vajra of the Form of Desire!
Oṃ, svāhā to the invisible vajra!
Oṃ vajrakhacarīṇī svāhā.
Having kindled the fire with fuel-sticks of bitter potency, one who is composed and wrathful should offer *vajri* flowers; thus the Vajra will become an executor of his commands. // 1 //
Having thus kindled the fire with those very fuel-sticks, one who is full of great wrath should offer a garland into the solar fire; he [the deity] shall then become a servant obeying his commands.

Having kindled the fire with those very fuel-sticks, being well-composed and filled with wrath, he should offer a garland into the fire of Vajrapāṇi; that [deity] shall then become a servant who obeys his command.
Having kindled the fire with those very same fuel-sticks, the Buddha, filled with great wrath, should offer his robes as oblations; in an instant, [the opponent] becomes a servant of his command.
In this regard, these are their heart-mantras:
Hūṃ, svāhā to the one who brings about the subjugation by means of the vajra!
Hūṃ! To the Vajra who brings the sun under control, svāhā!
Hūṃ! To Vajrapāṇi, the subduer, svāhā!
Hūṃ! Svāhā to the Vajra that brings all beings under the power of the Buddha!
Then, one should teach the secret mudrā and the knowledge of the karma-mudrā:
while dwelling together with a beloved woman, [one should apply] collyrium to her bhaga.
Having cast [the substance] therein, one should stir it; by means of that, one brings the eyes under control. // 1 //
Having pierced the realgar with the *bhaga*, one should seal it with the *vajra-bandha*;
through the fourfold signs, there is likewise fourfold accomplishment. // 2 //
Having placed rocanā in the bhaga, one should press it with the secret fist;
once placed there, it blazes forth, and one becomes equal to Vajradhara. // 3 //
Having pierced the bhaga with saffron, that bhaga is covered by the sattva-vajra; it blazes forth, and one becomes equal to Vajradhara. Thus [it is said]. (4)
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ vajraguhya rativaśaṃkara sidhya huṃ.
Oṃ vajraguhya sidhya hūṃ.
Oṃ, secret vajra, be accomplished! Hūṃ.
Oṃ, O secret holder of the vajra, accomplish [this], hūṃ!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the great mudrās of the activity of the Vajra family:

"In brief, the great mudrās are [attained] through the application of the vajra-activity, by means of the meditative absorption of the Vajra Wrathful One, and through the application of the vajra-fist. (1)
Likewise, here the supreme samaya [mudrās] arise from the union of the syllable *huṃ* and the fingers;
likewise, here the dharma-mudrās arise from the syllables beginning with *oṃ*, such as *a* and so forth. // 2 //
In brief, the action seals (karmamudrā) are formed by making the action-fist twofold;
they are pure and bring about all accomplishments through the application of vajra-action. // 3 //
The detailed procedure for the Karma Maṇḍala of the Vajra Family from the *Sarvatathāgatavajrasamaya*, the Great King of Kalpas, is completed.
The Emanation of Deities from Samādhi:
Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Vajra-Samaya-Seals of All Tathāgatas" and spoke this supreme mantra of all vidyās: OṂ SARVATATHĀGATAVAJRASAMAYE HŪṂ.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this self-vajra-sasaya-mudrā: "Hūṃ vajri maṭ."
Then the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha spoke this jewel-samaya-mudrā: "Hūṃ! O Bhr̥kuṭivajra, roar!"
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this self-dharma-samaya-mudrā: HŪṂ PADMAVAJRI TRIṬ.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśva spoke this own Action-Samaya Mudrā: HŪṂ VAJRAKARMĀGRI KṚṬ.
The delineation of the maṇḍala:
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke again this Trilokavijaya Four-Seal Maṇḍala.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme Seal Maṇḍala.
Resembling the Vajra Realm, it is known as Krodhavajra. // 1 //
"One should delineate the entire maṇḍala by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala; one should draw [deities] such as Trilokavijaya everywhere around the Buddha. Thus, [verse] 2.

Regarding the mudrās: here, in this four-mudrā maṇḍala, having performed the detailed ritual for summoning and so forth through the yoga of the great maṇḍala, and having caused [the disciples] to enter the four-mudrā maṇḍala, one should teach the secret mudrā-knowledge.
Having oneself drawn the four-mudrā maṇḍala, which is pure reality (śuddhadharmatā), [one should teach it].
By reciting [the mantra] while dwelling together with a woman, accomplishment is attained. // 1 //

Having personally drawn the maṇḍala of the four mudrās, which is the pure nature of phenomena (dharmatā), one attains accomplishment by gazing at a woman with passion while reciting [the mantra]. // 2 //
Having personally drawn the maṇḍala of the four mudrās, which is the pure nature of phenomena, one succeeds by setting it in motion while kissing a beloved woman. // 3 //

Having personally drawn the maṇḍala of the four mudrās, which is the pure nature of phenomena (dharmatā), one should embrace it while reciting [the mantra]; thus, all accomplishments (siddhi) are attained. // 4 //
In this regard, these are the seals of the pure nature of phenomena (*śuddhadharmatāmudrā*):
Oṃ sarvatathāgataviśuddhadharmate hoḥ.
Oṃ vajraviśuddhadṛṣṭi jjaḥ!
Oṃ, at the gate of natural purity, hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Vajra of the actions of body, speech, and mind that are entirely pure, strike!
Then, one should teach the secret and most esoteric mudrā of the mandala of the four mudrās:
"Having entered this mandala with the five excellent qualities of desire,
one attains supreme accomplishment by sporting with the wives of others."
Then her heart-verse is: "Ho! O Vajrakāma!"
Then, having duly taught the four samaya-mudrās, beginning with the Vajrākrānti-triśūla-mudrā, together with their detailed rituals,
and having offered vajra-instruments, musical instruments, and cymbals by means of that application of the four mudrās,
one should perform the worship of dance and offerings while singing the heart-song of the Vajrasattva-saṃgraha, using the mudrā, pratimudrā, upamudrā, and jñānamudrās.
In this regard, this is the worship consisting of the offering of dance:
By means of the application of the Vajra Dance, one should bind the two fingers of the Vajra-Krodha mudrā at the heart as the Vajra-Hūṃkāra mudrā. (1)
In the same manner, dancing and grasping the left [hand] with the right fist, one should turn it around and place the tips against the forehead with the mouth. (2)

Then, dancing in that very place and releasing [the previous mudrā], one should join the palms in the *samakuḍmala* position, place the *agryañjali* at the heart, and bow with the body trembling from inner devotion. (3)

The fingers of the Vajra-krodha [mudrā] are properly joined with their tips facing upward; having turned them thus toward the uṣṇīṣa, the index fingers are well-positioned at the face. (4) Thus it is said.
II.6. The Mandala of the Single Seal:
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again spoke this Vajra-Samaya-Krodha-Samaya: HŪṂ.
The delineation of the maṇḍala:
Now follows its maṇḍala;
now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme secret maṇḍala.
Resembling the Vajradhātu and known as Vajrahuṃkāra. // 1 //
By means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala, one should draw the external maṇḍala;
in its center, one should correctly draw the Vajrin upon a moon-maṇḍala. // 2 //
Holding the great mudrā of the vajra-huṃkāra with his hands joined at the vajra, standing firmly in the pratyālīḍha posture, and possessing the proper color and form—thus [he is]. // 3 //
Then, having performed the detailed procedure for all the rites of accomplishment in this secret maṇḍala, one should proclaim the knowledge of the secret mudrā of Vajrahuṃkāra.
Having entered this maṇḍala, one should accomplish the *trilokavijayāṅgulī*; by piercing the *bhaga*, every ritual action (*sarvakarma*) is successfully accomplished.
Then his heart-mantra for accomplishment is: *huṃ vajrasamaya kṛta*.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrā for the practice of the laughter of Vajrahuṃkāra:
"Having properly entered the maṇḍala and being established in the supreme Great Mudrā, dwelling together with Vajrahuṃkāra, one shall become the performer of all activities. Thus it is said.
In that regard, its heart-mantra for accomplishment is: *huṃ vajrasamaya huṃ*.
Then, one should teach the fourfold binding of the mudrās according to the proper method; in that very way, the accomplishments (siddhis) arise.
Just as it is with the mandala, so too is the common accomplishment (sādhāraṇasiddhi) for all images painted on cloth and other media.
Then Vajrapāṇi, having summoned all the Tathāgatas, spoke thus:
"May the Blessed Ones, all the Tathāgatas, empower this family of mine, so that all sentient beings may attain all accomplishments according to their desires."
Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, having gathered together once more, spoke these words for the sake of empowering this *Trilokavijaya-kalpa*:
"Excellent, O Vajrasattva! Excellent, O Vajraratna!
Excellent, O Vajradharma! Excellent, O Vajrakarman!"
This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna, the secret of all Tathāgatas, and the compendium of the Mahāyāna. Thus it is said.
The extensive ritual procedure for the Great Kalpa King, the Vajra Samaya of all Tathāgatas, is completed.
Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, having once again assembled and knowing [the situation], spoke thus to the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
“O child, act in accordance with the command of all the Tathāgatas by releasing this body of Maheśvara from the strike of your foot.”
Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi spoke thus to those Tathāgatas:
"I have been consecrated by the Blessed Ones as the wrathful one who subdues all the wicked;
therefore, this [being] has been slain by me."
"How then shall I release him?

Then, for the sake of restoring life to the body of Maheśvara, the sovereign of all the three worlds, all the Tathāgatas emitted from their own hearts this heart-mantra for summoning back the consciousness of the deceased:
OṂ VAJRASATTVA HŪṂ JJAḤ.
Now follows the binding of its mudrā:
having firmly formed the secret hook (guhyāṅkuśī) with the ends extended together,
and placing it upon the head of the deceased, he shall regain life once more.

Then, as soon as this had issued forth, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Bhasmeśvaranirghoṣa, having come from the world-system Bhasmacchatrā and entered the body of that Maheśvara, uttered this inspired utterance:
"Oh, how truly unsurpassed is the Buddha-knowledge of all the Buddhas, that even this dead body has attained the state of a living element! Thus it was said.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi uttered this heart-mantra called "The Emission of the Feet": Oṃ vajra muḥ.
Now follows the binding of its mudrā:

having raised the fingers of the Vajra-krodha [mudrā] so that their tips are joined while remaining [in place], one should turn them over and lift them up from beneath the two vajras. Thus it is said.
Then, as soon as this had been spoken, Mahādeva was released from the feet of Mahāvajradhara and restored to life.

Then, having empowered the body of Maheśvara with life, that Tathāgata established him in the position of crown prince within this very world-system for the benefit of all sentient beings and for the sake of subduing the wicked.
Then, from the soles of the feet of Vajrapāṇi, there issued forth this mudrā of the bodhicitta of all Tathāgatas, named Candrapādā:
Oṃ candrottare samantabhadrakiraṇī mahāvajriṇi hūṃ.
Now follows the binding of its mudrā:
having made the vajra-bind firm, with the little fingers and thumbs raised together, and being well-drawn up once they have been raised together, it is proclaimed as "Candraprabhā."
Then, as soon as she had emerged, from that very sole of his foot, the Tathāgata Candrottara himself issued forth;
he was consecrated upon the half-moon on the head of that Maheśvara as Vajrapāṇi set his feet upon him,
and he stood at the left side of Vajrapāṇi.
Then, all the Tathāgatas, having placed a vajra-spear into the hand of the friend Vajrapāṇi,
consecrated him with the vajra-name-consecration, "Vajravidyottama, Vajravidyottama."
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajravidyottama, performing a dance-offering with that vajra-spear in a circular movement, uttered this inspired utterance:
"O, how wonderful! The supreme mind of enlightenment of all Buddhas, by the mere touch of the tips of whose feet I have attained Buddhahood! Thus he spoke.
Then the great bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
having emerged from that vajra-anger samādhi, addressed these words to the Blessed One:
“Blessed One, all the Tathāgatas placed a vajra in my two hands and consecrated me as Vajrapāṇi.”
"Therefore, I shall assign the positions for these deities and others belonging to the external vajra families within this Great Maṇḍala of Victory over the Three Worlds,
so that those beings will become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening."
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, uttered this Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣa: Oṃ vajrasatvoṣṇīṣa hūṃ phaṭ!
Then, as soon as this was spoken, from all the uṣṇīṣas of the Tathāgatas there issued forth the form of the Blessed Vajrapāṇi,
which, becoming rays of light of various colors,
illuminated all the world-systems.
Once again, they surrounded the head of the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi,
and having become the mass of splendor of the uṣṇīṣas of all the Tathāgatas, they remained there. Then, from that mass of splendor, this Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣa issued forth.
Oṃ, homage to the Uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas, mass of splendor, whose crown is invisible; Hūṃ! Blaze! Burn! Vidhaka! Rend! Split! Hūṃ Phaṭ!
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi uttered this supreme mantra of his own knowledge: Oṃ niṣumbha vajra hūṃ phaṭ!
Then Vajrapāṇi again uttered this heart-mantra from his own heart: OṂ ṬṬAKKI JJAḤ.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme personal vidyā: Oṃ vajra-ratnottama jvālaya hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this supreme personal vidyā-mantra: Oṃ svabhāvaśuddha vajrapadma śodhaya sarvān vidyottama hūṃ phaṭ!

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśva spoke this supreme mantra of his own vidyā: Oṃ vajrakarmottama vajradhara, remember the samaya! Subha-nisumbha, attract! Cause to enter! Cause to descend! Bind! Seize the samaya! Perform all my rites, O Mahāsattva! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajravidyottama offered this, his own heart-mantra, for the purpose of worshipping the feet of the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi: Oṃ suṃbha niḥsuṃbha vajravidyottama hūṃ phaṭ!
Then Krodhavajra, the King of Vidyās, prostrating at the feet of the Blessed One, offered this heart-mantra: HŪṂ VAJRAŚŪLA.
Then Māyāvajra, the King of Vidyās, spoke this heart-mantra: Oṃ vajramāya vidarśaya sarva huṃ phaṭ!
Then the Vidyārāja Vajraghaṇṭa bestowed his own heart-mantra: Oṃ vajraghaṇṭa raṇa raṇa hūṃ phaṭ.
Then Maunavajra offered his own heart: Oṃ vajramauna mahāvrata hūṃ phaṭ!
Then Vajrāyudha gave his own heart-mantra: Oṃ vajrāyudha dāmaka hūṃ phaṭ!
The Vidyārājas.
Then Vajrakuṇḍali, the Vajra-Wrathful One, offered this heart-mantra of his own to the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi—a mantra to be honored by prostrating at his feet:
Oṃ vajrakuṇḍali mahāvajrakrodha! Seize! Strike! Burn! Cook! Destroy! Split the head with the vajra! Pierce the heart, O Vajra-Wrathful One! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Then Vajraprabha, the Vajra Wrath, gave this own heart-mantra:
Oṃ vajraprabha māraya saumyakrodha hūṃ phaṭ!
Then Vajradaṇḍa, the Vajra Wrathful One, offered his own heart-essence mantra:
Oṃ vajradaṇḍa tanuya sarvaduṣṭān mahākrodha hūṃ phaṭ!
Then Vajrapiṅgala, the Vajra-wrathful one, bestowed this own heart-mantra:
Oṃ vajrapiṅgala, terrify all the wicked ones, O fearsome wrathful one, hūṃ phaṭ!
The Vajra Wrathful Ones.
Then Vajraśauṇḍa, the lord of the Gaṇas, offered this heart-mantra to the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi:
*Oṃ vajraśauṇḍa mahāgaṇapati rakṣa sarvaduṣṭebhyo vajradharājñāṃ pālaya huṃ phaṭ*. Then Vajramāla gave this, his own heart-mantra:
Oṃ vajramāla, to Gaṇapati: attract with the garland, cause to enter, cause to possess, bind, subjugate, slay! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Then Vajravaśī gave her own heart-mantra:
Oṃ vajravaśī mahāgaṇapate vaśīkuru hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the Gaṇapati Vijayavajra gave his own heart-mantra:
Oṃ vajravijaya vijayaṃ kuru mahāgaṇapati hūṃ phaṭ.
The Gaṇapatis:
Then Vajramusala, the Vajra-messenger, offered this, his own heart-mantra, to Vajrapāṇi:
Oṃ vajramusala kṛṭṭa kṛṭṭa sarvaduṣṭān vajradūta hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the messenger Vajrānila gave his own heart-mantra:
Oṃ vajrānila mahāvega ānaya sarvaduṣṭān hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the messenger Vajrānala gave his own heart-mantra:
Oṃ vajrānala mahādūta, set ablaze all, reduce all malevolent ones to ashes, hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the messenger Vajrabhairava gave his own heart-mantra:
Oṃ vajrabhairava vajradūta, devour all the wicked ones, O great yakṣa! Hūṃ phaṭ!
The messengers.
Then Vajrāṅkuśa, the Vajra-servant (vajraceṭa), offered this, his own heart-mantra, to the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi:
Oṃ vajrāṅkuśākarṣaya sarva mahāceṭa hūṃ phaṭ!
Then Vajrakāla offered his own heart-essence mantra:
Oṃ vajrakāla mahāmṛtyum utpādaya hūṃ phaṭ!
Then Vajravināyaka gave his own heart-mantra:
Oṃ vajravināyakāsya vighnaṃ kuru hūṃ phaṭ!
Then Nāgavajra offered this, his own heart-mantra, to the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi as a salutation at his feet:

Oṃ! O Nāgavajra, bring all wealth, grain, silver, gold, jewels, pearls, ornaments, and all other requisites! O Vajradhara, remember the samaya! Summon! Seize! Bind! Take away! Take away the lives! O Great Servant, hūṃ phaṭ!
The servants.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed this samaya for summoning all the vajra families: Oṃ vajrāṅkuśa ākarṣaya hūṃ!
Then he uttered the mantra for the time of entry: *huṃ vajrapāśākaḍḍha huṃ*.
Then he proclaimed the bond of the pledge: "Hūṃ vajrasphoṭa vaṃ!"
Then he uttered the Heart-mantra of Action: Oṃ vajrakarma sādhaya kṛt.
The delineation of the maṇḍala: Then Vajrapāṇi spoke this great maṇḍala of the entire Vajra family.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme great maṇḍala.
I shall describe the entire maṇḍala, which resembles the Wheel of Dharma.
In this regard, the heart-mantra for the ritual cord is as follows: Oṃ vajrasūtra ākarṣaya sarvamaṇḍalān hūṃ.
Having indeed driven a stake of khadira wood into the center of the mandala,
one should then double the cord and trace [the lines] with it.
In this regard, this is the heart-mantra of the stake: Oṃ vajrakīla kīlaya sarvavighnān bandhaya hūṃ phaṭ.
One should draw the circular mandala joined with four lines;
having gone out from its exterior, one should likewise [draw another] double that size. // 1 //
One should also make that [inner mandala] threefold; this is the threading of the outer mandala.
One should draw the lines for the corners by means of the application of the intermediate directions. Thus [ends verse 2].
The procedure for marking out the lines:
thereafter, one should mark them out and fill them with pure colors;
using the great left vajra-fist, one should draw the initial line as is convenient.
In this regard, the heart-mantra of the colored powders is:
Oṃ vajra-raṅga samaya hūṃ.
Then, standing in the center and being composed, the Vajrācārya should mentally open the four vajra-doors.
In this regard, this is the heart-mantra for opening the door:
Oṃ vajrodghāṭanasamaya praviśa śīghraṃ smara vajrasamaya hūṃ phaṭ.
One should install an image of the Buddha in a vessel made of gold or silver, or even one made of well-painted clay or a square brick.
In this regard, this is the heart-mantra of all Buddhas:
Oṃ sarvavid.
One should manifest the four great beings from all sides of the Buddha,
effecting the conquest of the three worlds, with Vajrapāṇi standing before him.
In this regard, these are the heart-mantras of the four great beings:
Oṃ suṃbha niḥsuṃbha hūṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ gṛhṇāpaya hūṃ ānaya ho bhagavan vajra hūṃ phaṭ // 1 //
Oṃ, Vajrabhṛkuṭi, wrathful one, bring all jewels! Hīḥ phaṭ! // 2 //
Oṃ vajradṛṣṭi! With the wrathful gaze, slay! Hūṃ phaṭ! // 3 //
Oṃ, O Vajra Viśvakrodha, perform everything; accomplish it through your universal form, hūṃ phaṭ! // 4 //
Whether entering or exiting, one should direct the mind toward the base of the thread;
known as Vajravega, one should thereby traverse the line. Thus it is said.
In this regard, this is the heart-mantra of Vajravega: *vajravega*.
Having emerged with the vajra-impulse, one should likewise draw the first maṇḍala and, in due order and according to the rules, [the deities] such as Vajramāyā and the others.
In this regard, their pledge-essences (samaya-hṛdaya) are as follows:
Oṃ vajracakra hūṃ. // 1 //
Oṃ vajraghaṇṭa hūṃ. // 2 //
Oṃ vajradaṇḍakāṣṭha hūṃ // 3 //
Oṃ vajrāyudha hūṃ // 4 //
Having proceeded with vajra-velocity to the second mandala in that same manner,
one should install the Vajra-wrathful deities, beginning with Vajrakuṇḍalin.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows: Oṃ prajvalita pradīptavajra hūṃ // 1 //
Oṃ vajrasaumya hūṃ // 2 //
Oṃ vajradaṇḍa hūṃ. // 3 //
Oṃ vajravikṛta hūṃ // 4 //
Then, Vajravega should draw all [the deities] beginning with Vajraśauṇḍa in their proper order upon the four gates.
In this regard, their pledge-heart mantras are as follows:
Oṃ vajramada hūṃ.
Oṃ vajramāle hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrārtha hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrāśi hūṃ.
Having approached with the speed of a vajra, one should draw [the deities] in the third mandala,
in their proper order and sequence, beginning with Vajramusala and the others.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ vajramusala hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrapaṭa hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrajvāla hūṃ.
Oṃ vajragraha hūṃ.
Having advanced with vajra-impetus, one should draw [the deities] in the fourth mandala:
the servants (ceṭas) beginning with Vajrāṅkuśa, in their proper order and according to tradition.
In this regard, these are their heart-mantras (hṛdaya).
Oṃ vajradaṃṣṭra hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrāmāraṇa hūṃ.
Oṃ vajravidhvaṃsana hūṃ.
Oṃ vajraharaṇa hūṃ.
Having emerged with vajra-impetus and stationed within the outer maṇḍala, one should draw all the Mothers in their proper order and sequence. // 1 //
At all the vajra-gates, those very ones are the gatekeepers. Hereafter, I shall explain in due order the detailed ritual procedure. (2) Thus it is said.
Then, having performed the rites of summoning and so forth in this great maṇḍala of the wheel of the three worlds,
the Vajrācārya himself, having bound the Vajrakrodhaterintiri mudrā, should speak as follows:
“I shall produce for you the wisdom of the Vajra-samaya;
this must not be spoken by you to anyone.
Lest, through its failure to protect you, you should meet an untimely death and fall into hell.”
Having said this, one should give this heart-mantra of the oath.
Having formed the Vajrakrodha-terintiri mudrā, one should display it [with these words]: "This Vajrakrodha-samaya shall burn your clan; starting from the head, it shall destroy your body."
If he should transgress the samaya, bind him!
Then, the holder of the vajra should bind the action-seal (karmamudrā) with this heart-mantra: Oṃ sarvatathāgata-vajradhara gṛhṇa bandha samaya hūṃ.
Now follows the binding of this mudrā:
having bound the little fingers and thumbs, the two hands are placed one above the other; this mudrā is celebrated as the Karmasamaya-vajrabandha.
Then one should consecrate with the water of the vajra by means of this heart-mantra: Oṃ vajrābhiṣekābhiṣiñca vajradharatve samaya gṛhṇa gṛhṇa.
Then, having bound the mouth with a cloth, he causes [the disciple] to enter by means of this heart-mantra: Oṃ praviśa vajra praveśaya vajra āviśa vajra ādhitiṣṭha vajra hūṃ.
Then, having caused [the disciple] to enter, one should cast flowers with this heart-mantra: Oṃ pratīccha adhitiṣṭha vajra hoḥ.
Then, wherever it falls, that [deity] of his is accomplished.
Thereafter, having released the binding of the face,
one should show the mandala in its proper sequence.
And one should not say of him, "Is he a god?
For what reason? Because there are beings with wrong views who will not have faith.
Is this the unfailing wisdom of the Blessed Buddhas?
Just as it is the established rule that Tathāgatas who have been consecrated by Vajrapāṇi in the Vajra family are indeed Tathāgatas themselves;
otherwise, it should be spoken only after giving the heart-mantra of the oath to those deities to whom they are devoted.
Then, having bestowed the consecration of the garland of vajra-jewel insignia and having placed the activity-vajra (karmavajra) into his two hands,
he should bestow a vajra-name.
As it is said: "The great mandala of the Vajra-samaya."
Then, one should teach the binding of the Mahāmudrā:
having made the Vajrabandha firm, with the collection of the thumbs inserted within.
Moving with the tips of her fingers slightly curled, she is known as the "Being with the Uṣṇīṣa. // 1 //
Having formed the vajra-bind, with the two middle fingers meeting at the thumbs, this is known as Tejorāśi, belonging to the Great-souled One Tejorāśi. // 2 //
Having formed the pair of vajra-mudrās with the little fingers joined to the thumbs, one should perform the firm hook-bind for the supreme Great Vidyā. (3)
Having formed the supreme Great Knowledge (mahāvidyottama) mudrā with firm restraint, it is known as the Heart (hṛdaya) because of the binding of the tips of the thumbs at the heart. // 4 //
Holding that very [finger] firmly with the middle fingers and the others, and turning it according to the application of the Vajra-ratna mudrā, let it rest against the mouth. // 5 //
Having indeed turned that very same [mudrā], which is positioned face-upward, over toward one's own heart, it is known by the name Catuḥpuṣpā of the Padmavidyottama. 6.
Starting from that very crown of the head, with the circle of the tips of the body revolving, this is the mudrā of the Vajra-Universal, which accomplishes vajra-activities. // 7 //
Having made the *satvavajrī* firm and joining the little fingers with the vajra-bond—this is the mudrā of this "Heart of the All-Pervader," which accomplishes everything. (8)
When the little finger and the thumb are bound together, and the three middle fingers of the left hand form a trident with the middle prong [extended], this is the grasping of the Vajra-mudrā. 9.
This is proclaimed as the Vajra-sūlā of the Supreme Vidyā-vajra;
hereafter I shall explain those known as Māyā-vajrā and the others. 10.
Having made the vajra-binding firm, one should then bind the left vajra;
this is known as the vajra-fist throughout all the vajra families. (1)
Having split that vajra in two and placed all the symbols [within them], one should establish them within the mudrās of all the vajra families. // 2 //
With the tips extended and resting on the back, the thumb of the senior [hand] grasps the lower [hand];
the syllable Oṃ is situated at the crown, and the vajra is firmly established there. // 3 //
The host of great mudrās of the Vidyārājas.
With the arms extended and resting upon the hand or likewise upon the back of the hand,
or held in the form of a fist, or turned toward the face.
The host of great mudrās of the Vajra Wrathful Deities.
The left thumb well-positioned and employed in the manner of a garland-binding,
while the right hand forms a fist with the tip of the sword [held aloft], is the sword-mudrā that bestows wealth.
The host of the great mudrās of Gaṇapati.
With her mace grasped in her right hand and her arm extended,
she displays flames from her right side and shakes her vajra-fist.
The host of messengers and great mudrās.
With the tips of her fangs bared in a haughty mien, she was struck down by the blow of a staff;
with her arms hanging limp from being drawn back, she snatched away [the victim] from both left and right.
The host of servant mahāmudrās.
The visualization of the entire mandala is performed by grasping the [left] vajra;
hereafter, I shall explain the sādhana and the ritual action itself. // 1 //
Whatever mudrā a sentient being may have, by means of that very self, one should meditate upon one's own self as the supreme accomplishment of the mudrā. (2)
The Great Protection of the Mind-Uṣṇīṣa, the Mass of Radiance, which bestows perfect accomplishment;
the Vajra-Hūṃkāra that accomplishes all, which indeed attracts everything when placed in the heart. // 3 //
The seals of the Buddha.
The supreme Vajra-Vidyā is the knower of all and the accomplisher of all;
the Great Mudrā of the Vajra-Spear bestows great accomplishment. // 1 //
The excellent accomplishment of the Māyā-vajra is indeed Ghaṇṭikā through its immersion;
Daṇḍakāṣṭhā is Nairvāṇī, while Vajravajrā is the slayer of Māra. // 2 //
The female Vidyārājas.
Jvālāgrī is the subduer of the wicked; Saumyāgrī is the slayer of all Māras;
Daṇḍāgrā is the striker; and Bhīmākṣī is indeed the terrifying one.
The Vajra Wrathful Ones.
Madanī is known as the one who intoxicates intensely; Mālā is remembered as the accomplisher of all things; Kāminī is the doer of what is dear; and Māraṇī is the slayer of all.
The mudrās of the Gaṇas.
Musalā, who destroys the wicked; Paṭā, as well as Sūtrapaṭā;
Jvālāgrī, the subduer of the wicked; and the yakṣiṇī Grahalāyikā.
The messenger mudrās:
Bhakṣaṇī is Vajradaṃṣṭrā, who slays all Māras;
Suvighnā is Vighnakartrī, who removes all obstacles; Hāriṇī is Sarvahāriṇī, who takes away everything.
The mudrās of the servants.
The detailed procedure for the great maṇḍala of the wheel of the three worlds from the *Sarvatathāgatavajrasamayamahākalparāja* is hereby completed.
The Emanation of Deities from Samādhi:
Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment Arising from the Pledge of the Vajra-Dhāraṇī of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme personal vidyā: OṂ VAJRASĀVITRE SVĀHĀ.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again spoke this supreme personal vidyā: OṂ VAJRADHĀRI HŪṂ.
Vajra-step, hūṃ phaṭ!

Then Vajrapāṇi again spoke this Vajra Maṇḍala of all the Vajra Families.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme Vajra Maṇḍala.
One should delineate the outer mandala as a square with its northern door facing outward. // 1 //
Within that, at the eastern gate in the same manner, one should install an image of the Buddha in its center, as appropriate. // 2 //
One should likewise draw the four excellent vajra-mudrās—Trilokavijayā and the others—on all sides of that maṇḍala. (3)
On all sides of those [deities], one should draw the family mudrās;
and likewise, the four gatekeepers, Vajraśauṇḍa and the others. // 4 //
One should draw Bhīmā, Śrī, Sarasvatī, and Durgā in the corners on the left;
and indeed, one should draw their respective mudrās in the outer corners. // 5 //
Furthermore, one should duly draw the goddesses in the outer maṇḍalas;
hereafter, I shall explain the detailed ritual procedure as it truly is. (6)
Regarding initiation into the maṇḍala:
here, in this vajramaṇḍala, having performed the ritual of the pledge (*samayakarma*) by means of the vajrāṅkuśa and other implements according to one's desire,
and having duly bound the mudrā of Vajradhāriṇī, [one should proceed].
One should say: "These pledge-mudrās must not be spoken of in front of anyone by you who has not seen the pledge, nor should the secret be disclosed."
Then, having placed that karma-vajra upon the Vajradhāri-mudrā, one should cause it to enter in the prescribed manner;
having caused it to enter, one should likewise cast that vajra away.
Wherever it falls, that becomes his *samayamudrā*, which brings [the deity] under control.
By means of that, one performs all activities.
Then, having released the binding of the face and shown the mandala correctly, he should explain the secret of the samaya-mudrās.
"These are your Samaya-mudrās, auspicious and performers of all rites; they are mothers, sisters, wives, daughters, and attendants. Thus it is said.
In this regard, her heart mantra is: Oṃ sarvavajragāmini sarvabhakṣe sādhaya guhyavajriṇi hūṃ phaṭ.

Then, having realized the state of the mind of universal purity, one performs all activities, even those that are the supreme mental mudrās; thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
Therefore, the mudrās of the samaya must be taught.
The fingers of the Samaya-krodha [mudrā] are firmly fixed at the head and the heart;
the hair-tuft on the face is raised upward from the mouth, and having placed them upon the head, they are made twofold. Thus, [1].
By means of the left-hand vajra-tip bind, one should press upon the prongs of the trident;

The commitments of wrath.
Pānamudrā, Mālā, Vajrā, and Ṣṭambhanāmitā;

The conventions of female servants.

Then Vajrapāṇi again spoke this own dharma-samaya: Oṃ hana hana huṃ phaṭ!
Then Vajragarbha spoke his own dharma-samaya: Oṃ hara hara hūṃ phaṭ!
Then Vajranetra proclaimed his own dharma-samaya: Oṃ mara mara hūṃ phaṭ!
Then Vajraviśva spoke his own dharma-samaya: Oṃ kuru kuru hūṃ phaṭ!
Then Vajravidyottama proclaimed his own dharma-samaya: Oṃ huṃ huṃ phaṭ!
Then Māyāvajra said: Oṃ cchinda cchinda hūṃ phaṭ!

Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ hūṃ phaṭ.

The Vidyārājas and Nakas.

Having said this,

From the *Sarvatathāgatavajrasamaya*, the Great King of Kalpas, the detailed ritual procedure for the *Sarvavajrakuladharmasamayamaṇḍala* is completed.

Then Vajrapāṇi again spoke his own supreme rite: [Oṃ vajravilāse pūjaya hūṃ]. Then Vajragarbha spoke his own supreme rite: Oṃ vajrābhiṣeke abhiṣiñce hūṃ.

The delineation of the maṇḍala:

Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme maṇḍala of ritual action;
one should delineate every maṇḍala by means of the yoga of the Vajra-maṇḍala. // 1 //
All the tips of the mandalas are situated in the center of the Buddhas;
one should indeed arrange the Mahāsattvas in a row in successive order. // 2 //
In its center, one should personally worship Vajravidyottama together with his consort, using the secret dance-worship of Vajralāsyā and the others.
Therein, the goddesses, in due order, through the yoga of the wheel-maṇḍala, should be depicted as dancing with their own mudrās and counter-mudrās. // 4 //
"For the sake of worship, by means of the application of the Vajra-dance of the Buddha and Vajrin, incense and the other offerings should be placed in the four gates in their proper order. (5)

Next, regarding the mudrās in this ritual maṇḍala: having performed the rites of summoning and so forth, and having duly bound the Vajradhāri-karmasamayamudrā, one should speak as follows: “This secret rite must not be told by you to anyone who has not seen the assembly of deities or who is ignorant of the ritual.”

Then, having entered himself [the deity], he says, "Enter," and performs the worship of dance and offerings with hand gestures (mudrā) and counter-gestures (pratimudrā).
From that time forward, he accomplishes all activities as desired through the vajra-mudrās of body, speech, vision, and mind.
Then, having released the binding of the face,

One should indeed perform the worship of Vajralāsyā and the others for Vajravidyottama. // 1 //
And one should worship the ritual maṇḍala with all the vidyās, in their proper order and according to the rules, through offerings of dance and ritual gifts. // 2 //
By means of the application of the vajra dance, one should contract the great mudrās;
having doubled the supreme pledge, one should resolve it as the counter-mudrā. // 3 //
By worshipping all the leaders with these offerings of dance, the accomplishment of the activities of Mahāvajradhara and the others will certainly be attained. (4) Thus it is said.
The detailed ritual procedure for the activity maṇḍala of all vajra families from the *Sarvatathāgatavajrasamayamahākalparāja* is hereby completed.
