"Command me: what is that secret of the Tathāgata? Thus [he asked].
Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Secret Vajra of All Tathāgatas and spoke this secret of all Tathāgatas:
"In whatever way all sentient beings are to be disciplined according to their own nature,
in that very way one who is pure through passion and the rest should act for the sake of sentient beings."
Then Vajrapāṇi spoke this secret of his own:
"For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings and for the cause of the Buddha's teaching,
one may kill all sentient beings, yet one is not stained by sin."
Then the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha spoke this secret of his own jewel,
for the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, through the application of the Buddha-body.
But one who has taken away all anxieties is not defiled by sin.
Then the Bodhisattva Vajranetra spoke this secret of his own dharma:
"Purity from passion is incomparable bliss, arising from the gift of the Victor’s domain;
he who consorts with the wives of others attains merit."
Then the Bodhisattva Vajraviśva spoke this secret of his own activity:
"For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings and for the cause of the Buddha's teaching, by performing all activities while uttering 'Vaṃ,' one attains great merit. Thus it was said.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, praised the Blessed Guhyadhārī Vajradhara with words of approval.
Excellent for you, Vajrasattva; excellent for you, Vajraratna;
excellent for you, Vajradharma; excellent for you, Vajrakarman!
This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna, the secret of all Tathāgatas, and the compendium of the Mahāyāna. Thus it is said.
The Great Ritual King named "The Vajra Samaya of All Tathāgatas," from the Compendium of the Reality of All Tathāgatas, is hereby completed.

Then all the Tathāgatas, having again assembled in a great gathering, requested the Blessed One, the Lord of All Dharmas, Avalokiteśvara— that very Vajradhara— by means of this hymn of one hundred and eight names.
O Padmasattva, Mahāpadma, Lokeśvara, Maheśvara, Avalokiteśa, foremost of the wise, Vajradharma—homage be to you! // 1 //
O Dharmarāja, Greatly Pure One; O King of Beings, Great-minded One;
O Lotus-natured One, Great Lotus, Lord of the Lotus—homage be to you! // 2 //
O Lotus-born one, with the splendor of a beautiful lotus, pure as a lotus and a perfect purifier; O you whose limbs are like a vajra-lotus, the most excellent lotus—homage be to you! // 3 //
O Great Universe, O Great World, O Great Task, O Great Paragon;
O Greatly Steadfast, O Great Hero, O Great Śauri—homage be to you! // 4 //
O intention of sentient beings, Mahāyāna, Mahāyoga, Grandfather;
O Śambhu, Śaṅkara, Pure Purpose, Buddha Padma—homage be to you! // 5 //
O you who have realized the true meaning of the nature of phenomena, the True Dharma, the Pure Dharma, and the Excellent Dharma;
O Great Dharma, the Foremost of the Good Dharma, the Wheel of Dharma—homage be to you! // 6 //
O Buddha-being, supreme among true beings, Dharma-being who sustains true beings, highest of beings, knower of true beings, being of beings—homage be to you! // 7 //
O Avalokiteśvara, supreme protector, great lord who beholds all, light of lights, for the sake of the world, lord of the world—homage be to you! //8//

O Great One, whose eyes are the world, the imperishable, the foremost of the imperishable, comparable to the imperishable; O All-Eyed One, the imperishable among the imperishable, the imperishable wheel—homage be to you! // 9 //
O lotus-handed one, O great-handed one, O consoler, O giver!
O Buddha-dharma, O Great Buddha, O you whose very nature is the Buddha—homage be to you! 10.
O Buddha-form, great form, vajra-form, possessor of beautiful form! O supreme light of the Dharma, most brilliant radiance, illuminator of the world—homage be to you! // 11 //
O Lord Padmaśrīnātha, foremost of lords, Dharmaśrīnātha, possessor of lords;
O Brahmanātha, Great Brahmā, Son of Brahmā, homage be to you! (12)
O Lamp, foremost of lamps, light of the lamp, excellent illuminator;
O Lord of the Lamp, Great Lamp, Lamp of the Buddha—homage be to you! (13)
O you who are consecrated by the Buddhas, O foremost of Buddhas, O son of the Buddha, O great wise one;
O you whose head is the supreme consecration of the Buddhas, O Buddha of Buddhas—homage be to you! 14.
O Buddha-eye, Great Eye, Dharma-eye, Great Seer;
O you whose entire essence is the knowledge of meditative absorption, Vajra-eye, homage be to you! 15.
Whoever thus contemplates or praises these one hundred and eight secondary names of yours with their whole being shall attain sovereignty over the world.
"We entreat you, O Hero, O Great Sage: having manifested your own family, reveal the supreme mandala of the Dharma. (17) Thus [they said].
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara, having heard the words of entreaty from all the Tathāgatas,
stood facing the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni,
and placing that vajra-lotus upon his own heart, uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! This vajra-lotus of mine is indeed supremely pure;
I am its father and it is my son—bless this family! Thus he spoke.
The Emanation of the Deities from Samādhi:

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Lotus Arising from the Samaya of the Vajra-Dharma of All Tathāgatas," and from his own heart he emitted this Heart-Mantra of All Tathāgatas, known as the "Dharma-Samaya of All Tathāgatas": *hrīḥ*.
Then, as soon as this had emerged, rays of light in the form of lotuses, possessing various colors, forms, marks, and modes of movement, issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.
Having purified the knowledge of the reality-nature (dharmatā) regarding passion and other afflictions throughout all world-systems,
they returned once more and entered the heart of Noble Avalokiteśvara.
Then the Blessed One spoke the supreme self-knowledge called the Dharma-Samaya of All Tathāgatas: Oṃ vajrapadmottama hrīḥ.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge: Oṃ vajra hūṃ phaṭ.
Then the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme mantra of his own vidyā: Oṃ vajraratnottama traḥ.
Then the Bodhisattva Vajranetra recited this supreme mantra of his own vidyā: Oṃ vajravidyottama hrīḥ.
Then the Bodhisattva Vajraviśva spoke this supreme mantra of his own vidyā: Oṃ vajraviśvottama aḥ.

Then indeed, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara entered the samādhi called "Manifestation of All Forms" and uttered this own heart-mantra called "The Commitment for the Discipline of the Entire World":
Oṃ huṃ hrīḥ hoḥ.

Then, as soon as this was spoken, from the heart of the noble Avalokiteśvara, that very Blessed One Vajradhara emerged, having assumed the forms of great bodhisattvas who bore the likeness of the noble Avalokiteśvara; they were established upon lotuses, bore the insignia of the lotus seal, and possessed diverse colors, forms, dress, and ornaments; they manifested the bodies of all sentient beings, beginning with the Tathāgatas.

Having manifested their own forms in all world-systems according to the needs of those to be trained, and having accomplished the discipline of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder,
they returned once more and,
through the yoga of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm, took their places upon moon-maṇḍalas on all sides of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, and uttered this inspired utterance:
Oh, how wonderful is the skillful means of all the Buddhas, whose very nature is compassion,
by which even gods are indeed disciplined through such means!
The delineation of the maṇḍala:

Then the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, having generated his own family and having offered it to all the Tathāgatas for the sake of attaining the supreme accomplishment of fearlessness for all sentient beings and the fruit of obtaining the knowledge and supernormal powers of the vajra-dharmatā, [proceeded].
He spoke the great maṇḍala named Sarvajagadvinaya.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme great maṇḍala, which resembles the Vajradhātu and is known as Jagadvinaya. (1)
It is square, with four gates, adorned with four archways, joined by four lines, and decorated with silk ribbons, garlands, and festoons. // 2 //
In all the corners of the maṇḍala and at the junctions of the gates and projections, one should mark out the outer maṇḍala, inlaid with vajra-jewels. // 3 //
Within that, one should draw a square line;
for the second, one should fashion the corners of the doors in the shape of lotuses.
By means of the application of eight pillars, one should draw an eight-petaled lotus;
in the center of its filaments, one should place the image of the Buddha. // 5 //
In this regard, the heart-mantra for entering the Buddha is: *buddha hūṃ*.
The Buddhas are to be depicted everywhere, established within the centers of lotuses;
likewise, the vajra, the jewel, the lotus, and the double lotus.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows: Oṃ.
Huḥ.
Wisdom.
Kṛḥ.
Having emerged with the speed of a vajra into the maṇḍala for the conversion of the world, one should there visualize Lokeśvara, manifesting all forms. //1//
On all his sides, through the yoga of Vajragarva and the others, one should depict the great beings, the Buddhas and so forth, who bear the lotus insignia. // 2 //
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows: Oṃ tathāgatadharma hūṃ / Oṃ vajrapadmāṅkuśa kośadhara vajrasattva hūṃ phaṭ //
Oṃ, slay, slay! O you who hold the lotus-flower weapon, whose arrow is unerring! Hoḥ!
Oṃ padmasaṃbhava padmahasta sādhu hūṃ!
Having entered the second maṇḍala with vajra-velocity, one should likewise draw the Tathāgata in the midst of the matted locks in its center. (1)
On all its sides, one should duly paint, in proper sequence, those bearing the lotus insignia, through the application of frowning expressions and so forth. // 2 //
In that regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
HŪṂ.
Oṃ padmabhṛkuṭi traḥ.
Oṃ, lotus-sun, blaze, hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Padmamaṇiketudhara Candra Avalokiteśvara, gladden me; grant me all aims quickly! Samaya hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Lotus-Laughter, Eleven-Faced One! Haḥ haḥ haḥ haḥ hūṃ!
Having entered the third mandala with vajra-velocity, one should likewise draw the Great Being seated upon a lotus. // 1 //
On all its sides, in due order and according to the rule, one should introduce the Great Beings by means of the application of the light of the lotus and so forth. // 2 //
In this regard, these are their heart-mantras:
DHAḤ.
Oṃ, Tārā, look upon me with your lotus eye; Samayasattva, hūṃ!
Oṃ, Padmakumāra, wielder of the lotus-power, cut, cut with the sword! Hūṃ phaṭ!

Oṃ! Padma Nīlakaṇṭha, you who hold the conch, discus, mace, and lotus in your hands; you who are clothed in a tiger skin; you whose sacred thread is made of a black serpent; you whose upper garment on the left shoulder is of deerskin; you who bear the form of Nārāyaṇa; three-eyed one, let out a loud laugh and cause [them] to enter! Grant me the pledges and bestow upon me accomplishment, O Avalokiteśvara! Hūṃ!
Oṃ! Brahmā, born from the lotus, recite, recite! O Lotus-Speaker, hūṃ!
Having advanced with vajra-impetus to the fourth mandala, one should there draw a four-faced lotus holding a lotus and a trident. // 1 //
On all its sides, the Great Beings (mahāsattva) bearing the lotus insignia should be depicted according to the ritual procedure, through the application of the Vajra-dance and other [mudrās]. // 2 //
In this regard, their heart-verses are as follows: three.

Oṃ, Padmanarteśvara, dance, dance! Worship all the Tathāgatas! Draw forth the Vajra-karma-samaya! Cause them to enter! Bind them! Cause them to possess [me]! Grant me the accomplishment of all activities, O Avalokiteśvara!
Hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Avalokiteśvara, giver of fearlessness! Protect, bind, and place the lotus armor; by the power of the samaya, haṃ!
Oṃ! O Great Fierce One, you of universal form, with terrifying faces made formidable by the jagged fangs of a lotus, strike fear into all! O Lotus Yakṣa, devour, devour! Shame, shame, shame, shame!
Oṃ, lotus-fist, you who are the pledge, bind! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Having advanced with vajra-velocity, one should draw [the deities] in all the corners;
by means of the yoga of Vajralāsyā and the others, one should draw the deities Padmalāsyā and the rest.
In this regard, these mudrās are as follows:
Oṃ padmalāsye rāgaya mahādevi rāgapūjāsamaye hūṃ.
Oṃ padmamāle abhiṣiñca abhiṣeka-pūjā-samaye hūṃ.
Oṃ, O Padmagīte, sing! At the time of the song-offering, hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Lotus Dance, dance at the time of initiating all worship, hūṃ!
Having emerged with vajra-velocity to the vicinity of the outer maṇḍala,
one should draw the four offering goddesses, Padma, Dhūpā, and the others.
In this regard, these are the offering mudrās:
Oṃ, at the time of the lotus incense offering, gladden [me], O beloved of the lotus lineage, O great leader, O delight of the lotus, hūṃ!
Oṃ! At the time of the offering of lotus flowers, O dweller in the lotus, O Great Śrī, O gatekeeper of the Lotus Family, accomplish all aims! Hūṃ!
Oṃ! At the time of the lotus-lamp offering, O beautiful one of the lotus family, O great messenger, produce illumination; O Padmasarasvatī, hūṃ!
Oṃ, at the time of the offering of lotus fragrance, O great female servant of the Lotus family, perform all my activities; lotus-accomplishment, hūṃ!
Then all the Gaṇas and others should be depicted correctly at the four lotus-doors, according to the meaning of their heart-mantras. Thus it is said.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ Hayagrīva, draw forth all those bound by the pledge of the Lotus Family with the great lotus-hook quickly; O holder of the lotus-hook, hūṃ jjaḥ!

Oṃ! Infallible Lotus Noose! O Wrathful One, draw forth and cause to enter! You who wear the garments of Mahāpaśupati, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and Brahmā; O Lotus Family, [bind] the commitments! Hūṃ hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Padmasphoṭa, bind all the commitments of the Lotus family; quickly! Hūṃ Vaṃ!

Oṃ! Six-faced one, wearing the guise of Sanatkumāra, cause the entry [of the deity] with the lotus-bell; bind all the pledges (*samaya*) of the Lotus Family and all the mudrās; bestow upon me all accomplishments (*siddhi*). O Padmāveśa! Aḥ Aḥ! Aḥ Aḥ Aḥ!
Now follows the detailed procedure for the lotus maṇḍala for the training of all living beings.
Therein, at the very beginning, the Lotus Master, having bound the Vajra-Lotus Samaya-mudrā and entered in the prescribed manner,
One should perform the ritual action through the yoga of the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu with these heart-mantras: Oṃ padmasphoṭādhitiṣṭha aḥ.
Then, having likewise received the command and likewise consecrated himself with the *samayamudrā*,
he took up the lotus-form.
Having recited the names of one's own lotuses and performed the ritual action with the lotus, goad, and so forth,
one should then accomplish the Great Being by means of those very same Dharma-mudrās.
Therefore, accomplishment is achieved in that very same way.
Then one should cause the lotus-disciples to enter.
Therein, first of all, one should give the Heart of the Oath to the lotus-disciple, saying:
"Today, you yourself must become the Lotus Being (Padmasattva)."
Then he should command: "This detailed procedure for the secret rite must not be told by you to anyone;
lest you fall into hell."
And by failing to avoid danger, one meets their end."
Then, one should bind the pledge-mudrā with this heart-mantra: Oṃ vajrapadmasamayastvaṃ.
Then, wearing a white upper garment and having covered his face with a white-red cloth, he should cause him to enter while reciting this heart-mantra: OṂ PADMASAMAYA HŪṂ.
Then, having performed the ritual actions as prescribed, one should place a lotus-form in the hand [of the disciple], saying: *oṃ padmahasta vajradharmatāṃ pālaya*.
He should say, "Of what nature is this vajra-dharmatā?
Then it should be said:
"Just as this red lotus is not defiled by defects of its lineage."
One should meditate upon the purity of all things; thus, one is not defiled by sins.
This is the nature of things here.
Then, one should teach the mudrā and the knowledge of the lotus family:
one should draw a lotus at the heart through the meditation on the lotus within the heart.
One would bring even Padmaśrī under one's control, let alone an inferior woman.
One should draw the image of the Buddha on the forehead and meditate upon it constantly;
through that meditation, one swiftly attains empowerment. // 2 //
One should visualize the image of the Buddha in the mouth, specifically upon the tongue;
thus the goddess Sarasvatī herself dwells constantly within one's mouth. (3)

Having placed the lotus within the uṣṇīṣa while remaining in meditative equipoise, one who visualizes the lotus in the uṣṇīṣa shall become a sky-walker and bring [others] under control. Thus [it is said]. // 4 //
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
"O Padmaśrī, bring [him] under control! Hoḥ!"
Bestow the lotus consecration; Vam!
Padmasarasvatī, purify! Hūṃ.
Subjugate those who move above the lotus! JJAḤ!
These are the knowledge-mantras of the mudrās of the Lotus family.
Whether visualizing an excellent lotus on a wall or in open space, this is the supreme method for bringing all sentient beings under one's control. // 1 //
Whether in the sky or in another place, while visualizing an excellent lotus, when one sees it, then one should grasp it; by choice, one shall attain invisibility. // 2 //
Whether on a wall or in open space, one should meditate upon the Viśvapadma; by seeing and grasping it, one then becomes possessed of the universal form (viśvarūpī). // 3 //
One should visualize a vajra-lotus either in the sky or in another location;
by grasping that very instant, one becomes a Padma-vidyādhara. // 4 //
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ, enter the wisdom-lotus of mastery over the entire world, Aḥ!
Oṃ, O Wisdom Lotus, remain; make [me] invisible! Vaṃ.
Oṃ, O Samādhi Universal Lotus, abide! O Blessed One, manifest your universal form! Ḍhaḥ!
Oṃ, O Samādhi Vajra Lotus, abide! Arise quickly! Hrīḥ!
Having painted Lokeśvara everywhere within the mandalas and other such diagrams,
one should summon him before it using the supreme Hayagrīva mudrā.
Having painted Lokeśvara within mandalas and other such settings, he shall indeed bring the world under his control by means of the Amoghapāśa mudrā. // 2 //
Having depicted Lokeśvara everywhere within the mandalas and other such areas,
one should perform the binding in front of him with the Padmasphoṭāgra mudrā.
Having painted Lokeśvara in mandalas and other such settings, the supreme induction of all [powers] occurs before him by means of the lotus and bell. Thus, [verse] 4.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ, draw in all the great beings with the foot-hook! Hūṃ Jaḥ!
Oṃ Amoghapāśa Krodha Hūṃ Hoḥ!
Oṃ padmasphoṭa vaṃ.
Oṃ, Padmaghaṇṭā, cause all to enter! Aḥ.
One should visualize oneself as a being with four lotus-faces;
then, having accomplished one's own self, one becomes possessed of many forms in an instant. // 1 //
Meditating upon one's own self as a lotus within a lotus by means of oneself, and abiding in the Vajradharma samādhi, one attains the imperishable lotus. // 2 //
Visualizing himself within the matted locks of Lokeśvara, one’s own self becomes like Amitāyus, the form of the Buddha. // 3 //
Meditating by himself through the samādhi of the Universal Form, one who abides in the samādhi of the Universal Form becomes equal to Lokeśvara. Thus [it is said]. //4//
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Padmaviśva.
The lotus of the Dharmakāya.
The empowerment of the Buddhas.
Lokeśvara.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of all the mudrās of the great maṇḍala.
First, regarding entry therein, there is the knowledge of the great mudrā:
[one should visualize oneself] situated in the center of a moon disc, according to the manner of the painted [image].
One should personally meditate upon oneself as being established upon a lotus for the sake of sentient beings. Thus it is said.
Now follows their ritual application.
By binding the great mudrā of the Buddha, one becomes equal to Amitāyus;
by joining the vajra and lotus, one becomes equal to Lokeśvara. // 1 //
Having bound the Buddha-abhiṣeka mudrā, he is indeed consecrated by the Sugatas;
the Padma and Padmā [mudrās] bestow the samādhi, while the Viśva [mudrā] grants universal sovereignty. // 2 //
The Buddha displays his manifold forms for those to be trained, bestowing the jewel-consecration;
likewise, he manifests Padmasattva, the Samādhi, Padmakrodheśvarī, and Śrī. (3)
Vajralokeśvarī bestows supreme accomplishment; Padmarāgiṇī [bestows] Buddhahood; and Vajrapadmā, the Mistress of Buddhas, grants excellent success. // 4 //
Kāmeśvarī bestows great passion; Tuṣṭi grants goodness;
Bhṛkuṭī pacifies anger; Padmasūryā bestows great splendor. (5)
Padmacandrā bestows great splendor; Hāsā, a beautiful smile; through Tārā, supreme accomplishment; and through Padmakhaṅgā, enjoyment.
Nīlakaṇṭhā is the great attractor; Paṇḍaravāsinī is accomplishment;
Padmanarteśvarī is accomplishment; and Abhayā bestows fearlessness. // 7 //
Pracaṇḍā is the subduer of the wicked; Padmamuṣṭi is the excellent accomplisher; Lāsyā [bestows] delight; Mālā [bestows] wealth; Gītā [bestows] everything; and Nṛtyā [bestows] happiness. // 8 //
Incense [bestows] delight, flowers [bestow] auspiciousness, lamps [bestow] vision, and fragrance [bestows] a sweet scent. // 9 //
Hayagrīvā is for summoning; Amoghā brings [beings] under control;
Padmasphoṭā is the great binding; and Ghaṇṭikā effects the possession of all. // 10 //
Then follows the knowledge of the pledge-seal (*samayamudrā*) of the Lotus Family:
having formed the *vajrabandha* and joined the thumbs and little fingers together, this is the seal of the Dharma-pledge (*dharmasamayā*), which bestows the qualities of a Buddha. (1)
Having formed the vajra-bond, with the tips of the thumbs and middle fingers joined together—this is the mudrā of the Supreme Vidyā of the Buddha, which bestows the state of Buddhahood. // 2 //
Having formed the vajra-binding, with the middle fingers joined in the vajra-position—this is the mudrā of Vajravidyottama, which bestows the state of a vajra-holder. // 3 //
That very same [mudrā], when with a jewel in the center, is the bestower of the vajra-jewel;
through the application of the central bud, it is the bestower of lotus-accomplishment. // 4 //
By joining the vajra-añjali mudrā, one becomes a performer of vajra-activities; by holding the dharma-vajrā mudrā, the samaya is accomplished in an instant. // 5 //
The vajra-binding, when joined at the tips, bestows the siddhis of the Buddhas; hereafter, I shall explain specifically the satva-mudrās. // 6 //
Having formed the vajra-añjali and likewise arisen with the hands held level, the little fingers and thumbs extended outward is proclaimed as the Viśvapadma [mudrā]. // 7 //
That very [mudrā], with the thumbs forming a cross-legged posture and the tips of the fingers slightly curled,
with a vajra at its center and a mass of matted hair upon the head, is celebrated as the Jaṭābuddha.
Having made the vajra-bind firm with the thumbs joined together below, the two index fingers are contracted; this is the mudrā arising from meditative absorption (samādhi). // 9 //
Having formed the palms together in the *añjali* gesture, with the two index fingers pressed like a vajra and the tips of the two thumbs opened wide, this is the mudrā of Amogheśvara. 10.
Having made the vajra-binding firm, one should bind it with the palms turned upward;
when the thumbs are joined together in the lotus position, it is proclaimed as the Padmabuddha mudrā. // 11 //
With the tips of the two thumbs joined like a vajra, one forms the hook and likewise the sword; with the opening of the final two fingers, the middle and ring fingers form buds at their tips.
Having formed the *samājañjali* with the thumbs bent and curled,
one should draw [the deity] in by seizing the index finger with the index finger of the lotus-arrow mudrā.
One should likewise form the palms joined and turned upward; this is the Sādhumudrā.
It bestows the cry of "Excellent! (Sādhukāra) and is celebrated as the Sādhupadma.

Having firmly joined the palms together with the tips of the fingers slightly curved and held against the face, the two little fingers are spread apart; this is called the Padmabhṛkuṭi mudrā. // 15 //
Having made the vajra-bind firmly, one should extend it toward the heart; this is known as Padmasūryā, with all the fingers forming a beautiful mandala. 16.
Having firmly formed an equal añjali with the two index fingers joined like jewels, the lotus, jewel, and banner-tip [mudrās] are extended over the head with the arms outstretched. // 17 //
Having extended the vajra-bind at the crown of the head together with the front faces, she becomes eleven-faced through her own face and the [face of] loud laughter. // 18 //
Joining the lotus-like hands with the thumbs raised together is the mudrā of Padmatāra; it bestows all accomplishments. (19)
The mudrā of Padmatāra is formed by the supreme binding of the lotus yoga;
this is the mudrā of Padmakhaḍga through the application of the sword-shape. // 20 //
The *kuḍmalāntya* is the great lotus;
likewise, the *aṅguṣṭhagadā* is formed by curling the tips [of the fingers] into a great conch while employing the vajra-bind.

Having firmly formed the vajra-añjali mudrā, it is encircled by the letter Oṃ on the right; the tip of the left thumb is used for recitation, while all the fingers are fully expanded like a blossoming lotus. // 22 //
Having joined the vajra-fingers on both the left and right, dancing with graceful movements, she stands upon the head as the Dancing Lotus. 23.
Having made the vajra-añjali firm, likewise [forming] the armor of all the fingertips, and having rotated it with the lotus, one places it at the heart; this is the "Firm-Maker. 24.
Having firmly formed the vajra-añjali through the application of the Guhya-yakṣa, the Padma-yakṣiṇī has her cupped hands extended and placed at her mouth. // 25 //
Having formed the vajra-fist and bent the two middle fingers, placing them upon the backs of one's own thumbs, this is declared to be the lotus-fist (padmamuṣṭi). // 26 //
Through the application of the Vajradhātu, arising from the vajra-añjali gesture, one should bind the supreme pledge of all the foremost goddesses of worship. (27)
Having made the vajra-bind firm, one should join the two index fingers; by drawing them together in front, it is proclaimed as the Hayagrīva mudrā. (28)
Having formed the lotus-añjali mudrā, with the two index fingers bound together, this is the Amoghapāśa mudrā; the index fingers and thumbs are linked like a chain.

Having formed the lotus-palms gesture through the application of the vajra-entrance, one should press together the two thumbs within the space between the little fingers and the ring fingers. (30) Thus it is said.
Now follows the knowledge of the Dharma-mudrās of the Lotus family:
hrī, grī, prī, hī, śrī.
Sī, dī, hīḥ, gī, dhī, krī, vī, vi, rī, ṣṭrī, aḥ.
Having formed the lotus-fist in two ways, one should perform the action seals (karmamudrās). Thus it is said.
The detailed procedure for the great maṇḍala for the discipline of the entire world, from the *Sarvatathāgatadharmasamayā-mahākalparāja*, is completed.
The Emanation of Deities from Samādhi:

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Lotus Empowerment of the Mudrā Arising from the Samaya of the Dharma-Dhāraṇī of All Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme personal vidyā: OṂ SARVATATHĀGATADHARMASAMAYE HŪṂ.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this supreme vidyā born of his own family: OṂ VAJRASAMAYE HŪṂ.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme personal vidyā: Oṃ maṇiratnasamaye hūṃ.
Then the Bodhisattva Vajranetra spoke this supreme personal vidyā: Oṃ padmasamaye hūṃ.
Then the Bodhisattva Vajraviśva spoke this supreme self-knowledge mantra: Oṃ karmasamaye hūṃ.
Then the Blessed One, the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, spoke this maṇḍala of the samaya-mudrās of his own family.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme maṇḍala of mudrās, which resembles the Vajradhātu and is known as the Secret Lotus (Padmaguhya). //1//
By means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala, one should delineate the entire maṇḍala;
in its center, upon an excellent lotus, one should indeed draw Vajradhātvīśvarī. //2//
On all sides of that, as above, the foremost of the Samayas, such as Dharmavajrī and the others, should be drawn, joined with their respective vidyās. // 3 //
In that regard, their mudrās are as follows:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatadharmeśvari hūṃ.
Oṃ, O Dharma-samaya Vajrapadminī, hūṃ! Oṃ, O Buddha-abhiṣeka Ratna-samaya, hūṃ!
Oṃ Tārā, remain in your pledge! Hūṃ.
Oṃ, to the one whose face is the universe, hūṃ!
Having emerged with vajra-velocity, one should draw a lotus in the center of that supreme maṇḍala of universal forms, surrounded by lotuses. (1)
On all its sides, lotus seals are established; the lotus emblems, which are the respective seals of the Sugatas, should be painted there. (2)
In that regard, their mudrās are as follows: Hrīḥ.
Oṃ Padmatathāgata!
Oṃ, Samantabhadra, you who hold the lotus, vajra, and hook in your sheath, hūṃ!
Oṃ padmarati / Oṃ padmatuṣṭi.
Having proceeded with vajra-velocity likewise into the second mandala, the consecrations of the Buddhas should be painted; in the midst of their matted locks is a great lotus. // 1 //
On all its sides, one should duly and in proper sequence establish the supreme pledges, each accompanied by the lotus emblem.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Śrīḥ.
Oṃ bhṛkuṭi taṭi vetaṭi padme hūṃ!
Oṃ padmajvāle hūṃ.
Oṃ somini padme hūṃ.
Oṃ, O Lotus-laughing one, eleven-faced one, diri diri, īṭṭe vaṭṭe, moving one, swaying one, bearer of flowers, ili, enter! Grant me success, hūṃ!
Having advanced with vajra-impetus to the third mandala likewise, one should place the lotus mudrā there in the center upon a beautiful lotus. // 1 //
In the same way, on all sides, one should draw them in due order as prescribed, each seated upon a lotus and marked with the lotus emblem. // 2 //
In this regard, their mudrās are as follows:
Dhīḥ.
Oṃ tāre tuttāre hūṃ.
Oṃ dhī hūṃ.
Oṃ, O holder of the lotus, the wheel, and the mace, O blue-throated one, accomplish, accomplish, hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Pāṇḍaravāsinī, born from the lotus, speak, speak, hūṃ!
Having entered with the speed of a vajra into the center of the fourfold, supreme mandala, one should draw a lotus in the middle of the lotus, its radiance filled with garlands of flames. (1)
On all its sides, in due order and as prescribed, lotus-marked figures should be painted, each established within the center of a lotus.
In this regard, their mudrās are as follows:
women.
Oṃ Padmanarteśvarī, worship all the Tathāgatas! Naṭṭa naṭṭa hūṃ!
Oṃ Abhayā, you who bind the lotus armor, protect me! Hūṃ haṃ!
Oṃ, O Mahāpracaṇḍī, Padmayakṣiṇī, you who assume all forms, terrify all the wicked! Eat, eat! Hūṃ Phaṭ!
Oṃ padmamuṣṭi aḥ muḥ.
Having approached with vajra-velocity, one should depict the offerings to the Buddhas;
the mudrās such as Padmāṅkuśī and others have, in brief, the lotus as their emblem. Thus it is said.
Now, their mudrās are as follows:
Oṃ padmaratipūje hoḥ!
Oṃ, to the lotus consecration offering, raṭ!
Oṃ, to the worship of the lotus-song: Gīḥ!
Oṃ, to the lotus dance-offering, kṛt!
Oṃ dhūpapadmini hūṃ.
Oṃ padmapuṣpi hūṃ.
Oṃ, O beautiful one of the Lotus family, illuminate the Dharma; worship, hūṃ!
Oṃ padmagandhe hūṃ.
The offering goddesses:
Oṃ, Padmāṅkuśī, attract the great Lotus family! Hayagrīva, by your pledge, hūṃ jaḥ!
Oṃ, at the time of the wrathful Amoghapāśa, enter, cause [them] to enter, all samayas! Hūṃ!
Oṃ padma-śaṅkale vaṃ.
Oṃ, O holder of the lotus and bell, quickly cause the pledges to enter; O six-faced one, Aḥ!
Then, having performed the detailed ritual procedures for summoning and so forth in this maṇḍala of mudrās,
and having caused the lotus-disciples to enter in the proper manner,
one should speak thus: "You must not tell anyone about the secret that is here."
"Lest you fall into hell, and lest there be sufferings in this very life"—
having thus induced possession, one should speak as follows.
“What kind of appearance is there in the path of their vision?
It is as follows: ‘Success (siddhi) is according to what one says.
If one should see white light, one should teach him the knowledge of supreme success.”
Then, if he should see yellow, he should teach him the knowledge for the production of wealth;
then, if he should see red, he should teach him the knowledge for winning over others;
then, if he should see black, he should teach him the knowledge for performing malevolent rites.

Then, having understood that "if one should see a variegated [vision], one should thereafter teach the knowledge of all accomplishments (*siddhi*)," he should release the face-binding as appropriate and generate the various knowledges according to the disciple's capacity as a vessel.
And one should teach the knowledge of the mudrās.
In this way, within all mandalas such as the Vajradhātu and others, one should teach the knowledges of the mudrās according to the capacity of the recipient; this is the examination.
The knowledge of the accomplishment of the four supreme siddhis arises;
one becomes the Great Being Lokeśvara, possessing a universal form by means of one's own self.
But by meditating upon the supreme Mahāmudrā, one shall attain accomplishment. // 1 //
Having made firm the commitment of the Buddha-consecration and being composed in meditative absorption, one who visualizes oneself [as the deity] attains the supreme accomplishment. // 2 //
One should visualize oneself as the Great Being Padmapadma; being well-composed, one attains for oneself the supreme accomplishment. // 3 //
By accomplishing the self-arisen action-seal (karmamudrā) consisting of Amogheśvara according to the prescribed ritual, one shall swiftly attain the supreme siddhi. Thus it is said.
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ padmasattvo ’haṃ sidhya hoḥ.
Oṃ, I am the consecration of the Buddhas; grant me success!
Oṃ, may I be established as the Samādhi of Dharma; Hoḥ!
Oṃ, I am Amogheśvara; grant me success!
Then there arises the knowledge of the accomplishment of the purpose.
Having pierced gold in the mouth, one should meditate upon it by oneself;
the single Great Mudrā of Viśveśvara shall become a thousandfold. // 1 //
Taking a tola of gold, with the supreme pledge and great firmness, meditating upon himself, he alone shall become a thousandfold.
Having placed a pearl in one's mouth, one should contemplate one's own self as the Lord of the World; being one, one becomes a thousandfold.
Having gathered all jewels with both hands in the *karmamudrā*, while visualizing oneself as the deity, one may become a thousandfold. Thus, [verse] 4.
In that regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ padmahiraṇyaprada huṃ jjaḥ.
Oṃ, bestower of lotus-gold, hūṃ jjaḥ!
Oṃ, you who bestow lotuses and pearls, hūṃ jjaḥ!
Oṃ, O bestower of all jewels from the lotus, hūṃ jjaḥ!
Then there is the knowledge of winning over others:
"Meditating upon himself as the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) of Viśveśvara, he stands before someone holding a lotus; that person becomes enamored of him. (1)
Firmly grasping a red lotus with the Great Samaya Mudrā, and visualizing oneself as [the deity], one shall enchant all women. // 2 //
One should personally visualize oneself as a secret lotus in whatever manner appropriate; indeed, by gazing with the vajra-vision, one shall cause all the world to be filled with passion. // 3 //

By means of the application of the *karmamudrā*, having taken hold of the lotus according to the ritual procedure, one should cause all women to experience passion by rotating the thread with both hands. Thus, [verse] 4.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ viśveśvara mahāpadma hoḥ.
Oṃ samayapadma hoḥ.
Oṃ yogapadma hoḥ.
Oṃ karmapadma hoḥ.
Now follows the knowledge of malevolent rites (*abhicāra*):
while visualizing oneself as the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) of Viśveśvara, one should sever the lotus situated before the victim; his death will occur in an instant. (1)
Having firmly and correctly grasped the lotus with that very same supreme pledge-seal, one should tear apart the most solid thread; by whose name [it is torn], he perishes. // 2 //
Having formed the mudrā of meditative concentration, one should likewise [hold] the secret lotus;
indeed, he by whose name the lotus is severed shall perish. // 3 //

"By means of the application of the *karmamudrā*, one should seize the lotus according to the ritual procedure; if one is enraged, he should burst it open, and his life shall indeed burst asunder. Thus [ends verse] 4.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ mahāpadma ccheda māraya hoḥ phaṭ.
Oṃ, O Samayapadma, burst it open, destroy it! Raṭ phaṭ!
Oṃ, O Lotus of Dharma, cut and destroy! Dhṛṭ phaṭ!
Oṃ! O lotus of karma, burst it, burst it! [Take] his life! Kṛt phaṭ!
Then follows the secret knowledge of the mudrā of the Dharma-samaya:
one should visualize a lotus for women, and upon that, a vajra oneself.
By means of the union with the supreme vajra-lotus, one attains accomplishment while bringing delight. // 1 //
Having visualized a lotus for women, one should oneself delight the Buddha [therein] while meditating on [oneself] as wearing the Buddha-crown; thus one attains accomplishment in this. // 2 //
Visualizing a lotus for women, one should oneself be upon that lotus;
delighting the one with the tip of the lotus-lotus, one attains pure accomplishment. // 3 //
Having visualized a lotus upon Viśvanta himself for the sake of women, and delighting [them] at the tip of the universal lotus, one shall attain all accomplishments (siddhi). Thus [ends verse 4].
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ vajrapadma saṃyoga sādhaya hrīḥ.
Oṃ, O Buddha-crowned one, bring about union; Śrī!
Oṃ, lotus, lotus, accomplish the union, dhīḥ!
Oṃ, accomplish the union with the universal lotus, O woman!

Then follows the knowledge of the secret great mudrā of the Lotus Family as it truly is: the two index fingers are joined like a bud in añjali; the two thumbs are like the fingers of a Vajra-krodha; the two tips are like a jewel, and likewise a lotus; and the vajra-bind is exactly the same. (1)
Having brought the vajra-bond together, with the middle fingers standing level like sprouts and the index and ring fingers slightly bent, this is the firm mudrā of Śākyamuni. (2)
Dharmavajrā, residing in the heart, having been turned, goes to the forehead;
through the yoga of samādhi, having been turned onto the lap, she goes to the crown of the head. (3)
Having bound Vajradhātvīśvarī and the caitya through the application of the lotus, one should join them with the two middle fingers; this is proclaimed as the "Buddha-lotus."
That same [mudrā] with the vajra on the thumb, as well as those with two tips, the sword, and the hook—these are proclaimed as the secret mudrās of the Holder of the Lotus-Vajra. // 5 //
That same [mudrā], when released from the thumb, but with the index finger grasping the index finger and bent, is called Surati; it is likewise used for the act of "well done."
Having made the vajra-bind firm, with the thumbs inserted equally,
the middle lotus [finger] is placed at the brow with its tip slightly curved.
That same [mudrā], when shown at the heart, reveals the solar disc;
that same one, extended over the head and back with the binding of the banner, [is likewise]. // 8 //
Having made the vajra-bind firm, with the tips of the fingers bent together, it is likewise the lotus-sword through the supreme joining of the lotus-yoga. // 9 //
Having made the vajra-bind firm by inserting the left thumb, the conch [is formed] by the tips of the fingers raised from the staff of the thumbs, with the final lotus [at the end]. 10.
That same [hand], with all fingers contracted, with the little finger joined to the lotus [of the other hand], is used for counting the beads of a rosary by means of the right thumb. // 11 //
Having made the vajra-bind firm, with the little fingers joined like lotuses, the lotus-eyed one, with the tips of the thumbs together, performs a dancing movement. 12.
Having made the vajra-bind firm, the two little fingers are joined with the lotus; they should press the tips of the two bent [middle fingers] within the armor formed by the two thumbs. // 13 //
That same [mudrā] is the *aṅguṣṭhadaṃṣṭrā*, with the thumbs inserted evenly;
beyond this, I shall explain the supreme, unsurpassed commitments (*samaya*). (14)
Having formed the vajra-bind at the base, with the index fingers joined at the lotus [of the thumbs], and the thumbs bound in the paryanka posture—this is known as Guhyaviśveśvarī. // 15 //
In the same way, with the vajra-bind, the little fingers are joined at the middle;
with the two thumbs as vajras, one places the Tathāgata in the middle of the band.
In the same way, having formed the vajra-bind with the thumbs joined at the lotus, one should hold it turned upward toward the mouth while remaining in meditative absorption upon the lap. (17)
In the same way, in the vajra-binding, the fingers are joined evenly at the tips;
having made all the fingers firm, the two index fingers are joined like a vajra. (18)
In the same way, in the vajra-binding, the two index fingers are joined at the lotus;
the thumbs form a cross-legged posture, with the middle fingers contracted in form. // 19 //
In the same way, within the vajra-bind, the vajra is formed by joining the thumbs;
likewise, the sword and goad are formed by the two index fingers, while the little fingers are joined with the lotus.
In the same manner, having formed the *valitā* [mudrā] with the index finger and thumb held together,
one should pull up the left index finger very firmly.
That same [mudrā], however, when the index finger and thumb are brought together, is the bestower of praise for the great-souled Padmatuṣṭi. // 22 //
In the same way, one should perform the vajra-bind, with all the fingertips joined together; the two thumbs should press against each other's tips, positioned with their points meeting. // 23 //
That very Sūryā is in the heart, while she who bears the lotus-banner is placed upon the head;
and having transformed herself into Hāsā, she stands as Padmāṭṭahāsinī.
Having placed the vajra-bind at the base through the supreme yoga of Dharmavajrā, the joining of the little finger and the thumb is indeed this samaya of Tārā. (25)
In the same way, within the vajra-bind, with the two thumbs [one forms] Khaḍgā and Padminī;
likewise here, Talacakrā and likewise Jāpadātrī.
In the same way, when the vajra-bind is released from the two *khaṭaka* gestures and bound again at the heart, it is proclaimed as the "Secret Protection" (*guhyarakṣā*). // 27 //
In the same way, in the Vajrabandha [mudrā], the little fingers are joined like lotuses;
the index fingers are firmly contracted, and the thumbs are spread apart like fangs. // 28 //
That same [mudrā], when formed by the application of the fist with the two thumbs pressed against the face, is proclaimed as the Padmaguhyamahāmuṣṭi, the foremost of the Samayas. // 29 //
And for all the others known by names such as Padmalāsyā and so forth, having formed the vajra-bind at the palms, the binding is exactly like that—thus it is said. (30)
Then there are the secret dharma-mudrās of the Lotus family:
hrāḥ, grā, prā, hā, sra.
Sā, daḥ, haḥ, gā, dhā, krā, vā, va,
rā, ṣṭra, maḥ.
The action seals (karmamudrā) are, in brief, simply the two hands joined together in a fist.
The detailed procedure for the Padma-guhyamudrā-maṇḍala from the *Sarvatathāgatadharmasamayā-mahākalparāja* is completed.

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called Padma, the empowerment arising from the commitment-knowledge of the commitment of all Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme vidyā of himself: Oṃ dharmasamādhijñānatathāgata hūṃ.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this supreme vidyā of his own family, which arises from the dharma of his own lineage: OṂ VAJRADHARMA HŪṂ.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme personal vidyā-mantra: OṂ RATNADHARMA HŪṂ.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this supreme personal vidyā-mantra: OṂ DHARMADHARMA HŪṂ.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśva spoke this supreme self-knowledge-mantra: Oṃ karmadharma hūṃ.
The delineation of the maṇḍala:
Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this maṇḍala of his own dharma.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme maṇḍala of gnosis.
That which resembles the Vajradhātu is known as the knowledge of phenomena (dharmajñāna). // 1 //
One should delineate the entire maṇḍala by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala;
in its center, one should paint the Tathāgata Jñānavajra. // 2 //
On all his sides, the Great Beings, beginning with Viśveśvara, should be depicted according to the prescribed rule, fully complete and composed in meditative absorption. Thus [it is said].
In that regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ jñānabuddha hūṃ. (1)
Oṃ Jñānaviśveśvara Hūṃ. // 2 //
Oṃ, you whose crown is the Buddha of Wisdom, hūṃ! // 3 //
Oṃ, O Lord of the Dharma of Gnosis, hūṃ! // 4 //
Oṃ jñānāmogheśvara hūṃ. // 5 //
Oṃ jñānapadmabuddha hūṃ. // 6 //
Oṃ, you who hold the lotus-king of gnosis, hūṃ! // 7 //
Oṃ jñānapadmamāra hūṃ // 8 //
Oṃ, O Wisdom Lotus Joy, hūṃ! // 9 //
Oṃ, O one with the frown of the lotus of wisdom, hūṃ! // 10 //
Oṃ jñānapadmasūrya hūṃ. // 11 //
Oṃ jñānapadmacandra hūṃ. // 12 //
Oṃ jñānapadmahāsa hūṃ. // 13 //
Oṃ jñānapadmatāra hūṃ. // 14 //
Oṃ jñānapadmakumāra hūṃ. // 15 //
Oṃ, Jñānapadmanārāyaṇa, hūṃ! // 16 //
Oṃ jñānapadmabhāṣa hūṃ. // 17 //
Oṃ, O Lord of the Dance of the Wisdom Lotus, hūṃ! // 18 //
Oṃ, protect the lotus of gnosis, hūṃ! // 19 //
Oṃ jñānapadmayakṣa hūṃ. // 20 //
Oṃ, knowledge-lotus-fist, hūṃ! // 21 //
Oṃ, O Goddess who causes the lotus of wisdom to bloom, hūṃ! // 22 //
Oṃ jñānapadmamāle hūṃ. // 23 //
Oṃ, O song of the lotus of gnosis, hūṃ! // 24 //
Oṃ, to the dance of the lotus of primordial wisdom, hūṃ! // 25 //
Oṃ, Padma-jñāna-dhūpe, hūṃ! // 26 //
Oṃ padmajñānapuṣpe hūṃ // 27 //
Oṃ, to the lamp of lotus-wisdom, hūṃ. // 28 //
Oṃ padmajñānagandhe hūṃ // 29 //
Oṃ padmajñānāṅkuśa hūṃ. // 30 //
Oṃ, Padma-jñāna-amogha-pāśa, hūṃ! // 31 //
Oṃ padmajñānasphoṭa hūṃ // 32 //
Oṃ, O Padma-jñāna-āveśa, hūṃ! // 33 //

Regarding initiation into this Padmadharma-maṇḍala: having performed the detailed ritual procedures such as the summoning [of the deities] and so forth, and having caused [the candidate] to enter in the proper manner, one should speak thus: "You must not speak of this to anyone else."
"May you not fall into hell; may there be no sufferings for you," [said] Jñāna.
Then one should generate the knowledges for him.
Through the meditative absorption of Lokeśvara, one should visualize a lotus in the heart;
having attained the lotus-samādhi, one quickly flies up in an instant. // 1 //

By means of the meditative absorption of Lokeśvara, through the cultivation of a lotus on the forehead, one who practices until it becomes firm becomes a traveler through the sky in an instant. // 2 //
Meditating on a lotus upon the tongue through the samādhi of Lokeśvara, he quickly becomes fully accomplished and travels through the sky. // 3 //
One should visualize a lotus at the crown of the head through the meditative absorption of Lokeśvara;
once accomplished, one quickly rises upward in an instant.
In that regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ, enter the heart of the lotus-gnosis!
Oṃ, enter for the lotus wisdom empowerment!
Oṃ, O supreme vidyā of lotus-wisdom, enter!
Oṃ, enter, O Lotus Wisdom Uṣṇīṣa!
One should visualize a lotus disc either in the sky or in another location;
by this method, once perfected, one becomes invisible in an instant. // 1 //
One should visualize a lotus disc either in the sky or in another place; visualizing oneself as mounted upon it, one becomes invisible. (2)
One should visualize a lotus disc either in the sky or in another location;
when one sees it, then one should seize it quickly, [and one becomes invisible]. // 3 //
One should visualize a lotus-form either in the sky or in another place;
having seen it, one should eat that lotus, and in an instant one becomes invisible. Thus [it is said]. (4)
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ padmākāśa.
Oṃ Padmaratha!
Oṃ, O Lotus Wisdom, receive!
Oṃ, Padma-rasāyana!
Having taken a lotus disc of various colors and shapes in one's hand and having formed the great mudrā, one becomes the bearer of all forms. // 1 //
One should cause a lotus disc of various colors and shapes to be drawn;
meditating upon it therein, one shall become a bearer of many forms. // 2 //
One should visualize a lotus disc of variegated colors and shapes, either in the sky or in another location; it will become manifest in both sound and form. // 3 //
One should have fashioned a lotus disc of variegated colors and shapes;
mounted upon it, one will certainly become a traveler of the sky and a master of assuming forms at will. Thus [ends verse 4].
In that regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ padmadhara viśvarūpapravartaka āviśa.
Oṃ, cause the universal lotus to revolve for me!
Oṃ, enter the universal lotus of meditative concentration!
Oṃ! Lift me up from the seat of the universal lotus; abide in me as the one whose form is the universe.
Having properly bound the single supreme Great Seal through meditative absorption, one should offer the secret lotus; [the subjugation] will certainly be accomplished. // 1 //
And having properly bound the single supreme mudrā known as the samaya.
Having taken that lotus with it, one should offer it; thus, one will become a bringer of subjugation. // 2 //
Having bound the auspicious mudrā established by meditative concentration, one should offer the lotus of knowledge to whomsoever; he will quickly come under one's control. // 3 //

And having bound one of the mudrās called *karma*, being endowed with the *samaya*, to whomever one gives it, that person becomes well-subdued; by the giving of the lotus, it shall happen in an instant. Thus, [verse 4].
In this regard, these are their heart-mantras.
Oṃ mahāpadma hoḥ.
Oṃ samayapadma hoḥ.
Oṃ jñānapadma hoḥ.
Oṃ karmapadma hoḥ.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) of the Knowledge Maṇḍala;
one should accomplish the Great Seals by means of the yoga of the Dharma Maṇḍala.
Henceforth, I shall fully explain how the foremost of those bound by the commitments (samaya) should achieve accomplishment.
By means of the yoga of the Dharma-maṇḍala, one should establish the lotus upon the lotus;
having formed the Dharma-fist in two ways, the Karma-mudrā is likewise formed in two ways. Thus it is said.
The detailed ritual procedure for the mandala of primordial wisdom from the *Sarvatathāgatadharmasamayamahākalparāja* is hereby completed.

CHAPTER 18a: THE EXTENSIVE RITUAL FOR THE KARMA-MANDALA Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Lotus Arising from the Empowerment of the Samaya of the Dharma and Karma of All Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme personal vidyā: OṂ SARVATATHĀGATAKARMĀGRA HŪṂ.
Then Vajrapāṇi spoke this supreme vidyā of his own, which arises from the activity of his own family: OṂ HŪṂ DHĪḤ.
Then the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme personal vidyā-mantra: Oṃ ratnakarmasamaye hūṃ.
Then the Bodhisattva Vajranetra spoke this supreme self-knowledge-mantra: Oṃ padmakarmi hūṃ.
Then the Bodhisattva Vajraviśva spoke this supreme self-knowledge mantra: Oṃ viśvakarmi hūṃ.
Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this maṇḍala of his own activity:
"Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme maṇḍala of activity, which resembles the Vajradhātu and is known as the Padmakarma. (1)
By means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala, one should delineate the entire maṇḍala; everywhere around the Buddha, one should draw all those who bear the lotus insignia. Thus, [verse] 2.
In this regard, their vidyā-heart mantras are as follows:
Oṃ padmabhūriṇī hūṃ. (1)
Oṃ, O Sovereign of Viśvakarman, hūṃ! // 2 //
Oṃ, O knowledge-mantra of the ritual empowerment of the Sovereign of the Tathāgatas, hūṃ! // 3 //
Oṃ, O Mistress of Dharma-Action, at the time of the worship of knowledge, hūṃ! // 4 //
Oṃ amoghakarmeśvari hūṃ. // 5 //
Oṃ padmakarmabuddhe hūṃ // 6 //
Oṃ, O Padma-karmavajriṇī, hūṃ! // 7 //
Oṃ, O Padmakāminī, at the time of the ritual of the offering of slaying, hūṃ! // 8 //
Oṃ padmakarmatuṣṭi hūṃ // 9 //
Oṃ padma-karma-bhṛkuṭi hūṃ traḥ. // 10 //
Oṃ padmakarmasūrye hūṃ. // 11 //
Oṃ, O Padmakarmadhvaja, hūṃ! // 12 //
Oṃ padmakarmahāse haḥ // 13 //
Oṃ padmakarmatāre hūṃ. // 14 //
Oṃ padmakarmakumāri hūṃ. // 15 //
Oṃ, O Padmakarmanārāyaṇī, hūṃ! // 16 //
Oṃ, Padmakarmabrāhmī, hūṃ! // 17 //
Oṃ, O Mistress of the Dance of Lotus Activity, hūṃ! // 18 //
Oṃ padmarakṣa-karmasamaye hūṃ // 19 //
Oṃ, Mahāpracaṇḍī, slayer, lotus-toothed one, performer of rites, hūṃ! // 20 //
Oṃ, Padmakarmamuṣṭi, strike! Hūṃ! // 21 //
Oṃ ratipūje hūṃ jaḥ // 22 //
Oṃ abhiṣekapūje hūṃ hoḥ // 23 //
Oṃ gītapūje hūṃ dhaḥ // 24 //
Oṃ, to the worship of dance, hūṃ vaḥ! // 25 //
Oṃ, to the incense offering, Āḥ. // 26 //

wherever the absorption occurs, there one should point it out. // 1 //
Having indeed bound the tips of the pledges (samayāgrīn), one should search for the treasure; wherever it becomes firm, there one should indicate the treasure to be located. // 2 //
Having assumed the samādhi-mudrā, one should search for the treasure; wherever the wise one remains, there one should indicate the treasure to be found. // 3 //
Having formed the mudrā consisting of karma, one should search for the treasure;
wherever the karma-mudrā is rotated, there one should indicate it to be located. // 4 //
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ mahāratna parīkṣāviśa.
Oṃ, O firm pledge of the Jewel, reveal yourself!
Oṃ, jewel-examination, enter through knowledge!
Oṃ, O jewel-work, cause it to revolve!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the secret mudrās of the jewels.
One should seek the treasure through the union of the two organs;
by cultivating the Mahāmudrā, one shall obtain the treasure through its penetration. // 1 //
Having indeed bound the tips of the fingers together and likewise joined the two women, one should designate that place as a treasure-trove where the mudrā becomes firm. // 2 //
Through the union of the two organs, one should search for the treasure;
by meditating upon the knowledge-seal (jñānamudrā), the knowledge of treasures arises. // 3 //

"Having indeed bound the action-seal (karmamudrā) through the meditative absorption of the two organs, wherever that seal bursts open, one should point out a treasure-trove there. Thus [ends verse 4].
In that regard, their heart-mantras and so forth are as follows:
Oṃ mahāmaṇi saṃyogaviśa.
Oṃ, be firm in the union of the samaya for me!
Oṃ, enter, enter the treasury of knowledge, the union!
Oṃ, shatter all karma and its conjunctions!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of all the mudrās of the great maṇi family.
Now, as for the great mudrās:
by meditating upon the great mudrās according to their written descriptions, they are realized.
Abiding in the center of the moon mandala, one accomplishes the supreme goal of all.
Then, the activities of the great mudrās occur:
the Buddha-mudrā brings about Buddhahood, which is the excellent accomplishment for Vajragarbha; with the Ratnāṅkuśī one should attract, and with the Maṇirāgā one should bring delight. // 1 //
Maṇyudagryā brings contentment; Maṇidṛṣṭi takes away wealth; Maṇimālābhiṣekā, however, bestows great splendor through Maṇisūryā. // 2 //

Like a wish-fulfilling gem that grants according to one's desire, it is the jewel of the Dharma that brings laughter and fulfills all aims; it is the supreme gain, the foremost renunciation that bestows the Dharma not yet attained. // 3 //
Through the path of speech, one attains mastery over the jewel-wheel—the great treasury of the jewel-treasury—as well as the accomplishment of a rain of jewels and great wealth. // 4 //
The Maṇipūjā [mudrā] brings about the state of being highly worshipful; the Ratnavarmā [mudrā] makes it firm;
the Ratnadaṃṣṭrā [mudrā] secures wealth; and by means of the Maṇimuṣṭi [mudrā], one attains success.
Now, herein in this great maṇḍala is the knowledge of the samaya-mudrās:
The mudrā consisting of vajra-jewels bestows the consecration of all Buddhas;
by forming the great vajra-gem [mudrā], the vajra-jewel is accomplished. (1)
Having formed the two vajras into a jewel, one obtains wealth from the Vajra-holder;
with that very [gesture] of the thumb-vajra, one should offer the jewel situated at the heart. // 2 //
Having bound the jewel at the tip of the bud, one becomes Lokeśa, the Giver of Wealth;
one should bestow the Vajrakarmamaṇi, the Great Universal Jewel Banner. // 3 //
Through the supreme jewel of the Vajradhātu, one shall attain the state of a Buddha-jewel;
by binding the thumbs with the vajra [mudrā], the palms are joined at the tips and the backs are drawn together. // 4 //
This is declared to be the Vajra-jewel from the hand of Vajragarbha;
by means of this measure of the Buddha, one obtains the Great Vajra-jewel. // 5 //
Having formed the Ratnavajrī mudrā with the fingers raised level in the middle,
by merely binding it in this way, one shall obtain self-consecration.
That same [mudrā], when formed as a bud with the middle and little fingers joined, is called Avalokita; by means of this, one should bestow wealth.
By means of the vajra-ratna application, the index, thumb, and little fingers, with the nails joined by the two middle fingers, are raised as equal hooks from the ring fingers. (8)
Having made the vajra-bind firm, with the two index fingers formed into jewels and the faces of the thumbs extended, [this mudrā] at the heart bestows the accomplishment of all aims. (9)
Having formed the vajra-binding with the middle fingers joined at the jewel, this is the mudrā of the jewel-mark, which bestows the precious jewel. // 10 //
That very same [mudrā], joined with the hook and held together by the two index fingers, is known as the *sarvārthakarṣaṇī* mudrā, the jeweled-treasure hook. // 11 //

Having formed that same [mudrā] as a *valitā*, one should seize the index finger with the [other] index finger; by means of the application of drawing in an arrow, one draws in and impassions the world. 12.
That same *sādhukāra* [mudrā], however, with the index finger joined to the thumb;
likewise, that same [mudrā] with the tips of the fingers covered by the joining of the thumbs. // 13 //
Then, placing the tips of the fingers again for a moment upon the mouth between the thumbs, that is known as the "Jewel Gaze," which destroys all objects of vision. (14)
The garland of the accomplishment of all aims, however, bestows self-consecration;
that very same [garland], when joined by placing the thumb-tip against the heart, [performs this]. (15)
In the heart is Maṇisūryā, who bestows great splendor;
and situated on the head is Samānā, split at the tip of her banner.
The great vajra-jewel previously fulfills all aspirations;
that very same [jewel], transformed through play, takes the form of laughter. (17)
Indeed, by the laughter known as the Ratnāṭṭahāsa, she accomplishes all aims;
and through meditative absorption, she is the remover of wealth, possessing the foremost jewel-lotus of all.
That same [mudrā], when the little finger and thumb are extended at the end and the index fingers are placed like jewels, is the bestower of great gifts. // 19 //
One should seize the wealth of the worlds by means of the Bhaṇikośā mudrā;
it consists of the vajra-bandha with the tips of the circles joined and the thumbs inserted together. 20.

When the ring finger is positioned like a jewel, it bestows the status of a universal monarch (cakravartin); that same gesture, when raised with the palms joined and placed over the face, [performs another function]. // 21 //
But having indeed made a resolve with his speech, he takes away wealth by his own command;
having bound the great vajra-gem, he causes a rain of excellent jewels to fall.
But by pressing all the fingers together, one rains down wealth fourfold; having bound the great vajra-gem mudrā and dancing, [one does so] from the center of the uṣṇīṣa. // 23 //
Having worshipped according to the ritual with all manner of jewels, one is worshipped by all;
then, one should embrace the *Sarvārthasiddhi* mudrā at the region of the throat. (24)
Known as Maṇibandhā, she is remembered as the armored protectress;
she alone, joined with the Yakṣas and stationed in the mouth, serves for the sake of all accomplishments. (25)
Known as Maṇidaṃṣṭrā, she seizes all objects out of fear;
having made the vajra-bind firm, the tips are bent and well-restrained. // 26 //
By properly grasping the two thumbs together, the fist-mudrā bestows accomplishment;
this is for the foremost commitments of worship through the application of the Vajradhātu. // 27 //
In this context, the supreme commitments are conceived through the application of the jewel as it truly is;
however, those same [commitments] are conceptualized through the application of the central jewel.
"By means of the yoga of Ekāṅkuśī and the others, she accomplishes all activities. Thus it is said.
Now, there are the knowledges of the Dharma-mudrās of the Mahāmaṇi family:
TRAḤ, GRAḤ.
Three times: Hrīḥ,
Śrīḥ, Iḥ.
raḥ haḥ, dhrīḥ dhīḥ, kṛ, vā, ro.
Ḍhaḥ, Ya, Aḥ.
Having formed the jewel-fist in two ways, one should accomplish the action seals (karmamudrās). Thus it is said.
The detailed procedure for the great maṇḍala of Sarvārthasiddhi from the *Sarvatathāgatakarmasamayamahākalparāja* is completed.

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Jewel Arising from the Samaya of the Dhāraṇī of the Consecration of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this mudrā of his own: OṂ VAJRARATNASTŪPE HŪṂ.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this mudrā arising from his own family: Oṃ vajrābhiṣekamāle abhiṣiñca samaye hūṃ.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke this, his own mudrā: Oṃ vajraratnābhiṣeke hūṃ.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this, his own mudrā: Oṃ, consecrate me with the Vajra-dharma!
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśva spoke this, his own mudrā: Oṃ sarvābhiṣeka-pūjā-samaye hūṃ.
The delineation of the maṇḍala:
Then the Blessed One, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, spoke this maṇḍala of the pledge-mudrās of his own family.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme maṇḍala of mudrās.
Resembling the Vajra-realm, it is known as the Secret Jewel. // 1 //
Through the yoga of the great maṇḍala, one should delineate the entire maṇḍala;
in its center, one should draw the Buddha-mudrā according to the proper rule. // 2 //
One should first draw a jewel upon a seat in front of Vajradhātu;
[then] a garland of jewels, a jewel on a lotus, and a jewel surrounded by jewels.
In that regard, their mudrās are as follows:
Oṃ traḥ.
Oṃ maṇisamaye hūṃ.
Oṃ maṇiratnābhiṣekamāle hūṃ.
Oṃ maṇiratnapadmi hūṃ.
Oṃ maṇiratnavṛṣṭisamaye hūṃ.
Having emerged with vajra-velocity into the mandala of all accomplishments, one should draw a great jewel-gem in the center of the Vajraratna [mandala]. // 1 //
On all its sides, the Ratna-ācārya should properly and sequentially draw [the deities], each accompanied by their own seal and jewel. // 2 //
In that regard, their mudrās are as follows:
Oṃ, bestower of the accomplishment of all aims, great vajra-jewel commitment, jewel, accomplish all my aims, dhāraṇī, hūṃ!
Oṃ maṇiratnākarṣe hūṃ.
Oṃ! O Maṇiratnasamayāṅkuśī, summon the Jewel Family! Jaḥ!
Oṃ maṇirāgasamaye hūṃ.
Oṃ maṇisārthi hūṃ.
Having entered the second mandala with vajra-velocity,
one should likewise draw a jewel in its center, joined with two eyes.
On all sides of that [maṇḍala], one should duly draw her own mudrās, beginning from the east as before, accompanied by their respective jewel-marks. // 2 //
In this regard, their mudrās are as follows:
Oṃ, O Vajramaṇiratnanetrā, bring [them] here; subjugate all accomplishments of purpose! Swiftly, O Hook of the Gaze, hūṃ!
Oṃ, Vajramaṇiratnamāle, confer the empowerment! Hūṃ!
Oṃ, jewel-sun, blaze forth! O you who possess all great splendor, hūṃ!
Oṃ, at the tip of the jewel-moon banner, hūṃ!
Oṃ maṇihāse hasa hūṃ.
Having approached with the force of a vajra, one should draw a jewel-lotus;
on all its sides, one should draw [the deities] in due order, exactly as prescribed. // 1 //
In that regard, their mudrās are as follows:
Oṃ maṇisamādhipadmini hūṃ.
Oṃ, at the time of relinquishing the jewel-treasure, hūṃ.
Oṃ, in the treasury of the jewel-samaya, hūṃ!
Oṃ maṇisamayacakre hūṃ.
Oṃ maṇibhāṣāgri hūṃ.
Having approached with vajra-impetus the fourth, supreme mandala, one should [offer] a rain of jewels there, [visualizing] a vajra conjoined with jewels. (1)
One should draw it exactly as it is, surrounded by the action seals (karmamudrā), employing the jewel symbols in their proper order according to the rules. // 2 //
Now, their mudrās are as follows:
Oṃ ratnavṛṣṭi sādhaya mahāmaṇi hūṃ.
Oṃ, at the time of the great worship, dance! Aḥ.
Oṃ maṇiratnasamayarakṣe haṃ!
Oṃ vajramaṇiratna draṃṣṭrākarāle hara hara hūṃ!
Oṃ maṇisamayamuṣṭi hūṃ.
Regarding initiation into this Maṇiguhyamaṇḍala: having performed the ritual actions as prescribed and having caused the disciples to enter, one should say:
“You must not speak of this method to anyone;
lest you suffer great poverty, untimely death, or fall into hell.
Having said this, he should cause [the disciple] to generate his own jewel-like samaya-knowledges.
Having drawn the Vajraratna mudrā in the sky through the Vajraratna samādhi,
and having placed it upon one's own forehead, one will certainly become a king. (1)
Having drawn the Vajraratna, one should bind the supreme samaya;
by placing it in the locations for consecration, kingship will certainly be attained. // 2 //
Having drawn the Vajraratna with the Vajraratna-samādhi, and having established that jewel of gnosis, one becomes a king created by oneself. // 3 //
Having drawn a vajra-jewel in the sky, one should bind the action-seal (karmamudrā);
having established it in its own place, one becomes a king created by oneself. Thus [it is said]. //4//
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
"Consecrate me with the great vajra-jewel!"
Consecrate me with the jewel of the samaya.
Sprinkle me with the consecration of the jewel of the Dharma.
Consecrate me with the jewel of karma.
One should visualize the Vajraratna at the heart as the Mahāmudrā;
by so visualizing, one attains the most wonderful consecration. // 1 //
Visualizing the Vajraratna at his forehead while remaining well-composed, and having indeed bound the Ratnavajra mudrā, he shall become a king over all. // 2 //
By meditating on the Vajraratna at the tongue through the Vajraratna-samādhi, one shall obtain empowerment and the state of sovereignty over the Dharma. // 3 //
"Meditating with perfect concentration upon the Vajraratna in one's own uṣṇīṣa, and having indeed bound the karma-mudrā, one becomes a king who performs excellent deeds. Thus [ends verse] 4.
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ vajraratnahṛdayābhiṣiñca hoḥ.
Oṃ vajra-ratna-abhiṣeka traḥ.
Oṃ, empower with the vajra-jewel wisdom, vaṃ!
Oṃ, O Vajraratnoṣṇīṣa, abide within me!
Having painted a vajra-jewel upon a cloth or similar surface by himself, and meditating upon it as the Great Seal (mahāmudrā), he shall indeed become a great king. // 1 //
Having painted the unsurpassed Vajraratna upon a cloth or similar surface, one should meditate upon Satvavajra; thus one shall become the lord of the samayas. // 2 //
Having painted the Vajraratna himself upon a cloth or similar surface, and meditating upon the dhyāna-mudrā, he will certainly become a Lord of Dharma. // 3 //
Having painted the unsurpassed Vajraratna upon a cloth or similar surface, one should meditate upon the action-seal (karmamudrā); thus, one will oneself become the lord of actions.
Thus [ends the fourth].
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
*vajraratnabimbādhiṣṭha*.
The consecration of the image of Vajraratna.
Enter the image of the Vajra-jewel!
Form the image of the Vajra-ratna!
One should visualize [the deity] as being made of gold, or silver, or the diamond-jewel (vajra-ratna), or even consisting of other jewels; thus visualized in the heart, one is consecrated. // 1 //
Having placed gold, or another jewel, or the unsurpassed diamond-jewel (vajraratna) upon the forehead once again, one shall become a king of great wealth. // 2 //
One should visualize a golden jewel, another kind of gem, or a diamond-jewel;
by placing it within one's own mouth, one becomes the Lord of Speech. // 3 //
One should visualize a golden [wheel], or another jewel, or indeed a diamond-jewel (vajra) upon the uṣṇīṣa; by visualizing it further, one shall become the master of all rites. Thus [ends verse 4].
In that regard, these are their heart-mantras:
Oṃ vajra-ratna-hṛdayābharaṇa hūṃ.
Oṃ, Vajra-jewel consecration, bestower of the great purpose!
Oṃ, Vajra-ratna-vācas-pate!
Oṃ, O Great Lord of Vajra-Jewel and Action!
Then, one should teach the secret knowledge of the Maṇikula-samayamudrā:
"Having formed the great vajra-gem and likewise inserted that gem into the female organ, one attains accomplishment by meditating upon the Mahāmudrā. (1)
Having bound the jewel with the supreme pledge-seal upon the female organ with the supreme pledge-seal, success shall be attained through that binding in all consecrations. // 2 //
Having bound the great vajra-gem while meditating upon the dharma-mudrā, and having pierced that gem within the female organ, there shall be unsurpassed accomplishment. // 3 //
Having pierced the jewel of the *karmamudrā* with the *karmamudrā* in the female organ, one should bind it; thus there will be accomplishment, the unsurpassed in all rites. Thus [it is said]. (4)
In that regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ mahāsiddhiḥ.
Oṃ, may there be the accomplishment of the pledge-consecration.
Oṃ, may there be the accomplishment of the Dharma!
Oṃ, may there be the accomplishment of all actions!
Now, the binding of the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) in this mandala is as follows:
Having formed the Ratnavajrāṅkurā mudrā, with the middle, ring, and little fingers extended and joined together, it should be placed upon the head; this bestows the supreme siddhi. (1)
Having formed the vajra-bind, with the tips knotted and the two thumbs and ring fingers like a vajra, it is turned around to bestow empowerment. (2)
By means of the vajra-jewel application, that very same [mudrā] is transformed; when the tips of the index fingers are joined, it bestows empowerment. // 3 //
Having formed that very same [mudrā] with the thumb and the index finger through the application of the Dharma-vajra, and placing it upon the forehead, it bestows the great Dharma-abhiṣeka. 4.
Having firmly placed the Karma-vajrī upon the forehead and rotated it, one bestows the consecration while placing the garland of all consecrations. // 5 //
Having bound the Ratnasaṃbhava mudrā, which is the pledge-mudrā born of the Vajradhātu,
one is consecrated upon the forehead by means of the jewel-establishment.
With the thumbs bound in the paryaṅka posture and the two index fingers joined at their tips, one should form the *maṇimukha* at the ends; thus one shall obtain the Great Vajra-Jewel. // 7 //
Having formed the vajra-bind, one should extend the jewel-fist;
the jewel, however, is formed by the two middle fingers, and it bestows the consecration of the jewel-garland. 8.
Having formed the vajra-bind, with the middle fingers joined at the tips and the two index fingers slightly opened, one forms the lotus; thus one attains success. // 9 //
Having bound the jewel with the two middle fingers and keeping all the other fingers raised, by visualizing the jewels themselves, one will come to possess an excellent retinue. (10)
Having joined the vajra-jewel through the union of the middle finger and the thumb, with the ring and little fingers made equal, the tongue is placed in the mouth as the bestowing of jewels. 11.
That very threatening finger (tarjanī) is the Vajra; situated there, it is likewise the Hook (aṅkuśī).
The drawing-in of the threatening finger by the threatening finger is the bestower of satisfaction upon those two. 12.
Having bound the jewel with the two middle fingers and remaining with the tips of the other fingers contracted, one should join the tips of the ring fingers and cover them with the two thumbs. (13)
That same Sūryāvartā, however, with arms extended over the head, joined with the application of laughter, is the Maṇi-dhvajāgrakeyūrā. 14.
Having formed the vajra-bind, with the index fingers raised toward the mouth, one should visualize a lotus with those [fingers], while the two middle fingers are made into a jewel. 15.
That very same [mudrā], when applied with the final offering, is the Vajrakośa;
when applied with the vajra-wheel and drawn forth from the mouth, it is that very same [mudrā]. // 16 //
Having formed the Vajraratnāṅkurā mudrā, one should extend all the fingers;
having placed that upon the head, one should cause a rain of jewels to fall. // 17 //
That same [mudrā], when joined with the wheel, is formed by doubling the jewel at the heart;
it is the fist with the middle fingers joined at their joints, having the tips of the index fingers as the grasping claws of a jewel. // 18 //
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the pledge-mudrās (samayamudrā).
One should bind these very great mudrās by joining them together in a hollowed embrace.
In brief, these secret and most secret [mudrās] shall bestow fourfold accomplishment. Thus it is said.
In the Vajra-secret, one should not bind [the mudrās] at all times according to the literal rule.
Hereafter, I shall explain the Dharma-mudrās in brief. Thus it is said.
With *traiḥ*, *graiḥ*, *haiḥ*, *saiḥ*, *gryaḥ*, *khadvyaiḥ*, *haiḥ*, *dhraiḥ*, *dhyaiḥ*, *kraih*, *vaih*, *krayaiḥ*, *rai*, *yyaḥ*, and *maiḥ*—
this secret fist of the peak of secrets, when performed in two ways, accomplishes all rites. Thus it is said.
The detailed procedure for the maṇḍala of the secret jewel mudrās from the *Sarvatathāgatakarmasamaya*, the great king of kalpas, is completed.
The Emanation of Deities from Samādhi:

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment Arising from the Commitment of the Wisdom of the Consecration of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme self-knowledge-mantra: Oṃ sarvatathāgatābhiṣekajñānottama hūṃ.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this supreme personal vidyā: Oṃ vajrajñānābhiṣeka-samaya hūṃ.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme self-knowledge mantra: OṂ MAṆIRATNĀBHISHEKAJÑĀNA HŪṂ.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra recited this supreme personal vidyā: Oṃ dharmābhiṣekajñānaṃ hūṃ.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśva spoke this supreme mantra of his own vidyā: Oṃ sarvābhiṣekajñāna hūṃ.
The delineation of the maṇḍala:
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha spoke this maṇḍala of the wisdom of his own family:
"Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme wisdom maṇḍala."
Resembling the Vajradhātu, it is known as the Jewel Wisdom (Ratnajñāna). // 1 //
One should delineate the entire mandala by means of the yoga of the great mandala;
however, the symbols should be drawn in the heart through the yoga of the dharma-mandala. Thus [it is said]. (2)
Now, here in this great maṇḍala, there are the heart-mantras of gnosis:
Oṃ sarvārthasiddhijñāna hūṃ. // 1 //
Oṃ maṇijñāna hūṃ. // 2 //
Oṃ maṇijñānāṅkuśa! // 3 //
Oṃ maṇijñānarāga. // 4 //
Oṃ maṇijñānatuṣṭi // 5 //
Oṃ, jewel of the vision of wisdom, hūṃ! // 6 //
Oṃ, the empowerment of primordial wisdom. // 7 //
Oṃ maṇijñānasūrya. // 8 //
Oṃ Maṇijñānadhvaja! // 9 //
Oṃ maṇijñānāṭṭahāsa! // 10 //
Oṃ maṇijñāna padma hūṃ. // 11 //
Oṃ, jewel of knowledge, renounce! 12.
Oṃ, treasury of the jewel of wisdom. // 13 //
Oṃ, the jewel-wheel of gnosis. // 14 //
Oṃ, speak with the jewel of wisdom! 15.
Oṃ, rain down the jewel of the gem of primordial wisdom! // 16 //
Oṃ maṇijñānanṛtyapūjāsamaya hūṃ // 17 //
Oṃ maṇijñānarakṣa. // 18 //
Oṃ maṇijñānayakṣa. // 19 //
Oṃ maṇijñānamuṣṭi. // 20 //
Regarding initiation into the maṇḍala: having performed the detailed ritual procedure here in this maṇḍala according to the rules,
he should speak to the disciples as follows.
“You must not speak to one who has not seen the maṇḍala of the Dharma;
lest your time of death should come quickly while you have not yet attained success.
Having said this,

One should generate the knowledge of the dharma of the Jewel family by means of meditative absorption, having painted [the deity] upon a cloth or other support, O Vajragarbha; while visualizing it, one should request wealth, saying, "Grant me jewels! // 1 //
Having painted the interior of the *vajra* upon a cloth or similar surface through meditative absorption (*samādhi*), one should visualize it and request the jewels, speaking the words, "Give! (3).
Having painted Vajragarbha on a cloth or other medium and visualizing him, one should supplicate with the words, "Grant the true Dharma through meditative union; O Wisdom! (3).
Having painted Vajragarbha upon cloth or other supports and visualizing him, one should request with the words: "O embodied one, perform the rite through meditative union! // 4 //
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ, bestow all aims, Blessed One, Vajragarbha!
Oṃ, O Blessed One Vajragarbha, bestow all jewels!
Oṃ, bestow the true Dharma, O Blessed One, Vajragarbha, True Being!
Oṃ, bestow the sublime activity, O Blessed One Vajragarbha!
Whether in the sky or in another place, being well-composed in meditation, one should entreat the noble being Ākāśagarbha for the attainment of all desired aims. // 1 //
Whether in the sky or in another place, being well-composed in meditation, one should supplicate the noble being Ākāśagarbha for a collection of jewels. // 2 //
Whether in the sky or in another place, meditating with a well-composed mind, one should entreat the noble being Ākāśagarbha for the perfection of the Dharma. // 3 //

In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-siddhi-jñāna-tantra*:
one perceives those very [elements] as blue like the sky and in the form of lotuses;
for indeed, the accomplishments (*siddhi*) of the *vidyā* arise within the great *Padmakula*.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulāsiddhijñānatantra*:
"Whether in the sky or in another place, those very ones, pure as the sky, emitting circles of light rays—if one beholds them, one shall attain accomplishment. Thus it is said.
Beings such as Vajrasattva and others, radiant with moon-maṇḍalas,
first manifest themselves in their own true forms at the time of accomplishment.
The extensive tantra of the rituals for the knowledge of the accomplishments of all families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Knowledge-Seals for the Accomplishment of the Superknowledges of All Tathāgata Families.
In this regard, here is the Tantra of the [Superknowledge] Accomplishment of the Tathāgatas:
