Abiding in the samādhi of Vajrasattva, one should [visualize] the Tathāgatas within the entire body.
And while meditating, one should likewise manifest Bodhisattvas from one's own body.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulābhijñāsiddhi-tantra*:
Having bound the great mudrā of Vajrasattva while well-composed,
the practitioner attains the five supernormal knowledges (*pañcābhijñā*) by means of this ritual procedure.
In this regard, this is the knowledge of the divine eye:
having stabilized the mahāmudrā, one should bring forth the visual consciousness;
by means of that, whatever one contemplates, one sees it even if it is very far away.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
Having attained the Mahāmudrā concentration, one should bring forth the auditory consciousness;
whatever task one contemplates by means of that, one hears it even if it is situated very far away.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
Having attained the Mahāmudrā, one should bring forth the mental consciousness;
by means of that, whoever one looks upon as a sentient being, one knows their mind. // 1 //
Having attained the Mahāmudrā, whether for oneself or for another, one perceives a form with the mind; from that, one brings about birth. // 2 //
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrapāṇi.
Then, the accomplishment of the knowledge of the methods of supernatural power (*ṛddhi*) occurs:
having attained the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) concentration, whatever supernatural power one desires,
or wherever it may be, that indeed shall be manifested through that concentration.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Mahābodhicitta.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulābhijñāsiddhi-tantra*.
Having firmly bound the Trilokavijayā mudrā with a well-concentrated mind, the practitioner attains the five superknowledges (pañcābhijñā) by means of this rite. // 1 //
Enraged, he shall, through the application of the divine eye and other powers, become omniscient in an instant regarding all activities in their proper order and sequence. // 2 //
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakulābhijñāsiddhi-tantra*:
"By forming the *mudrā* of Jagadvinaya and remaining well-composed, the practitioner attains the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*) through this ritual procedure. (1)

But one who is attached to passion, by performing according to the rules and in the proper sequence, will become possessed of all superknowledges through the yoga of the divine eye and so forth. // 2 //
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Lokeśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-abhijñā-siddhi-tantra*:
"Having bound the excellent mudrā for the accomplishment of all aims while being well-composed, the practitioner attains the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*) by means of this rite. (1)
Performing the worship of the Buddha in the proper sequence,
he perceives the five superknowledges through the application of the divine eye and the others.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
The Extensive Tantra of the Rituals for the Knowledge of the Superknowledges of All Families.

Then the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatakulasatyasiddhitantra*. In that regard, the *Tathāgatasatyasiddhitantra* is as follows: "The performance of an oath is by means of speech that conforms to the truth."
But by upholding great truth, one shall swiftly attain Buddhahood.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakula-satyasiddhi-tantra*:
"One born of the Tathāgata family should take an oath regarding the pledge;
by upholding the Vajra-truth, one shall attain the supreme accomplishment."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-satyasiddhi-tantra*:
having made oaths that are difficult to transgress with the Vajradhārīs, [one attains success].
One should protect this truth, for if one desires supreme accomplishment, this is indeed necessary.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-satyasiddhi-tantra*:
Having made an oath regarding the True Dharma, one [attains] the supreme Great Padma family.
One should maintain the commitment of truth if one desires the highest accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradharma.
In this regard, here is the Maṇikulasatyasiddhitantra:
Having made oaths that are difficult to transgress during the worship of the Buddhas, one should maintain the supreme truth; thus, one shall obtain empowerment.
[Thus spoke the Blessed One,] Buddhapūja.
The Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Oaths of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatasamayatatvasiddhi-tantra*.
In this regard, the *Sarvatathāgatasamayatatvasiddhi-tantra* is as follows:
"When it is said, 'You are the pledge (*samaya*)', [one binds] all the mudrās within the families."
Having bound it firmly by themselves, they proceed; thereafter, it is not accomplished [by others].
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Great Samayasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakula-samaya-tattva-siddhi-tantra*:

"When 'You are well-pleased' (*surata*) is uttered, all mudrās that have not been previously accomplished are themselves mastered through the invocation of the reality (*tattva*) by the Great-Souled One."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Great Samaya Being.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-samaya-tattva-siddhi-tantra*:
"By means of a single *huṃ* alone, one should briefly bind all mudrās oneself,
or cause them to be bound by another, or [cause] another to bind them themselves."
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-samaya-tattva-siddhi-tantra*:
"When it is proclaimed that 'all is pure,' whether by oneself or for another,
unions such as those involving women and so forth do not lead to liberation in any way whatsoever."
In this regard, here is the Maṇikula-samaya-tattva-siddhi-tantra.
In brief, all mudrās are accomplished by means of the syllable Oṃ alone.
And they are the foremost in all worlds, as well as the objects of worship for the self-existent ones. Thus it is said.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Mudrās of the Accomplishment of the Reality of the Samayas of All Families.
Then the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, proclaimed the Tantra of the Mudrās of the Siddhi of All Tathāgatas.
In that regard, the Tantra of the Siddhi of All Tathāgatas is as follows:
"Holding the Buddha-mudrā while recollecting the Tathāgata..."
Practicing this, one swiftly accomplishes even the stable awakening of a Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Siddhi-tantra* of the Tathāgata family:
Having bound the great mudrā of Vajrasattva and meditating upon it,
Vajrasattva will appear before one, and accomplishment (*siddhi*) will become even swifter.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-siddhi-tantra*:
"Having bound the supreme pledge (*samaya*) through the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) of Vajrasattva,
and while visualizing Vajrasattva, the accomplishment (*siddhi*) shall become twofold."
In this regard, here is the *Padmakulasiddhitantra*:
"Having bound the mudrā consisting of the Dharma through the samādhi of Lokeśvara,
and while meditating upon the Lord of the World, accomplishment shall become twofold."
In this regard, here is the Maṇikulasiddhitantra:
Having taken hold of the action-seal (karmamudrā) through the vajragarbha-samādhi,
and meditating upon Vajragarbha, accomplishment shall become twofold.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Accomplishment of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra for Accomplishing All Siddhis of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, this is the Tantra for Accomplishing the Siddhis of All Tathāgatas:
"Whether for oneself or for another, one who accomplishes the recollection of the Buddha..."
Indeed, by binding all the mudrās, they are then accomplished in that very instant.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
In this regard, here is the tantra for accomplishing all siddhis of the Tathāgata family and so forth:
One should accomplish all mudrās while contemplating, "I am Kāma.
Through the application of vajra-recitation, one accomplishes the supreme of all siddhis.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, this is the *Vajrakula-sarvasiddhisādhanatantra*:
"Visualizing oneself as the vajra-form with a well-concentrated mind, one should bind all the mudrās; for they attain accomplishment at that very moment."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vajra of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the *Tantra for Accomplishing All Siddhis of the Lotus Family*:
"Visualizing oneself as the form of a lotus by means of one's own self,
the accomplishment consisting of all-knowledge is declared to belong to the Great Lotus Family."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulasarvasiddhisādhanatantra*:
One should visualize oneself as a jewel-mountain with blazing rays;
the accomplishment consisting of all forms of worship is taught within the Great Jewel Family.
Thus said the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Accomplishment of the Supreme of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Seals Empowered by All Tathāgatas*.
In this regard, the *Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Empowerment of the Tathāgata* is as follows:
"Having bound the seal of Vajradhātvīśvarī while being well-composed in meditative concentration..."
Having placed it on the heart, the ūrṇā, the throat, and the head, one is empowered by the Buddhas.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
In this regard, there is this *Tathāgatakulādhiṣṭhānasiddhitantra*:
Having made the Sattvavajrī firm through the *vajrasattva-samādhi*,
one should place [the mudrā] upon the heart, the *ūrṇā* (between the eyebrows), the throat, and the head, and thereby bestow empowerment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Siddhi-tantra* for the empowerment of the Vajra family:
Having bound the Vajra-hūṃkāra mudrā while being well-composed,
the empowerments of samādhi are established at the heart, the ūrṇā, the throat, and the crown of the head in that very instant.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajranātha.
In this regard, here is the *Siddhitantra* for the empowerment of the Lotus Family:
Having firmly joined the vajra and the lotus through the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) of Lokeśvara,
empower and fashion [the disciple] with [the mantras] residing in the heart, the *ūrṇā*, the throat, and the crown of the head.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulādhiṣṭhānasiddhitantra*:
"Having bound the great vajra-jewel with the *Vajragarbha* samādhi,"
One should arrange [the syllables] located in the heart, the *ūrṇā*, the throat, and the head for the sake of self-consecration (*svādhiṣṭhāna*).
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajragarbha.
The extensive tantra of the ritual procedures for the empowerment of all families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Seals for the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Empowerment of the Tathāgatas is as follows:
Having placed a jewel together with a vajra upon the forehead, it is firmly established there.
Having performed [this], one is consecrated by the Victors with the Vajra and Ratna [mudrās].
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatakulābhiṣekasiddhitantra*:
"Beginning with the Buddha-mudrās, such as Vajradhātvīśvarī and others, in front [of the practitioner],
she shall consecrate him by means of the garland [mudrā] on the four sides."
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulābhiṣekasiddhitant*ra:
"Having placed the vajra initiation garland upon the forehead,
he is consecrated by that garland initiation by the Vajradhara."
In this regard, here is the *Padmakulābhiṣekasiddhitantra*:
Having visualized Dharmavajrī established before one and upon the crown of one's head,
one who is consecrated by her is consecrated by the Buddhas as a Lord of the World (*lokeśvara*).
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulābhiṣekasiddhitantra*:
Having formed the Vajra-ratna-aṅkura mudrā and placed it upon the forehead,
one who is consecrated by that [mudrā] by the Buddhas shall be consecrated in the sovereignty of worship.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
The Tantra of the Accomplishment of Empowerment for All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatasamādhisiddhi-tantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Sarvatathāgatasamādhisiddhi-tantra*:
"Having bound the mudrā of all the Buddhas through the taking of food, one should remain in meditative equipoise."
Indeed, in Japan, those who know the mantras shall swiftly attain accomplishment.
Thus said the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatakula-samādhi-siddhi-tantra*:
"Through the yoga of the empowerment of sentient beings by means of the Vajradharma Samādhi,
the heart-mudrās and the gentle vidyās are swiftly accomplished through recitation."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Samādhi of the Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-samādhi-siddhi-tantra*:
"By meditating, 'You have arisen from passion; I am Wrath,' it shall bring about the swift accomplishment of the heart-seals, mantras, and vidyās."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-samādhi-siddhi-tantra*:
"Through the yoga of the pervasion of loving-kindness (*maitrī*), one should accomplish the heart-mantra and so forth;
in the family of Lokeśvara, recitation (*jāpa*) swiftly bestows accomplishment."
To him, the Blessed One, the Noble Avalokiteśvara, said:
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-samādhi-siddhi-tantra*:
By meditating with a well-composed mind upon the *sarvākāśa-samādhi*,
and practicing within the heart-seals (*hṛnmudrā*), mantras, and vidyās, one shall become all-pervading.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
The Extensive Tantra of the Rites for the Accomplishment of Samādhi in All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgata-pūjā-mudrā-siddhi-tantra*.
In this regard, the *Tathāgata-pūjā-siddhi-tantra* is as follows:
Having first performed worship with incense and other offerings, one should remain well-composed in meditation.
Then, one who desires accomplishment, by practicing thus, shall indeed attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulapūjāsiddhitantra*:
"By means of the fourfold secret worship, proclaiming the secret of worship,
one who performs worship through these, such as the offering of oneself and so forth, shall attain accomplishment."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulapūjāsiddhitant*ra:
By proclaiming the great secret of the wrathful ones during the great worship of the Wrathful Vajra,
and by forming the wrathful fist, one will indeed quickly achieve success within my family.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-pūjā-siddhi-tantra*:
"By offering through mind and speech those practices proclaimed in the profound and vast sūtras, one shall swiftly attain accomplishment."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-pūjā-siddhi-tantra*:
"By worshipping with parasols, banners, and flags, and by performing royal offerings..."
The entire family of jewels is accomplished, or all gifts are accomplished.
Thus said the Blessed One, Vajragarbha.
Endowed with the self-consecration and the others, one becomes equal to Vajrasattva;
through the four miracles, one should stabilize the universal vajra-samādhi.
"All accomplishments," said the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Empowerment, Meditative Absorption, Worship, and Accomplishment of the Empowerment of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatābhijñājñānasiddhitantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatābhijñājñānasiddhitantra*:
"The Buddha-samādhi within the body is indeed this superknowledge (*abhijñā*) of the Sugata."
Through the thorough understanding of that, one shall attain the accomplishment of Buddhahood.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulābhijñājñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"By meditating with a well-composed mind upon the superknowledges (*abhijñā*) such as the divine eye and so forth,
one becomes self-arisen with the five superknowledges and shall attain the state of Vajrasattva."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulābhijñājñānasiddhi-tantra*:
Having generated the higher knowledge (*abhijñā*) of the Wrathful One and practicing with well-composed concentration,
one becomes spontaneously self-arisen with the five higher knowledges and shall attain supreme accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakulābhijñājñānasiddhi-tantra*:
Having generated the superknowledge of passion (*rāga-abhijñā*) and meditating with a well-concentrated mind,
one becomes a self-arisen possessor of the five superknowledges and shall attain pure accomplishment (*siddhi*).
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajranetra.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulābhijñājñānasiddhi-tantra*:
Having generated the superknowledge of worship and meditating with a well-concentrated mind,
one becomes self-arisen with the five superknowledges and shall attain the supreme of all siddhis.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Attainment of Knowledge through the Superknowledges of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatabodhijñānasiddhi-tantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatabodhijñānasiddhi-tantra*:
Abiding in the samādhi of Vajrasattva and possessing the recollection of the Buddha himself, [one should practice].
Cultivating this wisdom of the enlightenment of the Buddha, one shall attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakula-mahābodhi-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
Abiding in the samādhi of Vajrasattva and meditating upon the Mahāmudrā,
one who meditates upon this wisdom of great awakening shall attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-mahābodhi-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
Abiding in the samādhi of the Wrathful King, grasping the hand of the supreme pledge-consort,
one who meditates upon this wisdom of great enlightenment shall attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-mahābodhi-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
Abiding in the samādhi of Lokeśvara and likewise reciting the Dharma-mudrā,
one shall attain accomplishment by meditating on this knowledge of great awakening.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-mahābodhi-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
Abiding in the samādhi of Vajragarbha, performing good deeds through the action-seal (*karmamudrā*),
one shall attain accomplishment by meditating upon this wisdom of great awakening.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Accomplishment of the Wisdom of Great Enlightenment of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Pleasing of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Pleasing of the Tathāgatas is as follows:
"One who seeks the awakening of a Buddha himself, while indeed performing the welfare of sentient beings..."
Having become possessed of the recollection of the Buddha, one effects the pleasing of all Buddhas.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrarāga.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulānurāgaṇasiddhitantra*:
Just as one who possesses the sense objects should practice Vajrasattva,
by means of the impelling of reality, he quickly becomes enamored and attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulānurāgaṇasiddhitantra*:
"Indeed, for the sake of carrying out the Buddha's command through malevolent rites against the wicked,
and for the sake of purifying sentient beings, there is this Vajra-attachment [rite] by means of the Wrathful Deities."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Conqueror of the Three Worlds.
In this regard, this is the *Siddhitantra* for the passion of the Lotus Family:
beholding with passion, loving-kindness and compassion, preaching the Dharma,
and granting fearlessness to all— this is the passion for all Buddhas.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajranetra.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulānurāgaṇasiddhitantra*:
the bestowing of empowerment, the giving of gifts, and the accumulation of wealth—all that should be applied for the sake of the Buddha; this is the *Buddhānurāgaṇa*.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Ākāśagarbha,
in the *Sarvakulānurāgaṇasiddhividhivistaratantra*.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of Subjugating All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, this is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of Subjugating the Tathāgatas:
Passion indeed is not an obstacle; when purified, it likewise bestows happiness.
This yoga, performed for the sake of all sentient beings, brings about mastery over the Buddhas.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulavaśīkaraṇasiddhitant*ra:
"Having indulged in desire, being of a blissful nature and saying 'you are one who delights,' one should accomplish Vajrasattva, who has been brought under control by the impelling of reality."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Samantabhadra.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulavaśīkaraṇasiddhitantra*:
For the sake of the Buddha’s command, for the purification of sentient beings, for the sake of fearlessness for embodied beings,
and for the protection of the Buddha’s teaching, one should bring even Māra under control.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrahuṃkāra.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-vaśīkaraṇa-siddhi-tantra*:
One should indeed examine the purification of passion through the blossoming of a lotus petal;
one should both be impassioned and cause others to be impassioned for the sake of discipline, as a means of subjugation.
Thus spoke the noble Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-vaśīkaraṇa-siddhi-tantra*:
For the purpose of the consecration of all Buddhas, one should place the Vajra-jewel upon the head day after day and be consecrated; thus, one shall bring all Buddhas under one's control.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
The Tantra of the Accomplishment of Subjugating All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Slaying of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, this is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Slaying of the Tathāgata:
"Not seeing the welfare of all sentient beings, and not purifying them through the reality of Buddhahood,"
Or, by means of mind, action, or speech, through the attainment of the accomplishment of killing.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulamāraṇasiddhitantra*:
"Due to the non-attainment of all accomplishments and due to lack of exertion toward one's family [of practice],
by slaying with the great vajra-slap, one attains accomplishment swiftly."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrapāṇi.
In this regard, here is the Vajra Family Tantra of the Accomplishment of Killing:
"Because of the subduing of the wicked, because of wrath, because of the need to discipline non-sentient beings,
and because of inflicting suffering upon oneself— one should kill by means of the syllable HŪṂ."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-māraṇa-siddhi-tantra*.
Due to a lack of compassion, due to a lack of loving-kindness, due to not purifying wicked beings,
and due to deceiving oneself, one will not attain accomplishment while killing.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-māraṇa-siddhi-tantra*:

By causing the death of beings through the loss of their own lives to misfortune, through misfortune resulting from the pursuit of gain, and indeed through poverty, one shall attain accomplishment (*siddhi*).
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the fulfiller of all hopes.
Some, through the application of non-attainment, are intent on the destruction of the Buddhas;
for the sake of uprooting them, we swiftly bestow accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Samantabhadra.
The extensive tantra of the ritual procedures for the accomplishment of the slaying of all families.
Then the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, proclaimed the *Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Seal of Protection for All Tathāgatas*.
In this regard, the *Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Protection of the Tathāgatas* is as follows:
"The constant non-abandonment of all sentient beings is the very nature of the worship of the Buddhas."
May I always maintain mindfulness of the Buddha and protect this most wonderful [state].
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakularakṣāsiddhitant*ra:
"O Vajrasattva, the mere grasping of the name even once is this great, eternal protection that bestows accomplishment in an instant."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakularakṣāsiddhitant*ra:
"Contentment with the *vidyā*-tantras and the nature of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds."
Indeed, through devotion to Vajrahuṃkāra, I shall protect both myself and others.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrahuṃkāra.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-rakṣā-siddhi-tantra*:
"The purification of passion is great loving-kindness toward sentient beings and the granting of fearlessness;
through the recitation of the name of Lokeśvara, may there be this most wonderful protection."
Thus spoke the Blessed One Vajradharma.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikularakṣāsiddhitantra*:
"One should ensure that each day is not spent in vain, by applying oneself according to one's capacity."
Through renunciation, the Buddha, and the Bodhisattva, I shall protect [them] with the most wonderful [means].
Thus spoke the Blessed One Vajrarakṣa.
The extensive tantra on the ritual procedures for the accomplishment of the protection of all families.

Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi said this to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, please accept this *tantra* of the family of all Tathāgatas, by means of which all sentient beings, having attained mastery over all ritual procedures (*kalpa*), [shall reach their goal].”
"They will swiftly and fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi:
“Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi! Well-spoken;
we accept it and empower it.”
Then all the Tathāgatas, having gathered together once more, bestowed words of praise upon the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
"Excellent is it for you, O Vajrasattva! Excellent is it for you, O Vajraratna!"
Excellent for you, O Vajradharma; excellent for you, O Vajrakarman!
“This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna, the secret of all Tathāgatas, and the compendium of the Mahāyāna. Thus [it is said].
The extensive tantra of the ritual procedures for the accomplishment of all rites and means from the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha* is hereby completed.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgataguhyasiddhi-tantra*.
Therein, at the very beginning, is the *Sarvatathāgatottamasiddhiguhyatantra*:
"One who is well-composed, meditating upon the Buddha-bodhi-samādhi..."
Thinking that "enlightenment is easily attained," he awakens to this realization.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Supreme Accomplishment of the Tathāgata Family:
Having bound the Sattvavajrī at the heart, saying "O beloved, you are my wife," and having said "Become firm," one should accomplish all the mudrās. (1)
Even if one has not attained success through one's own actions, by addressing her as "the secret wife" according to this ritual method, one will most certainly attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Satvavajra.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Supreme Accomplishment of the Vajra Family:
For in whatever way one may be provoked to anger, by means of the Vajra-Hūṃkāra mudrā,
even while slaying all the Buddhas, one shall cause them to grant accomplishment out of fear.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Huṃkāra of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakulottamasiddhiguhyatantra*:
"By maintaining the samādhi-mudrā and gazing with the vajra-vision upon one's own wife or the wife of another, one shall obtain the desired siddhi."
Thus spoke the Blessed One Padmarāga.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Supreme Siddhi of the Jewel Family:
"By means of the union of the two organs, one speaks of supreme bliss;
having offered one's own organ to all the Buddhas, one attains accomplishment swiftly."
Thus said the Blessed One Maṇirāga.
The Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Supreme of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Samaya of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Samaya of the Tathāgatas is as follows: Having said, "You are the samaya," one should cause all women to experience passion.
Do not cause the welfare of sentient beings to decline; you shall certainly cause the Buddhas to rejoice.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Mahāvairocana.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Samaya of the Tathāgata Family:
"Passion indeed is not to be despised; one should arouse passion for all women.
By guarding this secret samaya of the Vajra-holder, one attains accomplishment."
Thus spoke the Blessed One Vairocana.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Samaya of the Vajra Family:
"Even while slaying, one should slay the world through the respectful performance of the actions of body and speech;
for the sake of purification by means of the syllables *hūṃ*, this is indeed the samaya that bestows the accomplishment of one's aims."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Trilokavijaya.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Samaya of the Lotus Family:
"Passion is pure for those of pure nature, yet it is impure for the practitioners of other sects."
But by observing the rule of those with pure souls, one shall attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Samaya of the Jewel Family:
Having first bound the Vajra-Jewel with the Vajragarbha-samādhi,
one who takes away the wealth of the wicked shall become a bestower of the accomplishment of the samaya.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajraratna.
The Extensive Tantra of the Secret Ritual for the Accomplishment of the Samaya of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Secret Tantra of the Dharma-Accomplishment of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, the Secret Tantra of the Dharma-Accomplishment of the Tathāgatas is as follows:
"Meditating with perfect concentration upon the intrinsic purity of all phenomena,"
Indeed, while performing all activities, one attains the accomplishment of awakening.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhātu.
In this regard, this is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Dharma of the Tathāgata Family:
"The passion for all sentient beings and non-detachment from sense objects,
as well as the purity of the lover and the beloved, is the secret dharma that bestows excellent accomplishment."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajraguhya.

In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Attainment of the Dharma of the Vajra Family: By means of the yoga of the *huṃ* syllable at the nose, slaying all malevolent beings while abiding in the subtle-vajra samādhi, one shall attain supreme accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Dharmahuṃkāra.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyatantra of the Dharma-Accomplishment of the Lotus Family*:
"By means of the application of the subtle vajra, one should delight all women;
through the samādhi of Vajradharma, one attains the accomplishment of dharma."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Dharma-Accomplishment of the Jewel Family:
"By means of the union of the two organs, fulfilling all hopes."
"One attains unsurpassed accomplishment regarding women or beloved ones," thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajraratna.
The Extensive Tantra of the Secret Rituals for the Accomplishment of the Dharmas of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Activities of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, this is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Activities of the Tathāgatas:
Abiding in the samādhi of Vajrasattva, one should cultivate the recollection of the Buddha.
Entering the body of a woman, one may bring another woman under one's control.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vairocana.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of Ritual Actions of the Tathāgata Family:

Established in the samādhi of Vajrasattva, entering [the consort] through the vulva, one should correctly pervade the body of the woman; even if she is motionless, one should cause her to experience passion.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrarāga.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Ritual Accomplishment of the Vajra Family:
Having firmly bound the Vajra-Hūṃkāra mudrā and being well-composed, he should enter the bhaga while enraged; then, with his mind, he should cause it to fall.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasamaya.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of Activities for the Lotus Family:
Having bound the mudrā consisting of the activity of the Dharma and through the lotus samādhi,
one may enter by way of the vulva and protect all women as well.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrapadma.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of Activity for the Jewel Family:
having bound the activity-vajra-jewel with the vajra-jewel samādhi,
Entering through the vulva of women, he enters them in an instant and dances within.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajraratna.
The Extensive Tantra of the Secret Rituals for the Accomplishment of the Activities of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Purification of the Maṇḍalas of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, there is this Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Purification of the Wheel of All Tathāgatas:
one should fashion a secret maṇḍala having the form of the wheel of Dharma.
One should install the Buddha there, surrounded by his consort and the mudrās. // 1 //
Having entered that secret place, one should immediately say to the Buddha:
"O Lord, these are indeed your wives; please give them all to me. // 2 //
Speaking thus in all the systems of family mudrās, one attains the secret accomplishment of the Buddhas who possess incomparable splendor. // 3 //
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Attainment of All Mandalas of the Tathāgata Family:
One should draw a mandala resembling the Vajradhātu;
it is the supreme method for all the Tathāgata families.
One who desires accomplishment should speak immediately upon entering that maṇḍala: "O Surata, you are my pledge (samaya); O Vajrasattva, grant me success this very day! (2)
Reciting this heart-mantra, one shall accomplish all siddhis;
being satisfied by the yoga of the impelling of reality, he quickly attains success.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of All Mandalas of the Vajra Family:
"The wise one should indeed draw the yoga of all mandalas of the entire Vajra Family, which has the form of Trilokavijaya. (1)
Having entered that very place quickly, one should indeed speak while requesting success:
"You have arisen from passion.
In this way, success is achieved for all.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrahuṃkāra.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Lotus Family Maṇḍala:
"By means of the yoga for subduing the world, the wise one should indeed draw the maṇḍalas within all the Lotus Families; having entered it, he should speak these words. (1)
“O Great Lotus of the nature of passion, O All-pervading Lord, grant me swift accomplishment!
Having spoken thus, he attains success within all mandalas. // 2 //
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Maṇḍala of the Jewel Family:
One should draw the maṇḍalas through the yoga of the accomplishment of all aims;
having entered into the great jewel families, one should indeed speak these words. (1)

“Of all the accomplishments of one’s intentions, the accomplishment of the desire for passion is supreme. Accomplish, accomplish, O Great Being, Blessed One, for the sake of all accomplishments! // 2 //
Speaking thus while entering all the mandalas, one attains the great siddhi, the unsurpassed secret of worship. // 3 //
From that time forth, having attained self-mastery, he constantly accomplishes the supernatural powers;
yet when a power does not manifest quickly, they are accomplished through the impelling of the principles (tattva).
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
This is the extensive tantra of the secret ritual procedures for the accomplishment of the maṇḍalas of all families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Secret Siddhi Tantra of All the Tathāgatas’ Mudrās.
In this regard, here is the Secret Siddhi Tantra of the Tathāgata Mudrās:
"The great goddesses of the Tathāgatas are beloved and bestow all happiness."
Or rather, since even that speech which follows the truth does not succeed when it is [contradicted] by the truths.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulamahāmudrāguhyasiddhitantra*:
"Having indeed bound the great mudrā in the proper sequence as prescribed, one should speak this reality and secret [teaching] with vajra-words. (1)
I myself am Vajrasattva; you are my consort dwelling in the heart. Embracing my entire body, lift me up with vajra-pride! // 2 //
The Great Goddess Vajragarvā, impassioned by the impelling of reality, having become firm throughout the entire body, is swiftly accomplished according to the rule. (3)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Lord of Vajragarvā.

In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-samayamudrā-guhyasiddhi-tantra*: "Be accomplished, be accomplished! Today, in this pledge, I am the pledge; you are my beloved. By this exhortation, she who is quickly enamored becomes accomplished.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyasiddhi-tantra* concerning the Dharma-mudrā of the Lotus Family:
"Awaken, awaken, O Great Being! You are my most beloved wife.
Through such an exhortation, she who is quickly impassioned attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradharma.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyasiddhitant*ra of the Action Seal (*karmamudrā*) of the Jewel Family (*maṇikula*):
“O Vajriṇī, you are my wife who performs all activities; may you be accomplished for me today!
By such an exhortation, she who is swiftly impassioned becomes accomplished.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Secret Accomplishment of All Mudrās of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatasamayaguhya-siddhi-tantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatasamayaguhya-siddhi-tantra*:
for the benefit of the non-Buddhists (*tīrthika*), the Consort of the Buddha was kept secret.
It should be known that it is accomplished by means of the application of the written seal.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Samaya of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyasiddhi-tantra* of the Tathāgata-family Samaya:
"Pervading the minds of all sentient beings, it bestows happiness upon all sentient beings."
He is indeed the father of all sentient beings, the foremost desire of those who hold the supreme samaya.
Thus spoke the Blessed Ones, all the Tathāgatas.
This is the most wonderful secret of all the Buddhas;
it should be understood by one who possesses faith, for even that which is difficult to accomplish will indeed be achieved.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-samaya-guhya-siddhi-tantra*:
For those who are detached from passion and whose minds are shaped by the views of non-Buddhist outsiders,
this supreme commitment (*samaya*) of slaying should be understood as that which brings about accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-samayaguhya-siddhi-tantra*:
"Everything arises from the great elements;
how then can it be called impure?"
One will certainly attain accomplishment for the destruction of the heretics.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajranetra.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulasamayaguhya-siddhi-tantra*:
"When a collection of jewels is made through association with women,
one succeeds by thinking, 'Women are indeed the unsurpassed jewel.'"
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Executor of Commands.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Secret Attainments of All Times and Observances.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Tathāgatapūjāguhyasiddhitantra*.
In that regard, this is the *Tathāgatapūjāguhyasiddhitantra*:
"Being surrounded by women, the pleasure of playful dalliance..."
Having offered it for the worship of the Buddha, one shall attain the accomplishment of worship.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyasiddhi-tantra* of the worship of the Tathāgata family:
"One who is weary from the exertion of sexual union [should contemplate] that bliss born of sexual union."
By offering this fourfold prostration in worship, one attains accomplishment swiftly.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulapūjāguhyasiddhitant*ra:
Having bound the *huṃkāra-samaya* mudrā and embraced a woman,
by indeed offering the bliss of that embrace, he attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrahuṃkāra.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakulapūjāguhyasiddhi-tantra*:
Having visualized himself as Lokeśvara and gazing indeed at the face of his beloved,
he attains accomplishment by offering the bliss of that very gazing.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Lotus-eyed One.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyasiddhitantra* for the worship of the Jewel Family:
Having become a bearer of the action-seal (*karmamudrā*) and adorned with all ornaments,
one succeeds by embracing a woman and offering wealth during the worship.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajraratna.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Secret Siddhis of the Worship of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisatva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Guhyapūjāsiddhi-tantra* of all the Tathāgatas.
In this regard, this is the *Guhyapūjāsiddhi-tantra* of the Tathāgatas:
"One should take pleasure in the wives of others in such a way that no one may know of it."
Visualizing oneself as the Buddha, one shall attain accomplishment through worship.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulaguhyapūjāsiddhitantra*:
Having attained the meditative absorption of Vajralāsyā, one should bind the Vajramālā [mudrā];
then, having bound the Vajragītā [mudrā], one should perform worship with the Vajranṛtyā [mudrā].
The supreme consecration of delight in sensual pleasures is a bliss greater than the bliss of dance and song; for there is indeed nothing else [like it], and thus this secret worship is unsurpassed.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulaguhyapūjāsiddhitant*ra:
One should worship according to the prescribed method with secret worship;
having meditated upon Trilokavijaya, one shall attain the accomplishment of worship.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajraguhya.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyapūjāsiddhitantro* of the Lotus Family:
"By means of the secret yoga as it truly is, one should thoroughly worship the Dharma-mudrā."
Abiding in the mudrā of the world’s discipline, one attains the accomplishment of worship.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-guhyapūjāsiddhi-tantra*:
By properly accomplishing the action seal (*karmamudrā*) through secret yoga,
one attains the accomplishment of worship through the yoga of the accomplishment of all aims.
Thus said the Blessed One Vajragarbha.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Secret Worship of All Families.
Then the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, proclaimed the Secret Siddhi Tantra for Unveiling the Families of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, this is the Secret Tantra on the Accomplishment of the Arising of the Reality of the Tathāgatas:
"In brief, Buddhahood indeed arises from meditative absorption and primordial wisdom."
Through the application of the assembly of beings, one swiftly attains the unsurpassed state.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata.
In this regard, there is this *Guhyatantra* on the accomplishment of revealing the great reality of the Tathāgata family:
"The sentient being is without beginning or end, characterized by arising from space."
Samantabhadra is the self of all; he is desire, the lord of the entire world. // 1 //
That mind which, because of its firmness toward all sentient beings, is called "sentient being";
through meditative absorption and certainties, it becomes equal to a vajra and attains the state of a vajra. // 2 //
Through the yoga of the empowerment of sentient beings, one becomes Vajrasattva once again;
he himself is the Blessed One, the Being, the Tathāgata of the vajra-body. // 3 //
Through the penetration of one's own mind and so forth, the awakening of a Buddha occurs according to the rule;
that very Blessed One becomes the entire family of all Tathāgatas.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the being without beginning or end.

That very [nature] is known as the Tathāgata family; that very same is remembered as the Vajra family; that very same is the pure Padma family; and that very same is said to be the excellent Maṇi family.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Wheel of All Tathāgatas.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Secret Siddhi of Producing All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Names and Symbols of the Seals of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, this is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Names and Symbols of the Tathāgatas:
That very Blessed One, the Being Vajrasattva, abides in the heart.
But samādhi, through its state of concentration, is that which accomplishes the awakening of a Buddha.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyatantra* concerning the accomplishment of the secret signs of the families of the Tathāgatas:

The vajra is so called because of its excellent penetration; the hook (*aṅkuśa*) because it releases those who are seized; the arrow (*vāṇa*) because of its subtle piercing; and the word "well done" (*sādhukāra*) because of satisfaction. (1)
Ratna is said to be from *racanā* (arrangement), Sūrya from *tejas* (splendor), Ketu is declared to be from *samucchraya* (elevation), and Smiṭa is celebrated as *hāsa* (laughter). // 2 //

The lotus is due to the purity of passion; the sheath is from cutting down the enemies that are the afflictions; the wheel is from the yoga of the mandala; and it is called recitation because of the vocal utterance. // 3 //

It is the "all-vajra" because of its universality; it is "armor" due to its connection with being impenetrable; it is "fangs" due to its connection with being terrifying; and it is "binding" through the application of mudrās. // 4 //
For just as the Blessed One is eternal and Vajrasattva is all-pervading,
so too one succeeds by meditating upon the vajra, the insignia, and so forth.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the emblem of all Tathāgatas, in the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Designations of the Emblems of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Secret Tantra of the Arising and Accomplishment of the Binding of the Mudrās of All Tathāgatas.

In this regard, this is the Secret Tantra of the Arising and Accomplishment of the Binding of the Tathāgata Mudrās: Having indeed assumed the vajra-paryaṅka posture, one should bind the vajra-bind with both hands.
Abiding in the samādhi of Vajrasattva, one shall swiftly attain Buddhahood.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
In this regard, there is this *Guhyatantra* on the accomplishment of the arising of the binding of mudrās for the Tathāgata family:
Just as a royal edict is sealed with the king’s own seals, so too are people sealed by the seals of those of great soul. (1)
Through the application of the reflections of the vajras of body, speech, and mind, one who understands that this is the Mahāmudrā of the Great Beings attains accomplishment. // 2 //
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Mahāmudrā.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra on the Accomplishment of the Arising of the Binding of Mudrās in the Vajra Family:
"Just as a person might be bound by intense oaths that are not to be transgressed, so too are all the Tathāgatas [bound] by those which cannot be overstepped. (1)
For those who are bound by the supreme mudrās of the vajra-bond and the bonds of the samaya do not transgress [the vow] until death; knowing this, one attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasamaya.
In this regard, there is this *Guhyatantra* on the arising and accomplishment of the binding of the Dharma-family mudrās:
"For the words of the Vajra are in no way to be transgressed by the Victors;
knowing that 'this is the binding,' his Dharma will be accomplished."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradharma.
In this regard, there is this *Guhyatantra* on the arising and accomplishment of the binding of the mudrās of the Karma family:
"The command of Vajra and the vastness of karma are indeed not to be transgressed;
however, for one who possesses the command, having understood that karma, success is swiftly attained."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajra.
The Extensive Secret Tantra on the Arising and Accomplishment of the Binding of Mudrās for All Families.
Then the Blessed One spoke thus to the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
“This too, Blessed One, has been accepted and empowered by me.”
Then all the Tathāgatas, having gathered together once more, bestowed words of praise upon Vajrapāṇi, the sovereign of all the Tathāgatas.
Excellent for you, Vajrasattva; excellent for you, Vajraratna;
excellent for you, Vajradharma; excellent for you, Vajrakarman!
This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna, the secret of all Tathāgatas, and the compendium of the Mahāyāna. Thus it is said.
The extensive tantra of the secret ritual procedures for all families from the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha* is completed.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatadharmottamasiddhitantra*.
In this regard, the *Tathāgatadharmottamasiddhitantra* states:
"Cultivating the meditative absorption on the Buddha-dharma, one should remain well-composed."
Through the yoga of recollecting the Buddha, one attains the supreme accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata.
In this regard, there is this *Tathāgatakuladharmottamasiddhitantra*:
"Abiding in the samādhi of all sentient beings, one should meditate with perfect concentration."
Through the practice of the recollection of passion, one shall attain the supreme accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Samādhi of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakuladharmottamasiddhitantra*:
By meditating in front upon the form of Trilokavijaya in that manner,
one becomes possessed of the power of Vajrapāṇi and shall become a conqueror of the three worlds.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, this is the *Padmakuladharmottamasiddhitantra*:
"By meditating thus before him upon the Dharma that disciplines the world,
he brings about discipline endowed with the excellence of all aspects."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradharma.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikuladharmottamasiddhitantra*:
"By meditating in that manner before him upon the form of Sarvārthasiddhi,
who is endowed with the excellence of all aspects, one shall obtain the perfection of all aims."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrapāṇi.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Accomplishment of the Supreme Dharma of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatadharmasamayasiddhitantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatadharmasamayasiddhitantra*:
having become possessed of the recollection of the Buddhas (*buddhānusmṛti*), one should say, "Vajra, Vajra!"
Through the application of the subtle vajra, one attains the accomplishment of a Buddha.
Thus said the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakula-dharmasamayasiddhi-tantra*:
"By meditating upon the samādhi of Vajrasattva through the subtle vajra,
one attains the state of Vajrasattva while uttering the mantra of Vajrasattva."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the Vajra Family Dharma-Samaya-Siddhi Tantra:
By visualizing oneself in the form of Trilokavijaya right before one’s eyes and uttering "huṃ huṃ huṃ huṃ," one attains unsurpassed accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrahuṃkāra.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-dharmasamayasiddhi-tantra*:
"Meditating upon the form that disciplines the world from the subtle vajra..."
By uttering "Purify! Purify!", one attains the highest perfection.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Vajradharma.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-dharmasamayasiddhi-tantra*:
"While meditating on the form of the accomplishment of all aims from a subtle vajra,"
Having uttered "sidhya sidhya," the supreme accomplishment of one's purpose shall come to pass.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Maṇidharma.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Accomplishment of the Samaya of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatasaddharmajñānasiddhi-tantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Sarvatathāgatasaddharmajñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"The true Dharma is indeed without syllables, yet it arises from the wisdom of meditative absorption."
Therefore, the letter *a* is known as the non-arising of all phenomena. // 1 //
By meditating through this application of the mudrā with wisdom, the Sugata’s gnosis, which consists of all syllables, is accomplished in an instant. (2)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Mañjuśrī, who is all the Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakula-saddharmajñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"A faithful person who believes in this sūtra, which is the reality of all Tathāgatas, and who maintains and recites it, shall attain unsurpassed accomplishment."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-saddharma-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
for the benefit of sinful beings and for the fulfillment of the Buddha’s command.
However, for the sake of disciplining the wicked, it is accomplished through killing.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vajra Family.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-saddharmajñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"Having realized the purity of intrinsic nature, it is known as the ultimate truth;
by meditating upon this primordial [nature], one quickly attains accomplishment through the Dharma."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, there is this *Maṇikulasa-ddharmajñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"By practicing this Dharma of the Jewel Family, which bestows benefit upon all sentient beings and fulfills all hopes, one quickly attains accomplishment."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Jewel of Dharma.
The Extensive Tantra of the Rituals for the Attainment of Knowledge of the True Dharma of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Activities of the Samādhis of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, this is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Activities of the Samādhis of the Tathāgatas:
"The activity of the samādhis of the Buddhas is that which accomplishes the awakening of the Buddhas."
Cultivating this, one shall indeed attain supreme accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
In this regard, there is this *Tathāgatakulasamādhikarmasiddhi-tantra*.
Through the meditative absorption of Vajrasattva, which is supreme and possesses vast activity,
one achieves success through the realization that it is the "Universal" (Viśva) which effects the welfare of all sentient beings.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajra.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-samādhi-karma-siddhi-tantra*:
"Indeed, for the purpose of purifying evil, it bestows the removal of all sins;
even the killing of all sentient beings is accomplished through faith."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vajra-holder.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-samādhi-karma-siddhi-tantra*:
Having purified himself of all evils through universal purification, he performs all activities;
by means of the realization that "this is the ritual action," it is accomplished.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Padma.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulasamādhikarmasiddhitantṛ*:
For those who eat all things and are destitute, fulfilling all their hopes, the one whose self is everything—the *Sarvārthasiddhi*—is accomplished; of this there is no doubt.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Ratnadhvaja.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Accomplishment of the Samādhi and Activities of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatasūkṣmajñānasiddhitantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatasūkṣmajñānasiddhitantra*:
"One should eternally apply the method of the subtle vajra in accordance with all phenomena."
One shall attain the five superknowledges endowed with the excellence of all aspects.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, this is the *Sarvatathāgatakulasūkṣmajñānasiddhi-tantra*:
One should not reveal these mudrās before anyone other than a qualified master, nor before one who is not a disciple, nor before one who lacks faith; for their accomplishment is most secret.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-sūkṣmajñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"By means of the application of the subtle vajra, through the yoga of the syllable *HŪṂ* at the nose."
Abiding in the samādhi of the Vajra Wrathful One, one should accomplish all activities.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajra.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-sūkṣmajñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
Having stabilized the vajra-vision through the application of the subtle vajra,
and abiding in the great lotus samādhi, one shall attain the accomplishment of passion.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Padmarāga.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulasūkṣmajñānasiddhitantra*:
With a blazing gaze and through the extremely subtle Vajraratna-samādhi,
by means of the application of the subtle vajra, there shall be the attraction of all objects.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi.
This is the Sarvakulasūkṣmajñānasiddhi Tantra.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatacakṣurjñānasiddhitantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatacakṣurjñānasiddhitantra*:
when either a mudrā or a meditative absorption (*samādhi*) is employed for the sake of accomplishment (*sādhana*).
Then he sees bright elements in the sky, having the appearance of stars. // 1 //
Then the wise one should know: "This is my Buddha-eye. From that time forward, he shall accomplish all the rites of the Buddhas. // 2 //
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulacakṣurjñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"Whatever entities exist, whether stationary or moving, one sees their reflections racing through the sky. (1)
To one who comes while [the practitioner] goes, the Vajra-eye attains purification;
indeed, by knowing this and performing worship, one attains unsurpassed accomplishment. // 2 //
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulacakṣurjñānasiddhi-tantra*:
With his eyes, he sees from the right and left, in the sky, the realms of space revolving swiftly, resembling clouds. (1)
Upon seeing them, one should indeed not be afraid; those mudrās originate from the Vajra.
By grasping them, the mudrās are accomplished through the eye of the mudrā. // 2 //
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajra.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-cakṣur-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
"When they see mandalas that are white, red, black, or yellow, then they indeed attain their intention and achieve success through the Vajra-eye. (2)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-cakṣur-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
"In the sky they resemble jewels; in gold and other [precious substances], they are similar."
"But when one with the eye of space sees within the sky, one attains accomplishment forever," said the Blessed One Vajragarbha.
This concludes the *Extensive Tantra of the Ritual for the Accomplishment of the Knowledge-Eye of All Families*.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Supreme Accomplishment of the Activity of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, the Tantra of the Supreme Accomplishment of the Activity of the Tathāgatas is as follows:
"By means of the yoga of the activity maṇḍala, one should worship all the Leaders."
For the sake of the ripening of the bliss of passion, one shall attain the accomplishment of Buddhahood.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulakarmottamasiddhitantra*:
Performing the secret worship while contemplating, "I am Passion," one shall attain the supreme accomplishment, possessing a splendor equal to Vajrarāga.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Kāma.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulakarmottamasiddhitantra*:
"One who performs the secret worship while contemplating, 'I am the Wrathful One,' shall attain the supreme accomplishment comparable to that of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrapāṇi.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-karmottama-siddhi-tantra*:
"Meditating with a concentrated mind upon the purification of desire,
one shall attain accomplishment by worshipping the Buddhas with vowels and drops."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulakarmottamasiddhitantra*:
Having assumed the pride of the Vajra, one should bow with a heart trembling in devotion;
one who is constantly supreme in prostration shall obtain consecration.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Jewel of the Vajra Empowerment.
The Tantra of the Extensive Ritual Procedures for the Accomplishment of the Supreme Rites of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Guhyasiddhi-tantra of the Samaya of the Activity of All Tathāgatas*.
In that regard, this is the *Guhyasiddhi-tantra of the Samaya of the Activity of the Tathāgata*:
"Desire and all other pleasures always abide within my heart."
Oh, how wonderful is this lack of weariness regarding the welfare of sentient beings, which is taught here! // 1 //
For this is the ritual procedure of action through the samādhi of the Tathāgata;
by meditating thus, one should worship the Buddhas and attain the supreme accomplishment. // 2 //
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyasiddhi-tantra* of the Tathāgata Family’s Ritual Pledge:
"I am Samantabhadra, the object of desire who bestows happiness upon all sentient beings;
abiding in the meditative absorption of Vajrasattva, one shall attain accomplishment through worship."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Kāma.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-karmasamaya-guhyasiddhi-tantra*:
"I am Samantabhadra, the Wrathful One, who brings benefit to all sentient beings;
by means of the yoga of Vajra-hūṃkāra, one who worships shall attain accomplishment."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrapāṇi.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-karmasamayaguhya-siddhi-tantra*:
"I am Samantabhadra, passion itself, who personally bestows all happiness;
abiding in the form of the discipline of the world, one shall attain accomplishment by making offerings."
Thus spoke the Blessed One Padmarāga.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-karmasamayaguhya-siddhi-tantra*:
"I am Samantabhadra, the King, who bestows great benefit upon all sentient beings;
by worshipping in the form of Sarvārthasiddhi, one shall attain accomplishment."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Sarvārthasiddhi.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Secret Attainments of the Samaya of the Activities of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatakarmadharmatottamasiddhitantra*.
In that regard, this is the *Tathāgatakarmadharmatottamasiddhitantra*:
"Facing toward the south with the tip [of the hand], one should don the armor through one's own samādhi."
When tied in the form of a turban, it will provide ultimate protection.
Thus said the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulakarmadharmottamasiddhitantra*:
Having drawn the form of a vulva on a wall with a raised phallus,
if one contemplates a woman while performing the gentle rite, she shall come under his control.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the noble Vajrapāṇi.

In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-karmadharma-uttama-siddhi-tantra*: Having drawn the face of a yakṣa upon the ground, and having struck its foremost finger-nail down upon the region of the eyes, one shall summon excellent women.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-karmadharmottama-siddhi-tantra*:
Having taken a lotus with both hands and having observed its purity of passion,
one should likewise arouse passion in women by means of the Vajra-gaze.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-karmadharmottama-siddhi-tantra*:
Abiding in the vajra-ratna samādhi and grasping a jewel with both hands,
one may subjugate all women through the yoga of the Ratna-hūṃkāra.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrahuṃkāra.
The extensive jewel of the ritual procedures for the supreme accomplishment of the activities and dharmas of all families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Ritual Activities of All Tathāgatas.
In that regard, this is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Ritual Activities of the Tathāgatas:
"Having applied the ritual procedure for worship, whatever activity one may contemplate,"
Having informed [the deity] of each respective [intention], the wise one should accomplish the mudrā.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhātu.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulakarmakāryasiddhitantra*:
Having applied the procedure for secret worship through the *vajrasattva-samādhi*,
whatever task one declares shall swiftly attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Siddhi-tantra* for the ritual activities of the Vajra family:
Having performed the great secret worship of the family with the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) of the Wrathful One,
whatever the wise one contemplates, that shall swiftly attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrakrodha.
In this regard, there is this *Siddhitantra* for the ritual activities of the Lotus Family:
"Having performed mental worship through the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) of Lokeśvara..."
Whatever task a wise person contemplates, they shall quickly attain it all.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Holder of the Lotus.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-karmakāryasiddhi-tantra*:
Having performed worship with incense and other offerings through the Vajragarbha-samādhi,
whatever task the wise one contemplates, all that is accomplished in an instant.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajragarbha.
The extensive tantra concerning the ritual procedures for accomplishing all the activities of every family.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Yoga of the Empowerment of the Seals of All Tathāgatas*.
In that regard, this is the *Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Yoga of the Empowerment of the Tathāgatas*:
"Through the application of the subtle vajra, one is absorbed in the yoga of the Buddha."
The practitioner who accomplishes the Buddha-mudrā shall attain supreme siddhi.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vajrapāṇi.

In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulasattvādhiṣṭhānayogasiddhitantra*: "For the *sattva*—which is the essence of all bodies—is established within the self in the body. Having thus empowered oneself, one should cultivate the thought, "I am the *sattva*," through the ego-sense (*ahaṃkāra*).
"It is accomplished," said the Blessed One, the Vajrasattva who is the realization of the Mahāyāna of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, this is the *Vajrakulavajrādhiṣṭhānayogasiddhitanta*:
"As is the being, so is the mudrā; as is the mudrā, so indeed am I.
By means of this yoga of contemplation, one should successfully accomplish all mudrās."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, this is the *Padmakula-dharmādhiṣṭhāna-yoga-siddhi-tantra*:
through the application of the Dharma-mudrā, there is meditation with the subtle vajra;
indeed, all those seals of speech are the samādhi of the Great Being.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-karmādhiṣṭhāna-yoga-siddhi-tantra*:
"By meditating, 'The Blessed One is all the consecrations of the Buddhas and the accomplishments of the *pajā* samaya,' one should accomplish the vajra-activities."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrakarma.
The Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Cultivation of the Mudrās of All Families.
Then the Blessed One [and all the Tathāgatas], having again assembled, bestowed words of praise upon the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, the Great Bodhisattva, the Universal Monarch of all Tathāgatas:
"Excellent, O Vajrasattva! Excellent, O Vajraratna!"
Excellent for you, O Vajradharma; excellent for you, O Vajrakarman!
"This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna,
the secret of all Tathāgatas, the compendium of the Mahāyāna. Thus ends the detailed ritual procedure for the *Sarvakalpaguhyottaratantra*, extracted from the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha*.

CHAPTER 26a: THE TANTRA OF THE SUPREME ELIMINATION OF ALL CONCEPTUAL CONSTRUCTIONS Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi uttered this inspired utterance: "This secret is not suitable for those of perverted views or for those who are dispassionate."
For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, I shall likewise explain the ritual procedures.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this extensive ritual procedure for the service of all the Tathāgata families.
In that regard, this is the extensive tantra of the ritual procedure for the service of all the Tathāgata families;
therein, this is the extensive tantra of the ritual procedure for the service of the heart-mantras.
Having beheld the great maṇḍala and performed worship with incense, flowers, lamps, perfumes, and mudrās,
one then begins the recitation (jāpa) with vajra-speech.
In this regard, the procedure for recitation is as follows:
Just as one staying in that place should perform worship properly with incense and other offerings during the four sessions for four months,

and having praised all the Tathāgatas with the "One Hundred and Eight Names of the Mahāyāna Abhisamaya of All Tathāgatas," one should perform the worship of self-dedication by bowing with the yoga of the four mudrās using the four mantras.
Oṃ, I offer myself for the service and worship of all Tathāgatas; O Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas, please empower me!
Oṃ, I offer myself for the worship and empowerment of all Tathāgatas; empower me with the vajra-jewel of all Tathāgatas.
Oṃ, I offer myself for the sake of setting in motion the worship of all Tathāgatas; O Vajradharma of all Tathāgatas, set me in motion!
Oṃ, for the sake of the ritual of worship to all Tathāgatas, I offer myself; O Vajra-activity of all Tathāgatas, act upon me!

“Then, one who is not detached from all qualities of sensual desire, consuming all food and enjoying all pleasures, with his heart’s intent focused on his own self as the image of the Buddha— visualizing it before him even by means of mere speech according to his will—
and reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times with vajra-speech, he quickly attains accomplishment,” so said the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
“Now, if one desires the supreme accomplishment (*uttamasiddhi*), one should have the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, painted in the center upon a cloth.

By means of the yoga of the maṇḍala of the four great beings (*caturmahāsattva*), the great beings should be painted with their colors and ornaments as desired, established upon moon-maṇḍalas; and in the corner sections, the family goddesses (*kuladevī*) should be painted.
Then, having performed a grand worship of the cloth, one should recite according to the proper method of recitation for as long as four months.”
Then one should recite throughout the entire night.
Then, at dawn, one attains the supreme accomplishments (siddhis), beginning with the reality of all Tathāgatas; thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.

Now, if one should desire the accomplishment of the mudrā, one should bind the Sarvatathāgatasattvavajrī-mudrā before the cloth painting and, according to one’s desire, correctly bind the vajra-speech [mantra] one hundred thousand times.
And while releasing [the breath], one should recite;
then at the end, throughout the entire night,
reciting for a short time without resting.
One should recite the mantra while forming the mudrā accordingly; then the mudrā blazes, enters [the body], rises up, and utters speech.
Then, by means of binding the mudrā, one flies up, assumes any form at will, becomes invisible, and performs all ritual actions.
"By merely binding all mudrās, they perform all activities exactly as required," said the Blessed One, Vajradhara.

“Now, if one desires meditative absorptions (*samādhi*), one should begin with the subtle vajra and take delight in that absorption; one should practice it through the yoga of the heart for as long as four months.
Then, at the end, one should remain for the entire night having entered the meditative equipoise while seated cross-legged.”

Then, at dawn, all the accomplishments (siddhis), beginning with those of all the Tathāgatas, become manifest. Thereupon, one obtains whatever is desired; thus spoke the Blessed Lord Vajrasattva. Now follows the ritual for the accomplishment of activity (karmasādhana).
In that very manner, reciting for one month, one should accomplish [the goal]. Then, at the end, one should recite throughout the entire night.
Thereupon, all rites are accomplished—thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
“Now, as for the ritual applications:
by reciting [the mantra] once, protection is afforded to oneself, one’s kin, villages, and cities.”

Having also effected possession through the binding of armor and other rites, one causes all these entities— such as the sandalwood-scented *grahāgraha*, the hand-holding *vajrāṅkuśa*, the jewel, the sun, the banner, the row of teeth, the lotus, the sword, the wheel, the tongue, the universal vajra-armour, the fang, and the fist-seals—
to enter [the disciple] by means of a single recitation.
One should fasten a vajra to a peacock-feather plume for the rite of illusion (*māyākarma*).
Then, Satvavajrī should bind that peacock-feather plume with the mudrā; one should recite the mantra until the mudrās of all the Tathāgatas enter it.
Thereafter, one sees various forms emerging from the plume.
From that time forth, by means of that peacock-feather whisk (*piñcchaka*), he displays all forms according to the prescribed ritual.
By whirling that very same whisk after it has been consecrated with a single recitation, he displays all forms to himself.
By means of that very same whisk, he displays worldly feats of illusion (*māyākarma*).
He also manifests the images of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;

he shows the Tathāgatas in all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, together with their circles of assemblies, performing the miraculous transformations of a Buddha such as the subduing of Māra’s armies,
until he himself becomes a form of a Buddha endowed with the excellence of all aspects.
“Desiring to perform subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*), one should bind the *satvamudrā* of all the Tathāgatas and recite [the mantra] until that mudrā blazes.
From that point on, by binding this mudrā, one pleases and brings under control all the Tathāgatas;
how much more so other sentient beings?”
“Now, by one who desires to accomplish the supreme mundane attainments, having first recited in that same manner for one month with eight thousand repetitions,
he should then, at the end, form the mudrā and recite throughout the entire night in that same way until the mudrā blazes.
"From that time forth, by means of the binding of mudrās, one becomes either a worldly siddhi or a vidyādhara-siddhi," so said the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
The detailed procedure for the ritual service of the Tathāgata family is completed.
Now follows the detailed procedure for the ritual service of the Vajra family:
"In that regard, at the very beginning, one should first act in this manner;
likewise, according to whatever is desired to be done."
"One should recite one hundred thousand syllables;
one should recite this throughout the entire night.
From that time forward, one becomes capable of both subduing and favoring all sentient beings," so said the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
Then, if one should wish to accomplish [the rite], one must have a cloth painting (paṭa) executed according to the rules.
Thereafter, having performed worship in that same manner for one month while consuming all desired foods and acting according to one's will,
one should recite with the voice of Vajra eight thousand times at each of the four junctions of the day.

This continues until the end of the month, at which time, having performed a grand worship of the cloth painting and having bound the Great Mudrā of Vajrahuṃkāra, one should recite the mantra until the sound "Hūṃ" issues forth from that binding of the mudrā.
Then, at dawn, Maheśvara and the other lords of the gods, together with their hosts and retinues, will stand before one and seek instructions.
Then the Vidyādhara should speak thus: "Whenever I say, 'Come' or 'Do this,' you must then come and carry out my command.
From that moment on, he becomes the sovereign of the entire triple world;
and according to his will, he wanders through the whole of the three realms in a mere moment, issuing his commands.
Furthermore, he returns again,
exercising both restraint and favor,
and enjoys divine pleasures and the enjoyments of the three worlds according to his own will.
Having gratified all women, beginning with the consorts of all the lords of the gods, he enjoys them;
yet no one whatsoever is able to do anything to him.
