Having subdued all wicked deities and others with the sound "Hūṃ," he lives for as many hundreds of thousands of kalpas—thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.

“Now, if one should desire the accomplishment of the mudrās, having performed the recitation as prescribed, at the end of the month, one should bind the Vajra-Hūṃkāra Samaya-mudrā and recite throughout the entire night.
Then, at dawn, the mudrās become accomplished.
Thereafter, by binding the mudrās according to the rules and employing the syllable HŪṂ, [one succeeds].”

[These include] traveling through space, manifesting all things, invisibility, displaying illusions, entering into all beings, summoning, subjugating, generating universal satisfaction, bringing forth all kinds of jewels, displaying great flames of splendor, displaying a rain of jewels, emitting loud boisterous laughter, purifying, cutting, and piercing all sentient beings, revolving the wheel of the seasons, causing the manifestation of reality as it is, setting in motion all ritual activities, protecting, paralyzing, immobilizing, terrifying, and killing; sealing all sentient beings, engaging in acts of sensual pleasure and delight, performing consecrations, causing all states of being to sing, dance, summon, enter, burst open, and possess, and so forth.
"He performs all activities," said the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
“Now, if one should desire the means for subtle knowledge, one practicing the *vajra-hūṃ-kāra* samādhi must accomplish it for one month by means of that same recitation-yoga (*jāpayoga*).
Then, at the end, one should recite throughout the entire night with this very samādhi,
until at dawn one becomes possessed of the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*) and becomes capable of favoring and restraining all sentient beings,” so said the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
“Now, if one should desire the accomplishment of ritual actions (*karmasādhana*), one should practice by reciting [the mantra] in that very same manner for one month.
Then, at the conclusion, one should recite throughout the entire night.
Thereafter, all ritual actions are accomplished,” so said the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
Then, by means of that which has been uttered once with the desired intention, all rites—such as protection and so forth—are accomplished.
The detailed procedure for the ritual practice and the accomplishment of the Vajra family is completed.
Now follows the detailed procedure for the ritual service (*upacāra*) of the Lotus Family (*padmakula*):
"In that regard, first of all, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times; once this has been previously accomplished, the practice (*sādhana*) proceeds."

On the cloth, the Blessed One Sarvajagadvinaya and the others are to be depicted; on all his sides, the four Great Beings are to be made according to the arrangement of the four maṇḍalas, and at the end, the goddesses.
Then, that very same detailed procedure for recitation should be performed, and at the end of the month, one should recite throughout the entire night.
Thereupon, the Blessed One Sarvajagadvinaya arrives.
"He bestows the boon at the appropriate time," said the Blessed One, Vajradhara.

Now, if one should desire the accomplishment of the mudrā, one should likewise form the Padmavajrī mudrā and, having released it as prescribed, recite the mantra at the four junctions of the day with eight thousand recitations.
Then, one should recite throughout the entire night while maintaining the mudrā.
At dawn, success is attained.
"Then, by means of binding the mudrās according to the rules, one brings about the discipline of the entire world," so said the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.

“Now, if one should desire the accomplishment of the method of meditative absorption (*samādhinaya*), then at the end of the month, throughout the entire night, one should perform the recitation (*jāpa*) by means of whichever meditative absorption is desired.
Thereupon, at dawn, all meditative absorptions will become manifest,” so said the Blessed One, Vajradharma.
Then, if one should desire the accomplishment of ritual actions (*karmasādhana*), reciting in that same manner, one should recite for the entire night at the end of the month;
thereupon, the exhaustion of all karma occurs—thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
The detailed procedure for the ritual service of the Lotus Family is completed.
Now follows the detailed procedure for the ritual service of the Jewel Family.
“In that regard, first of all, having performed the fourfold prostration to all the Tathāgatas, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times.
Then, in the same manner, one should depict the Blessed One Sarvārthasiddhi upon a cloth painting by means of the yoga of the four-mudrā maṇḍala.
Then, having performed worship in the same manner, one should accomplish [the practice] in the same manner.”
At the end of the month, one should recite [the mantra] for the entire night.
Then, at dawn, the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha, the Bodhisattva who is the Jewel of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas, will arrive and bestow empowerment.

Through that empowerment, one becomes a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) of the knowledge-holders (*vidyādhara*) throughout the triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system—so said the Blessed One Vajradhara.

Now, if one should desire the accomplishment of the mudrās, then by that same application of Dharmavajrī, the Vajraratna-mudrā should be accomplished according to the rules; it becomes the performer of all desired actions.
"Now, if one wishes to accomplish the knowledge of jewels, one should likewise meditate upon the samādhi arising from the Vajra-jewel according to the following sequence:
'How can there be the production of a jewel from space, which is devoid of intrinsic nature?
And how can there be the production of the body of a Bodhisattva from a jewel? "

"Having cultivated this samādhi during the four junctions of the day, one should recite it; thereafter, at the end of the month, one should recite throughout the entire night with that very same samādhi.
Then, at dawn, all the Tathāgatas will arrive and confer upon one an empowerment according to one's desire. Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
“Now, if one should desire the accomplishment of desires, reciting in that same manner at the end of the month, one should recite throughout the entire night.
Then, at dawn, the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha becomes the accomplisher of all aims. Thereafter, one may perform all ritual activities. Thus spoke the Blessed Noble Vajradhara.
The detailed procedure for the ritual service of the Jewel Family is hereby completed.
Now follows the detailed procedure common to the ritual service of all families.
In that regard, from the very beginning, there is the detailed procedure for the ritual service (*upacāra*) of all heart-mantras (*hṛdaya*).

Having uttered, "May the heart-intentions of all the Tathāgatas be accomplished," one should recite the heart-mantra according to one's preference and perform the rite of accomplishment (*sādhana-vidhi*).

In this regard, the procedure for the ritual service of the mudrās is as follows: Having said, "May all mudrās become objects of enjoyment for me," one should bind the samaya-mudrā and recite the mantra according to one's inclination and capacity. Thereafter, accomplishment will occur accordingly.
In this regard, this is the procedure for the ritual service (*upacāra*) of all mantras:

having said, "May the accomplishment of speech free from conceptual proliferation (*niḥprapañca*) come to pass; may the meditative absorptions (*samādhi*) of all the Tathāgatas arise within me," one should recite the mantra according to one's preference.
This is the accomplishment.
In this regard, this is the procedure for the ritual application of the *vidyā*:

“Those beings of mine who are blinded by ignorance, and all the Tathāgatas who have become the restraint (*saṃvara*) through the attainment of *vidyā*”—having said this, one should recite the *vidyā* as desired and bring about the accomplishment (*sādhana*). Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Vajradhara. “Now follows the detailed procedure for the vajra-recitation (*vajrajāpa*), by means of which the heart-mantras (*hṛdaya*), mudrās, and *vidyās* may be employed according to one’s wish.”

"Whichever sentient being's heart-seal, mantra, or vidyā one should accomplish through the purpose of recitation— that person, whether oneself or another, will be accomplished as the object to be attained," said the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
The detailed procedure for the recitation common to all families is completed.
Now follows the detailed procedure for the accomplishment common to all families.
In that regard, first of all are the accomplishments of the Tathāgata family;
namely: the accomplishment of the fulfillment of purpose, the accomplishment of supernatural powers, the state of a vidyādhara, and the great accomplishment.
“In that regard, the accomplishment of the object occurs as follows:

wherever there may be a suspicion of a treasure, one should form the mudrā and, through one’s own meditative absorption, gaze upon that location of the treasure with the vajra-vision. If one sees a vajra-form arise, it should be known thus: ‘There is a treasure here.’”
Then, having bound the Vajrasphoṭa Samaya-mudrā and dug it up, one should take it according to one's desire; thus one attains it without delay—so said the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.

“In that regard, the accomplishment of the perfection of supernatural powers (*ṛddhisiddhi*) occurs. Having recited the mantra ‘Vajrasiddhi’ while performing the mudrā, there arise four kinds of supernatural powers, namely: walking and sitting upon the surface of water, as well as manifesting all forms such as those of the Tathāgatas and others, for as long as one desires.”
He is invisible;
he travels through space, flying upward to a thousand *yojanas* and moving downward as well;
and from all directions, at a speed according to his desire, he comes back after circling from a distance of a thousand *yojanas*.
By means of a vision extending for a thousand *yojanas*, he knows the desires of all sentient beings;
he sees all phenomena with his eyes and hears them with his ears.
By means of that vision extending for a thousand *yojanas* in all directions, he lifts up all women who are pleasing to his mind from their bodies and brings them [to himself].
It seizes all objects, including all gold, fine gold, jewels, pearls, and so forth,
and no one at all is able to do anything to it;
it becomes invisible even to a diamond.
How much more so with others?
Possessing the strength of ten thousand men, eternally healthy, constantly enjoying all desires, perpetually youthful, and possessing a divine form,
one beholds and worships all the Tathāgatas together with Vajrasattva, and attains the unsurpassed vajra-siddhi for four thousand years.
"He lives," said the Blessed One, the Vajra-miracle of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, the accomplishment of the siddhi of the Vajra-Vidyādhara occurs as follows:
by accomplishing the mudrās, one becomes a "Vajra-Vidyādhara"; through that siddhi, one becomes a universal monarch (cakravartin) of the Vajra-Vidyādharas.
“Enjoying all desires, he travels through a thousand buddha-fields in a single instant and returns;
he experiences all pleasures;

possessing the vitality of a sixteen-year-old and bearing hair that is curled like a ringlet, he becomes a great Vajra-Vidyādhara who, beholding all the Tathāgatas together with Vajrasattva, remains for a great kalpa,” so said the Blessed One.
The holder of the vidyās of all Tathāgatas.
Therein, the accomplishment of the great siddhi occurs;
by accomplishing one's own mudrā through the meaning of the heart-mantra,
one's own mudrā becomes embodied in a living being.

In a single instant, manifesting in manifold forms throughout all world-systems in the ten directions and initiating manifold activities, he beholds all the Tathāgatas together with Vajrasattva; having honored them with all the offerings to the Tathāgatas endowed with the excellence of all aspects, and having accomplished the welfare of all sentient beings without exception, he returns once more, enjoying all the desires, pleasures, and mental well-being of all world-systems, endowed with the excellence of all aspects.
“The Great Bodhisattva, equal to Vajrasattva, shall possess a lifespan lasting for all great eons without exception,” so said the Blessed One, the Accomplishment of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, these are the accomplishments of the Vajra Family:
namely, the accomplishment of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds, the accomplishment of all empowerments, the accomplishment of all happiness and mental well-being, and the supreme accomplishment.
“In that regard, the accomplishment of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds occurs.
Having bound the mudrā of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds and having trampled Maheśvara with the left foot, one should perform the sādhana. Then, that image emits a sound.”
Then the syllable *huṃ* should be employed.
As soon as the syllable *huṃ* is employed, Maheśvara and all the other lords of the three worlds, together with their retinues,
will come before the practitioner and become subject to his commands.
From that time forth, he becomes Vajradhara, the sovereign of all the three worlds;
he travels through the sky and returns after traversing the entire wheel of the three worlds,
and with the syllable *huṃ*, he subdues wicked gods and all other beings.

"Taking the form of the Vajra-hūṃkāra of all Tathāgatas, governing the entire triple world by his command, and beholding and pleasing all the Tathāgatas together with Vajrasattva, he lives for a thousand years," said the Blessed One,
Vajra-hūṃkāra.

“In that regard, one who is accomplishing this mudrā for the attainment of all consecrations should first consecrate oneself with the Jewel Mudrā of the Consecration of All Tathāgatas and then perform the accomplishment. Thereafter, for one who has accomplished it, there is a fourfold consecration.”
These are the vajra consecration, the jewel consecration, the dharma consecration, and the action consecration.
Among these, when the vajra consecration is obtained, one becomes a Vajradhara of all the Tathāgatas;
with the jewel consecration, one becomes the sovereign of all jewels.
"In the empowerment of Dharma, one becomes a King of Dharma;
in the empowerment of Action, one attains the accomplishment of all mundane and supramundane activities"—thus spoke the Blessed One, the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas.
“In this regard, this is the accomplishment of all happiness and mental well-being:

namely, by constantly performing the worship of all Tathāgatas through secret worship, one attains the accomplishment of all happiness and mental well-being of all Tathāgatas. Thus spoke the Blessed One, the All-Tathāgata-All-Happiness-and-Mental-Well-Being.
“In this regard, this is the supreme accomplishment, namely: ‘I am equal to Vajradhara’—thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.”

In this regard, these are the accomplishments of the Lotus family (*padmakula*), namely: enchantment (*anurāgaṇa*), subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*), protection (*rakṣa*), and the accomplishment of the lotus (*padmasiddhi*).
“In that regard, the accomplishment of enchantment occurs:

through the proper cultivation of the ruby (*padmarāga*), one becomes capable of enchanting all sentient beings, beginning with all the Tathāgatas. Likewise, by the recollection of one’s own Lokeśvara, one becomes capable of bringing all sentient beings under one's influence.”
"By means of the samādhi of the pervasion of loving-kindness (*maitryaspharaṇa*), one becomes capable of protecting, shielding, and guarding the entire world.

By means of one's own *padma*-samādhi, having grasped a lotus with the hand and accomplished it, one takes the form of Lokeśvara, endowed with the excellence of all aspects, and lives for four thousand years. Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Lotus of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, these are the accomplishments (*siddhis*) of the Jewel Family (*maṇikula*).
Namely: the accomplishment of the empowerment of all families,
the state of great splendor,
and the fulfillment of all hopes.
And the accomplishment of the jewels.
“In that regard, there is the accomplishment of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas;
namely, the bestowing of one’s own empowerment, the offering of lamps, and the fulfillment of the perfection of generosity.

By accomplishing the jewel according to one’s ability and worshipping all Tathāgatas with the four accomplishments, one will soon attain success. Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Jewel of All Tathāgatas.
The extensive procedure for the common accomplishments of all families is completed.
“Now I shall further explain the *Sarvakalpopāyasiddhitantro*,” said the Blessed One, the Being without beginning or end.
[In that regard, first of all is the *Hṛdayopāyasiddhi-tantra*:
Just as the world is to be disciplined, so is success desired;
therein, the seal (*mudrā*) is indeed the great means (*upāya*) that bestows all success.
In this regard, here is the *Mudropāyasiddhitant*ra:
"The world is disciplined through dispassion (*virāga*), yet the accomplishment of the mudrā arises from passion (*rāga*).
Therein, the supreme cultivation (*bhāvanā*) as the means (*upāya*) brings about all accomplishments."
In this regard, here is the *Tantra of the Accomplishment of Mantra-Method*:
"This world has fallen away from the truth; mantra-accomplishment is not desired [by them].
But the method that is free from conceptual proliferation (*niḥprapañca*) is supreme and brings about all accomplishments."
In this regard, there is this Tantra of the Accomplishment of Knowledge and Means:
"One who is attached to ignorance does not attain the accomplishment of knowledge;
therein, the means is the excellent, vast [method] that bestows all accomplishments."
The Tantra of the Accomplishment of All Rituals and Means.
“Now I shall further explain the tantra of the accomplishment of merit for all kalpas,” said the Blessed One, the Sarvatathāgata.

In that regard, having first performed the *Svahṛdayapuṇyasiddhi-tantra* and offered the fourfold worship, one attains great merit; for through the supreme merit of worshipping the Buddha, one succeeds—of this there is no doubt. Thus it is said.
In this regard, here is the *Mudrā-puṇya-siddhi-tantra*:
"By guarding the secret samaya, one attains great merit; for even one who lacks merit shall quickly achieve accomplishment through the protection of the samaya. Thus it is said.
In this regard, here is the *Mantrapuṇyasiddhi-tantra*:
Through the primordial words of the Buddhas, one shall obtain great merit;
even one who lacks merit quickly attains accomplishment through the gift of Dharma.
In this regard, here is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of Knowledge and Merit:
"Giving is indeed the foremost of merits; by giving, one acquires merit.
Having fulfilled the perfection of giving, one swiftly attains Buddhahood. Thus it is said.
The Tantra of the Accomplishment of Merit for All Rituals.
"Now, I shall further explain the *Sarvakalpaprajñāsiddhi-tantra*.
In that regard, first of all is the *Hṛdayaprajñāsiddhi-tantra*:
"By entering the letter A, one understands all letters;
by meditating upon one's own face and the faces of others, one shall attain accomplishment."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
In this regard, here is the *Mudrā-prajñā-siddhi-tantra*:

"Wisdom is proclaimed as the samādhi called 'Penetrating Insight' (*nairvedhikī*); by means of that wisdom, the mudrās are accomplished, and one who meditates upon them accomplishes [the goal] in an instant."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, foremost in wisdom.
In this regard, here is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of Mantras and Wisdom:
Because of this samādhi called "Following the Sound of Wisdom," which is free from conceptual proliferation,
one will swiftly attain the accomplishment of mantra through its cultivation.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrabuddhi.
In this regard, here is the *Vidyā-prajñā-siddhi-tantra*:
"Among the various specific mantras of the *vidyās*, no distinction whatsoever exists;
by meditating thus with wisdom (*prajñā*), accomplishment (*siddhi*) will certainly be swiftly attained."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Wisdom-Knowledge of all Tathāgatas.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Accomplishment of Wisdom in All Kalpas.
"Now I shall explain the *Kalpasaṃbhārasiddhi-tantra*," said the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi.
In that regard, from the very beginning, there is the *Sarvahr̥tsambhārasiddhitantra*.
One who performs all forms of worship indeed increases their accumulation;
thus, the accumulation of wholesome qualities (*kuśala-dharma*) is accomplished.
In this regard, here is the *Mudrā-saṃbhāra-siddhi-tantra*:
"Through the entry into many wheels and the visualization of many maṇḍalas,
the great siddhi of the mudrās of the equipment-offerings proceeds."
In this regard, this is the *Mantrasambhārasiddhi-tantra*:
"Through the yoga of rejoicing and so forth, by reciting the true Dharma, and by the performance of many recitations, the accomplishment of mantra will certainly be attained. Thus it is said.
In this regard, here is the *Vidyāsaṃbhārasiddhi-tantra*:
"Because ignorance has been thoroughly abandoned through the method of the perfection of generosity,
one who has fulfilled the accumulations attains accomplishment swiftly."
The Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Accumulations for All Rituals.
The extensive tantra of the ritual procedures for all kalpas is completed.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Knowledge Tantra of the Arising of the Symbols of All Families.
In that regard, how does the Vajra-born arise?
That very Blessed One is the Being (*sattva*), the mind of all, the self-sovereign Lord;
he is the firm Being of the self-arisen ones, the Vajra of body, speech, and mind.
The supreme being among beings, through the meditation on the vajra within the heart, is known as Vajrasattva; for the vajra is established in him.
By means of the yoga of knowledge, that very universal [Self], having emerged from the heart of the Buddhas of incomparable splendor, becomes manifold in form.
He himself would become a Victor equal in number to the atoms of all world-realms;
indeed, from those very Vajra-bodies, Vajrasattva would arise.

From that very [source] arise the primary beings (*ādisattva*), who are the origin of all signs; from those signs arise the great beings (*mahāsattva*), and from them arises this entire system. Thus it is said.
Whoever should hear this, believe it, hold it in their heart,
and always contemplate it with joy, shall swiftly attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Knowledge Arising from the Reality of All Tathāgatas.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke the extensive tantra of the ritual procedures for the knowledge arising from all ritual manuals.
In that regard, first of all, there is the Tantra of the Knowledge Arising from the Rituals of All Tathāgatas.
The knowledge of the Buddhas is indeed non-conceptual and eternal;
yet, because it proceeds from that non-conceptual knowledge through conceptualization, it is called a "kalpa" (ritual).

In this regard, here is the *Jñānatantra* on the arising of the ritual manual (*kalpa*) of the Tathāgata family: "That which is non-conceptual yet whose nature is conceptualization, wherein conceptualization arises from conceptualization—that is Vajrasattva, the Great Being; therefore, it is called a 'ritual manual' (*kalpa*)."
In this regard, there is this *Jñānatantra* arising from the ritual manual (*kalpa*) of the Vajra family:

"For just as rituals that grant the accomplishment of the ritual manual (*kalpasiddhi*) are written down and conceptualized, they are therefore called 'ritual manuals' (*kalpa*) by those whose nature is free from conceptual construction (*vikalpa*)."
In this regard, here is the Knowledge Tantra (*jñānatantra*) concerning the arising of the *Padmakula* ritual manual (*kalpa*):
Passion is born from conceptual construction (*vikalpa*), and it is established within the lotus (*padma*).
From that, indeed, the accomplishments (*siddhi*) that endure for an eon (*kalpa*) arise.
In this regard, here is the Knowledge Tantra arising from the Ritual Manual of the Jewel Family:
"For jewels are indeed free from conceptual construction, yet they are highly exalted by their powers;
in the same way, divine accomplishments arise without being conceptually constructed."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
The Knowledge Tantra of the Origin of the Ritual Manuals of All Families.
Now follows the Knowledge Tantra of the Origin of the Heart-Essence of All Ritual Procedures.
Through the performance of one's desires, that which is desired is accomplished;
because he is the means for achieving meditative absorption (samādhi) and resides within the heart, he is therefore called "Hṛdaya" (the Heart).
Now follows the Tantra of the Knowledge Arising from All Mudrās.
Just as the royal seal and supreme edict are difficult to transgress and indestructible, so too is that which is trusted by the signs of the Great Soul proclaimed as the "Seal" (mudrā).
Now follows the Knowledge Tantra of the Origin of Mantras.
For it is indeed untransgressible, difficult to pierce, and secret;
because it is deliberated upon for the sake of secret accomplishment, it is therefore defined as "mantra."
Now follows the Vidyāsaṃbhavajñāna-tantra.
Because it exists for the destruction of ignorance and for the attainment of the supreme accomplishment of the science of speech,
and because the accomplishment of knowledge is found therein, it is proclaimed as "Vidyā" (Knowledge).
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
The Knowledge Tantra on the Origin of All Ritual Manuals, Heart Mantras, and the Like.
Now follows the Sarvakalpajñānotpattitantra (The Tantra on the Arising of Knowledge of All Ritual Procedures).
In that regard, from the very beginning, there is the *Hṛdayajñānotpattitantra*.
The heart-mantra should be understood as that which, when recited, reveals the heart of oneself or another,
and perceives and hears what is yet to be, what has been, and what is to come.
In this regard, there is this *Mudrājñānotpattitantra*:
"Having bound one particular mudrā according to the prescribed rite and having composed the mind, one should gaze upon the entire world as it truly is. Thus it is said.
In this regard, here is the Tantra on the Arising of Mantra-Knowledge:
Whoever utters the mantra once while speaking with their own tongue shall bring all that which is past, present, and future into truth.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, this is the tantra for the arising of knowledge and wisdom:
"Having uttered the vidyā even once, he should perceive with his mind the past, the present, and the future, according to the instruction of Vajravāk. Thus it is said.
The extensive tantra concerning the procedure for the arising of knowledge of all ritual procedures is completed.
Now follows the tantra for the practice of the secret body, speech, and mind vajra-mudrās common to all families.

In this regard, this is the method for accomplishing the secret body-mudrā of the Tathāgata family: seated in whatever manner, one should accomplish it in the cross-legged posture; according to the instructions of the painting, the Great Being shall attain success.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, this is the method for accomplishing the secret body-mudrā of the Vajra family:
one should accomplish it while standing firmly in the *pratyālīḍha* posture according to the illustration, being thoroughly enraged; one will succeed, there is no doubt in this.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrahuṃkāra.
In this regard, this is the practice for the secret body-seal of the Lotus Family:
Seated in the vajra-paryaṅka posture with both hands in the vajra-bind, having become the body of meditative concentration, one should accomplish the birth of the Lotus [Buddha].
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Padmasattva.
In this regard, this is the means for accomplishing the secret body-seal of the Jewel Family:
whether standing, sitting, or walking, in whatever manner one may be, one succeeds through the consecration of the Vajra-Jewel; of this there is no doubt.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Vajragarbha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulaguhyavāṅmudrāsādhanatantra*:
"The tip of the tongue is not excessively protruded, and it is joined with both the teeth and the lips."
One should accomplish all ritual manuals (kalpa) by means of the excellent sound of vajra-speech.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajravāca.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulaguhyavāṅmudrāsādhanatantra*:
"The speech of the wrathful one, firm and profound, is the syllable *huṃ* that swirls like a cloud."
The great vajra, bursting forth with wrath, is the practice for the speech of the Vajra-wrathful deity.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrahuṃkāra.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-guhyavāṅmudrā-sādhanatantra*:
"Without exhalation, with subtle breath [and subtle speech well-manifested],
all recitations are accomplished within the womb of meditative concentration and gnosis."
Thus spoke Sarvatathāgatasamādhijñānagarbha.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-guhyavāṅmudrā-sādhana-tantra*:
"By means of speech that is perfectly clear, one who is always supreme in prostration and also disciplined in recitation will quickly accomplish everything."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the one whose activity is the extensive ritual for the worship of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulaguhyacittamudrāsādhanatantra*:
"The Blessed One is indeed Desire, eternal, the bestower of happiness upon all sentient beings;
by meditating [on him] as Vajrasattva himself, one quickly attains accomplishment."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Kāma. In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulaguhyacittamudrāsādhanatantra*,
for the benefit of all sentient beings and for the sake of subduing the wicked.
For the sake of protecting the Buddha’s teaching, wrath is the supreme means for attaining accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Sarvatathāgatavajrahuṃkāra.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the practice of the secret mind-mudrā of the Lotus family:
Just as a lotus is unsullied by the defects of its dwelling yet possesses a beautiful color, so too is the mind.
In that way, through my passions and faults, passion shall arise; thus it is accomplished.
Thus said the Blessed One Padmarāga.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-guhya-cittamudrā-sādhana-tantra*:
"When indeed, for the sake of accomplishing all the aims and activities of all sentient beings, shall I rain down showers of jewels? Once accomplished, may I swiftly accomplish everything."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Ākāśagarbha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulaguhyavajramudrāsādhanatantra*:
whether standing, sitting, or walking, in whatever manner one may be.
One who performs everything with the secret hand in the vāmamudrā succeeds.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Sarvatathāgataguhyavajrapāṇi.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulaguhyavajramudrāsādhanatantra*:
"Whether standing in whatever manner or performing whatever action,
by forming the *vakrajrodha* finger-gesture and covering it with a cloth, one attains accomplishment."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Wrathful King of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-guhyavajramudrā-sādhana-tantra*:
"By forming the lotus-fist with the left hand while it is covered [by the right],
one shall swiftly attain the accomplishment (*siddhi*) of the lotus."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-guhyavajramudrā-sādhanatantra*:
"Having indeed formed the jewel-fist (*ratnamuṣṭi*), with the left hand covering the [right] palm,
however it may be performed, one shall surely attain the accomplishment of jewels."
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.

In this regard, here is the tantra for the accomplishment of the mudrās common to all families: "Indeed, by means of the application of the great mudrā and through the meditative absorption (samādhi) of one's own being..."
Through vajra speech and vajra vision, supreme accomplishment is swiftly attained.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas.
The *Sarvakulaguhyakāyavākcittavajramudrāsādhanatantra* is completed.

Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, having summoned all the Tathāgatas, spoke thus: "O Blessed Ones, Tathāgatas, proceed! These ritual manuals (kalpas) are empowered and proclaimed. Then all the Tathāgatas, having come together once more in assembly, [spoke].
Once again, they offered words of praise:
"Excellent! To you, Vajrasattva; excellent! To you, Vajraratna;
excellent! To you, Vajradharma; excellent! To you, Vajrakarma!"
This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna, the secret of all Tathāgatas, and the compendium of the Mahāyāna. Thus [it is said].
The unsurpassed tantra of all ritual manuals from the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha* is hereby completed.
CHAPTER 26b: CONCLUDING EPILOGUE OF THE *SARVA-TATHĀGATA-TATTVA-SAṄGRAHA* Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, rising from his seat, entreated the Blessed One with these one hundred and eight names:
"O Vajradhātu, Great Being, you who are the ultimate reality of all purposes!"
O Śākya King, of great wisdom, whose nature is vajra—homage be to you! // 1 //
O source of beings, O reality of the ultimate meaning, O great method that is the cause of beings!
O being of beings, who acts for the sake of the great welfare of beings—homage be to you! // 2 //
O Buddha-dharma, Great Dharma, Turner of the Wheel of Dharma, [Great Speaker, Foremost Vidyā, Great Being], homage be to you! // 3 //
O Great Action, O Great Protector, accomplisher of all rites! O Great-Souled One, supreme in the conduct of beings; for the sake of sentient beings, homage be to you! // 4 //
O you who have attained all the perfections, O knower of the wisdom of omniscience, O great skillful means for all sentient beings, O great wisdom—homage be to you! // 5 //
O supreme among the most compassionate, O you whose nature is compassion! O you who are great loving-kindness in all giving, O you who perform every action—homage be to you! // 6 //
O Lion of the Śākyas, Great Śākya, Śākya among the Śākyas, Great Sage! O All-pervading Lord, Great Vinaya, of interpretable meaning, supreme among the Vinayas—homage be to you! [7]
O you who have attained equality with the realm of phenomena, O Tathāgata who is the realm of phenomena; O Vajra Lord, Great Lord, Multitude of Beings, homage be to you! // 8 //
O Great Radiance, O Great Light, O Great Hero, O Great Strength!
O Great Hero, foremost among the truly valiant, O Śambhu, O Hero—homage be to you! // 9 //
O Brahman, self-existent, Blessed One, Hero of the Śākyas, Great Sage! O Sage who is the soul of all, Pure One, King of Dharma, homage be to you! (10)
O you whose body is space, supreme among bodies, who realizes the three bodies as no-body; O all-body, great body, vajra-body—homage be to you! 11.
O Speechless One, O Supreme Speech, O Revealer of the threefold speech, O All-Speech, O Great Speech, O Vajra Speech—homage be to you! 12.
Mindless mind, supreme mind, you who reveal the three minds and the mindless;
all-mind, great mind—homage be to you, O Vajra Mind! (13)
Non-vajra, vajra, supreme vajra, purifier of the triple-vajra and the vajra-less;
O all-vajra, great vajra, vajra of vajras, homage be to you! 14.
O all-pervading one, supreme among the peaks of existence, Lord of the Sugatas, Victorious One!
O Great King of the triple world, Vairocana, homage be to you! 15.
And whoever should hear this *Nāmāṣṭaśataka* even once, or should recite it, or even contemplate it, shall all attain Buddhahood. (16)
I entreat you, O Protector, for the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings;
having generated great compassion, please turn the wheel of Dharma. (17)
Then the Blessed One Vairocana, having heard the command of the Lord of all Tathāgatas, summoned all the Tathāgatas and spoke thus:
“O Blessed Tathāgatas, proceed to enter into assembly!”
Then all the Tathāgatas, having assembled together, spoke this verse:
"For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, throughout all worlds and in every way."
"May the wheel of Dharma be turned for the sake of disciplining the universe.

As soon as this was spoken, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, manifested throughout all Buddha-fields and all world-systems, appearing before all sentient beings, and even within every single atom-dust mandala, he turned the wheel of Dharma.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this verse once more: "For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, throughout all worlds and in every way,
let the universal vajra-wheel be set in motion according to what is needed for their discipline."

Then, as soon as this was spoken, in the same manner, in all buddha-fields, even unto all mandalas of atoms, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vajradhātu, set in motion all the vajra-wheels, beginning with the Vajradhātu.
Then the Mahābodhisattva Trilokavijaya spoke this verse:
"For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, throughout all worlds and in every way,
let the Wheel of Wrath be set in motion, subduing the universe according to their needs."
Then, as soon as this was spoken, in all buddha-fields, even unto all the circles of atoms, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Trilokavijayin, set in motion the wrathful wheel of all the Tathāgatas.
Then the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this verse:
"For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, throughout all worlds and in every way, may the lotus-wheel be set in motion, according to the needs of those to be trained."
Then, as soon as this was spoken, in all buddha-fields, even unto all circles of atoms, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Dharmarāja, set in motion the wheel of the Dharma.
Then the noble Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha spoke this verse:
"For the sake of the welfare of all beings, throughout all worlds, in every way."
"Just as the entire universe is governed, so let the wheel of jewels be set in motion."
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all sentient beings within all buddha-fields— whether subtle or gross—
all beheld every Tathāgata situated upon the lion throne in the gabled pavilion of the peak of the vajra-jewel at the summit of Mount Sumeru, turning all the wheels beginning with the Vajradhātu.
Then, at that time, the great bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this verse:
"For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, act according to what must be done; enter into this supreme human state and set the vajra-wheel in motion."
Then the Blessed One again summoned all the Tathāgatas and spoke thus: "O Blessed Tathāgatas, proceed once more to assemble."
Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, having again entered into assembly, entered into the heart of Vairocana.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, having realized himself as the vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, spoke thus to Vajrapāṇi:
"O son of good family, you too enter into my heart."
"All the maṇḍalas of all the Tathāgatas and all the Vajra families have entered into the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, authorized by all the Tathāgatas, spoke this verse:
"For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, I shall practice in every way."
To enter the vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Buddhas. Thus it is said.
Then, as soon as this had been spoken, as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all the world-systems throughout all world-systems—
those Tathāgatas each manifested emanation-bodies equal in number to the atoms in all world-systems and entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana.

Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi [perceived] within all the Tathāgatas and within all the bodies, all the locations for the utterance of speech, all the flows of the mental continuum, all the diamond methods, all the major and minor limbs, all the places, all the primary marks, all the secondary characteristics, all the pores of the skin, and all the mandalas of atoms of every dust mote of the Blessed One Vairocana.
And having entered into their hearts, they remain there.

Then the Blessed One, having recently attained perfect awakening, the vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, realized himself as the body of all Tathāgatas; from the summit of Mount Sumeru, he proceeded toward the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), and having arrived there,
he sat beneath the Blessed One’s Bodhi tree in accordance with worldly custom.
Again, taking up blades of grass, he uttered this inspired utterance: "Aha!
How supreme is the welfare of oneself for those who teach beings, that for the sake of those to be trained, the wise indeed destroy the views of the heretics."
"For the sake of purifying the world that is undisciplined and blinded on all sides by false views, through the light of knowledge, one should attain the awakening of a Buddha. Thus [it is said].
Then the gods of the desire realm (kāmāvacara), not knowing the reality of the Blessed One, said:
"O Śramaṇa, why do you endure such intense and such terrible sufferings for the sake of awakening?
Then the Blessed One, having spread out those grasses and sat down, spoke thus to those gods:
“Friends, proceed toward my awakening!
Then the gods who frequent the realm of desire, not understanding the meaning of what the Blessed One had said, approached Śakra, the lord of the gods;
having approached, they reported this account to Śakra, the lord of the gods.
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, surrounded by a host of deities belonging to the realm of all desires, reported this account to Mahābrahmā, the sovereign of the realm of form.
Then Mahābrahmā, together with the deities of the realms of all desires and form, reported that account to Īśvara, the lord of the three worlds.

Then Maheśvara, the lord of the three worlds, spoke thus to Nārāyaṇa and all the other lords of the gods: "O worthy ones, comply! For the sake of conforming to the world, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, will again manifest supreme perfect enlightenment. You should know that the Tathāgata is not a mere human being."
Only gods become Tathāgatas; even if they were to strive among humans, they would not attain the state of a Tathāgata.
"Therefore, it is well; proceed there to pay him homage.

Then Maheśvara and the other lords of the gods, having stationed themselves at the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), approached the Blessed One where he was seated at the seat of awakening; having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One.
They spoke thus to the Blessed One: “O Blessed One, out of compassion for us, please rise from this grass mat.”
"Having sat upon divine seats, in order to fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Then the Blessed One spoke thus to the lords of the gods:
"O sirs, proceed to grant me my unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
Then they spoke as follows:
“O Blessed One, we are not capable of bestowing enlightenment.
If we were capable, we ourselves would have fully awakened to perfect enlightenment.”
Then the Blessed One, illuminating this very meaning, spoke further these verses:
"It is neither material nor immaterial, neither real nor unreal, neither pure nor impure.
Having realized this wisdom, which is the enlightenment of the Buddhas, one becomes a Victor."
Then those lords of the gods remained silent for a moment.
Then the Blessed One, rising from that grass seat, spoke thus to those gods:
"O worthy ones, apply yourselves to realize such wisdom as this."
They spoke thus:
“We are not able, Blessed One.”
Then the Blessed One, sitting on that very seat, spoke this verse:
"By means of the penetration of the mind, make the thought of awakening firm;
having made the vajra firm within sentient beings, realize yourself as the Buddha."
Then they said,
“So be it,” and having done so, they all departed.

Then, when the night had turned to dawn, the Blessed One— acting in accordance with the world, having conquered Māra, and having awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment— praised the noble Vajrapāṇi, who resides within his own heart, with these one hundred and eight names for the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of beings, without exception.
Vajrasattva, Mahāsattva, [Mahāyāna, Mahātman / Mahāprabha, Mahāśuddha, Mahānātha], homage be to you! // 1 //
O Vajrarāja, Great Vajra, Vajra of all Tathāgatas, Great Being, Great Hero, Great Skillful Means, homage be to you! // 2 //
O Vajrarāga, Greatly Pure, All-Happiness, Great Bliss, Supreme Bliss, Without Beginning or End, Great Desire—homage be to you! // 3 //
O Vajrasādhu, great satisfaction, you who grant applause and bring joy; O great rapture, great delight, supreme gladness—homage be to you! // 4 //
O Great King Vajraratna, O Greatly Wise One, who confers self-consecration; O Greatly Radiant One, adorned with all jewels, homage be to you! // 5 //
O Vajra-splendor, O Great Splendor! O Vajra-light, O Great Radiance!
O Conqueror’s light, O Great Flame! O Buddha-light, homage be to you! // 6 //
O Vajraketu, Great Banner, Great Standard, Bestower of Wealth, O Ākāśaketu, Great Pole, Flag of Renunciation, homage be to you! // 7 //
O Vajrahāsa, Great Laughter, Great Joy, Delighter;
O You who possess the impulse of joy, who delight in passion, and who delight in the Dharma—homage be to you! // 8 //
O Vajradharma, Great Dharma, Purifier of all dharmas;
O Buddha-Dharma, Supreme True Dharma, Dharma of Passion, homage be to you! // 9 //
O Vajra-sharp one, great treasury, great-minded one of wisdom-knowledge; O great sword that cuts through evil, weapon of the Buddhas—homage be to you! 10.
O Vajra-cause, Great Wheel, Buddha-wheel, Great Treasure, Sovereign of all maṇḍalas, Supreme Dharma, Wheel of Dharma—homage be to you! // 11 //
O Vajra-speech, great speech, free from conceptual proliferation, great syllable, syllable-less, great recitation, speech of the Buddhas—homage be to you! 12.
O Vajra-action, supreme among good deeds, great action, performer of auspicious deeds; O secret worship, great worship, worship of the Buddhas—homage be to you! // 13 //
O Vajrarakṣa, great armor, supreme coat of mail, most firm; O great protector, great essence, Buddha-vīrya, homage be to you! // 14 //
O Vajrayakṣa, great wrathful one, terrifying to all the wicked! O supreme Yakṣa, the great skillful means of all Buddhas—homage be to you! 15.
O Great Union, Great Seal, Binder of the Great Samaya!
O Great Fist, Supreme among Seals, Vajra Fist, homage be to you! (16)
You are to be saluted, honored, worshipped, and treated with respect by the Tathāgatas, because you are said to be the bodhicitta that is without beginning or end. (17)
Having relied upon you, all the Victors and the heroic Bodhisattvas have arisen and will arise as the supreme causes for the awakening of a Buddha. (18)
Homage to you, Vajrasattva; homage to you, Vajraratna.
Homage to you, Vajradharma; homage to you, Vajrakarman. // 19 //
By whatever merit is gained from praising you with the foremost names and bowing down with sincere devotion, may everyone indeed attain the enlightenment of a Buddha. (20)
Whoever should correctly recite this supreme eight-hundred-name mantra even once,
established in excellent devotion, shall attain the state of all Buddhas.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
Then all those Tathāgatas bestowed their applause upon the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi with a single voice.
Excellent for you, Vajrasattva; excellent for you, Vajraratna;
excellent for you, Vajradharma; excellent for you, Vajrakarman!
"This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna, the secret of all Tathāgatas, which summarizes the Mahāyāna. Thus [it is said].

Thus spoke the Blessed One, and with joyful minds, the noble Bodhisattva Satatasamitābhiyukta and all others, having entered into their own hearts, rejoiced in what was spoken by the Blessed One and Vajrasattva.
Thus ends the Mahāyāna Sūtra titled *The Compendium of the Reality of All Tathāgatas*.
Oṃ, homage to the Buddha.
